terminology.visibility: action/service surface classification: 'advertised' = declared in a shipped SCPD document AND (at service level) present in the served device_description.xml serviceList (16 of 17 services, everything except AudioIn); 'hidden' = service omitted from the serviceList even though its SCPD ships (AudioIn only); 'internal' = callable on the wire but not SCPD-declared; supported class, EMPTY on this build (verified: all 205 canonical actions appear in their service's SCPD actionList)
terminology.reachability: 'callable' = dispatched to a real implementation; 'hidden-callable' = reachable by action name on the control path but not SCPD-declared: EMPTY on this build
terminology.fault_vocabulary_caveat: identical fault-code vocabularies across builds do NOT prove identical error behavior; a fault-code vocabulary delta claim is made only where control flow was also compared

canonical_action_records.definition: every action object under services.*.actions in this dataset; 195 unique action names (some names recur across services)

scpd_defined.definition: actions declared in shipped SCPD documents (opt/htdocs/xml/<Svc>1.xml actionLists): all 205 canonical records + 2 removed SystemProperties actions (ProvisionCredentialedTrialAccountX, ResetThirdPartyCredentials) that remain SCPD-advertised but have no canonical record because they are absent from the 86.x dispatch surface
scpd_defined.source: documentation.json visibility field + SystemProperties dispatch note

device_advertised.definition: SCPD-defined actions on the 16 service registrations present in the served device_description.xml serviceList; excludes AudioIn whose service is hidden (SCPD ships but service unlisted); includes the 2 stale SystemProperties advertisements

binary_dispatched.definition: canonical records that resolve to a binary dispatch path; 199 reach a real implementation handler (141 ptr-table 'direct', 57 id-table 'virtual', 1 strcmp chain) and 6 resolve to the AudioIn reject-all stub
binary_dispatched.source: documentation.json dispatch records; extractor action_tables carry 195 rows across 14 tables - the shared ConnectionManager table 0x10f118d4 binds both CM services (6 records from 3 rows) and QPlay dispatches via a strcmp chain rather than a table

implemented_actions.definition: binary-dispatched records whose dispatch reaches a real implementation (excludes the 6 reject-all stubs)

removed_stale.definition: SCPD-defined actions removed from the live dispatch surface in 86.x: 6 canonical records dispatched to the AudioIn reject-all 401 stub + 2 SystemProperties actions absent from the dispatch table entirely (a stub name lookup miss faults 401 identically, so wire behavior matches the stubs)

meta.scpd_crossvalidation: SCPD ground-truth cross-validation (post-rootfs-sweep): all 16 advertised services in opt/htdocs/xml/*.xml compared against the extracted dispatch/SV tables. ACTION PARITY 206/208: the only SCPD-only entries are the two known advertised-but-removed SystemProperties ops ProvisionCredentialedTrialAccountX + ResetThirdPartyCredentials; the 6 AudioIn actions advertise AND dispatch to reject-all 401 stubs, consistent with prior findings. STATE-VARIABLE PARITY: all SCPD names present in the binary tables; binary additionally dispatches UNADVERTISED SVs: Queue {QueueID,QueueOwnerID}, RenderingControl {HeightChannelLevel,RoomCalibrationBondedZoneInfo,SonarCalibrationAvailable,SonarEnabled}, hidden state variables served by handlers but never declared in SCPD. ARGUMENT PARITY: full arg-name match on spot-checked services (AVTransport all 42 actions). This validates the binary-driven extraction pipeline against the shipped advertisement files end-to-end.

records.obj: vret(member,+0x6c) -> f_1019db74: getter thunk adjusts this by -0x3a8 and returns the embedded DeviceProperties service object at zp+0x9d70
records.notes: Availability gate: dispatch at 0x1068bde8 ANDs rec.cap_flags with *(member+0x934), a u16 service-capability mask on the zoneImpl sub-object at zp+0x3a8. The mask is supplied at zp-aa construction: f_100c1478 loads it via lhz from a config object field +0x184 (0x100c1a70), passes it as arg8 through f_1018d27c into the zoneImpl ctor f_10691e00, which stores it to member+0x934 at 0x10692c20. There is no per-record enabled byte in this router: the prior enabled values were extractor artifacts that captured the next record's obj getter store. This service requires capability bit 0x1 of the mask. obj resolution: the member's runtime primary vptr is the derived table 0x10e98278 installed by the zp-aa ctor at 0x1018dbd0, not the base zoneImpl table 0x10f02034 written by f_10691e00 (whose slots +0x6c/+0x78/+0x7c/+0x88 are the pure-virtual stub 0x10809540). vret(member,+0x6c) -> f_1019db74: getter thunk adjusts this by -0x3a8 and returns the embedded DeviceProperties service object at zp+0x9d70. request_vtable.provenance: Request object lifetime: the request object arrives as r5-in at main router f_101953c8 (zp-aa vfunc; table 0x10e97d5c), is forwarded as r5-in to fallback router f_1068bc0c (call at 0x101956e4), forwarded again as r5-in to the per-service name-dispatcher (e.g. ZGT vtable 0x10f113b0 slot +0x8 = f_10732ff8, which strcmp-scans the name table at 0x10f113dc), and finally forwarded as r4-in to the matched action impl (e.g. GetZoneGroupAttributes f_10733878 at slot +0x24). Per-service dispatch vtables carry one slot per action (ZGT: 11 slots). The request object is allocated by the UPnP HTTP request layer above the zp vfunc entry; its ctor does not form a direct addis/addi reference in .text.
resolved_findings: Resolved at boundary: no .text ctor stores either candidate vtable (0x10ebc650/0x10ebd234) - the request object is allocated by an out-of-line UPnP-stack component and only consumed here. Slot semantics stand from caller patterns: parse 0x08, commit 0x0c, fault 0x14, in-arg 0x1c/0x20, out-arg 0x24, ctx 0x34, finalize 0x38.

Established: the complete request-object call chain is proven from zp-aa vfunc entry through the fallback router and per-service name-dispatchers down to the action impl (see provenance). Per-service dispatch vtables are mapped (e.g. ZGT 0x10f113b0, 11 action slots, name table 0x10f113dc).

request-object provenance pushed one level deeper: the service-route loop f_10352848 calls entry->vfunc[0xc8](entry, f_1053cc50(in_ctx)) at 0x10352940-0x10352960; f_1053cc50 is a getter returning *(in_ctx+0x288) - so the UPnP request object lives in the +0x288 slot of the HTTP-side request context handed to the dispatcher. Additionally the vtable at 0x10f10e88 was proven to be the class-A arg-record vtable (slot +8 = setName f_1055eaf0 stw +0x50, +0xc = getName f_1055eb00, +0x44 = the name-table arg accessor f_1073181c calling both record allocators) - it is the arg container class, not the request class.

CORRECTION: the 'request object at httpd_ctx+0x288' claim is disproven - +0x288 inside the route-binding container class is its name buffer (f_1053c234 passes container+0x288 as the strcmp target to by-name finder f_1053dba0) and doubles as an iteration cursor (f_1053cc5c advances +0x288 against *(+0x4) count). f_1053cc50 is only a thunk to element accessor f_1053db64 (bounds-checked, 40-byte-stride array at container+0x14). The iterated 'element' is the route binding record {+8: control-URL path strcmp'd by f_101953c8 against a 13-entry service table whose per-entry enable byte is zp+0x571c XOR 1, +0x70: action-name string consumed by the per-service name-dispatcher's binary search}. The request object proper reaches the name-dispatcher as r5-in (ZGT f_10732ff8 raises 401 via req->v[+0x14] on name miss, tail-calls v[+0x38] finalize).
request_vtable.callsite_proof: Slot semantics confirmed at concrete callsites in GetZoneGroupAttributes f_10733878: req->vtable[0x34] at 0x107338b0 returns the ctx object (result->+0x6c non-null check, ->+0x178 = zone-group impl); req->vtable[0x08] at 0x107338e4 is the arg-parse call made before the action body; req->vtable[0x14] at 0x10733904 is raise-fault; req->vtable[0x24] at 0x107339ac is get/create out-arg record by name (r4 = literal "CurrentZoneGroupName", repeated for "CurrentZoneGroupID"); the returned out-arg record has its own vtable (slots +0x10/+0x24 called at 0x10733950/0x107339c0 - a different class).
request_vtable.dispatch_chain: zp->vfunc[0xc8] = f_101953c8 (the per-service route matcher over the "/XxxService/Control" table) is invoked by f_10352848, which iterates a service container (*(r30+4) entries, element accessor f_1053cc50) and calls each entry's route-handler vfunc until one claims the request. f_10352848 is called by dp_impl internal-dispatch functions f_103548f4 and f_10355628 (joinZone/ValidateBondedState forwarding paths). The HTTP request path reaches the same zp vfunc from the UPnP HTTP action layer.
request_vtable.disproven: CORRECTION: the previously-listed candidate vtables 0x10ebc650 and 0x10ebd234 are NOT the request vtable. Their slot+0x34 impl f_1035a760 reads this+0x1ac0 and returns an enum code (0x41a/0), not a ctx object; slots +0x0c/+0x14/+0x1c/+0x24 are lock-guarded field getters (mutex at this+0x268 via f_10988558/f_10988984) copying +0x1aa1(byte)/+0x1aa2(strlcpy string)/+0x1abc(halfword)/+0x1abe(byte). They are sibling vtables of a state/session class in the UPnP-stack family, not the request interface.

special_values.REL_TIME: target is an absolute time position (H:M:S); in stream mode always allowed, in indexed mode requires capability bit 0x200000; negative target rejected with 711 in indexed mode

f_102b9088 indexed path: strcmp Unit vs TRACK_NR (0x10eb0498)

Target.description: Destination operand whose syntax depends on Unit: a decimal track ordinal for TRACK_NR, or a [-]H:M:S time for REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA.
Target.format: utf-8 text, buffer cap 1024 bytes (1023 chars + NUL)
Target.accepted_values: TRACK_NR: textual decimal whose strtol result lies in 1..65534. REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: three u8-wrapping decimal components; computed value = h*3600+m*60+s seconds.

special_values.TRACK_NR text beyond 1..65534 (incl. '0': rejected with 711: validation is (strtol_result - 1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned on the UNMASKED value; the u16 truncation (rlwinm r4,r30,0,16,31 at 0x102b938c) only sizes the record field and never rescues an out-of-range text - '65537' faults, it does not wrap to track 1
special_values.TRACK_NR with trailing junk, leading whi: accepted - strtol skips ws/sign and endptr is NULL so the tail is ignored
special_values.'--H:M:S' or signed components ('-5:00:0: accepted: the outer '-' is consumed manually, then each %hhu applies strtoul sign/wrap rules, so '--0:1:0' parses as negative-(251:00:00 wrapped) - a quirk of layering the manual sign over %hhu
special_values.'00:00:00' or '-00:00:00' (REL_TIME/TIME: zero magnitude -> success WITHOUT submitting any request (0x102b92d4-0x102b9318); '-00:00:00' under REL_TIME still faults 711 because the sign check precedes the zero check
special_values.'-H:M:S' (REL_TIME, indexed mode): rejected with 711 - sign flag byte nonzero and Unit != TIME_DELTA (0x102b9258-0x102b9270)
special_values.'-H:M:S' (TIME_DELTA, indexed mode): accepted; parser negates only the low seconds word (neg at 0x102ab920, hi word stays 0) plus a separate sign byte; submitted as a negative relative offset
special_values.'-H:M:S' (stream mode): not sign-checked at all - the negated seconds word *1000 yields a negative millisecond operand passed straight to the session vfunc; outcome is downstream-determined
special_values.'256:00:00' / '999:99:99' (either mode): accepted with u8 wraparound: 256->0, 999->231 etc.; there is no upper bound check on the total
special_values.'1 :2:3' (whitespace before a colon): rejected - the ':' literals in the scanf format must match immediately
special_values.'01:02:03junk': accepted - sscanf stops after the 3rd conversion and the tail is never inspected

Target.validation: TRACK_NR (indexed mode only): strtol result must satisfy (t-1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned else 711; on success u16 field t&0xffff is recorded in the rchsrcreq tag-8 record (the truncation is field-width only; the range check ran on the raw strtol value, so no wrap-to-valid exists). REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: f_102ab830 failure -> 711 indexed / 701 stream; indexed-mode leading '-' under REL_TIME -> 711; indexed-mode zero magnitude -> silent success no-op; stream mode performs no sign or zero gating. Missing/unparsable at the request layer -> 402.

evidence.notes: f_102ab830 Target parser: optional '-' then sscanf '%hhu:%hhu:%hhu', requires 3 fields, computes h*3600+m*60+s i64
bound check: cmplwi (t-1) vs 0xFFFD; u16 t&0xffff stored via rlwinm 0,16,31 at 0x102b938c into rchsrcreq tag-8 record
rlwinm r4,r30,0,16,31 computes the u16 record field from raw strtol result r30; the following addi r30,-1 + cmplwi 0xFFFD at 0x102b9394-0x102b939c validate the UNMASKED value
parser: secs = h*60+m then *60+s via shift/subf; bc on cr4.eq (first char '-') -> neg r7 at 0x102ab920; out pair {secs_word, 0} + separate sign byte at *arg2

Target.notes: Track normalization: strtol -> record field = value & 0xffff -> range check on the RAW value (raw-1 <= 0xFFFD). Ordering means the stored u16 equals the input for every accepted value; masking cannot wrap an out-of-range ordinal into range.

Seek.events_triggered: No UPnP event is emitted synchronously by this path; the SOAP response is committed immediately after the engine accepts the request while the actual position/track change is applied asynchronously by the chsrc transaction or streamer session. Any LastChange/state-variable update therefore originates downstream of the async apply and is not statically proven in this path.
Seek.state_transitions: None synchronously. The accepted seek is queued/applied by the player engine after the call returns; decoder, position and track-index state change happen inside the async transaction/streamer path, not in this handler.
Seek.return_behavior: The impl returns an integer status. On 0 the wrapper commits an empty 200 OK via req vfunc +0x0c (0x102f9494). On nonzero the code is forwarded to the request fault path req vfunc +0x14 at 0x102f944c and surfaces as the UPnPError errorCode. Caveats: (1) the wrapper tests cr0 rather than r3 at 0x102f9440; impl epilogues' stack-canary xor. leaves cr0.eq=1 on normal return, so rc reaches the completion vfunc +0x0c with r4=rc which handles the status-bearing response - the +0x14 branch is effectively a fallback. (2) In stream mode rc==0 only proves a session object accepted the call; the session vfunc's byte result is captured to a flag that gates a log line (0x102b91d8) and is not reflected in the SOAP status - a rejected streamer seek still reports success. (3) In indexed mode rc==0 only proves the rchsrcreq was enqueued, not that the seek applied; a zero-magnitude time target returns 0 without enqueueing at all.

/QPlay/Control.description: QPlay (QQ Music) authentication service; QPlayAuth dispatch is statically bound (strcmp-matcher 0x1073a4f0, exec 0x1073a5d0) and the request/response grammar and the Seed->Code transform are fully decoded.

QPlayAuth.description: QPlay authentication handshake (fully decoded end to end): dispatcher f_1073a4f0 strcmp-matches QPlayAuth -> exec f_1073a5d0. Exec calls req->v[+0x1c] to fetch arg Seed (0x10f11d64), parses via f_1056157c into a stack buffer capped at 0x80, gates on req->v[+0x08] parse-ok -> emits 402 (0x192) Invalid Args on failure, 401 (0x191) for unknown action names. On success it calls impl->v[+0x08](impl, seedBuf, codeOut, 0x80, midOut, 0x15, didOut, 0x15) where impl = req member +0x04. IMPL PROVEN STATIC: the impl object is constructed by f_10466750 (vptr 0x10ed1d18, installed at ctor site 0x1018f280) and its v[+0x08] = f_104666b4. f_104666b4 computes Code via f_1064548c(codeOut,0x80,seed) -> f_106453bc: ZZ0062 digest-init type 2 (proven MD5 - libsonoscrypto ZZ0062 dispatches type1=SHA-256, type2=MD5, type3=SHA-1 at 0x6b60-0x6b78), ZZ0064 update with seed bytes, ZZ0064 update with a 16-byte static key at 0x10efc7ac (53 6f 6e 6f 73 03 11 19 88 09 10 17 1e 22 ff ff = "Sonos"+11 bytes, preceded by literal 62800021), ZZ0061 finish, then RserializeData(digest,0x10,out,cap) serializes the 16-byte MD5 into codeOut. So Code = serialize(MD5(Seed || key16)). MID = "62800021" - f_106453a8 returns that literal (0x10efc7a0), copied via strlcpy f_10906304 cap 0x15; DID = snprintf "%u" of singleton 0x110b8150 member +0xcc (f_106454a8 -> getInstance f_1090ad44 -> f_10908350 reads +0xcc). Outputs emitted individually via req->v[+0x24] with names Code(0x10eb95c4)/MID(0x10f11d6c)/DID(0x10f11d70), response committed via req->v[+0x0c]. Correction: an earlier note claiming f_104666b4 was a MuseDebugInfo formatter and a wrong attribution is itself wrong - the impl vtable at 0x10ed1d18 statically binds it as v[+0x08]; the nearby MuseDebugInfo literals belong to a different function.

resolved_findings: Established: +0x3a8 resolves per class - on the audio-settings object it is a u8 selector byte propagated into DSP state setters (leaf f_10d8d93c writes the halfword arg into a 0x20c-stride record); the stw catalogue entries are vptr slots on unrelated classes at the shared offset. Next step: enumerate values written by the stb stores to name the selector vocabulary.

Producer chain completed as far as static evidence reaches: the ctor f_100df3fc loads the incoming record pointer from stack+0xf8 (lwz at 0x100df47c), reads byte 0 of that record (lbz r26,0(r3) at 0x100df494), and stores it to +0x3a8 (stb at 0x100dfa30). The record is the member bonded-configuration blob delivered at rc_impl construction; byte 0 is the member channel-position assignment. On model-9/Playbar the bonded-role query f_101b4e50 is a compiled-out return-0 stub (satellite/stereo-pair roles exist only in the model-8 fenway vocabulary: UNBONDED_DEVICE, BONDED_STEREOPAIR, BONDED_TO_SUB, BONDED_STEREOPAIR_AND_SUB, HT_BONDED_SATELLITE), so the concrete byte-0 values assigned by the bonded-config negotiator are not present in this image. 0x5704.description: Implementation-capability field read at 24 load site(s); gates action behavior paths
0x5704.effect: zp+0x5704 is the low byte of the device-model feature-flags word (+0xd0) on the product descriptor singleton, taken at zp-aa construction from the singleton getter and propagated into per-request SOAP context. It is a device-model capability byte, not a per-request computed predicate.
resolved_findings: Established: zp+0x5704 is a ctor-arg-derived config byte propagated into the SOAP per-request record. Still unknown: which config dimension it encodes (the +0x56fc..+0x5702 cluster suggests device/capability id fields). Next step: trace the ctor-arg source word (callers of f_1018d27c, arg slot 0xc4) to name the flag.

Named: zp+0x5704 is the device's audio-input-present capability. The producer chain: product-descriptor singleton 0x110b8150 flag word +0xd0 -> low byte +0xd3 -> booleanized by f_10908540 (returns byte!=0) -> caller f_100c1478 supplies it as the first stack arg -> zp-aa ctor f_1018d27c stores it at zp+0x5704 (0x1018dc70) -> SOAP router copies it into each request record at 0x101955b0.

Feature gated: in the UPnP service-registration builder (0x10433xxx), the same f_10908540 result at 0x10433318 selects the registration branch that emits '/AudioIn/Control' + 'urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:AudioIn:1' (target 0x10433a70). Nonzero byte -> AudioIn service exists; zero -> it is never registered. This matches the record's affected_services=[AudioIn].

Flag-word structure: +0xd0/+0xd4/+0xd8 are a 3-word capability bitfield on the MDP-populated product descriptor (product names {S43,ZP120,ZP90,BR200,S1,Sub,S3}, model codes A100/A200/A101/A102/B100/D100/C201/C100/X999/C200). Enumerated accessors: +0xd0 bit16 (andis.0x1 gate in f_109085a8 -> +0xd8 bit3), bits18/19 (f_109085fc/f_10908610), bits8-15 nonzero test (f_1090855c), bits16-31 nonzero test (f_10908578), high-halfword>>1 value (f_10908594); +0xd4 bits 2/4/13/21; +0xd8 bits 3/11/23. No accessor inspects individual bits of the low byte: it is only booleanized, so zp+0x5704 carries a unit flag.

Byte encoding resolved for S9: the model ctor f_10908f38 match-else ladder writes +0xd0=0x00008000 for ZPS9/Playbar (addis/ori constants at 0x10909184-0x10909190), so the flag word low byte +0xd3 = 0x00 and byte +0xd1 = 0x80. Two accessors partition the word: f_10908540 reads lbz +0xd3 and returns (byte != 0) - this is what zp+0x5704 caches; f_1090855c reads lwz +0xd0 and masks 0xff00 (the +0xd1/+0xd2 byte pair). Since +0xd3 = 0 on S9, the AudioIn/Control service registration gate evaluates false on Playbar - consistent with Playbar having no analog line-in jack (its only input is the TOSLink TV path, handled through the +0xd1 flag byte instead). The low byte is therefore a per-model analog-input-present byte written as a constant per product id, not a runtime bitmask.

cross-build check completed via the play1-model8 86.8 fenway binary (anacapad-m8-86.8.extracted): that build carries the full bonded-role vocabulary {UNBONDED_DEVICE, BONDED_STEREOPAIR, BONDED_TO_SUB, BONDED_STEREOPAIR_AND_SUB, HT_BONDED_SATELLITE} plus satellite DSP presets (dsp_preset_satellite.xml, satellite_processor.bin) - on satellite-capable hardware the role query is a real getter. On model-9 Playbar the same query (f_101b4e50) is a return-0 stub, so zp+0x571c = bool(role==1) is always false: the flag means "this zone is a bonded secondary member" (role 1 = the non-primary/surround member of a bonded set), which a Playbar can never be since it is always the HT primary. Affected services remain the HT/media set (HTControl, AVTransport, GroupRenderingControl, Queue).

cr_return_convention.description: Impl-return ABI: impls signal outcome as r3=code + CR0.eq=(code==0) set inside the impl (e.g. cmpwi cr0,r3,0 or mr. before blr - proven in f_102d0ac8 at 0x102d0cac/0x102d0dd4). Wrappers consume it with `beq cr0` -> emit else fault(r3). Impls that never write CR0 (DP/SP secondary-base accessors, null stubs) leave the flag stale from the request-parse layer; their post-impl fault branch is then driven by parse-layer state.

Otherwise field worker f_100d9d40: InstanceID!=0 -> 0x2be; fixed-output gate on +0x7ff/+0x801 -> 0x1f5; range check cmplwi 0x64 -> >100 gives 0x192; channel strcmp {Master,LF,RF} -> 0x192 if unknown; stores Master +0x7da (0x100d9f00, shadow +0x3c8, flag +0x3d4), LF +0x7dc, RF +0x7de; apply f_100d7f34; dirty byte +0x7f0.

Producer tail: field write + dirty-byte store, then f_1067c6ec(impl+8) which sets the event-source pending flag +0x110 (f_1067c46c) and wakes the upnpeventing sender (f_10678c50 -> sender+0x10e); f_100d993c schedules the deferred EQ snapshot f_100d7d6c -> f_100d78a4 ('AMV%hd LV%hd...' blob pushed to impl+0x3bc vfunc +0x14). The backing-field writer chain: the serializer reads values through getter vfuncs on the injected state object; the member fields themselves are written by the setter-path delegates (runtime-injected vptrs, same proven boundary as impl workers).
Resolved: backing field bound via the RCS LastChange emitter's literal->load correlation: +0x849 lbz in the RCS state-object block (+0x7da..+0x849, emitter f_100e27b0).

Producer: sonar-availability recompute f_100e1fec writes +0x849 at 0x100e2080/0x100e2634 and sets dirty +0x848 at 0x100e20ec; called from SetRoomCalibrationStatus f_100e32f4, f_100e3450, f_100e382c. Other writers: ctor, f_10725030. Emit reads +0x849 under dirty +0x848.

Producer tail: field write + dirty-byte store, then f_1067c6ec(impl+8) which sets the event-source pending flag +0x110 (f_1067c46c) and wakes the upnpeventing sender (f_10678c50 -> sender+0x10e); f_100d993c schedules the deferred EQ snapshot f_100d7d6c -> f_100d78a4 ('AMV%hd LV%hd...' blob pushed to impl+0x3bc vfunc +0x14). The LastChange XML is built lazily when the eventing worker invokes source vfunc +0x14 (f_100e32ec -> f_100e323c -> f_100e27b0), which emits only groups whose dirty byte is set and then clears all dirty bytes at 0x100e2eb8-0x100e2ed4.

x-rincon-cpcontainer.notes: fully decoded: two record forms verified in table bytes; kind consumed as browse-class selector (branches at 0x10389388/0x103894b0); flags are runtime-patched masks with lib_flag 0x1000000 = local library; namespace split RDCPA=containers/RDCPI=items proven by entry contents.

cp_id_map.notes: kind_enum f1 (4=album,5=artist,0xc=station,0xd=playlist/artist-album-list,0xe=playlist,0xf=track-list,3=track) and flag words f2 are inferred groupings, not proven semantics; f3=0x1000000 marks local-library entries. Extended 8-word records canonicalize legacy service URI domains (radea:/npsdy: on-demand track ids, rdradio: station ids) onto internal path templates + an explicit source scheme (x-sonos-http:/x-sonosapi-radio:) - i.e. service-URI rewrite rules.

uri_rewrite_entries._shape: 8 words: {match_prefix, kind_enum, flags, short_id, source_ext, path_template, source_scheme, trailer}

cp_id_map.record_forms: two record forms coexist in the 0x10e7747c table: (1) 6-word RDCPA/RDCPI records {cp_id*, kind, flags, lib_flag, short_prefix*, path_template*}; (2) 8-word raw-service records {cp_id*, kind, flags, short*, ext*, path*, service_scheme*, service_ext*} e.g. 'radea:Tra.' {kind 3, flags 0x2020, 'Tra.', '.mp3', 'ondemand_track::tra.%s', 'x-sonos-http:', '.mp4'} - service-URI prefixes carry the playable scheme + extension pair.
cp_id_map.kind_semantics: kind is the content-class selector consumed by the browse/translate walk (f_103893xx): kind==5 (artist) and kind==0xc (station) take dedicated branches at 0x10389388/0x103894b0; other observed values: 3=track (radea/npsdy Tra. -> ondemand_track), 4=album (GLBALBUM), 0xd=artist-views/library container (ARTALBUM/ARTCOMPILATIONS/ARTSINGLESEPS/LIBPLAYLISTS), 0xe=playlist (GLBPLAYLIST/LIBPLAYLISTS), 0xf=toptracks (ARTTOPTRACKS).
cp_id_map.flags_semantics: the flags word (+8) is a runtime-patched behavior mask: the browse init writes into table flag slots (stw at 0x10389350, 0x10389768, 0x103897f4) rather than treating them as read-only constants. The separate +0xc lib_flag (0x1000000) marks local-library records (mymusic: paths, mp./Alb. prefixes) vs global-catalog records (explore:/station: paths). Individual flag-bit names are not statically recoverable: no code reads the initializers with named constants, the mask is computed at init. Boundary.

namespaces.RDCPA: container id namespace - albums, artist views, playlists (browse containers)
namespaces.RDCPI: item id namespace - tracks and stations (GLBTRACK/ARTSTATION/GLBSTATION)
namespaces.radea/npsdy: raw service-URI prefixes (Rhapsody/Napster service types) with playable scheme+ext
namespaces.radio-radea/radio-npsdy: radio source-URI variants of the service prefixes

x-sonos-vli.grammar_detail: decoded at the sole consumer f_10687998: it formats the member id as 16 hex bytes via the '%s%02x%02x...%02x' chain (0x10687a84, 16 byte loads r3+0x0..0xf - the RINCON uuid), then emits 'x-sonos-vli:%s:%u,%s' = <hex member id>:<channel index>,<backing source URI>. The backing-source scheme is classified by a strncmp ladder: bluetooth: (len 0xa), spotify: (0x8), uri: (0x4), tvproxy: (0x8). A strchr(','') scan after formatting sanity-checks that the member id carries no comma, since the source URI is comma-appended.
x-sonos-vli.role: virtual line-in routing: names WHICH member's physical line-in/tvproxy/bt source the zone should pull, which channel, and the real backing URI. Consumed through the AVTransport line-in path; the x-sonos-vli:*:audio:* glob is the protocolInfo service-type pattern.

SonosSeekTime.description: Sonos time-position operand produced by f_102ab830: an optional leading '-' sets a separate sign flag, then sscanf('%hhu:%hhu:%hhu') must convert exactly three decimal fields. Each %hhu applies strtoul semantics per component - leading whitespace skipped, own optional +/- sign allowed, result truncated to u8 so >255 wraps mod 256. The ':' separators match literally (no whitespace before them); trailing characters after the third field are ignored. Output is a {seconds_word, fraction_word=0} pair (printed as '%lld.%06lld') plus the sign byte; a leading '-' negates only the seconds word. Total range 0..934575 s (255:255:255); there is no upper-bound check.
SonosSeekTime.format: [-]H:M:S where each component is a scanf %hhu (u8, mod-256 wrap); exactly three required; trailing junk ignored
used_by: AVTransport.Seek (Target for REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA, both indexed and stream modes)

evidence.notes: sign skip via cmplwi '-' + r3+=cr4.eq; sscanf fmt at 0x10eafc7c; secs=(h*60+m)*60+s; neg on cr4.eq; stw {secs,0} pair + sign byte

SonosSeekTime.notes: Action-specific restrictions layer on top: e.g. Seek indexed mode rejects a set sign flag unless Unit==TIME_DELTA, and treats a zero-magnitude pair as a silent no-op success. Stream mode performs no sign or zero gating.

SonosTrackOrdinal.description: Sonos track-ordinal operand: strtol(text,NULL,10) on the raw string - base 10, leading whitespace and +/- accepted, endptr NULL so trailing junk is silently ignored ('5junk' -> 5), saturates at LONG_MIN/MAX. Acceptance range is validated on the UNMASKED strtol result as (value-1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned, i.e. exactly 1..65534; a separate u16 truncation (value & 0xffff) sizes the downstream record field and cannot wrap an out-of-range input into validity.
SonosTrackOrdinal.format: decimal integer, strtol base 10; accepted lexical range 1..65534

evidence.notes: strtol(r26,0,10); rlwinm &0xffff at 0x102b938c sizes the record field; addi r30,-1 + cmplwi 0xFFFD at 0x102b9394-0x102b939c validates the raw value

SonosTrackOrdinal.notes: The mask-before-validate ordering looks alarming but is inert: the record field is computed pre-check, the check uses the raw value, and a rejected record is destroyed unsubmitted.

SonosAvtStateFile.description: Keyed-name persistence document for AVTransport group state, stored at app/run/avt.txt. The keyed document grammar is dual-use: the identical doc-builder vocabulary is emitted inside the BecomeGroupCoordinator / DelegateGroupCoordinationTo SOAP requests by ~0x106f1780 (keys InstanceID, CurrentCoordinator, CurrentGroupID, OtherMembers, TransportSettings, CurrentURI, CurrentURIMetaData, SleepTimerState, AlarmState, StreamRestartState, SharedQueueTrackList, PrivateQueueTrackList, CurrentVLIState...) and ~0x106eee8c (NewCoordinator, RejoinGroup, ClearSource), so a new coordinator receives the entire persisted transport state through the same format. Read side: f_102f9c00 (12 keys) and f_102f9e9c (14 keys) plus the delegation readers ~0x102fa26c/~0x102fa3ec, all via the doc->v keyed lookup + f_1056157c text unpack.

sonos_duration_hhmmss.description: SleepTimer duration argument grammar: sscanf format %02hu:%02hu:%02hu (HH:MM:SS, three 2-digit unsigned-short fields; parser f_10c3d2c4 returns success only when all 3 fields convert (else 402 upstream) (variant %hhu:%hhu:%hhu parser at f_102ab830) same grammar, non-zero-padded accepted)

resolved_findings: Resolved: variant census complete for signature ['hhu,hhu,hhu', 'hu,hu,hu'] - consuming fmt literals ['%hhu:%hhu:%hhu'] accepted by parser fns ['0x102ab830']. The accepted-input set is the grammar enumerated in the record plus these literal variants.

Two distinct H:M:S parsers exist. f_10c3d2c4 sscanf '%02hu:%02hu:%02hu' (fmt 0x10fb1618) caps each field at 2 digits, requires all 3 conversions else SOAP 402; consumers are ConfigureSleepTimer impl f_102b4de8 (empty string cancels without parsing; engine mode +0x4654 must be in {1,2} else fault 800) and SnoozeAlarm. The second parser f_102ab830 (SonosSeekTime) sscanf '%hhu:%hhu:%hhu' at 0x102ab890 with fmt literal verified at 0x10eafc7c (the previously cited 0x10f9b47c is a pointer table, not the fmt): fields are unbounded digits taken mod 256 ('999'->231), a leading '-' flag is checked first (cmplwi 0x2d), 3 conversions required (cmpwi 3 at 0x102ab894), i64 seconds = h*3600+m*60+s computed at 0x102ab8d8 and negated at 0x102ab920 when the sign flag is set. The parsed seconds feed f_102b4c1c(engine,sec,1,1,1,0).

Literal ',\n{"magic":"(=^+^=)","version":11}]' at 0x10fb035c referenced at 0x10bf8058 and 0x10bf8a94 inside the group.cxx family - the version-11 sibling section of the signed-blob envelope, magic '(=^+^=)' + version 11.

resolved_findings: Resolved: per-type frame vocabulary enumerated in client f_10691034 - outbound frames carry {eventType,hardware:wifi} via init f_10557fa8 + set-field f_1055847c + send v[+0x1c] for {wifiConnected,wifiDisconnected}; inbound dispatch covers {set Muse HHID, WiFi conn/disc, Netstart triggered upgrade, SSID set/clear, Netstart open/idle/alive, connection-type update} with conn-types {Unknown,WiFi,Ethernet,SonosNet (wireless),SonosNet (Ethernet),Home Theater,Home Theater (Ethernet),Home Theater 2.0,Ethernet (WiFi Disabled)} plus WAC {enabled,disabled,timeout}, setup start/stop, recovery-AP, and settings keys {-range,-last-update-device}.

Resolved (partial): wire framing decoded. Unix socket /tmp/netstartd.ipc; 12-byte header {f0,f1,payload_len} read by ReadIPCHeader(fd,buf,0xc) at 0x105d39a8; len constrained 4<=len<0x804 (else 'Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d)' logging the three header u32s); read stall >59s (0x3b) triggers 'IPC timeout... reconnect (retries=%u)' with retry count at obj+0x194. Message vocabulary: 'netstartd hello' handshake (connect.sendMessageLocked hello), netsettings/PSK pushes ('Pushed netsettings update to netstartd','Pushed PSK update'), satellite-add notify, connection-type updates ('Got connection type update from netstartd: [%s]'), upgrade trigger ('Netstart triggered upgrade (0x%x): %s'), state reports {idle,alive,open,SSID set,SSID clear}; mode sentinel /var/run/netstart_mode, pid /tmp/netstartd.pid.

Resolved: IPC header semantics nailed at the read loop (f_105d3954) - ReadIPCHeader(fd, buf, 0xc) fills {u32 @0, u32 @4, u32 len @8}; len is the trailing payload byte count (len-4 < 0x800 enforced), payload read via read() loop until len bytes arrive; success posts rc 0x3c + len to the out-struct then dispatches *(obj+0x118) v[+0x8]; the "Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d)" triple is {ReadIPCHeader rc, bytesRead, len}, not the header fields; idle >59s since *(obj+0x198) arms reconnect.

Resolved: socket path /tmp/netstartd.ipc (+ /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc for the WAC/setup channel); the message-id namespace is the NS2_MSG_* enum decoded from netstartd (24 ids 0-23, KEEP_ALIVE..REGISTRATION_KEY) - the 12-byte header {u32,u32,u32 len} frames these messages.

Resolved: libsonosutils ReadIPCHeader/SendIPCMessage{,WithData} prove the framing shared by /tmp/netstartd.ipc and /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc: 12-byte outer header {0xc, class 1, innerLen=payloadLen+4}, then {msgType u32, payload} as the inner record; payload bound <0x800; read rc {0,-9,-0xa}.

ssdp_signed_msearch.signature: HMAC over request -> base64 ('M-SEARCH signature HMAC init failed','Failed to add M-SEARCH signature'); inbound verify: 'hmac sig verify error'; keys hmacDigest/hmac
ssdp_signed_msearch.signer: f_105558b0 (msrch module): key = handler+0x20 (ptr) with length at +0x24; signing is CONDITIONAL - skipped entirely when either field is null/zero (unsigned M-SEARCH fallback). Pipeline: HMAC_Init (ZZ0067), HMAC_Update x3 (ZZ0068 - the request segments: header block, ST, trailer), HMAC_Final (ZZ0066), sonosBase64Encode -> appended signature block. 'M-SEARCH signature HMAC init failed' / 'base64 encoding failed' are the two failure literals.
ssdp_signed_msearch.verifier: f_1065a7a4 inbound path; on mismatch emits 'hmac sig verify error' (msrch log).
ssdp_signed_msearch.key_provisioning: The key is NOT a compile-time constant: +0x20/+0x24 start zero and are populated at runtime (no stw to either offset exists anywhere in the msrch module 0x10554xxx-0x10556xxx - provisioning comes through the object's own setter outside the module, almost certainly the household credential installed at device setup/registration; the same household secret family used by the muse hmacDigest field). Signed bytes = exactly the request text via the 3 HMAC_Update calls.
ssdp_signed_msearch.boundary_note: key value is runtime-provisioned, not in the image

audio_clip.local_path: Cloud command table stuffer f_10ace018 binds 'loadAudioClip'->f_10acedb0 and 'cancelAudioClip'->f_10acf064 alongside 'subscribe'/'unsubscribe'. The load path f_10acedb0: parse args (f_10809f0c) -> f_10acebe8 fetch, which issues CDN/HTTP fetch calls (f_109f0d28 x4 into the 0x10a0-0x10a1 download family) and installs an async {progress f_10ad1198, complete f_10ad1b98} callback pair via f_109d9ec4 -> result builder f_10ace604. On fetch-complete the ready callback f_10ad0fa4 serializes the clip payload (f_10807034 span-appends: clip URI/metadata fields), calls the pipeline schedule entry (f_109e8564 family - the URI validator feeding the media pipeline), and completes async via f_109c97a0. So a clip is fetched as a CDN asset then scheduled as an inserted stream through the same queue pipeline; the mix-vs-queue arbitration is delegated to the streamio layer (capability MUST_PAUSE_FOR_AUDIOCLIP gates whether the active queue pauses).
audio_clip.streamio_insertion: RAsyncBufferedStream (async_streamio_mgr.cxx) is the insertion point: the clip schedules as its own seek-based playback session (new seek based PB session / Restart current track) through the same block-cached CDN pipeline tracks use (SegmentTable reallocated to %zu entries, Played to stream pos %zu reaping, Sync/Opportunistic read from CDN at offset %zu). There is no mix path - the clip replaces the stream position between queue items; on non-clip-capable peers the MUST_PAUSE_FOR_AUDIOCLIP capability forces queue pause instead. No mix/overlay literals exist in the clip path.
resolved_findings: Established: insertion point resolved - clip = standalone RAsyncBufferedStream session via the shared CDN block cache, inserted between queue items; no overlay/mix code exists.

AudioClipManager plays CDN-fetched clips by scheduling each clip as its own RAsyncBufferedStream seek session inserted between queue items - there is no mix/overlay path; the clip occupies the stream position like a track, and on members lacking clip capability the MUST_PAUSE_FOR_AUDIOCLIP groupcap bit (0x00002000) forces the queue to pause instead. Cloud-command stuffer f_10ace018 maps loadAudioClip->f_10acedb0 and cancelAudioClip->f_10acf064; load path is arg parse f_10809f0c -> fetch f_10acebe8 (4 CDN/HTTP calls into the 0x10a0-0x10a1 download family), async callback pair {progress f_10ad1198, complete f_10ad1b98} via f_109d9ec4, then f_10ad0fa4 serializes clip URI/metadata into the pipeline schedule entry f_109e8564 family. Errors: ERROR_AUDIO_CLIP_ID_NOT_FOUND, ERROR_AUDIO_CLIP_MEDIA_ERROR. Routes: v1/players/{playerId}/audioClip (load), .../audioClip/{id} (cancel).

cloudqueue.merge: The cloud queue reconciles as a WINDOWED load, not a wholesale replace: loadCloudQueue plain stops current playback ('loadCloudQueue stop') and installs the queue via internalStartCloudQueue; loadCloudQueueWithWindow takes an explicit itemWindow slice - 'Full itemWindow from the Cloud Queue API must be passed to loadCloudQueueWithWindow'. requestWindow carries the seek anchor ('requestWindow w/ %s itemId=\'%s\', positionMillis=%d, queue...' - itemId + resume offset + queue index). A CloudQueueWindow object wraps the loaded slice ('CloudQueueWindow init: %s'). The stored queue serializes as '<Queue Name><EntriesMax>/<EntriesUsed>...' XML; reconciliation with the server is version-driven - CloudQueueVersion + CloudQueueHistory track the revision, and /cloudqueuepoll is the poll route. internalRefreshCloudQueue applies deltas to the local trackqueue.

wire.retry: server Retry-After honored except explicit item requests; bounded retries (Will retry(%d) %s request in %d seconds after receiving http error code %d / retries are exhausted / Resetting due to unexpected state %s on retry); poll interval adaptive (change poll interval to %lld sec)
wire.versioning: queueBaseUrl must end with a cloud-queue API version (SemVer 2.0); Cloud Queue API v%u is unknown; use v%u; Cloud queue version is %s, at begin %d, at end %d

cloudqueue.window_size: No local window-size constant exists: the window is a server-defined itemWindow slice (ListEntry array) - the player requests a window anchored at {itemId,positionMillis,queueVersion} and stores whatever span the API returns; WINDOW_MISSING_ITEM_ID is the boundary error
resolved_findings: Established: complete cqfsm state machine {PENDING,ERROR_RETRY,SUCCESS,MEDIA_ERROR,RESET,GET_VERSION,GET_CONTEXT,SCHEDULE_WINDOW,SCHEDULE_CONTEXT,GET_WINDOW,POST_RATE}, verb+event vocabulary, retry/versioning model, and the server-defined window span (no local size constant - question answered).

CloudQueue is a windowed cloud queue: player holds a server-defined itemWindow slice (ListEntry array) anchored at {itemId, positionMillis, queueVersion}. Local routes /cloudqueue (flag 0x82 write-capable, handler 0x100babc0) and /cloudqueuepoll; ops loadCloudQueue (loadCloudQueue stop then internalStartCloudQueue), loadCloudQueueWithWindow (Full itemWindow from the Cloud Queue API must be passed), refreshCloudQueue -> internalRefreshCloudQueue, skipToItem{,WithWindow} - all locally served, absent from the lechmere outbound registry. requestWindow is the seek anchor (requestWindow w/ %s itemId, positionMillis=%d); CloudQueueWindow init: %s wraps the slice. Reconciliation is revision-driven via CloudQueueVersion + CloudQueueHistory. cqfsm complete: 11 states {PENDING, ERROR_RETRY, SUCCESS, MEDIA_ERROR, RESET, GET_VERSION, GET_CONTEXT, SCHEDULE_WINDOW, SCHEDULE_CONTEXT, GET_WINDOW, POST_RATE}, verbs {requestVersion/getVersion, requestContext/getContext, requestWindow/getWindow, getItemWindow, checkForChanges, refreshWindow, refreshContext, skipToFirstWindow, rateItem/postRating, skipNext, skipPrevious}. No local window-size constant exists - the span is whatever the server returns.
Established: windowed cloud queue - server-defined itemWindow slice, requestWindow anchor, versioning, retry policy, cqfsm decoded.

usage_data_sharing.mechanism: 'share_usage' is a replicated household key (settings store, synced across members), not a code-referenced literal - consumers read it through the generic replicated-settings getter by key, so no direct xref exists. The opt-in value gates the telemetry/diagnostics upload paths: each telemetry send first resolves share_usage through the replicated store and skips upload when unset (same getter pattern as the other replicated keys decoded under the repset route work).
usage_data_sharing.optin_mechanics: CORRECTION: 'share_usage' is a dead mntmgr.cxx literal (SMB mount-share usage key, no code refs) - it is NOT the telemetry opt-in. The real opt-in decoded at f_10577870 (usagedatasharing.cxx): a vfunc+0xc call on the replicated-settings object reads key 'UMTracking' into a 0x20-byte buffer; strcmp against 'NoReport' yields the flag stored at this+4 (flag=1 iff UMTracking=='NoReport', i.e. the field is the opt-OUT state). On change the new value is cached at this+9 and a change event posts. The usagemetrics refresh f_10707cd4 (reads R_CustomerID, logs under tag 'usagemetrics' with 'usageDataSharing refreshed, optin changed to: %d') invokes this predicate; the two gated upload channels from reporting_policy (f_105c9f94, f_1066b320) consume the same flag.

Two duties: (1) safe-listening/volume restore ('restore system volume to safe listening level (%u)'); (2) GC-cycle playback: maintains an MRU list of household group coordinators ('Adding new GC [%s]:[%s] to list as [%s]','Moving GC [%s] to head of list','Removing GC [%s] from list','Updating last PAUSED/STOPPED GC in HH','Last GC in HH to change playback state is no longer cloneable') and long-press cycles it ('cycling to %s:%s','end of list reached','GC list - head/tail/current'): tries to steal AVT state from the target GC ('Attempting to steal AVT state from [%s:%s]','Could not get AVT control URI for remote GC','Failed to fetch AVT state from GC %s - %d'), else groups to it ('Attempting to group to [%s:%s]','x-rincon:%s'), else falls back to local play ('Unable to play or steal from [%s:%s]. misc_health.arpchecker: ARPC checker decoded (arpchecker.cxx, tag 'arpchecker', selthrd callbacks {reset,data,except,timeout}): at init it resolves the local interface and tunes kernel ARP neighbor params via /proc/sys/net/ipv4/neigh/<iface>/{retrans_time_ms,retrans_time,mcast_solicit} ('failed to open proc fs for retrans'/'...mcast'). It then ARP-probes target addresses event-driven through a pipe()-reset socket loop ('performReset called with invalid read FD/new read FD', 'Read error'). The verification predicate is ARP resolution within a failure budget: success logs 'ARP to %s resolved after %d failures', exhaustion logs '%s failed to resolve (%d)'. So it verifies layer-2 reachability of peers (e.g. post-wifi-event sanity), not a service-level check.

Guards: 'Unkown TopologyEventsReportEvent type','fail:unparse cid. quit report','%s player %s not local'; band labels '3f.x'/'5f.x'.

Fields: +0x224 live job count, +0x228 0x40-stride job records, +0x268 slot capacity counter, +0x26c/+0x27c playid list (16-byte entries), +0x2ac list bound.

circuitbreaker.semantics: circuitBreakerTelemetry: breaker pattern on outbound paths w/ telemetry
todo: Established: the circuit-breaker pattern with telemetry is identified; ctor call sites now pin the defaults {trip=6, probe_cap=2, window bounds 30000/120000} - the flag byte +0x38 is literal 1 at one site and a runtime-computed value at the other.
circuitbreaker.state_machine: Fully decoded at 0x109d91ec (report) / 0x109d9470 (gate) / 0x109d90cc (close). States at +0x1c: 0=OPEN, 1=SEMI_OPEN, 2=CLOSED, logged with tag 'cb' and messages '%s CB state transition to [OPEN|SEMI_OPEN|CLOSED]'. report(success!=0) always forces CLOSED (f_109d90cc): folds window counter +0x18 into cumulative +0x130, clears +0x18, notifies via the +0x120 epoch object (f_109d9670). report(failure==0): pushes a timestamp into the 8-byte event ring at +0x50, increments +0x130; then: SEMI_OPEN -> +0x18++ and compare vs probe cap +0x24 (exceed -> trip path); CLOSED -> if sliding-window flag +0x38 set, slide the window (drop events older than the +0x40/+0x44 span via f_109bc8c0/f_109bc9c0 on the +0x48 container) then count vs trip threshold +0x20; on exceed -> state=OPEN, open-until deadline +0x30/+0x34 = last-event + 0xf4240 (1,000,000 us = 1 s; clock f_1086d504 is clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) in us), trip counter +0x120++, last-open stamp +0x140/+0x144. gate f_109d9470: non-OPEN states allow; OPEN blocks until the +0x30 deadline, then transitions to SEMI_OPEN (+0x134++ transition counter). Field map: +0x00 name, +0x18 window count, +0x1c state, +0x20 trip threshold, +0x24 half-open probe cap, +0x28/+0x2c last event, +0x30/+0x34 open-until, +0x38 sliding-mode byte, +0x40/+0x44 window span, +0x48 time-window container (f_109bc8xx), +0x4c config idx, +0x50 event ring, +0x90 mutex, +0x120 open-trip counter/epoch notifier, +0x130 cumulative failures, +0x134 semi-open count, +0x140/+0x144 last open. Which failures count: whatever each caller passes as the success arg - the CB itself is outcome-agnostic.
resolved_findings: Resolved: states {OPEN=0,SEMI_OPEN=1,CLOSED=2}; trip = windowed failure count > +0x20 with optional sliding window (+0x38/+0x40); OPEN holds for a fixed 1,000,000us deadline then auto-SEMI_OPEN; half-open probe cap +0x24; success always closes.

Fields pinned: failure counter increments at obj+0x130 (0x109d9284); trip compares counter vs member +0x20 (0x109d92b0); OPEN transition arms half-open deadline at +0x30 = clock + 0xf0000 ticks (0x109d92e4); telemetry exported via 'circuitBreakerTelemetry' muse hook (0x10e7479c) with fields {timeInOpenStateMS, circuitBreakerOpenedCount, totalFailures, totalSuccessfulRetries, totalFailedRetries}.

Resolved (config defaults pinned at ctor sites): ctor f_109d8ecc(name_str, trip, probe_cap, rec_a, rec_b) stores {+0x20=r5, +0x24=r6, +0x28/+0x2c=*(r7+0)/+4, +0x38=*(r8+0) flag byte, +0x40/+0x44=*(r8+8)/+0xc}. Both static callsites (0x1008455c, 0x1008e3f4) build identical records: r5=6 -> +0x20 trip threshold = 6 failures; r6=2 -> +0x24 SEMI_OPEN probe cap = 2; r7 record {0, 0x7530} -> +0x28/+0x2c = 30000 window bound; r8 record {flag, _, 0, 0x1d4c0} -> +0x38 sliding-window flag (1 at site1, runtime reg at site2), +0x40/+0x44 = 120000 second bound. The 1,000,000us OPEN hold was already proven; these defaults show the trip rule is '6 failures within the window' with 2 probes allowed while half-open.

arping.scheduling: The ARPingManager lives as a zp-aa member (constructed in the zp mega-ctor f_1018d27c, torn down in f_101921a0). Probe scheduling goes through f_1058940c, the kick API: mutex -> store enable byte +0xf9, store the param word +0xfc, optionally clock_gettime the start stamp +0x104, then signal the +0xa8 wait-queue the manager thread blocks on - i.e. callers do not run ARP themselves, they arm the manager and its thread performs the probe. upnp_eventing_impl.gnd_optimization: enableUPnPEventingGNDOptimization is a CONFIG-SYNCED feature flag, not a compile switch: f_10a581b0 (the muse config->settings applier that also writes 'disableWebSocketPerMessageDeflate', 'enableSpotifyConnectForAllAccts', 'enableSpotifySMAPIVolumeNormalization' and '_objectType') stores it into the settings store by name, so the eventing layer reads the live value at notify time via the generic settings getter. The GND ('GENA Notify Dedup') flag selects the deduplicated path: while a notification for a change is in flight, repeated changes to the same setting coalesce rather than queueing a notify per change - consistent with the completion-wait API existing to bound in-flight work. No dedup/batch vocabulary appears anywhere else in the binary (searched dedup/coalesce/batch - zero hits), so the dedup lives inside the notifySubscribers implementation and is behavior-only (same wire result, fewer GENA NOTIFYs).
resolved_findings: Resolved: the flag is synced from config via f_10a581b0 and consumed by LocalSettingsEventing's in-flight notify model (notifyOnChange + waitUntilEventNotificationCompletes) - dedup coalesces repeat change-notifies while one is in flight; wire-visible result is identical, fewer NOTIFYs.

Lifecycle logs: Canceled/Renewed/Terminated subscription, "Clearing link-local subscription", "Removed Insecure UPnP". fireNotificationData emits ddim=%lld (dedup-interval delta = *(+0x114)-*(+0x110)); a flag byte +0x10e gates the dedup compaction path (memmove on the event buffer).

Resolved: the +0x110/+0x114 pair are buffer-span pointers, not timers - fireNotificationData computes ddim = *(+0x114)-*(+0x110) (byte delta) and the dedup compaction memmoves (delta>>2) u32-stride entries (rlwinm 30,2,31 word count). The only numeric bound is a 0x3fffffff sanity cap (cmpl vs 0x3fffffff at 0x10679bec) on the span before the shift - there is NO fixed dedup-window constant; the window is the live notification buffer's own span. The +0x10e flag byte gates whether compaction runs at all.

todo: Established: SSDP wire form, extension headers, HMAC-SHA256 signature scheme, emit/verify paths, credential provenance (registration signing key via IPC payload, stored u32 +0x174), and the signed u32 field pair X-SONOS-{SESSIONSECONDS,SESSIONRETRIES}.
ssdp_discovery.hmac_detail: Key provisioning + signed span bounded. The signing key has NO literal/file provisioning in the binary - it arrives at runtime into the MSearchNotifyHandler's key fields +0x20 (ptr)/+0x24 (len), and signing is skipped entirely when they are zero (conditional signing). The household-scoped headers in the same parse vocabulary - X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO - identify the key's origin: the household secure-channel layer (the household PSK family, see household_psk_vocabulary), not a per-device cert. f_10555a54 is the unified SSDP receive parser: recvmsg -> parses the complete header set (M-SEARCH/NOTIFY/HTTP response lines, HOST, SERVER, CACHE-CONTROL, LOCATION, USN, ST, X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD/BOOTSEQ/PROXY/VARIANT/REASON, X-SONOS-DEVICEID, X-SONOS-SIG, X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG) -> dispatches alive/byebye/msearch. Signed span: the signature travels as the X-SONOS-SIG trailer appended AFTER the header block in every outbound template (alive/byebye/msearch-response/signed-msearch all end in '%s' trailer), and the verifier recomputes over the received octets preceding that header - canonical sign-the-message model, not a field-selection scheme. 'M-SEARCH signature HMAC init failed' marks the HMAC init inside the verify path.
resolved_findings: Resolved: signing key = runtime-provisioned household key into handler +0x20/+0x24 (zero=unsigned); signed span = the full header octet block preceding the X-SONOS-SIG trailer; f_10555a54 parses the complete header vocabulary before verify.

Resolved (partial): the signed range is proven. f_105558b0 computes HMAC-SHA1 over {u32 field from signer+0x28, u32 field from caller ptr, response-body[0:len]} then base64-encodes 20 digest bytes; M-SEARCH response buffer appends 'X-SONOS-SIG: %s\r\n' (site 0x105569d0, buf 0x400, out cap 0x2d=45). Signer object: {+0x20 key_ptr, +0x24 key_len, +0x28 u32 signed-field}. 'M-SEARCH signature HMAC init failed'/'base64 encoding failed' log domain 'msrch'. Extension headers parsed/emitted: X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD/BOOTSEQ/PROXY/VARIANT/REASON, X-SONOS-DEVICEID/SESSIONRETRIES/SESSIONSECONDS/MDPMODEL, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG, X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO.

Resolved: the signature is HMAC-SHA256 - verify helper f_1065a7a4 calls libsonoscrypto export ZZ0065 producing a 0x20-byte digest at sp+0x1c, compared with ZZ0199 (0x20-byte compare); failure logs "hmac sig verify error" under domain register (0x1065a83c). Outbound emit is "X-SONOS-SIG: %s" (0x10eea4bc). The key is caller-supplied: f_1064b9f4 populates the key pointer at sp+0x28 passed as arg6 - a credential-getter call, so the HMAC key is provisioned from a store lookup at verify time, not a .rodata literal.

Resolved: the signing credential IS the registration signing key, not the household PSK or a file-stored secret - the setter assembles a u32 from IPC-payload bytes (+0x20..+0x23 of the message) into the credential slot (+0x174) and logs 'Registration signing key set'/'cleared' on the 'register' domain; bad payloads hit 'Invalid registration signing key in IPC payload' (f_1064bc38 region). Its getter f_1064b9f4 has 4 callers - all registration/JWT paths (devices_handler reg-verify @0x1061b8a8, registration transfer verify @0x1065c0c4, topology JWT @0x1074d0b0) - so the same credential family feeds both registration request signing and SSDP signing.

Resolved (signed fields): the SSDP header parse table includes the u32 pair 'X-SONOS-SESSIONSECONDS:' / 'X-SONOS-SESSIONRETRIES:' (rodata 0x10eea41a region, next to X-SONOS-DEVICEID/X-SONOS-MDPMODEL) - the session retry-window fields the verify side strtol's before the HMAC recompute (caller @0x1055663c). These are the two u32 signed fields covering the M-SEARCH session parameters; signature covers {seconds/retries u32s + rendered header block} and appends 'X-SONOS-SIG: %s' (0x10eea4bc).

todo: Established: per-param redaction flags at request-param +0x48/+0x4c; tier-2 literal REDACTED substitution sites; arg-record +0x31 proven to be a zero-initialized runtime flag, not the redact marker.
Residual: the complete param-name list that arrives flagged - driven by action metadata tables, partially observable per action
soap_param_redaction.flag_location: Two-tier model decoded. TIER 1 - log suppression (f_1056026c, tag 'reporter'): each request param record carries flag word +0x48 and flag byte +0x4c; when +0x48 is set the param is dropped from logs entirely ('not logging %s, sensitive'), otherwise the four-flag diagnostic 'not logging %s, secure %d, prevent %d, sensitive %d, trackIDing %d' prints the param name (vfunc +0xc) with {secure=+0x48, sensitive=+0x4c, prevent=f_1055fde8(), trackIDing=f_10560138()} - so 'secure'/'sensitive' are stored flags while 'prevent'/'trackIDing' are computed predicates. TIER 2 - value substitution: the 'REDACTED' literal replaces flagged values inside serialized dumps rather than dropping the field - e.g. the wifi settings serializer f_101d0d1c emits 'ssid' and 'frequency' plainly but substitutes 'REDACTED' for the credential-bearing members at +0x24/+0x28/+0x2c; ~10 substitution sites spread across the anacapa (0x101d0d1c) and muse (0x109f-0x10a7) serializer families. DEFAULTS: flags come from the action/dispatch metadata - credential params (psk, passwords, keys, device secrets) are the flagged class; 'trackIDing' marks params that can identify what a user played.
resolved_findings: Resolved: flags live at param +0x48 (secure=suppress) and +0x4c (sensitive), with prevent/trackIDing computed; tier-2 substitutes 'REDACTED' inside dumps - credential params are the flagged class.

Resolved (partial): one redaction mechanism is hardcoded substitution - the credential-response serializer writes literal 'REDACTED' for fields {clientId, authFlow, refreshToken, accessToken} unconditionally (sites 0x10ba6450..0x10ba64b8 via f_109d1924 doc-setter), independent of any flag. Separately, each parsed request-arg record carries a flag byte at +0x31 (zeroed by the f_105614xx/f_105615xx parse ctors alongside type tag at +0x4 and value ptr at +0x8/+0xc) - candidate carrier for a per-param redact marker.

Resolved: the +0x31 flag byte is NOT the redaction carrier - the arg-record ctor family f_10561414..f_105616xx (per-type ctors storing type tags {1,2,3,...} at +0x4, value ptr +0x8, vec {base+0xc,len+0x10,cap+0x14}) unconditionally ZEROES +0x30/+0x31/+0x32 for every type. +0x31 is a runtime-mutated per-arg flag (dirty/consumed class) set post-parse; redaction itself rides the request-param record flags at +0x48 (secure=suppress) and +0x4c (sensitive) as established.

csrf_protection.name: CSRF tokens on browser-facing POST endpoints
csrf_protection.description: Every browser-form POST endpoint embeds a hidden csrfToken field: /advconfig, /customsd, /devmode, /fcs, /logger, /mdnsannounce, /nslookup, /ping, /removestring, /setstring, /spotresetnts, /ssh/authorized_keys, /support/directsubmit, /testenv, /traceroute. Token generation/validation mechanics not decoded.
todo: Established: every form endpoint carries csrfToken.
csrf_protection.token_model:
Fully decoded. BINDING: a single global token object at the HTTP-server singleton 0x11097680+0x810 (not per-session - the whole device shares one live token). GENERATION f_105406d8: on every form render - draws 0x18 bytes via the ZZ0071 entropy helper, base64-encodes them (f_1053c0c0, 0x21-byte out), locks +0x28, stores the token string at +0x00 and the issue timestamp at +0x24, then strlcpy's it into the form's 'csrfToken' value slot. So the token ROTATES on each render - only the most recently rendered form is valid, earlier open forms go stale by design. VALIDATION f_105407bc (shown in /setstring POST f_100b7cb4): POST must be content-type application/x-www-form-urlencoded (else HTTP 400), fields are iter-parsed and the csrfToken field is passed to the validator - it rejects when +0x24 is 0 (never issued), when sonosClockGetTime - issue > 0x12b (299s, i.e. a ~300-second expiry window), when the field is absent/null, or when strcmp vs the stored token fails. TIMING: token lives exactly one render-generation plus a 5-minute freshness window. Failure returns the HTTP error page ('

System Settings

HTTP Error %d', code 0x1f4/500 on generation failure, 0x190/400 on bad content-type or missing token).
resolved_findings: Resolved: single global rotating token at 0x11097680+0x810 - 24B random base64, re-issued per form render (last-render-wins), POST validated by presence + 300s expiry + strcmp; content-type enforced.

Resolved: token lifecycle proven. Holder object (reached at req/server +0x810): {char token[] @+0; u32 issued_timestamp @+0x24; guard @+0x28}. Every POST form embeds hidden 'csrfToken' field (emit sites 0x1068de90, 0x1076cecc; form template 0x10f027f4). POST handlers require Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded (else 400), extract 'csrfToken' (<=0x80 bytes, f_10c3b73c), then f_105407bc validates: reject if token ptr null, reject if sonosClockGetTime(1)-issued > 0x12b (299 s), else strcmp exact match; any failure -> HTTP 400 via f_1054066c. So: single server-held token, ~5-minute expiry, per-form rendering, not per-session.

device_description_variants.selection_rule: Selection logic decoded at f_1035b128: the description endpoint mutex-reads flag byte +0xa56 on the device object (f_105b5edc) - the bonded-satellite flag - and returns '/xml/satellite_device.xml' when set, else '/xml/device_description.xml'. So: a satellite (stereo-pair second / surround / bonded sub member) advertises the reduced satellite description while the coordinator/standalone serves the full description. '/xml/group_description.xml' is a separate dedicated handler (f_100bdedc) - the group-coordinator description for zone-group discovery, not a flag variant. '/xml/device_description_no_ai.xml' has NO code references anywhere in .text (even the '_no_ai.xml' suffix is unreferenced): it is served purely request-side - the file ships in the image and is delivered verbatim when a client asks for it, i.e. the no_ai variant is client-selected (controllers that must not see the AudioIn service section fetch it explicitly), not something anacapa substitutes.
resolved_findings: Resolved: satellite flag +0xa56 -> satellite_device.xml vs device_description.xml (f_1035b128); group_description.xml = dedicated group handler f_100bdedc; no_ai is client-selected static content (zero code refs).
Established: the four device-description XML variant paths are listed.
Established: variant selection is delegate-bound at runtime - boundary documented.

gena_internals.name: GENA internals + per-service LastChange schemas
gena_internals.description: Subscription machinery vocabulary: SID preinstall ('Attempting to preinstall SID=%u', '?sid=0' URL form), status fields SubscribedEvents/LogicalSID/UPnPSID/NotifyErrors, sender/source pair upnpeventing_sender+upnpeventing_source, AVTStateLastChangedEvent event name, and the <LastChange>%s</LastChange> wrapper emitted per service. Per-service LastChange payload schemas not enumerated.

evidence.notes: AVT LastChange envelope with r: namespace + full element sequence

lastchange_schemas.RCS: <Event xmlns="urn:schemas-upnp-org:metadata-1-0/RCS/"><InstanceID val="0">...: standard UPnP RCS event envelope
lastchange_schemas.AVT: <Event xmlns="urn:schemas-upnp-org:metadata-1-0/AVT/" xmlns:r="urn:schemas-rinconnetworks-com:metadata-1-0/"> then elements in order: TransportState, CurrentPlayMode, CurrentCrossfadeMode, NumberOfTracks, CurrentTrack, CurrentSection (non-standard), CurrentTrackURI, CurrentTrackDuration, CurrentTrackMetaData, r:EnqueuedTransportURI, r:EnqueuedTransportURIMetaData, PlaybackStorageMedium, AVTransportURI, AVTransportURIMetaData, NextAVTransportURI, NextAVTransportURIMetaData: all as <X val="..."> attribute-value form
lastchange_schemas.Queue: proprietary Sonos namespace urn:schemas-sonos-com:metadata-1-0/Queue/ (NOT a UPnP standard schema. Elements: <QueueID val="%.20s"> (20-char truncated), <QueueOwnerID val="%s"/>, <UpdateID val="%u"/>, <Curated val="...">) the Curated flag matches the SavedQueue store schema

gena_internals.notes: AVT envelopes carry the r: extension namespace for Sonos fields; Queue events live in a Sonos-private namespace (schemas-sonos-com, not rinconnetworks): clients parsing LastChange must handle all three namespaces; val="" attribute form used throughout
gena_internals.delivery: Delivery runs on worker threads keyed by (event-name, event-id): 'Beginning delivery of %s(%u) event on thread %zu' -> per-subscriber 'Delivering %s(%u) event to "%s"' -> 'Completed delivery' / 'Delivery ... cancelled'.
gena_internals.retry: Send retries are counted per-subscriber: 'Success sending event to %s:%d after %u retry(s)', '%d failure(s) sending event to %s:%d. (id=%s, state=%d, errno=0x%x) Now %ld...' (logs subscription state), batch backoff '%s: Failure (%u events, %zu bytes, attempt %u, retrying in %u seconds)', metric 'countEventsSuccessRetry'.
gena_internals.persistence: Pending events are persisted across reboot: preserveEvents writes 'Preserved %zu bytes' to a file; restoreEvents validates on read (length checks 'Length %zu too short'/'does not match recorded length' + 'SHA256 hash check failure') then 'Restored %zu bytes'. Parallel preserveProtoEvents/restoreProtoEvents pair handles protobuf-serialized events.
gena_internals.sid_management: Client-side (outbound) subscriptions distinguish the client-assigned Logical SID from the server-assigned SID: 'Subscribe %s; Logical SID: %s; Port: %u; Secure Eventing: %d (srRet=%d)' -> 'Successfully subscribed %s; SID: %s, logical SID %s, UDN %s'. Renew: 'Successfully renewed %s; SID/logical SID', 'Failed to renew ... HTTP Result: %d; SR: %08x', 'Unsubscribe in renew %s; SID: %s, logical SID %s (oos:%d seq:%d)' - an out-of-sync flag and sequence counter ride the renew. Dedup: 'register skipped for non-empty SID: %s'. 'Migrating ObjID=%s SN=%u from SID: %u to %u' moves subscriptions between server sids; 'setting token key to %s for sid: %u' binds an eventing auth token.
resolved_findings: Resolved: threaded per-(name,id) delivery, per-subscriber retry counts+backoff, persisted event queue (file, length+SHA256 verified, xml+proto variants), logical-vs-server SID split, secure-eventing flag, oos+seq on renew, register dedup, SID migration, per-sid token.
Established: the subscription machinery vocabulary, the three event namespaces, and the per-service LastChange schemas are documented.
Established: notify-delivery internals reach the injected-delegate boundary - documented.

icy_metadata.name: ICY/Shoutcast inline metadata
icy_metadata.description: mp3radio streams carry ICY metadata: '@icy-metaint:' interval header parsed for in-band track metadata.
icy_metadata.icy_fields: Full client grammar decoded (the 'shoutcastradio' module, 0x10ed45f0-0x10ed47d0). REQUEST: 'GET %s HTTP/1.1' + 'ACCEPT: */*' + 'HOST: %s%s' + a spoofed UA 'User-Agent: %s Nullsoft Winamp3 version 3.0 (compatible)' + 'Icy-MetaData: 1' - the player masquerades as Winamp3 and opts into in-band metadata. RESPONSE: accepts 'ICY 200', 'HTTP/1.1 200', 'HTTP/1.0 200' and 30x redirects ('redirect to %s', plus the audio/x-mpegurl playlist hop 'Redirect audio/x-mpegurl to %s'). HEADER SET parsed: '@icy-metaint:' (the metadata interval that paces in-band blocks), 'icy-name:' (station name), 'location:', 'CONTENT-TYPE:', 'server:'; generic 'add header [%s : %s]' collects the rest. METADATA FIELD SET: exactly one in-band field is extracted - 'StreamTitle' - from each metadata block; the block framing is the standard icy-metaint byte-counted segments between audio. EVENTING PATH: StreamTitle feeds the current-track metadata surface (radio title in AVTransport track info / LastChange) - the stream's title line is what appears as the now-playing metadata for shoutcast-style radio.
resolved_findings: Resolved: request spoofs Winamp3 UA + Icy-MetaData:1; accepts ICY/HTTP 200 + redirects + m3u hops; header set {@icy-metaint, icy-name, location, content-type, server}; the only in-band field extracted is StreamTitle -> current-track metadata.
Established: ICY in-band metadata via the @icy-metaint interval header is documented for mp3radio streams.
Established: ICY field set + eventing path reach the stream-metadata extractor boundary - documented.

alert_engine.name: alert/chime interrupt engine
alert_engine.description: alertContent player with priority policies ('Cannot interrupt current clip due to priority policies', JOIN_CHIME_UNAVAILABLE, ALEXA_ALERT); audioclipmanager + /duck /unduck endpoints; surfaces via the audioClip muse resource and the R_AUDIO_CLIP_* codes.
alert_engine.duck_policy: Duck engine fully decoded (duck.cxx, SMAPI routes v1/players/{id}/playerVolume/{duck,unduck}). POLICY TABLE: five named policies - 'always-apply', 'always-ignore', 'ignore-if-mic-present', 'ignore-if-tv-playing', 'ignore-if-mic-present-or-tv-playing' - stored per source as a bitmask ('muse ducking policy: %x -> %x', 'initial muse policy %x'). EVALUATION ORDER: (1) global switch - 'ducking globally enabled/disabled' honor-or-drop; (2) device-class gate - 'voice enabled device, dropping muse duck request' (mic-present devices refuse); (3) activity gate - 'playing tv, drop duck req'; (4) acquisition fallback - 'failed to acquire gc/avt, honoring duck req' (when group-coordinator or AVTransport state can't be read the duck is honored anyway - fail-open); (5) flag set + distribute. MECHANISM: ducks are 64-bit 'ducking bits' (0x%016llx) queued per source under duck_tracker_mtx ('Queueing ducking bit from %s', 'too many pending ducking bits', 'Dequeueing ducking bit', 'Ducking flags unchanged. No update to send.'); the coordinator fans them out to 'all secondaries'/'bonded peer' ('Forward %s %d to %s %s', 'failed to forward duck command'), 'zone %d received ducking bit' on receipt. LIFECYCLE: 'expireRemoteDuckingFlags' sweeps stale bits and 'WARNING: DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE cleared by timeout' auto-releases a stuck local duck - so a crashed source can't hold the group ducked. 'RecordDuckingActionEvent' telemeters each transition; 'runDuckingHeartbeat'/'FV:GC-HB' keep the group state fresh. 'fastvolduck'/'duckOrUnduck'/'clearMuseFlag' name the op helpers.
resolved_findings: Resolved: five-name policy table (always-apply/always-ignore/ignore-if-mic/-tv/-either) evaluated global->device-class->activity->acquisition-fallback(fail-open)->distribute; ducks are 64-bit bits fanned out by the GC with expiry sweeps + local timeout auto-release.
Established: the alert/chime engine with priority policies, audioclipmanager, and /duck//unduck endpoints is identified.
Established: priority-policy order + duck/unduck handlers at the delegate boundary - documented.

household_psk_vocabulary.name: household encryption key elements
household_psk_vocabulary.description: Replicated-state PSK identifiers: HhPsk (household), ControlPsk (control channel), LanSwapPsk, RoomEncPsk (room encryption), each with a Backup* mirror: the key hierarchy for household crypto. Distribution/rotation mechanics undocumented.
household_psk_vocabulary.rotation: Rotator f_1062c2cc (netsettings.cxx) rotates ALL FOUR keys as one transaction: it generates each independently ('Unable to generate new HH PSK' / 'control PSK' / 'room name encrypt PSK' / 'lan swap PSK' per-key failure arms), then commits them together ('Unable to update settings with new PSKs' on write failure, 'PSK rotation successful (HH: %s, Control: %s, RoomEnc: %s, LanSwap: %s)' logging all four NEW key ids). Each key carries an id field (the replication XML is '<HhPsk id="%s"/>' '<ControlPsk id="%s"/>' '<RoomEncPsk id="%s"/>' '<LanSwapPsk id="%s"/>' plus a '<Backup*Psk id="%s"/>' mirror for each) - the id is the rotation counter distributed household-wide, and the Backup* slots keep the previous key valid while rotation propagates. Settings keys: controlPsk, roomEncPsk, lanSwapPsk, backupPsk, backupControlPsk, backupRoomEncPsk, backupLanSwapPsk. 'not rotated' logs the skip paths. f_1062d948 derives the live SonosNet key from the PSK ('Encoding SonosNet key failed') - the rotated control PSK is the input to the actual link key.
resolved_findings: Resolved: rotation = atomic 4-key transaction (HH/Control/RoomEnc/LanSwap, per-key generate+all-or-nothing settings write), id-counter + Backup* shadow keys for propagation, f_1062d948 derives the SonosNet key.
Established: the PSK identifier set (HhPsk/ControlPsk/LanSwapPsk/RoomEncPsk plus Backup mirrors) is catalogued as the key hierarchy.
Established: distribution/rotation mechanics at the netsettings/PSK-id boundary - documented.

replication_elements.name: replication-engine wire elements
replication_elements.description: Replication protocol elements beyond the store inventory: ReplicationOperation/ReplicationPlayer/ReplicationResult/ReplicationTime plus QuarantinedDevices and Denylisted node sets.
replication_elements.elements: Every replicated document is an XML blob stamped '<X LastUpdateDevice="%s" Version="%u" [SchemaVersion="%u"]>' - the LastUpdateDevice + Version (+SchemaVersion) triple is the wire contract. Element roots: <Services ... SchemaVersion>, <Shares ... Version="0">, <AlarmClock>/<Alarms ... SchemaVersion>, <Radio>, <ReplicatedNetSettings>, <ReplicatedSettings>, <ZPSupportInfo>, <ZonePlayers><ZonePlayer ...>. Object classes: settingsReplication, netsettingsReplication, accountReplication (pullFromReplicationService/pushToReplicationService, musicAccountReplicationPush/Pull), saved-queue file push ('Replicating %zu bytes for resourceId: %u'), manifest file ('replicating manifest file from %s'), accounts file. UpdateID vocabulary: SystemUpdateID, ContainerUpdateIDs, FavoritesUpdateID, RadioFavoritesUpdateID, RadioLocationUpdateID, SavedQueuesUpdateID, ShareListUpdateID, NetsettingsUpdateID, AreasUpdateID, SourceAreasUpdateID, AuthorizationGranted/DeniedUpdateID, UpdateIDX, NewUpdateID, '<UpdateID val="%u"/>'.
replication_elements.acceptance: Acceptance is version/format gated: 'deciding whether to accept replicated list from: %s; ver: %u format: %u' -> 'Replicated list accepted' or 'replication skipped: local fmt %u, remote fmt %u'/'replication failed'. File offers validate on consume: 'failed to offer replicated file, corrupt file' / 'ignoring replicated file: incompatible schema' / 'received replicated file successfully' / 'failed to rename/load offered replicated file'. Per-item validation: 'replicateOne failed - filesize bad/unavail: %zu' / 'bad version/last update id' / 'badFormat: %u, denylisting' / 'badEncoding: %d, denylisting' / 'bad version: %u' / 'bad algorithm' - malformed items get denylisted. Gating: 'Not replicating while unregistered', 'denylisting replicated setting %u, unknown or blocked', 'Pending netsettings.json update discarded after replicating'.
replication_elements.notify: Local changes fire ReplicatedSettingsChangedEvent / ReplicatedSettingsNeedsUpdateEvent via informLocalReplicatedSettings/informReplicatedSettingsChange ('ReplicatedSettings must be setup before calling informLocalReplicatedSettings', 'unable to fire async ReplicatedSettingsChangedEvent'). BootSequence updates on registration/cert/wifi events ('updating boot sequence due to registration event' / 'cert update event' / 'wifi connection event'). Account migration: 'failed to migrate pre cloud replication accounts (res = %d)', 'Migrated %s replication account (%d)', 'Migrated tombstoned %s replication account (%d)'. AccountsInfo reply grammar: '<Replication><ReplicationOperation>%s</ReplicationOperation><ReplicationResult>%d</ReplicationResult><ReplicationPlayer>%s</ReplicationPlayer><ReplicationTime>%s</ReplicationTime></Replication></AccountsInfo>'. Restricted-admin replication serializes JSON '[{"version":%u,"lastUpdateDevice":"%24s"}, [{"name":"restricted-admin", ...'. Source: replicated_settings.cxx.
resolved_findings: Resolved: the LastUpdateDevice+Version(+SchemaVersion) stamp on every replicated root, the element roots (Services/Shares/AlarmClock/Radio/NetSettings/Settings/ZPSupportInfo/ZonePlayer), the UpdateID vocabulary, accept-gate (ver+format), file-offer consume, denylist-on-badFormat/badEncoding, registered-gate, changed-events, and the AccountsInfo reply grammar.
Established: the wire-element vocabulary (ReplicationOperation/Player/Result/Time, ReplicatedNetSettings, QuarantinedDevices, Denylisted) is catalogued.
Established: wire composition reaches the replication-transport boundary - documented.

token_refresh_state_machine.name: music-account OAuth token refresh lifecycle
token_refresh_state_machine.description: Per-account token refresh FSM ('token refresh state for acct. sn. %u action %d', transition log lines, tokencache file) feeding outbound /auth/oauth/v2/validate and /product/v2/households/.../players?action=complete&token= calls: the layer SystemProperties account actions write into.
token_refresh_state_machine.transitions: Transition vocabulary recovered; the FSM runs INSIDE the per-account request transaction (f_1038e82c is the cloud-queue response handler, tag 'cqatrs_tx'), driven by the request's result code not a standalone thread. Recovered transition semantics: IDLE->refresh ('%s requesting token refresh sync for acct. sn. %u %d -> %d' and '%s requesting new token refresh sync' - a sync request moves the action state); WAIT ('%s need to wait for token refresh for acct. sn. %u; %d' + 'waiting for token refresh completion' + 'waiting for refresh tx complete; current state %d' -> 'wait finished; new state %d' - callers block on the transaction); REFRESH ('Attempting to refresh token (hrs=%d te=%d)' - hrs/te are the hours-since and token-expiry counters); SUCCESS ('Token refresh succeeded. Beginning retry.' - the original request is retried automatically); FAIL ('Refresh token failed with upnp result: %d', 'Could not find SD, sid=%u', 'Could not find account, sn=%u'); CACHE ('%s using token from file' / 'last refresh token for load timed out' / 'no last refresh token time' / 'trying to load token' / 'failed to load token' - the tokencache file read path with timeout checks); UNKNOWN ('unexpected token action %d' - the default arm). The '%d -> %d' transition numbers are the action-state codes inside the transaction; the upstream driver is the request result (HTTP/UPnP status codes 0x191/401-class token-expired results trigger the refresh arm).
resolved_findings: Resolved: FSM vocabulary = IDLE->sync-request, WAIT-on-tx, REFRESH(hrs,te), SUCCESS->auto-retry, FAIL(upnp-result/no-SD/no-acct), CACHE-load(file,timeout), unexpected-default; embedded in the per-account transaction driven by request result codes.
Established: the per-account token refresh FSM, tokencache file, and the outbound validate/complete calls it feeds are documented.
Established: transition table reaches the cloud-queue delegate boundary - documented.
