albumart_proxy.name: /getaa album-art proxy
albumart_proxy.role: local HTTP album-art endpoint: serves cached/proxied art to controllers; URI forms /getaa?u=<url>&v=<ver>, /getaa?m=1&u=<url> and /getaa?s=1&u=<url> (m=/s= size variants), plus upstream '?albumArt=true' fetches; art cached as <dir>/AlbumArt_{GUID}_Large.jpg
albumart_proxy.params: u= source URL (validated: 'AlbumArtURI longer than expected.'), v= version/etag-style param, m=1 / s=1 select medium/small variants; '%s?albumArt=true' marks upstream art requests
albumart_proxy.flags: enableSecureAlbumArt feature flag gates a secured art fetch path; AlbumArtistDisplayOption + GetAlbumArtistDisplayOption control whether album-artist metadata is displayed (microsoft:artistAlbumArtist DIDL extension supported in sort/filter caps)

evidence.notes: request processor: m/s/vli/u param parse + u-terminator
worker thread: 32-slot ring + TCP_INFO abort check

albumart_proxy.request_grammar: GET /getaa?{m|s|vli}...&u=<url>[&v=<n>] (query parsed by f_10c3b72c: param names <=32 chars, values <=1024 chars, '&'-separated. Recognized params (compared in order m,s,vli,u via strcmp at 0x100c35cc-0x100c3618): 'm' medium-variant flag, 's' small-variant flag, 'vli' virtual-line-in image flag, 'u' upstream image URL. IMPORTANT: 'u' is the TERMINATOR) when encountered, parsing stops and the request proceeds; any params AFTER u= are never read. 'v' is NOT parsed by the handler at all: it appears in emitted URIs (/getaa?u=%s&v=%u) purely as a client-side cache-buster/etag. Unknown params are skipped silently
albumart_proxy.response: image bytes streamed back via vliStreamImage (f_101867c8), logged as 'invoking vliStreamImage on %s %u %u %u %s' and 'Fetching album art for %s: %s'. Response header: Cache-Control: private, max-age=15780000 (~6 months). Failure path: 'vliStreamImage failed on %s %u %u %u %s' then status 0x194 sent via f_100b4614: upstream fetch failures surface as 404
albumart_proxy.async_model: handler f_100b8c2c is async: logs 'queueing album art request %s %u %u %u', lazily creates the mod_zp_aa server singleton (new 0x428a0, ctor f_10299a48) at 0x11096c98, enqueues the request into a 32-slot ring of 0x2134-byte entries (f_10299c34) and returns. Worker thread f_10299e5c blocks on a condvar, pops slots, probes the client socket with getsockopt(TCP_INFO) and takes an abort path (f_100c34fc slot-discard) when the peer is already in CLOSE/CLOSE_WAIT/CLOSING: clients that give up early are never served
albumart_proxy.param_semantics: m/s/vli select the image path BEFORE the request object is built: no flags -> default fetch (u URL streamed direct); m -> f_100c2f94 variant; s -> f_100c31c8 variant; vli -> direct vli-image fetch f_100be6ec. The three u16 fields carried on the request (+0x180/+0x182/+0x184) ride through to the vliStreamImage call - request dimensions/ids, not user params
albumart_proxy.arturi_cap: albumArtURI emission capped at 1024 bytes (buffer obj+0x54, len at +0x458, f_10381528); overflow logs 'AlbumArtURI longer than expected.' in the favorites log domain
todo: Residual: the concrete prefix value - it is stored config on the +0x3ac sub-object member +0x140 (likely /jffs or /var cache root set at init); the member chain is proven, the seeding site is init-config data.
albumart_proxy.fetch_path: Wire grammar '/getaa?u=%s&v=%u' (u = source art URI, v = version); five sites rewrite upnp:albumArtURI values into this form (f_102a1130, f_1034a3e8, f_1034b4f4, f_10425f64, f_1047b7b8). Queuer f_100b8c2c 'queueing album art request %s %u %u %u' (uri + 3 numeric params); fetcher f_100c34fc 'Fetching album art for %s: %s'. Upstream schemes resolved: x-sonos-http: prefixed URIs, old Rhapsody direct-ns.rhapsody.com imageserver '/imageserver/images/%s/300x300' ('Unknown old Rhapsody album art URI type: %s' fallback), rdradio/RDCPA art namespaces ('rdradio:artist:Art.', 'RDCPA:ARTALBUM:', 'RDCPA:ARTCOM...', 'explore:artist:mainreleases::art.%s'). Generated-art filename pattern '%s/AlbumArt_{%08X-...}_Large.jpg'. Metadata serializer f_104387f4 applies 'audiobook'/'podcast' content-type special-casing to art handling; 'omit missing metadata album art: %s' is a user setting; 'AlbumArtURI longer than expected.' is the length guard.
resolved_findings: Resolved: /getaa?u=&v= wire grammar, 5 rewrite sites, queue+fetch functions, upstream scheme map (x-sonos-http/rhapsody-imageserver/rdradio/RDCPA/explore), Large.jpg naming, audiobook/podcast special-casing, omit-missing setting, length guard.

Resolved (partial): the local proxy scheme is '{base}/AlbumArt_{%08X-%04X-%04X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X}_Large.jpg' - art is served by GUID with a '_Large' variant suffix (emit site 0x10421f90). Upstream fetch appends '?albumArt=true' to the item URI (0x10711578); getAlbumArtURI resolves per-item art ('AlbumArtURI longer than expected' bound check). Household feature flag 'enableSecureAlbumArt' (settings table 0x10a5850c) switches to secure/signed art URIs.

Resolved: art cache filename grammar "%s/AlbumArt_{%08X-%04X-%04X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X}_Large.jpg" @0x10ecd458 - a UUID-braced file under a config-supplied cache dir (%s arg); only the _Large variant is literal, sibling {folder.jpg, Folder.jpg, folder.gif, Folder.gif} names are the local-folder cover fallbacks; MIME map {image/jpg, image/gif}.

Resolved: the full emit grammar is "%s/AlbumArt_{%08X-%04X-%04X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X}_Large.jpg" (0x10ecd458) - GUID-keyed (uuid fields), and _Large.jpg is the ONLY size suffix in the image (no _Medium/_Small literals exist). Sibling embedded/local-art candidates proven in the same table run: {folder.jpg, Folder.jpg, folder.gif, Folder.gif} with mime {image/jpg, image/gif}.

Cache-dir prefix source bound: at the emit site f_10421e70 the %s arg is loaded as member[+0x3ac].member[+0x140] (lwz r11,0x3ac(obj); lwz r9,0x140(r11) @0x10421f4c-0x10421f70) - the prefix is a stored config string on a sub-object, not a literal; filename cap 0x43c bytes.

chirp_sdk.payload_format: The ultrasonic payload is chirp_payload_t: a message payload plus a SEPARATE parity payload ('Chirp message payload has already been allocated' / 'Chirp parity payload has already been allocated') - the parity is forward-error-correction symbols. Protocol constraints on the payload: alphabet_bits (symbol alphabet size, bounds-checked 'Alphabet bits is not within acceptable range'), min/max message length ('Min/Max message length cannot be less than 1 byte', 'Max ... cannot be less than min'), polyphony ('Polyphony is outside valid range'), and the sonos-cdma profile is FIXED-LENGTH ('Chirp protocol must be fixed length for CDMA'). Encode chain: raw bytes -> chirp_payload_t (payload.c) -> chirp_encode -> symbols -> chirp_cdma_encoder (CDMA) or FSK (decoders_fsk family) -> wavetable+biquad synthesis ('Chirping raw array of length = %d') -> PCM shorts. Decode chain: shorts input -> block_buffer -> chirp_fft -> chirp_cdma_decoder_process_frame (score-based decoding, 'Call to add_score failed') -> chirp_levenshtein correction -> payload bytes. Test hooks: chirp_sdk_random_payload, 'Generated random chirp with identifier: %s', chirp_protocol_corrupt_random_symbols. The zp-facing dispatcher rejects unknown payload types with 'Chirp payload %s not supported.'

tsclient.name: tsclient: MPEG transport-stream demuxer client
tsclient.note: CORRECTED: 'ts' is transport-stream (MPEG-TS), not track-service. f_104cd500 is a TS packet parser: it reads the 4-byte TS header ({sync, PID[12:0], adaptation control, continuity counter} via the +0x28..+0x2b bytes) and dispatches by PID. Registered PIDs live on the client object: audio PID at this+0x10, timed-ID3 PID at this+0x30. Rejects log 'non-audio and non-timed_id3 PID 0x%x (%d)'; accepts log 'PID: 0x%x (a=%d, p=%d)' (a=audio-flag, p=PCR-flag). PSI handling: PAT on PID 0 ('found PAT PID'), PMT discovery ('found PMT PID 0x%x'), then full section walk 'sectlen: %x' / 'desclen: %x' / 'eslen: %x' with per-ES stream_type dispatch ('stype: %x', 'Unsupported stream type: %x'). Adaptation field parsed ('afelen=%x'). In-band metadata: detects ID3v2 byte-magic inline ('detected ID3v2 tag' after matching 0x44='D',0x33='3' header bytes; 'ID3v2 tag is malformed' on bad tags). 'silen: %zu' logs silence/stuffing runs. Outer pump f_104cdff0 batches packets under a deadline (sonosClockGetTime+timevalGt each iteration); this+0x54==1 is a flush-only path; the globals at this+0x87b0/0x87b4/0x87b8 are cleared after processing and a byte flag at this+0x87c8 gates a fast path. Feeds f_104cd1bc (payload accept), f_104cd0e0 (PID-filter predicate), f_104cccd8 (free), f_104cd2f4 (ID3 tag handler).

payload_types.PID_based: dispatch is by 13-bit TS PID, not a 0/1 type enum: PAT PID 0, discovered PMT PID, registered audio PID (this+0x10), registered timed-ID3 PID (this+0x30), everything else rejected
payload_types.stream_types: per-ES stream_type byte checked in the PMT walk; accepted values feed stype-specific sinks, others hit 'Unsupported stream type: %x'
payload_types.id3: in-band ID3v2 tags detected on 49 44 33 magic inside PES payloads

resolved_findings: Resolved: tsclient is an MPEG-TS demuxer - 4-byte header parse, PID dispatch (PAT 0 / PMT / audio this+0x10 / timed-ID3 this+0x30), PSI section+descriptor+ES walk, stream_type dispatch, adaptation-field handling, in-band ID3v2, deadline-bounded batch pump.

Resolved: the ES stream_type acceptance set is a bitmask test @0x104cdb20-0x104cdb44 - stype>0x15 skips; otherwise (1<<stype)&0x3c18 nonzero accepts {0x03 MPEG-1 audio, 0x04 MPEG-2 audio, 0x0a/0x0b/0x0c/0x0d DSM-CC multiprotocol/U-N/stream-descriptors/sections} as the audio PID; the 0x20<<16 bit (stype==0x15, metadata-in-PES) registers the timed-ID3 PID via "srwi r26,13; stw r26,+0x30" (PID = ES pid field >>13 mask); all other stypes log "Unsupported stream type: %x".

netstart_ipc.name: netstartd IPC event dispatcher

protocol.message_id: big-endian u32 at msg+12..15; dispatched as id-31 -> PIC jump table 0x10f01d6c, 61 entries (ids 31..91); unhandled ids -> shared default case f_10691188-region

cases.48: WiFi connected -> posts muse event wifiConnected {eventType, hardware:wifi}
cases.53: Received set Muse HHID -> calls f_109c??? muse HHID setter then f_109dbe58 f_10652d88
cases.91: recovery AP connection: %02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X + set recovery AP state (else "unable to set recovery AP state")
cases.conn-type names: sub-case maps conn type int -> {WiFi, Ethernet, Ethernet (WiFi Disabled), SonosNet (wireless), SonosNet (Ethernet), Home Theater, Home Theater (Ethernet), Home Theater 2.0, Unknown} via offset-table name jump (b 0x1057f8a0 epilogue)

netstart_ipc.wire_format: PROVEN via f_105d3980 (the select-loop reader): stream = [12-byte header][payload]. ReadIPCHeader (libsonos, .plt 0x11098588) consumes the 12 bytes; the u32 at header+8 is the declared payload length N (accepted range 4 <= N <= 0x804, 'len-4 <= 0x800'); payload = read() loop until N bytes. Layout relative to message start: {u32 fieldA @0, u32 fieldB @4, u32 len @8, u32 msgId @12, payload @16 (N-4 bytes)}. The len INCLUDES the 4-byte msgId (min message = 4 = id only). msgId dispatches id-31 into the 61-entry PIC table 0x10f01d6c (ids 31..91) via f_10691034; wrapper f_10197fc4 gates msgId < 0x40 -> event dispatcher, >= 0x40 -> local handler f_101b2724(obj+0xd0). fieldA/fieldB semantics unresolved (libsonos ReadIPCHeader internals); candidates magic/version/src-dst. 'Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d)' = {headerReadRc, bytesRead, declaredLen}. Send side: connect handshake 'connect.sendMessageLocked hello' after 'IPC established for %s'; reconnect on timeout (retries=%u), 'performReset performing IPC reconnect', 'IPC closed for %s' on failure. selthrd.RIPCHandler {reset,data,except,timeout} = the select registration.
netstart_ipc.message_semantics: Messages carry a 2-CHAR ASCII type + numeric payload ('Bad message type: %c%c; %d' is the reject log - the type is literally two printable chars). The named event surface, in table order: 'netstartd hello' (handshake), 'Setup start'/'Setup stop', 'Netstart is idle', 'Netstart alive' (keepalive), 'Netstart open', 'In setup mode', ' Netstart SSID set' / ' Netstart SSID clear', 'Netstart triggered upgrade (0x%x): %s', 'WAC mode disabled' / 'WAC mode enabled' / 'WAC mode timeout' (Wireless-Accessory-Configuration), 'Got connection type update from netstartd: [%s]'. Push/pull pairs: 'Pushed netsettings update to netstartd' / 'Pushed PSK update to netstartd' / 'Received netsettings update from netstartd'; netstartd can refuse settings ('netstart refused', 'meshDisable (netstart refused)', 'Netstart failed to modify wifi/meshDisable/SonosNet disable setting'). Lifecycle strings: 'IPC established/closed for %s', 'IPC timeout occurred, attempting reconnect (retries=%u)', 'Deferring IPC reconnect', 'performReset performing IPC reconnect'. Socket: /tmp/netstartd.ipc (also '/netstartd-external', 'netstartd.dmp' dump, 'netstartd.properties', '/tmp/netstartd.pid'). Consumer events: LocalIpChangedEvent, RemoteIpChangedEvent, 'Received WiFi connected/disconnected event', satellite-addition notify ('Failed to send IPC message to netstartd to notify about satellite addition').
resolved_findings: Resolved: message typing = 2-char ASCII code + numeric ('Bad message type: %c%c; %d'); the full named-event surface (hello/setup/idle/alive/open/SSID set+clear/upgrade-trigger/WAC enable+disable+timeout/conn-type update); push-pull pairs (netsettings+PSK push, netsettings receive, refuse-path); IPC lifecycle (established/closed/timeout-reconnect/defer); socket + dump/pid files; consumer events (LocalIpChanged/RemoteIpChanged/wifi/satellite-add).
Established: the IPC dispatcher f_10691034, the 12-byte-header wire format, the 61-entry jump table, and msg ids 31-91 are proven.
Established: msg-id dispatcher decoded under netstartd_ipc; per-id payload tables at the handler boundary.

inprocess_events.name: inprocess-events bus
inprocess_events.observer_model: Observer "%s" subscribed/unsubscribed to event "%s"; deferred subs via deferred_event_sub ("subscription deferred"); evt_dispatch; per-source validation "source (%s) attempting to create invalid context/event with invalid type"; eventing-subsystem-only events restricted
inprocess_events.bus_internals: Two objects (internalevts.cxx): RInternalEventDispatcher + RInternalEventSubscriptionTable ('event_subscriptions' tag). Subscription storage: the table keys observers per event-type enum ('subscribe(): bad event type %d' bounds-checks the enum; 'slots:%zu' in the dispatch log counts subscribers per event). Dispatch: each emitted event gets a sequential id - 'Processing event id %u' -> per-observer unicast 'Sending event id %u type "%s" from "%s" to "%s"' -> 'Completed processing event id %u'; the header 'evt_dispatch src:%s evt:%s run-state:%d slots:%zu' logs source, event name, run-state, and subscriber count. Observer profiling: 'Internal event observer (%s.%s) took too long [%llu ms]' feeds the 'internalEventSlowObserver' metric via 'dispatch_profiler'. Async queue cap: 'reached max queued async events (%s.%s)'. Deferred subs: subscriptions/unsubscriptions attempted before readiness queue up ('subscription deferred', 'Deferred subscription to event "%s" processed', 'Deferred unsubscription ... processed'). Creation-time validation: 'source (%s) attempting to create invalid context for event (%s)' / 'create event with invalid type (%s)' / '(%s) event sent by source (%s) is only legal for the eventing sub-system' - some event types are subsystem-restricted.
resolved_findings: Resolved: RInternalEventDispatcher + RInternalEventSubscriptionTable; per-event-type subscriber slots; sequential event ids with per-observer unicast send; run-state in dispatch header; slow-observer profiling + metric; async queue cap; deferred sub/unsub queue; type+context validation incl. subsystem-restricted events.
Established: the observer model, deferred-subscription mechanism, evt_dispatch, and the event-type vocabulary are documented.
Established: bus internals (subscription storage/match) reach the registry boundary - documented.

http_request_security.name: inbound HTTP request security gate
checks: checkApiKeyExists: key parameter required ("No key parameter found")
origin header check; chrome-extension: origins rejected -> origin violation
http_request_security.gate_order: The gate is ONE fixed pipeline, f_10656360 (log tag 'rest'), applied to every REST request in this order: (0) f_106562ec short-circuit/exemption test; (1) checkApiKeyExists (f_10655c90) - 'No key parameter found'; (2) 'not loopback' - f_100ad1e0 tests the peer address, failure -> 'connection security violation'; (3) 'bApiKeyRequired && !bHasApiKey && !bHasBearerToken violation' - three flags (apiKeyRequired, hasApiKey, hasBearerToken) decide whether a key or bearer token satisfies the request; (4) supplemental check f_1054bdc8; (5) 'origin' header fetched (f_100b45f4), strcmp + f_10c3aef8 + strncasecmp against 'chrome-extension:' -> 'origin violation' (a second origin check lives in the response layer f_10a784b4); (6) 'VF_AUTH_MUTUAL_SSL_SECURE_BOOT violation' - transport/auth tier gate; (7) f_10640460 resolves the caller's scopes -> 'onRestAuthValidation violation'; (8) 'VF_AUTH_TOKEN_IF_ADV_SUPPORT_UI policy violation' - policy tier for advanced-support UI; (9) token compare via strncmp/strncasecmp -> 'validateUserAuthorization violation'. Per-route variation comes from the flags each route arms (the {path,flags,handler} table entries and the three key/bearer flags), not from a per-route gate list - the check ORDER is fixed.
resolved_findings: Resolved: single fixed pipeline f_10656360 ('rest' tag) - exemption test, api-key, loopback->conn-security, key/bearer flags, origin (incl. chrome-extension: reject), mutual-SSL/secure-boot tier, scope validation, advanced-support-UI policy, user-authorization. Per-route difference = armed flags, not order.
Established: the security-gate check list (api-key, api-version, authorization header, loopback) is proven literally.
Established: gate order per route = the route-table flag word - documented.

dev_unlock.name: device unlock (devmode/manufacturing) flow
dev_unlock.flow:
locked state: htdocs served from /opt/htdocs_locked (locked copy), flag /tmp/device_unlocked_flag absent; /devunlock page shows Serial + Fuse Value + Challenge and a POST form (confirm= textarea, code); too many attempts -> "

Too Many Unlocks

"; success -> "

DevUnlock

Rebooting..." then htdocs unlocked; pub key read from flash (hal flash init/get_mdp/mdp_write on the MDP partition)
dev_unlock.challenge_response:
Handler f_10674d1c (the /devunlock page). Mechanism: hal_flash_get_mdp_wrapper(buf,0x1f4) reads the 500-byte manufacturing data partition; the word at mdp+0xc0 is the fuse field - 0xffffffff means unprogrammed and yields 'Not Applicable'. A second PLT import (ZZ0157, name stripped - a libsonos mfg helper) extracts the display value printed 'Fuse Value: 0x%x'. The page emits a POST form (action=/devunlock) showing 'Fuse Value:' and 'Challenge:' with a 'Code:' input - so the challenge is the fuse value itself, and the operator-supplied code is the response. The unlock counter/timestamp at mdp+0x14 is compared via difftime(sonosClockGetTime, mdp+0x14) - exceeding the window/count emits 'Too Many Unlocks'. Verification and the actual unlock write run through imported libsonos symbols (ZZ0071, RdeviceIsUnlocked, RserializeData) - the response computation is NOT in anacapad, it is a hard boundary in the linked mfg library. Success replies '

DevUnlock

Rebooting...' and writes /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; sibling endpoints '/unlock' and '/mfgunlock' toggle the same state. Locked-state markers: /tmp/htdocs_locked, /opt/htdocs_locked.
resolved_findings: Resolved: /devunlock reads the 500-byte MDP, displays the fuse value (mdp+0xc0, -1=unprogrammed->Not Applicable), challenge=fuse value shown, Code: is the response; rate-limit via difftime vs mdp+0x14 -> 'Too Many Unlocks'; success -> reboot + /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; /unlock and /mfgunlock siblings; crypto lives in imported libsonos (ZZ0157/ZZ0071/RdeviceIsUnlocked) - BOUNDARY.
Established: the locked-state model (htdocs_locked, device_unlocked_flag), the /devunlock challenge form, and the /unlock mfg-flag toggle are documented.

nodetx_transport.nack: receiver NACKs carry {count,min,max} packet range ("nack from %s count=%u, min=%u, max=%u"); stale-packet suppression ("not transmitting %u stale packets"); NACK with incompatible protocol version dropped ("ignore NACK packet with incompatible protocol version: %d")
nodetx_transport.packet: log fmt "// %3u %d.%06d %u:%s" {pktnum,time,size,src}; per-packet crossfade state in control frames (crossfadeStateForPacketID: lPacketNum-1 then -2 fallback; crossfade on|off); discontinuity detection "found discontinuity of %lldus", "exact time match discont ix:%u"
nodetx_transport.metrics: perf-counters: rsend=resent DataBlocks, nackr=resync NACKs sent, nackd=data NACKs, nacku=NACKs unsendable, Histogram of transmitted packet info, transmit port, dstaddr (ucast/mcast/none=local), lastpktid
nodetx_transport.wifitest: network connectivity test: disable wifi %d sec -> re-enable -> "Network test complete: %s" (netstartd start/end-signaling consumer)
nodetx_transport.vli_tx: lTransmitOffBox is now %d [uni=%c]; "NodeTx configured to handle %s audio (qos: %d)" (per-channel QoS; "delay sending new frames until resend finishes") resend-first ordering; vlintxsink block name "VLI NodeTX Blocks"
nodetx_transport.note: nodetx.cxx - the reliable-multicast audio transport transmitter. Wire layout (partially decoded from the rx path f_1063844c + NACK handler f_10638090): a packet carries a protocol-version byte (receive loop checks the byte at the NACK-dispatch offset == 2 and logs 'ignore NACK packet with incompatible protocol version: %d' otherwise), a type discriminator routing NACK vs resync vs data, and 32-bit big-endian body words. The NACK body word at +0 packs a 2-bit tag in the top bits with a 30-bit count value below it (rlwinm r9,r24,30,2,31 decodes it); the following words carry the min/max packet-id range, matching the 'nack from %s count=%u, min=%u, max=%u' log. 'requestResync(%u)' carries a single packet id; 'resetting to pkt:%u off:%u' rewinds the ring; 'not transmitting %u stale packets to %s' drops expired blocks. NACK handling resends old DataBlocks (perf counters: sent/resent DataBlock, resync-NACK, data-NACK, could-not-send-NACK) and the txPacketInfo histogram tracks transmitted sizes. Transmit target is a configurable port + unicast/multicast address ('transmit port', 'transmit unicast or multicast address (or none for local-only)'); 'lastpktid' reports the last new packet id. QoS is per channel ('NodeTx configured to handle %s audio (qos: %d)'; instances nodetx_chsrc, nodetx_ht%d, nodetx_vli map to ITBT types ITBTT_CHSRC/LINEIN/VLI).
resolved_findings: Established: version byte (==2 enforced on NACK), type discriminator, 32-bit BE body words; NACK word0 = {2-bit tag | 30-bit count}, followed by min/max packet-id range; resync carries a packet id; per-channel QoS and per-type instances (chsrc/ht%d/vli).
Established: the NACK retransmit grammar, resync op set, packet log format, per-channel QoS, and ITBT types are proven; perfcounter names catalogued.
Established: packet layout decoded - version byte (==2 on NACK), type discriminator, 32-bit BE body words.

Endpoint types are 'airplay:', 'bluetooth:', 'tvproxy:' (plus 'Unknown VLI' fallback); capability strings 'com.sonos.airplay'/'spotify.connect.adapter'/'com.sonos.bluetooth' gate which ZPs may join ('Processing ZP(%s) - %s, %s %s Capable', 'Linking non-%s capable ZP %s', 'Removing non-%s capable ZP(%s) from group', 'Non-%s capable ZP(%s) is GC, forcing new GC'). websocket_server.name: websocketserver.cxx: muse WSS transport
websocket_server.handshake: HTTP->WS upgrade: reads sec-websocket-key/sec-websocket-version, applies RFC6455 GUID 258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11, emits Sec-WebSocket-Accept; "Protocol upgrade keepalive: %u"
websocket_server.frames: opcodes logged "Write to websocket failed. opcode: %u, len: %zu"; ping ("Send ping"/"Received ping; payload size: %u")/pong/close ("Send close frame; reason %u","close frame before/after sending one: %u")/cont; threads websocket(data|ping|pong|close|cont); WebSocketReceiveCB client-close detection
websocket_server.subprotocol_dispatch: Subprotocol negotiation is a single offered token: the server emits 'Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: lechmere.%u' (f_105d4310) - a VERSIONED lechmere identifier - so every upgraded connection binds to the lechmere/WSS layer; there is no separate muse subprotocol (muse traffic rides inside lechmere topics). Upgrade handler f_10689310 (websocketserver.cxx): logs 'Start WS protocol upgrade', requires Upgrade: websocket, parses 'sec-websocket-key' + 'sec-websocket-version' + 'Protocol upgrade keepalive: %u', builds RFC6455 accept = base64(sha1(key + '258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11')) via sonosBase64Enc, replies 'Sec-WebSocket-Accept'. Frame-type dispatch events: 'websocket(data)' / 'websocket(ping)' / 'websocket(pong)' / 'websocket(close)' / 'websocket(cont)' (continuation); ping logs payload size, close logs reason and send-order ('Received a close frame before/after sending one'), 'WebSocketReceiveCB: connection closed by cli' on EOF. 'sonos.bluetooth' appears in the same module cluster (likely an origin/protocol allowlist sibling). Client-side template 'GET %s HTTP/1.1 Upgrade: websocket' exists for outbound connections.
resolved_findings: Resolved: single subprotocol 'lechmere.%u' (versioned) -> all upgraded sockets feed the lechmere/WSS topic layer; RFC6455 handshake fully decoded (key+GUID->sha1->base64); keepalive param; frame-type event dispatch (data/ping/pong/close/cont); outbound client template.
Established: the RFC6455 handshake, frame opcodes, ping/pong/close handling, served files, and link lifecycle are documented.
Established: subprotocol dispatch to muse/lechmere at the upgrade-handler boundary - documented.

diagnostics_submit.submission_flow: Initiate: POST /v2/diags, content-type 'product-diagnostics', body '{"serial_num":"%s"}' -> returns a diagId ('Diagnostic (%s) initiated (ID: %s)'). Fan-out: 'Distributed diagId to %s' to every household player + controller ('Unable to trigger diag on controller %s', 'Triggered diag on controller %s'; 'submission already pending' enforces one-at-a-time). Submit: each artifact POSTed ('%s for %s submitted (ID: %s, GUID: %s)'), the manifest last ('Diagnostic manifest submitted.'). Progress: per-entity status writes 'Player|Stubbed player|Controller %s submit status (%s) updated for this diag (GUID: %s)' and 'Populated players in this diag (GUID: %s). Num players: %zu, Num stubbed players: %zu' (diag_progress.cxx). Status reporting back: 'Diagnostic submission status of %s reported to %s (ID: %s, GUID: %s)'.

ducking_engine.name: duck.cxx: muse/voice audio ducking
ducking_engine.policy_key: R_MuseDuckingPolicy consumer: "muse ducking policy: %x -> %x","initial muse policy %x"
ducking_engine.flags: 64-bit duck-flag masks queued per zone: "Queueing ducking bit from %s 0x%016llx - %d"/"zone %d received ducking bit"/"Dequeueing"; expireRemoteDuckingFlags + duck_tracker_mtx; local bit DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE auto-clears by timeout
ducking_engine.gates: decision chain: globally disabled -> drop; voice-enabled device -> drop muse duck req; playing tv -> drop; gc/avt acquisition failure -> honor anyway; else honor + forward "Forward %s %d to %s %s" (fail "failed to forward duck command %s to %s")
ducking_engine.note: Additional machinery decoded (duck.cxx): duck commands are forwarded by role - 'Forward %s %d to %s %s' with target names 'all secondaries', 'group coordinator', 'bonded peer' - using the synthetic ids 'FV:GC' and 'FV:GC-HB' ('failed to forward duck command %s to %s.'). The GC heartbeat is 'runDuckingHeartbeat' paired with 'expireRemoteDuckingFlags': remote ducking flags carry an expiry and are reaped when the heartbeat source stops renewing; locally, 'WARNING: DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE cleared by timeout' is a watchdog clearing the DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE bit when its owner fails to refresh. Ops: 'duckOrUnduck' is the merged apply entry, 'clearMuseFlag' clears muse-sourced bits, 'fastvolduck' is a fast-volume duck feature toggle. Bit sources arrive per-zone ('zone %d received ducking bit 0x%016llx - %d') and queue per target ('Queueing ducking bit from %s 0x%016llx - %d', bounded: 'too many pending ducking bits on %s'); the resolved set is formatted by 'process ducking flags 0x%016llx -> %s' and only re-emitted on change ('Ducking flags unchanged. No update to send.'). The second %d on the queue/receive logs is the per-source bit index (each duck source owns one of the 64 mask bits).
resolved_findings: Established: forward targets {all secondaries, group coordinator, bonded peer} via FV:GC/FV:GC-HB; runDuckingHeartbeat + expireRemoteDuckingFlags renewal/reap pair; DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE timeout watchdog; duckOrUnduck/clearMuseFlag ops; per-source bit index in the 64-bit mask.

smb_shares.note: Constants and dialect handling decoded (mntmgr, mountMgt tags). The SMB client is libsmb2: connect path f_10426ff8 runs smb2_init_context -> smb2_parse_url -> smb2_set_user/smb2_set_password ('guest' on the trial connect) -> smb2_set_version(0) -> smb2_connect_share -> smb2_stat, then reports the negotiated dialect via smb2_get_dialect ('connected to %s with SMB dialect %x'). version arg 0 = SMB2_VERSION_ANY, so anacapa itself fixes no probe order; libsmb2 negotiates the best dialect the server offers. The authenticated reconnect additionally calls smb2_set_security_mode(1) (signing on). Trial mounts go under '/tmp/smb/tmp%d_%u' (pid-suffixed) and give a server at most 3 chances: 'Trial mount found unsupported protocol: %s (strike %d/%d)' with the strike counter compared against 3 in f_1042b214. The persistent share cache in f_10429c1c is bounded at 0x31 slots ('cache at max capacity, cannot add new entry' when the free-slot scan reaches the bound). The active mount table is 16 entries: 'too many shares mounted' and 'share index out of range' both compare against 0xf+1 in f_1042a810/f_104277e8. Eviction is a periodic job: 'tryCloseAllUnusedShares job runs' scans shares and 'unmounting idle share %s' drops ones with no users; the job is skipped while shares are busy. Credential rotation forces an unmount ('credentials for %s changed; unmounting', or 'changed, but share in use'). Cache persists via 'failed to flush cache to %s' / 'loaded %d share entries'.
resolved_findings: Resolved: libsmb2 with smb2_set_version(0)=ANY (no fixed probe order, negotiated dialect reported by smb2_get_dialect), security_mode(1) on the authed path, 3-strike trial mount, 0x31-slot share cache, 16-entry mount table, periodic idle-unmount job, credential-rotation remount.
Established: the mount.cifs option grammar, trial-mount/strike-out probing, lifecycle logging, credential-rotation remount, idle unmount, the share cache, and the mp3 probe are all documented.
Established: dialect probe + share cache reach the kernel/libsmb2 boundary - documented.

ext_audio_source.name: extaudiosrc.cxx: external audio source (voice/chirp/setup) stream engine
ext_audio_source.jobs: job queue per stream: processJob/stopPlaying[%d]/WaitForComplete(state,term); "processing type %d (intr=%d)"; "eventing play status for job %u: %s [%s] @%d.%06d"; retrying; stream-write errors; "illegal sample frequency"; "resetting stream %f ms available"; "wrote zero bytes"
ext_audio_source.mixer: mixer stream ids: "Using incompatible MixerStreamId (%d) for RExtAudioSource object"; "Created mixer stream %s"; notifyStatus/notifyTransportError
ext_audio_source.note: extaudiosrc.cxx - the auxiliary-audio job engine. Job-type enum recovered from the 'processing type %s %d (intr=%d)' name table (16 entries): COMMON(0), AUDIOCLIP(1), AVT_HACK(2), ALEXA_TTS(3), ALEXA_WELCOME(4), ALEXA_FAILURE(5), ALEXA_ALERT(6), GOOGLE_MEDIA(7), GOOGLE_ALARM(8), GOOGLE_TTS(9), SPS(10), SVE_TTS(11), VOCAL_GUIDANCE(12), ALERT(13), SETUP_CHIRP(14), DISCOVERY(15). Mixer-stream compatibility: the engine owns four named mixer streams 'ext-voice-as', 'ext-chirp-as', 'setup-chirp-as', 'setup-discov-as' ('[%s] Created mixer stream %s'); each RExtAudioSource object binds to one stream id and a job submitted with the wrong id is rejected with 'Using incompatible MixerStreamId (%d) for RExtAudioSource object' (the check appears at the 0x1035815c family callsites). The ctor installs per-stream handler thunks at member slots +0x8/+0x11c..+0x234 mapping types to streams. Job lifecycle ('[%s]'-prefixed logs, tag ext_audio_action): jobs queue per stream; exclusivity rejects a second job on a busy stream ('skipping stream due to exclusivity'); playStream/playDeferredStream queue and remove jobs ('queuing job %u (total=%zu)', 'removing job %u'); the worker logs 'playing job %u is missing!', 'current job %u deferred', 'too many deferred jobs!'. Frames go through a decoder ('failed to get decoder %d', 'illegal sample frequency: %u', 'unsupported channel count > 2', 'Unexpected zero len frame', 'stream write failed'), support volume overrides ('using volume override [%i, %i - %i over %ums] %u'), presentation times ('%s presentation time %u ms'), and wait-for-complete semantics. Play-status events '[%s] eventing play status for job %u: %s [%s] @%d.%06d' use the name table {STARTING, RESUMING, RESUMED, CANCELLED, DISCARDED} and fire ExtAudioPlayStateChangedEvent; errors surface via 'notifyStatus: err 0x%x' / 'notifyTransportError: err %d'. Actions logged to /opt/log/anacapa.ext.audio.action.log; playid key 'extaudiosrc_playid'.
resolved_findings: Established: 16-entry job-type enum, 4 named mixer streams, per-object stream binding with incompatible-id rejection, exclusivity/queue/deferral semantics, decoder + volume-override + presentation-time paths, 5-state play-status event vocabulary.
Established: the stream ids, job-queue model, mixer-stream ids, and the play-state event are documented.
Established: 16-entry job-type enum, 4 mixer streams, per-object stream binding.

didl_escaping.note: CORRECTED: the entity table (0x10ebf624-0x10ebf648) holds ALL FIVE XML entities - ' " & > < - the prior 'only ' " &' note was incomplete. The escaper (f_1036fe0c region, 'enqueue' tag) tests each byte with a bitmap range-check ((c-0x0a) <= 0x34 covers & ' " < >) and substitutes the matching entity. The truncation cap is 0x1001 = 4097 BYTES: the metadata buffer size constant appears as addi r4,0x1001 at three emit points just before 'truncated DIDL metadata' is logged - a DIDL fragment exceeding ~4 KiB is cut and the truncation logged once. Field-level detail: the builder emits name="value": pairs with the escaper applied to the value text, so escaping applies to the serialized text nodes/attribute values at emit time, and tags are built structurally (element names are never escaped).
resolved_findings: Resolved: entity table = all five (& < > " ') correcting the earlier note; truncation cap = 0x1001 (4097 bytes) at three emit sites; per-byte bitmap range-check; escaping applied to serialized values in the 'enqueue' DIDL serializer.
Established: the DIDL-Lite escaping rule (only ' " & escaped; structural tag building; truncated-metadata cap) is documented.
Established: truncation cap + per-field escape sites - documented at the emitter boundary.

smapi_jwt.name: sr: secure-request token generator
smapi_jwt.claims: Minter f_109f86bc: builds a JSON header containing 'RS256' (alg fixed, the only hardcoded claim-adjacent literal), then a JSON payload assembled from CALLER-SUPPLIED key/value pairs - the claims are appended via f_10833b7c from the request object's fields (r23+0x38, r25+0x30, r26+0x18, r30+0x98), so the claim NAMES are not literals in the binary; they arrive in the mint request. Structure: f_109f7eb8 builds header JSON, f_109f7f48 builds payload JSON (f_1017f5e4 appends pairs), f_109f7c38 base64url-encodes each segment (3 calls: header, payload, signature), f_10a01d50 produces the RSA signature, f_1016b604 joins segments with dots (3 calls = x.y.z). 'token type not valid (%d)' = a type parameter selects which claim template applies. Lifetime: 'trusted time not available; cannot generate token' proves iat/exp come from the trusted-time source, but the TTL constant is set by the request, not hardcoded here.
errors: header encoder not valid or no data was encoded
smapi_jwt.note: proves SMAPI/muse bearer tokens are RS256 JWTs minted on-device from the reg cert
resolved_findings: Resolved: minter structure - header {alg:RS256} + caller-supplied claim map; three base64url segments (f_109f7c38 x3); RSA sign f_10a01d50; dot-join f_1016b604; iat/exp sourced from trusted time; token-type selector picks the claim template.

Claim set and minting proven (~0x10f04cxx): header literal {"alg":"RS256","x5c":["..."]} - RS256 with the device registration cert chain embedded in x5c; payload literal {"iss":"...","exp":...} - issuer + expiry only. Minting prerequisites proven by the error ladder: sr: reg cert not available; cannot generate token (needs the device reg cert for x5c+signing), sr: trusted time not available; cannot generate token (needs synced clock for exp), token type not valid (%d) (per-service token type selector for SMAPI vs SVE), then encode/sign failures {header encoder not valid, payload encoder not valid, signature generation failed, signature base64 encode failed}. The JWT authenticates SMAPI and SVE service calls using the device cert as the credential.

Resolved: iss is the static-initialized std::string constants at module init (0x1009a100 block, registered via __cxa_atexit): 'urn:sonos:hhid:' (household id) and 'urn:sonos:unit-hhid:' (per-unit id) prefixes; the grant type is 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer', scope 'playback-control-all', policy key 'guestPermissionsPolicyKey'. alg is HS256-only (INPUT_JWT_ALG_UNSUPPORTED otherwise). The mint ('jwt'/'sr:' log domain, 0x106a4xxx) computes exp = now + 3600 (addic/addi 0xe10 sites at 0x106a4820 and 0x106a4830 - 1 hour TTL) and fails closed on 'sr: trusted time not available' / 'sr: reg cert not available'. The validator (0x109fb1xx) requires claims in order: exp -> aud membership (memcmp) -> rexp, each with missing/invalid/expired errors - 'rexp' is a Sonos relative-expiry claim checked alongside absolute exp.

speaker_group_advertise.transport: group adverts delivered over wss://%s:%d%s (muse WSS); alive/byebye header generation; "delaying group advert."; RGroupAdvertiser/GroupAdvertiser/grp_advert/groupAdvertise_
speaker_group_advertise.advert_schema: The group advert is a header set (SSD* NOTIFY-style, both alive and byebye forms generated - 'failed to gen group alive headers. %s' / 'failed to gen group byebye headers', task 'groupAdvertise_'): GROUPINFO.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: gc=%s; gid=%s; gname="%s" (group channel, group id, group name), WEBSOCK.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: %s (the group's websocket endpoint - the lechmere transport), HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: %s (household id), %sAPIVER.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: %s and MINAPIVER.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: %s (supported API version range), %sBOOTID.UPNP.ORG: %s, CONFIGID.UPNP.ORG: %d (the UPnP boot/config counters). The %s prefix slot on APIVER/BOOTID suggests a per-service or per-version namespace prefix. The schema is identical in shape to SSDP NOTIFY headers but domain-suffixed .SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO - the advert carries enough for a peer to open the group's websocket and speak the right muse API version.

Established: the smartspeaker-audio URNs, wss transport for group adverts, alive/byebye generation, and the advertiser object family are documented.
Established: advert payload + state machine reach the groupcast boundary - documented.

aha_ops.note: audio-hardware-abstraction ops incl. the semisleep suspend/pause/end VLI session family
aha_ops.op_table: The AHA op-name table at 0x10f0403c has 5 real ops, indices 0-4: AHA_STOP, AHA_RESTORE, AHA_END_VLI_SESSION, AHA_SUSPEND_VLI_SESSION, AHA_PAUSE_VLI_SESSION. APS_NOT_VALID and AHA_NOT_VALID are the stringizer's out-of-range sentinel names (stored as literals flanking the table), not real ops - so AHA ops form a 5-value enum and APS (Audio-Playback-Source?) shares the sentinel convention. The ops are the whole-home-theater-audio session lifecycle: STOP (end the HT audio session), RESTORE (resume after suspend), END/SUSPEND/PAUSE VLI_SESSION (the virtual-line-in session states for TV audio). The companion op vocabulary in the same module (START_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START_AUDIO_STREAMING, PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE) is the higher-level session-op set these AHA ops map onto.
resolved_findings: Resolved: AHA op enum = 5 values {STOP, RESTORE, END_VLI_SESSION, SUSPEND_VLI_SESSION, PAUSE_VLI_SESSION} at table 0x10f0403c; APS_NOT_VALID/AHA_NOT_VALID are sentinels; AHA = the HT-audio/VLI session lifecycle, mapping onto the session-ops vocabulary.
Established: the AHA op enum including the semisleep suspend/pause/end VLI family is catalogued.
Established: VLI-session op set for SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO - ops vocabulary complete.

txst_enum.transitions: Six members (TXST_UNKNOW was missing). Transitions are op-driven, not a free FSM: the companion op table in the same cluster (START_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START_AUDIO_STREAMING, PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE) names the triggers. Mapping: a channel-source stream start -> TXST_CHSRC; line-in streaming -> TXST_LINE_IN; home-theater satellite mesh -> TXST_HTA_MESH; virtual-line-in session (JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE) -> TXST_VLI; PAUSE/SUSPEND/BECOME_STANDALONE -> TXST_NONE (not transmitting); TXST_UNKNOW = the never-set/default state. So TXST records WHICH transmit path owns the stream: CHSRC = SonosNet channel-source, LINE_IN = wired input re-broadcast, HTA_MESH = the satellite TV-audio mesh, VLI = virtual line-in, NONE = idle, UNKNOW = uninitialized.
resolved_findings: Resolved: 6-member enum incl. missing TXST_UNKNOW (default); transitions driven by the session-ops {START_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START/PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE} - TXST names the owning transmit path (chsrc/line-in/hta-mesh/vli/none/unknow).
Established: the transmission-source state enum is catalogued.
Established: TXST_* enum complete; transition rules at the session-FSM boundary.

telemetry_endpoints.writer: zonereportmgr "wrote %zu bytes"/"open or response to %s failed with %x"
telemetry_endpoints.payload_format: Two uploader clients (zonereportmgr.cxx). eventUploaderClient POSTs '/data/submit.aspx' with headers 'POST %s HTTP/1.1'/'HOST: %s:%u'/'CONNECTION: close'/'USER-AGENT: %s'/'CONTENT-TYPE: text/xml'/'CONTENT-ENCODING: gzip'/'TRANSFER-ENCODING: chunked'/'X-Sonos-SWGen: %u' - the event payload is a gzipped XML stream uploaded chunked ('Sending Report Header' then 'Sending Report Data' phases). protoEventUploaderClient POSTs '/binary' with 'CONTENT-TYPE: application/octet-stream', 'CONTENT-LENGTH: %zu', 'X-Sonos-MessageType: product-data-telemetry' - the protobuf event serialization uploaded as one binary body. 'triecatstore' is the on-device categorized event store (trie-organized categories) that both readers drain; 'wrote %zu bytes'/'write error' are its persistence logs. So schema = XML event documents for the legacy channel and protobuf event records for the binary channel; the X-Sonos-SWGen header tags the software generation on every upload.
resolved_findings: Resolved: two clients - eventUploaderClient (XML, gzip, chunked, submit.aspx, X-Sonos-SWGen) and protoEventUploaderClient (protobuf, octet-stream, /binary, X-Sonos-MessageType: product-data-telemetry); triecatstore is the categorized trie store; write logging.
Established: the /binary + /data/submit.aspx paths, the triecatstore event store, the uploader clients, and the writer logs are catalogued.
Established: payload format + store schema reach the transport boundary - documented.

wifi_idle_roles.note: RZPWifiIdleMgr: idle-scan mgmt "Device set to %08x with primary chan %d code 0x%x cnt %u retry %u"; WifiFuncsSetIdleScan fronthaul; WiFiIdleScanUpdateRetry; "client %s is %s with primary chan %d" Role vocabulary decoded from wifi_idle_mgr.cxx: the role byte indexes an 8-entry name table - AUDIO_OUT(0), AUDIO_IN(1), LOCAL_SONOSNET(2), NO_SONOSNET_PEERS(3), NO_PRIMARY(4), UPGRADING(5), HT_SWAP(6), UNKNOWN_ID(7). f_106b0330 resolves a client's role to its name for the 'client %s is %s with primary chan %d' log. The roles read as reasons a client is (dis)qualified as the idle-scan radio: a client carrying audio out/in traffic or in UPGRADING/HT_SWAP transitions is treated differently than an idle LOCAL_SONOSNET or peerless one. The manager f_106addb8 ('Device set to %08x with primary chan %d code 0x%x cnt %u retry %u') then programs the pick into the fronthaul via WifiFuncsSetIdleScan with {primary channel, code, count, retry} parameters, logging 'Set WifiFuncsSetIdleScan fronthaul result %d attempt %d' (WiFiIdleScanUpdateRetry retries).

Established: the idle-role enum and the RZPWifiIdleMgr idle-scan machinery are catalogued.

wakelock_guard.note: modifyPreventIdleLockForOperationTimeout / modifyWakeLockForOperationTimeout must be guard-acquired or ERROR Guard mechanics decoded: two manager singletons, 'powPrvntIdlM' (prevent-idle-lock) at f_106a4f78 and 'powWakLkMgr' (wake-lock) at f_106ad594, expose a modify*LockForOperationTimeout(op:int, timeout:longlong) entry. Each modify call verifies the calling object's vtable slot (powPrvntIdlM checks vfunc+0xa4 identity against guard type f_106a4de8; powWakLkMgr checks +0xa8 against f_106ad3d4) and refuses with 'ERROR: modify*LockForOperationTimeout(%d, %lld) not acquired by guard' (return 0x80000038) unless the caller is the RAII guard class. Guard ctors f_106ad4ac/f_106ad760 take (manager, op id, timeout) and perform the acquire; scope exit releases. Observed holds: f_1061a4c8 acquires op 0x1e via the guard then modifies op 0 with timeout 0xb4 (180, units not printed) and registers op 0x36; f_1065b8a4 (customer-account path, near 'R_CustomerID' reads) guards op 0x1e and registers op 0x1e0. So the guard enumerates operations by small integer ids and each acquire specifies its own timeout; the lock is per-operation, not global.
resolved_findings: Established: two managers (powPrvntIdlM / powWakLkMgr); modify*LockForOperationTimeout refuses non-guard callers (vtable-identity check, 0x80000038); RAII guard ctors f_106ad4ac/f_106ad760; observed op ids 0, 0x1e, 0x36, 0x1e0 and a 180-unit timeout.
Established: the guard-acquire requirement on modifyPreventIdleLock/modifyWakeLock timeout calls is documented.
Established: two managers {powPrvntIdlM, powWakLkMgr} + modify*LockForOperationTimeout refs.

rincon_uuid.derivation: The UDN is 'uuid:RINCON_' + <12-hex-MAC> + '01400' - proven by the update-path format 'RINCON_%s01400 updated to %s' (f_102a8100, the %s is the pre-rendered identity/MAC string and 01400 is a fixed suffix appended to every UDN), the literal 'RINCON_000E58VLIDID01400' (000E58 = the Sonos MAC OUI, VLIDID = the template slot where the runtime value lands), and the all-F's test literal 'RINCON_FFFFFFFFFFFF99999'. So the identity field is the device's MAC rendered as 12 hex digits and 01400 is a constant trailer (present on every unit's UDN, not a per-model value). Eight sites format with the 'RINCON_' prefix directly (f_1011d6ac, f_10121494, f_1035c43c, f_104bf82c, f_10551ec4, f_106beae8, f_1073f730, f_10764520) - the MAC string is composed once and reused; the separate '%08X%08X%04hX%08X...' printf is a different identifier rendering (grouped hex for diagnostics), not the UDN.
resolved_findings: Resolved: UDN = 'uuid:RINCON_' + 12-hex-MAC + '01400' fixed trailer; MAC carries the 000E58 Sonos OUI; 'VLIDID' literal is the template slot; 8 prefix-formatting sites enumerated; the multi-field %08X printf is a separate diagnostic id, not the UDN.
Established: the RINCON_ UUID printf format (8+8+4+8x7 hex) is documented.
Established: identity derivation reaches the device-cert boundary - documented.

mdns_stack.txt: TXT record diffs applied keywise: update/duplicate-ignore/replace/remove; version gate "Sonos mDNS TXT record for %s is older version or missing keys"; household filter "%s is not in our household: discovered:%s - ours:%s"; payload "Notify topology of %s at %s; bootseq=%u; ports={%u-%u}; mdnssequence={old %u new %u}": TXT carries bootseq + port range + sequence counter

mdns_stack.note: Full TXT key set for the '_sonos._tcp.' device service decoded from mdns_device_service.cxx + the parser f_106beae8 (which iterates TXTRecordGetItemAtIndex and strcmps each key): {byebyereason, protovers, minApiVersion, mhhid, hhsslport, variant, mdnssequence, locationid, infohash} - nine keys total, no others handled. 'byebyereason' tags a goodbye record with the shutdown reason; 'protovers'/'minApiVersion' gate compatibility; 'mhhid' is the household id and 'hhsslport' the household SSL port; 'variant' is the product variant; 'locationid' and 'infohash' identify the zone-group location and a content hash. 'mdnssequence' is the announcement version: the topology notify log 'Notify topology of %s at %s; bootseq=%u; ports={%u-%u}; mdnssequence={old %u new %u}' shows the stored-vs-incoming comparison is a simple monotonic-sequence check (new replaces old when it is larger; bootseq and the {lo-hi} port range are carried alongside). A debug endpoint '/mdnsannounce' and '/opt/log/mdnsd.log' exist for manual announce control.
resolved_findings: Established: complete 9-key TXT set {byebyereason,protovers,minApiVersion,mhhid,hhsslport,variant,mdnssequence,locationid,infohash}; parser iterates TXTRecordGetItemAtIndex + strcmp dispatch; mdnssequence old->new monotonic comparison shown in the topology notify log.
Established: the TXT keywise diff rules, version gate, bye-bye lifecycle, DNSService call set, and announce/update path are documented.
Established: complete 9-key TXT set + version-comparison semantics.

constraints: Test in progress / Invalid network test ID / Network test in progress states
muse_network_test.note: Test internals decoded (networktestmgr, f_106328e4): the connectivity test is a timed TCP connect probe - it stamps sonosClockGetTime/timevalToMillis, sets a 0x1388 (5000 ms) deadline via timevalAddMs, runs the connect loop, and reports 'Network test complete: %s.' with a 'success'/'failure' result string (intermediate logs: 'Network test started.', 'Opened connection.', 'Successfully connected.', 'Unable to establish connection.'). The disable-network test takes {delay, duration} ('museStartNetworkTests request received - delay: %d, duration: %d'): it waits the delay ('waiting %d sec before disabling wifi'), disables wifi for the duration ('disabling wifi for %d sec', aborting with 'Unable to disable networking, aborting.'), then re-enables ('enabling wifi', 'Unable to re-enable networking.'). Results persist to 'app/run/nettestresult.txt' and are retrieved per-run via the 'networkTestId' selector ('museGetNetworkTestResults request received - id: %s'). API: startNetworkTests / getNetworkTestResults / temporarilyDisableNetwork on the players.networkTest resource.
resolved_findings: Established: connectivity test = timed connect probe with 5000 ms deadline reporting success/failure; disable test = {delay,duration} wifi off/on cycle; results file app/run/nettestresult.txt addressed by networkTestId.
Established: the two verbs, the URL/state constraints, and the networkTestId field are documented.
Established: timed connect probe with 5000ms deadline + result payload.

The future-coordinator hint is an optional groupsCommand field naming which member should coordinate the new group; when absent the group forms anyway ('Creating group with undefined future coordinator hint') and GC election decides. healthcheck_job.schedule: "Next healthcheck scheduled to run in %u hour(s), %u minute(s), %u second(s)"; skip conditions "Not scheduling: %d %d %d %d %d %d"
healthcheck_job.note: healthcheck.cxx job body (f_103ae548, tag 'healthcheck'): on 'Healthcheck timer pop' the job invokes the shared liveness check f_103add58 (the 5-minute-cadence staleness probe also used by the healthcheck record), logs at level 7, and unconditionally reschedules ('Rescheduling next healthcheck', next interval printed as 'Next healthcheck scheduled to run in %u hour(s), %u minute(s), %u second(s)'). Failure path: the job's submit path is permission-gated - a strcmp against the 'SubmitPermission' settings key decides whether a health report may be submitted, tying it to the diagnostics-submit consent model. The watchdog side mirrors the same cadence ('Performing health check' / 'Waiting for next health check' / 'In watchdog thread, performing health check' / 'Watchdog health check callback must be non-null' / 'Invalid watchdog health check frequency') - the watchdog thread calls into the same check on its own timer. Reschedule mechanics (f_103ade20): the 'Next healthcheck scheduled to run in %u hour(s), %u minute(s), %u second(s)' values are derived by magic-constant division of a total-seconds interval held in the healthcheck object's schedule-state members - flags at +0x18b/+0x18c/+0x18d (the six %d of 'Not scheduling' are these state bytes) and a sonosClockGetTime timestamp written at +0x190. The interval is object state, not a config-key read in this function; the x3600/x60 decomposition is compile-time. The function self-chains: it calls itself to re-arm after each run.
resolved_findings: Established: reschedule interval lives in object members {flags +0x18b..+0x18d, last/next time +0x190}; log h/m/s comes from magic-division of total seconds; self-chaining re-arm.
Established: the schedule log and skip-condition pattern are catalogued.
Established: check + failure semantics via member fields {flags +0x18b..+0x18d, last/next}.

timezone_table.feed: http://update-timezone.sonos.com/timezone/timezones.xml: versioned ("Accepted new time zone table; version %u"); fallback "Invalid timezones file, loading default"
timezone_table.note: Apply path decoded (f_1015aaf8): the canonical table lives at /opt/timezones/timezones.xml (registered in the .init path table beside musicservices/musicservices.xml and localsettings.txt). Updating writes the new table to 'timezones.xml' under that directory (open64 O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC), fsyncs and closes it (durable commit), then the table is re-parsed; a malformed table triggers 'Invalid timezones file, loading default' and a copy/open failure logs 'Unable to open (or copy) timezones file'. The running system consumes the table in-process through the TimeZone query layer (TimeZoneForDesiredTime, CurrentTimeZone, GetTimeZone, GetTimeZoneAndRule, GetTimeZoneRule, SetTimeZone - also reachable via the systemTime.getTimeZoneInfo/setTimeZoneInfo API and the AlarmClockTimeZoneChangedEvent), so application is a file rewrite plus in-process re-read rather than an OS tzset. A missing table yields 'no timezone data available (%d)' and 'noTimeZone' state.
resolved_findings: Established: canonical path /opt/timezones/timezones.xml; apply = rewrite+fsync+re-parse with default fallback; consumers go through the TimeZone query layer and the systemTime API; AlarmClockTimeZoneChangedEvent on change.
Established: the TimeZone XML schema, the update feed URL, versioning, and the fallback path are documented.

The poll queries the 'wirelessnetworkstatus' muse resource (tag 'wirelessnetworkstatus'): f_101600f4 reads the health string and rssi from the returned record (health via getter f_10a081ec on the record object +0x200, rssi from +0x220) and fires 'fire event: health %s rssi %d'; the same pair is reported by 'status: health %s rssi %d'. Cancelling watchdog.'). A helper socket endpoint exists ('watchdoghelper', 'Unable to start watchdog helper on port %hu', routes '/watchdog', '/watchdog-legacy', '/watchdogs', '/watchdogcrash'). uri_service_map.resolution: Prefix matching is a static ordered cascade, not a longest-match table: the classifiers (f_1014f48c family and the per-prefix predicate thunks like f_101471f0) run strncmp against literal prefixes in fixed source order and the first hit wins. Specific stems are checked before generic ones by authorial order (e.g. 'x-rincon-playlist:' -> 'x-sonosapi-stream:' -> 'x-rincon-mp3radio://' -> sub-predicate families -> 'x-rincon-cpcontainer:' -> 'x-rincon-buzzer:' -> 'x-rincon-configmode:' in f_1014f48c). Collisions are resolved by including the ':'/'://' terminator in each literal, so 'x-sonos-http:' and 'x-sonosprog-http:' are distinct atoms rather than prefix/substring matches. Openers cascade too: 'Failed to open %s (%d) Trying MMS,RTSP next' shows http->mms->rtsp fallback when the first transport fails. No dynamic registration: every comparison is a literal in .rodata reached by generated predicate functions; nothing walks a writable registry.
resolved_findings: Resolved: first-match ordered strncmp cascade; ':'/'://' terminators make overlapping stems disjoint; transport fallback http->mms->rtsp on open failure; no dynamic registration (all literals).
Established: the URI-prefix -> service-impl map is catalogued.
Established: resolution precedence at the resolver-table boundary - documented.

rincon_didl_fields.description: urn:schemas-rinconnetworks-com:metadata-1-0/|{tiid,radioName,connotation,state,trackGain,chapterNum,chapterCount,linkUrl,isAd}; r:{radioName,streamContent,audioInputIcon,radioShowMd}; upnp:originalTrackNumber; res duration=" attr; classes object.item.audioItem.{podcast,show,audioBook.chapter}; loadFromExtraMd {pszTrackURI,pszExtraMd}; RTrackDIDLLiteMdExtractor; extractMimeTypeFromHttpContentType
rincon_didl_fields.field_semantics: Per-field semantics decoded: 'linkUrl' is emitted only for advertisement content - the tag parser logs 'found isAd in the tags and are setting the linkUrl: %s' so linkUrl carries the ad's click/target URI, and the reverse path parses 'linkUrl=' ('found linkUrl: %s'). 'isAd' is the boolean ad marker that conditions it. 'connotation' carries the station-rating connotation (thumbs-style) seen in the muse key vocabulary. 'trackGain' is the per-track replay gain. action_dispatch_records.description: Per-service action dispatch tables are sorted name-keyed records of stride 12 consumed by a binary-search dispatcher (e.g. f_10307608 ContentDirectory, f_10733b44 AlarmClock). Two record layouts exist: DIRECT {name_ptr, fn_ptr, 0} - used by AVTransport, ContentDirectory, ConnectionManager? no; used by AVTransport, ContentDirectory, DeviceProperties, GroupManagement, GroupRenderingControl, Queue, RenderingControl, VirtualLineIn - the middle word is the handler. VIRTUAL {name_ptr, pmf_voff|1, delta=0} - used by AlarmClock, HTControl, ConnectionManager (both URNs), MusicServices, SystemProperties, ZoneGroupTopology - the middle word is a pointer-to-member-function encoding (low bit set = virtual dispatch at impl-vtable byte offset value&~1, third word is the 'this' delta). The dispatcher then invokes req->v[+0x14] with 0x191 (401) when the name is absent.

Resolved: datatap.cxx (0x10ebb414+) proves the snapshot serialization is XML - root element <SPDIFTap>...</SPDIFTap> wrapping a rolling_data_tap buffer plus a metadata section ("Error: failed to read metadata from buffer!", "Datatap snapshot failed after %zu"). Two HTTP endpoints serve it: /snapshotspdiftap (live snapshot render) and /downloadspdiftap (file download), both in the hidden debug route table at 0x10e76554-0x10e7657c. Tap-manager gate vocabulary (audiotap_manager.cxx 0x10feb6fc+): "Location is not tappable", "Location is already being tapped", "Max number of blocks already being tapped" - the 3-block cap from audiotapmanager is enforced at registration.

Resolved (snapshot payload section order): f_1034308c emits <SPDIFTap>, then open64's the tap backing file, reads the 0x4000-byte metadata head (f_1038689c+f_10387b7c; failure logs 'Error: failed to read metadata from buffer!'), then streams the rolling buffer through sonosBase64Enc {Reset, Update(0x400 chunks into 0x545c buf), Finalize} each chunk written via f_10769df4, bounded by a gettimeofday+timevalAddMs(0x2710)=10s deadline and the 'Datatap snapshot failed after %zu' counter; then close+UNLINK of the tap file (snapshot consumes it), f_10387b04, and </SPDIFTap>. Payload order is therefore {metadata head block, base64 rolling-data stream} under the XML root.

Deepened: 'Location is not tappable' is emitted by the tap-request validator ~f_10d92300 in audiotap_manager.cxx, which walks a block-descriptor array at mgr+0x178 (0xc0-byte stride, capacity mgr+0x240, used-count mgr+0x244) and tests each candidate block via a vtable call (mtctr/bctrl at 0x10d923f8) - so tappability is a per-block virtual predicate on the block object, not a static location table; a successful match stores the tap into a free descriptor slot (idx*0xc0+0xb8) and bumps the used count. There is no compiled tappable-location list for non-SPDIF sources; eligibility is whatever each block class's vfunc returns.

evidence.notes: peers remove reset device from vanished list
invalid system settings → auto factory defaults

factory_reset.mechanics: <PresetNameList val="FactoryDefaults"/> is the settings-side reset verb; after reset the device broadcasts its removal so peers drop it from 'vanished' lists; corrupt system settings auto-trigger a reset
resolved_findings: Resolved: wipe set = the CSRF-posted Factory Reset/Remote factory reset form creates /jffs/factoryReset.txt (marker consumed at boot by the reset path); sonosFactoryResetFull removes the zone from the household (device: %s %s removed from vanish..) and wipes the jffs settings tree; preserves hardware identity/certs (device cert and household key material survive, matching the cert subsystem); LED shows LED_MODE_FACTORY_RESET during wipe; reboot follows the marker-file commit.

Wipe model decoded: the reset handler ~0x105e8b44 (mod_zp log scope) has two paths. SOFT: joins app/run + factoryReset.txt via f_105e674c, ensures the directory via f_1068a70c, writes the literal SOFT into the marker with sonosFileCreate at 0x105e8bd8 (failure logs unable to create factory reset file.), then sync() at 0x105e8c84 - the actual file deletion runs at next boot from the marker, outside anacapad. HARD: calls the imported sonosFactoryResetFull at 0x110995d8 (0x105e8ce4), an extern syscall/IPC stub not contained in this image - the wipe-and-reboot executes in the sibling-daemon/HAL layer, consistent with the multi-daemon boundary (netstartd owns boot-time persistence). The in-binary wipe set is therefore exactly: the SOFT marker write plus the hard-reset IPC; which files survive is decided by the boot-time consumer of app/run/factoryReset.txt, not by anacapad. conf/rdmconfig and conf/rdmlocation literals sit in the same string region with bad rdm location / RDM Config watchdog triggering - the retail-demo config the reset also clears.

Resolved: the boot-time reset chain is fully proven - /sbin/frcheck reads /jffs/app/run/factoryReset.txt (SOFT marker) and polls hal_inputs_get_buttons_state (button-hold detection), returning {0=hard,1=normal,2=soft}; etc/Configure lines 41-51 dispatch: stat!=1 -> sonosledmgrd --fr (reset LED mode), stat==0 -> /wifi/netstartd --hard-reset, stat==2 -> /wifi/netstartd --soft-reset. netstartd exposes FOUR reset levels: {--hard-reset, --soft-reset, --qareset, --qareset-lite} and performs the wipe itself ("mt: factory reset - removing preference", "ssidmgr: factory reset", WIFI_RESET, NS2_STATE_RESET; while reset pending it blocks START_ISLAND/START_OPEN_AP). sonosFactoryResetFull is the anacapad-side import that writes the marker file.

Resolved: the wipe mechanism is partition-level, not a file list - netstartd links libflash.so.1 and the hard path resolves to hal_flash_secure_erase_jffs (flash_secure_erase_whole on the jffs mtd). The flag set is actually four: {--hard-reset,--soft-reset,--qareset,--qareset-lite} plus --preserve-system and the /var/run/stopnetstartd sentinel. netstartd's mode FSM is literal: {IDLE,CHECK_UPDATE,CHECK_UPDATE_PREDELAY,CHECK_UPDATE_DELAY,CHECK_UPDATE_DONE,BEGIN_SETUP,HH_ALIVE,HH_FORWARD,ALIVE,CONTACT,CONFIG_DELAY,COMPLETE_WAIT,CHECK_CONFIG,CHECK_CONFIG_DELAY,CHECK_CONFIG_DONE}. libflash also exports hal_flash_ptable_{read,write}, hal_flash_get_bootsection/bootgeneration, hal_flash_read_fsn, hal_upgrade_{write_partition_platform,compare_ptable,ptable_redundant_config,bytes_in_part,reprogram_flash} - the partition table + dual-boot generation machinery used by the upgrade path.

frcheck tri-state binding proven from shipped /etc/Configure: exit 0 -> netstartd --hard-reset (plus sonosledmgrd --fr LED pattern), exit 2 -> netstartd --soft-reset (plus --fr), exit 1 -> normal boot (no reset, no --fr LED). The boot LED flag /var/run/sonosledmgrd.flash_booting_led is touched before frcheck runs. /jffs/Configure replaces the stock Configure entirely when present (exec chain), and /jffs/system/Configure.dev runs additionally + marks the build dev-unlocked. Kernel modules loaded by Configure: sonos_device.ko, chk.ko, hwevent_queue.ko, audiodev.ko, conditional ir_rcvr.ko, then the Atheros wifi stack {adf,asf,ath_hal,dfs?,ath_driver} + bridge.ko. rmem_max is raised to 262143 and icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts set.

dirObjFavorites vtable mapped (ctor ~0x1037ca04, table base 0x10ec0b08, ~40 slots): +0x0 f_1037e030, +0x24 f_1037ea40 = userradio.d.xml persistence op, +0x30 f_1037f1ac = replication acceptance (deciding whether to accept replicated list / Rejected version %u, schema %u), +0x5c f_1037ee34 = replication receiver (replicating favorites from %s + userradio.xml), +0x2c f_1037b644 = the userradio load path. resolved_findings: Resolved: Secondary linkage broken. Start recovery job is the stereo/satellite bond-monitor predicate - when the HT/satellite link drops, the topology monitor schedules a recovery job that re-establishes the bonded pair via the AddBondedZones path; the FSM is {bonded -> linkage-broken -> recovery-job -> rebonded-or-demoted}; bounded at the job scheduler.

recoverBondedZone FSM decoded via the zonesmonitor vocabulary: RZonesMonitor runs periodic monitorTopology%d polls; on detection it logs Topology monitor: Secondary linkage broken. Start recovery job and fires bondedZonePartnerDefunct -> recoverBondedZone -> refreshSonarState; terminal cleanup emits DefunctDeviceRemovedEvent, and the monitor itself is shut down via Stop topology monitor. VLI-group awareness: Found ZP(%s, %s) in VLI Group gates recovery on whether the defunct partner sits in a virtual-line-in group.

Resolved: recoverBondedZone retry mechanics proven at 0x103558a0-0x103559b4. Retry counter lives at this+0x1aec (incremented per retry, reset to 0 on terminal-status entry); each retry sets deadline = sonosClockGetTime()+10 (seconds) at *(r27). The retry-attempt bound is dynamic: ct compared against (r30>>4)*30 where r30 is an input-derived counter (rlwinm >>4, then *30 via x32-x2) - retries continue while counter < that bound. Status map inside the retry FSM: 0x409 = "Secondary doesn't see same topology" (retryable), 0x40b = "partner is incompatible" (resets counter, logs hard failure); a (status-0x409)>>16 <= 1 test selects the retryable band. Status 0x408 (not settled) drives the separate 10s reconnectHTSatellites retry documented earlier.

Resolved (settle-predicate identity): the topology-settle test inside the recoverBondedZone retry loop is a virtual call - vfunc+0x44 on the object at dp_zpimpl+0x1a80, invoked at 0x10355824-0x10355840 with the debug-name arg 'ValidateBondedState' (0x10e885b0); a false result diverts to the 'topology hasn't settled yet (ct=%u)' retry log at 0x103558d8-0x10355900 with the dynamic bound ct<(derived>>4)*30, while success logs 'recoverBondedZone successful %s; %s sent to secondaries' with member-state strings {(member missing), EQ only}. So the settle conjunction lives in the runtime-installed topology-impl delegate, not in the retry wrapper.

Confirmed boundary: the +0x1a80 member is a shared_ptr copied from a constructor arg - the store at 0x1035ea84 copies {ptr @r29+0, ctrl @r29+4} into zpimpl+0x1a80/+0x1a84 (same runtime-injection pattern as AlarmClock). vfunc+0x44 (ValidateBondedState) therefore resolves against an object whose concrete class is selected at runtime - the residual stands, proven-injected.

lechmere_wss.summary: lechmere.cxx cloud channel: RFC6455 WSS to lechmere.<env>.ws.sonos.com, negotiated subprotocol 'lechmere.<version>' (lechmere-v1 observed), inner TLV header layer ('failed to read lechmere header'), policy-key auth, app-level ping keepalive with 'TOO_MANY_UNACKED_PINGS' disconnect, and a full close-reason taxonomy driving reconnect decisions INNER FRAME FORMAT RECOVERED: 6-byte ASCII header {protocolVersion:2 chars, messageType:2 chars, extendedHeaderLength:2 chars} followed by extended header + payload (min frame len 6, checked cmpli 6 at f_105d539c). Parse errors 'Bad protocol version: %c%c', 'Bad message type: %c%c; %d', 'Bad extended header length: %c%c', 'could not recv extended header; expected %u read %u'. Message type validated via table lookup (f_11098e98 plt veneer); 2-char code registry AA..AK (.data 0x110941a4, 11 ptrs) dispatched via handler table built at f_10ac47fc region. Tunneled UPnP headers inside: 'x-sonos-method:', 'x-sonos-uri:', 'SOAPACTION:', 'X-Sonos-Udn'. Version str 'lechmere.%hhu%n'. AA..AK REGISTRATION DECODED: two consumers of the type table at 0x110941a4 found - f_10bd59xx walks entries 0..10 building records per code (2 lbz reads of each char, two calls to f_1082dfc0, entropy from mftb-based f_10809f0c, 0x100-byte alloc via plt 0x11098418); f_10bd65xx is a second walker (lwzu r28,[r22+4] over the table, counter 0..10) that strlen-checks each code (cmpli 0xf) and inserts it via f_10806d50 seeded with magic 0xc70f6907 (hash-table insert keyed on the 2-char code) building a per-code context record {+0,+4,+8,+c,+1c fields}. The codes are therefore a FIXED set of channel/stream identifiers registered into a keyed dispatch structure - they are not individually special-cased anywhere in code, so per-code semantics are data-driven (opaque map keys), which is the static-analysis ceiling for AA-AK message-type meaning. .got2 0x1108de34 points at the adjacent namespace/verb registry (0x110941d4). TWO-LETTER-CODE LAYER RESOLVED: the same keyed-map machinery used for AA..AK registration (f_10806d50 insert, seed 0xc70f6907) is consumed by f_1082dfc0 lookups in [Mm] ingestMigrationDataIntoBitFieldAry (0x10bd65xx-0x10bd6axx): migration/patch data is parsed as two-character tokens, each token hash-mapped to a field-id (<0xa, cmplwi 0xa) which sets bit 1<<fieldId in a bitfield array at ctx+0x98. So the two-letter-code alphabet is a shared field/channel registry: message-type codes (AA..AK) and migration field codes live in the same class of keyed dispatch structure. REGISTRATION LOOP FULLY DECODED (0x10bd65a4): the walker counter is bound at 0xa - only TEN codes (AA..AJ) are registered, each into a 0x24-byte record {code-str, len, loop-index at +0x1c} hash-inserted via f_10806d50/seed 0xc70f6907 then map-inserted via f_10bd6ec4; failures unwind through f_10807034 deletes. AA..AJ are the ten location-settings MIGRATION FIELD ids (bit positions 0-9 in ctx+0x98 bitfield); AK, the 11th table entry, is not a migration field - it belongs to a different channel role. Component tags recovered in the adjacent code: [Mg] settings manager, [Mm] locSetMigMgr migration manager (migrationmanager.cxx, keys __migration_data, __location_summation, _settings.json), [Pc] patch-completion ingest ([Pc] completePatchAttributeIngest() type mismatch [%s|%s|%u] vT[%d] aT[%d]), [Rq] request authz (isAuthorizedForNamespace, subvert-read/write guards), [Gp] group settings, [Vf] ValidationFailureMsg. NOTE: the 'uuuuubtnufr' table at 0x10e88fd4 is NOT a type map - it is a JSON escape table (control bytes -> \u or named \b\t\n\f\r) used by the attribute JSON emitter at 0x10a01xxx.; websocket permessage-deflate negotiation params {server_max_window_bits,client_max_window_bits,server_no_context_takeover,client_no_context_takeover} + parser errors 'unexpected parameter encountered'/'unexpected token encountered'

lechmere_wss.clock: 'could note use Date header for trusted clock seed: %s': the HTTP 101 Date: response seeds the trusted clock
lechmere_wss.auth_fields: policy-key record fields: userId, policyKey, museVersion
lechmere_wss.reader_dispatch: the reader returns a 0..10 code dispatched through a PIC jump table at 0x10ef12c8 in the ws-client read loop f_1059c088. Cases: 0-1 EVENT-class frames ('Unexpected TYPE EVENT' logged; loop continues); 2 HTTP-tunnel frame ('support for HTTP message dropped': the HTTP-over-lechmere tunnel is deprecated/dropped in this build on the OUTBOUND client path; the tunneled-UPnP pseudo-headers seen elsewhere belong to the server side /api/v1/websocket); 3 the real inbound command frame (payload queued at ctx+0x1f8, timestamped +0x310); 4 -> f_1070d01c (registration/ack-class frame); 5 SET_CONFIG-class (registration write; errors 'SET_CONFIG failed to read'/'failed to send registration'); 6 CHECK_CONFIG-class ('CHECK_CONFIG failed to return registration'); 7 'Unrecognized message type' (reader reject); 8 'read timeout'; 9 'read error'; 10 clean end-of-frame continue.

wire_framing.header: binary frame: protocol version (2 chars) + message type (2 chars) + extended-header length + optional extended header ("Bad protocol version: %c%c","Bad message type: %c%c; %d","Bad extended header length: %c%c","could not recv extended header; expected %u read %u")
wire_framing.negotiation: WS subprotocol negotiation; "protocol version negotiation failed due to unknown version (%s)"; server Date: header seeds the trusted clock ("could not use Date header for trusted clock seed")
wire_framing.conn_event: muse event "lechmereConnection" {status,protocolVer,reason,retry,uptimeMs} with states transport/closed/failed/opened; close logged "Close code (%d) %s"; thread/log "lechmere.%hhu%n"

Returning saved pattern'
led_engine.default_patterns: resumeDefaultLEDPattern maps R_LED_* to patterns: R_LED_BROKEN_DEVICE, R_LED_JOIN_HH, R_LED_BEGIN_SETUP_MODE, R_LED_IN_SETUP_MODE, R_LED_MUTED, R_LED_AUDIO_OFF, R_LED_PLAYING, R_LED_HHID (+ WAC/WAC_TIMEOUT/UPGRADE/etc. in the R_LED family)
led_engine.unresolved: pattern priority arbitration rules, the SetLEDState vs. override stack, which patterns correspond to which R_LED codes
resolved_findings: Resolved: priority model decoded - each request carries LedPatternPriorityLevel; applyLEDMode compares it against m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel and applies only on win; flash-mode stashes the active pattern for led_set_resumeDefaultLedPattern(Flash) restore; HAL path is led_get_hal_token + hal_led_{open,close,write,flash,brightness,diag}.

Arbitration model decoded: applyLEDModeLocked (f_10c8f06c, leds_zp log scope) is the single apply point. Its apply-time log names the full arbitration state: m_fLedBrightness, m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel (the queued request priority), m_lastClr, m_fade_effect, m_lLEDFlags, m_bIsInExclusiveBTMode, m_bIsBTConnected, m_bHasStatusLED, m_bHasMuteLED, useOnlyStatusLED. The eligibility gate f_10c8ee44 drops applies with two explicit reject reasons: not-ready/flag state (ignoring apply LED mode. m_bReady=%d, m_lLEDFlags=0x%llx) and the suspend bypass flag (ignoring apply LED mode due to suspend bypass flag). Pattern selection is therefore a request-with-priority model - setters queue {R_LED_code, priority} into m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel and the locked apply reconciles against flags, BT exclusivity, and LED hardware presence. R_LED code to pattern binding runs through set_pattern_for_mode(LED_MODE_*) calls (modes: FACTORY_RESET, BOOTING, JOIN_HH, JOIN_HH_OPEN, BYPASS_BLOCKED, BYPASS, CLONE_CHECK_FAIL) plus applyLEDMode R_LED_* codes (WAITING_TO_PAUSE, PLAYING, WARN, DEMO_MODE, DEMO_CONFIGURE_IR, HHID, BROKEN_DEVICE, JOIN_HH).

Resolved: the R_LED_* priority ordering is the sequential test order in applyLEDMode (f_10c918a0) - first matching flag wins, so highest-to-lowest: DEMO_CONFIGURE_IR > UPGRADE > BROKEN_DEVICE > BEGIN_SETUP_MODE > JOIN_HH_OPEN > JOIN_HH > IN_SETUP_MODE > BREAK_POP > WAC > WAC_TIMEOUT > SHUTDOWN > !HHID (no-household pattern) > TRANSFER_REGISTRATION > CONTROL_FEEDBACK > IDENTIFY_PLAYER > AUDIO_OFF > MUTED > FAULT > WAITING_TO_PLAY > WAITING_TO_PAUSE > PLAYING > HHID (default). The restore path resumeDefaultLEDPattern re-applies the subset {BROKEN_DEVICE, JOIN_HH, BEGIN_SETUP_MODE, IN_SETUP_MODE, MUTED, AUDIO_OFF, PLAYING, HHID} in the same precedence; 'unknown restore pattern' is the fallthrough. User SetLEDState toggles ride a separate on/off flag outside this stack (applyLEDModeLocked logs m_lLEDFlags + m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel; 'ignoring apply LED mode' when !m_bReady).

Literal block at 0x10e75434 proven to be the diagnostic-collection file manifest: the 21 /opt/log/anacapa.*.log paths sit contiguous with /jffs/upgrade_prev.log, /jffs/upgrade_tmp_prev.log, /jffs/watchdog.dmesg, /jffs/watchdog.log and the sibling-daemon logs (chronyd, dropbear, ledmgr.debug, netstartd, ...) - i.e. the set of files a diagnostic submission tars up. IPC framing decoded (ipc_msg.cxx, reader loop ~0x105d3954 under module ipc): the channel is a 3-field binary header read by ReadIPCHeader (0x11098588) followed by a bounded payload - the length check cmplwi 0x800 at 0x105d39bc rejects frames over 0x800 bytes, and malformed frames log Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d) with the three header fields. Body is then read() and dispatched; the loop is lock-guarded (f_10988558/f_10988984 pair). Connection lifecycle literals: IPC established for %s, IPC closed for %s, IPC timeout occurred, attempting reconnect for %s (retries=%u), performReset performing IPC reconnect for %s, Deferring IPC reconnect for %s - the select-thread registers selthrd.RIPCHandler.reset/.data handler pair. netstartd message vocabulary visible in the same region: Disabling networking, Enabling networking, Signaling start/end of network connectivity test, and the outbound IPC message to netstartd to notify about satellite addition.
