Resolved: the shared IPC wire format is proven from libsonosutils.so.1 (the lib both ends link). SendIPCMessageWithData writes a 12-byte outer header {w0=0xc outer-header-size, w1=1 (protocol class/version), w2=innerLen=payloadLen+4} followed by the inner record {w3=arg4 message-type/code, payload bytes}; SendIPCMessage (no-data variant) writes {0xc,1,4,arg4} with no payload. ReadIPCHeader reads 12 bytes, requires w0>=0xc (drains w0-0xc extra header bytes if larger), returns {0=ok,-9=bad args,-0xa=short/read-fail}; payload reads are caller-side. So the wire layout is [outer{sz=0xc,cls=1,innerLen}][{msgType}{data}] - the anacapad-side 'IPC message received (%d %d %d)' logs the outer triple and the msgType rides as the first payload word. Total bound from SendIPCMessageWithData: payloadLen < 0x800.

Resolved: per-msgType semantics on the netstartd side - the NS2_MSG_* numeric opcodes are proven ({0=KEEP_ALIVE..0x17=REGISTRATION_KEY}, see bin_netstartd) so the msgType field of the IPC envelope indexes this 24-entry vocabulary; the peer is driven through the NS2_STATE_* FSM (18 states, per-state handler slots in the .data.rel.ro table)

Daemon supervision layer recovered from shipped run* scripts in /etc: every daemon runs under a wrapper that gates on a /var/run/stop<daemon> flag (stopnetstartd, stopmdns, stopsddp, stopledmgrd, stopanacapa) and logs restarts via trackrestart appending date lines to /var/run/<daemon>.start (netstartd, sddpd, sonosledmgrd, anacapa, dropbear). runledmgrd additionally does stale-pid recovery: if /var/run/sonosledmgrd.pid exists without a live process it logs 'LED Manager PID %s is stale. Likely caused by an abnormal exit' (syslog pri 3) to /opt/log/sonosledmgrd.log then restarts. sddpd accepts a /jffs/dev_sddp.conf override of /etc/sddp.conf (-c flag). waitfordns() blocks daemons until /var/run/waitforip clears and resolv.conf has a nameserver. rundiagprocessd launches the diagprocessd fifo loop.

Resolved (IPC header semantics via shipped libsonosutils.so.1): the shared IPC frame is {u32 hdr_len=0xc, u32 version=1, u32 body_len, u32 msg_id, payload[]} - proven in SendIPCMessageWithData (lib @0x1658): writes {0xc,1,data_len+4,msg_id} then payload; ctx+0x70 is the socket fd, payload cap cmplwi 0x800 (returns -9 over 0x800, -1 on dead fd). ReadIPCHeader (@0x1508) reads 0xc bytes, rejects if buf[0] <= 0xb (ret -10) or arg bufsz <= 0xb (ret -9), then reads buf[0]-12 trailing header bytes in 0x40-byte __read_chk chunks - buf[0] is the header-block length, so the msg_id word + body are read by the caller per words[2]=body_len. The earlier '{type,length,seq}' guess is corrected: the 3 fixed words are {hdr_len,version,body_len} and 'Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d)' prints those three.

Resolved (anacapad->netstartd msg-id vocabulary + payload grammars, from shipped /wifi/netstartd): the IPC handler f_1000886c dispatches msg_id via a 0x2a-entry self-relative jump table at 0x1002f6f4 (ids 0x00-0x29; default arm 0x10008990 silently drops 0,13-17,25,31-38,40). Wire payload sits at msg+0x10 with body_len (u32be @+8) == payload_len+4 checked per arm. Map: 1='anacapa hello' (full subsystem re-init sequence), 2='anacapa byebye' (logs byebye then re-runs init), 3=small command (body 0x8, payload word 4), 4/5='Entering WAC open mode', 6=netsettings push: memcpy 0x69-byte blob msg+0x10 -> staged @0x1005543e (id u32be @+0x21, string @+0x25), 7=0x44-byte blob -> 0x100555e0 (PSK record), 8=0x25-byte blob -> 0x100557e0 (37B, Muse HHID), 9=commit: copies {msg+0x10->0x100551e0 (33B), msg+0x25->0x10055624 (65B)} and moves staged blobs into active slots, 10/11/12='Deferring WAC timeout' variants, 18='Anacapa triggering joinhh' (household join), 19='join cancel', 20=0x6c8-byte payload -> f_10013da4 (large config/scan blob), 21='Disabling wifi for start of test', 22/23/24/26='Enabling wifi for end of test' family, 27/28=disable-for-test family, 29='MeshDisable: new=%d' + ath0 scangetresults, 30=Muse HHID resend + match check, 39=SonosNet frequency set ('setting SonosNet frequency to %u in %u.%u seconds', WifiFuncsIsFreqSupported gate), 41=SonosNet enable/disable ('SonosNet already %s'). Staging globals {0x1005543e:105B, 0x100555e0:68B, 0x100557e0:37B} are memset on IPC reset (f_10008714), which also clears connected flag 0x10050104 and unlinks netsettings_check.txt.

Resolved: the per-route schema encoding for verb routes is a paired literal - URI template + comma-separated "param,param,...,verb" key (trueplay table @0x10e83240 demonstrates: v1/players/{playerId}/trueplay/discovery <-> "playerId,trueplay,detectSpeakers"). The brace params in the URI are the request fields; the comma list is {named params..., handler verb} - so per-route input schemas are partially recoverable from the literal pair even where the payload field names live in the request schema objects.

Deepened (param-literal census): of 532 'v1/' route templates in the rodata spec pool, 315 carry an adjacent comma-separated param-list literal (the {URI, params..,verb} pair) - e.g. 'playerId,trueplay,detectSpeakers' for trueplay/discovery. The remaining ~217 have no param-list literal; their bodies are either parameter-free (path-template args only) or carry schema defined elsewhere. Examples of no-param routes: audioClip, authorization/{invite,redeem,authorizeDevice,authenticateClient}, diagnostics/*, effectiveSettings, groupVolume, favorites, groups/{set,modify}GroupMembers, catalog/id/{objectId}.

Resolved: iterator split per extension family - ASX uses '<ref href="' + 'entryref' element scan (f_10461e04); WPL iterates 'ref'/'entryref' elements (f_10462c80 also hosts iterateM3UPlayList); PLS (f_10463164) fetches via the shared HTTP dataio (f_10545064 client + f_10546520 GET with 'Redirect to %s' handling), tokenizes lines CR/LF-terminated with '\' escapes and a 0x41f-byte bound (f_104611c8), then per line runs the 'x-file-cifs://' strncasecmp / inline 'http' prefix test before enqueue. The PLS key strings FileN=/TitleN=/LengthN=/NumberOfEntries have no rodata literals - URIs are extracted positionally from each line, not via INI-style key match.

Resolved: PLS line semantics fully decoded (f_104611c8): stream line loop tokenizes on CR/LF into a 0x41f-bounded token buffer, converts every backslash to slash (0x5c->0x2f @0x10461328/0x104613e8), trims whitespace, then routes per line through f_10461048: lines matching isKnownUriScheme f_10147bf4 ({x-file-cifs://, x-rincon-mp3radio://, mms://, rtsp://, aac://, x-sonosprog*} prefix ladder + helpers) submit via f_10460a50; lines failing the scheme test go to f_10460c0c which treats them as filesystem paths - f_1010a724 tests for a "//" UNC prefix (post-conversion \\server\share), requires a second "/" beyond position 2, then wraps the whole line into an x-file-cifs: URI (strlcpy "x-file-cifs:" + f_10c3a258 append) and submits; all other lines (FileN=, TitleN=, LengthN=, NumberOfEntries=, [playlist] section headers) are dropped - the PLS key structure is ignored entirely.

qplay_protocol.summary: Tencent QPlay support: /QPlay/Control SOAP endpoint (no matching /QPlay/Event route: the only service missing its event pair), a QPlayAuth action taking Seed/Code/MID/DID arguments (seed→code auth handshake: controller sends Seed, device answers with a Code computed from MID machine-id and DID device-id), a shared-T QPlay mode with context restrictions ('Calling updateSharedTQPlayMode in bad context!'), compile flag #QPLAY_SUPPORT#, and the device-description capability <qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability>QPlay:2</qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability>
qplay_protocol.unresolved: the post-auth control channel (UDP keepalive/position reports in public QPlay docs), how MID/DID are generated, and the replay/validity rules on Seed
qplay_protocol.soap: /QPlay/Control registered; QPlayAuth dispatch site 0x1073a4f0 does strcmp on the action name then calls vtable+0x14/+0x38 on the action object; sibling function at 0x1073a5d0 initializes string-arg records for Seed (via arg-parser f_1056157c), then Code, MID, DID
qplay_protocol.auth_args: QPlayAuth args: Seed (in), Code, MID, DID: matches the public QPlay auth scheme where the speaker derives an auth code from a controller-supplied seed bound to its IDs
todo: Residual: the external-name meaning of MID "62800021" (a registered partner/model identifier) and which identity field singleton+0xcc holds (device serial/household number) - both derivations are fully proven; only the domain naming is external.
resolved_findings: Resolved: QPlayAuth (Seed->{Code,MID,DID}) is the ENTIRE QPlay surface - impl f_104666b4 computes the auth values then returns 0 unconditionally with no session state and no event. No control/listen channel exists. Marking QPlay advertisement+handshake-only.

In-binary QPlay surface fully bounded: (1) device-description capability qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability emitted as QPlay:2 but gated by the per-model #QPLAY_SUPPORT# template token (device-description template block at 0x10ef8xxx), (2) /QPlay/Control SOAP endpoint with the single QPlayAuth{Seed in; Code,MID,DID out} action - dispatch 0x1073a4f0, arg records built at 0x1073a5d0, (3) shared-T QPlay as a transport mode on the http streamer: updateSharedTQPlayMode is called from the segment-fetch path (adjacent to resetSegmentFetchErrors/canFetchSegment error-budget logic and entering pauseTransition) and rejects calls from a bad streamer context. No dedicated QPlay wire codec, opcode table, or separate control channel exists in this image - after QPlayAuth the controller drives playback through the ordinary AVTransport/queue machinery in shared-T mode.

Resolved: QPlay is a first-class UPnP service - /QPlay/Control appears in the master control/event URL table @0x10e76060 (between /ZoneGroupTopology/Control and /MediaServer/ConnectionManager/Control), and the device description advertises <qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability>QPlay:2</qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability> plus a #QPLAY_SUPPORT# template token. QPlayAuth is a literal action/state-variable name @0x10f11d58. QPlay is the only advertised service with NO matching /QPlay/Event route.

Seed/Code buffer contract pinned from the exec handler: Seed parse cap 0x80, Code/MID/DID out caps {0x80,0x15,0x15}; the transform runs inside impl->v[+0x08] on the req member object (see services/QPlay record).

QPlayAuth value derivations proven: MID is the compile-time constant "62800021" (getter f_106453a8 returns literal 0x10efc7a0; strlcpy into out, cap 0x15). DID = snprintf "%u" of member +0xcc on the singleton @0x110b8150 (getter chain f_106454a8 -> f_1090ad44 getInstance -> f_10908350 reads +0xcc). Code = RserializeData(MD5(Seed || key16)) where key16 is the 16 bytes at 0x10efc7ac (53 6f 6e 6f 73 03 11 19 88 09 10 17 1e 22 ff ff) - hash type proven MD5 via libsonoscrypto ZZ0062 type-2 dispatch (type1=SHA256,2=MD5,3=SHA1).

scrobbler.summary: Audioscrobbler/Last.fm submission client implementing protocol 1.2 over raw sockets: GET handshake to post.audioscrobbler.com, form-encoded scrobble POSTs, BADTIME Date-header recovery, OK-response check; also embeds ws.audioscrobbler.com/2.0 for the newer API; last.fm REST auth: method 'auth.getMobileSession' + signed '&api_sig=' (md5 constants present); last.fm API key 49f9477923cc3ab8ed90029f6e7e1d9f; timing telemetry '%s failed, ret = %hu, tvStart = %d s %d us, m_tvConnectDone = %d s %d us, m_tvDone = ...'
anchors: BADTIME -- stealing time from Date: header
scrobbler.handshake: GET /?hs=true&p=1.2&c= HTTP/1.1 to http://post.audioscrobbler.com/ (c= = client id); service token 'lastfm'; on BADTIME response it logs 'BADTIME -- stealing time from Date: header' and resyncs clock from the HTTP Date: response header
scrobbler.submission: Raw 'POST %s HTTP/1.1' + HOST/CONNECTION: close/CONTENT-TYPE: application/x-www-form-urlencoded/CONTENT-LENGTH template; body fields 's=' (session from handshake) then per-track '&a[0]=' artist '&t[0]=' title '&i[0]=' timestamp '&o[0]=' source '&r[0]=&l[0]=' rating+length '&b[0]=' album '&n[0]=' tracknumber '&m[0]=' MBID: the classic submissions-protocol array
scrobbler.transport: Owns its own connection ('scrobbling openConnection to %s %s failed'), not the shared HTTP client; checks 'OK' status line ('Scrobbling failed. Status returned: %s')

resolved_findings: Resolved: Audioscrobbler 1.2 protocol - handshake GET http://post.audioscrobbler.com/?hs=true&p=1.2&c=<client> then form-urlencoded POSTs with per-track params incl &r[0]=(rating) and &l[0]=(length); clock trust via BADTIME stealing from Date header; trigger rides the same play-state transitions as TrackPlayRecorder.

Protocol details decoded (literal block at 0x10ee4cxx-0x10ee4exx): handshake GET /?hs=true&p=1.2&c=%s&v=%s&u=%s&t=%s&a=%s to post.audioscrobbler.com over a raw socket (CONNECTION: close), BADTIME recovery steals the Date: response header. Submissions are single form-encoded POSTs carrying the Audioscrobbler 1.2 indexed field set &b[0]=(album) &n[0]=(track-number) &m[0]=(musicbrainz id) &a[0]=(artist) &t[0]=(track) &i[0]=(timestamp) &o[0]=(source) &r[0]=(rating) &l[0]=(length). The submission body at ~0x105236c8 pulls each field through the f_1056fb1c settings-getter family (20+ consecutive calls) then emits scrobbling submission %s / scrobbling openConnection to %s %s failed / Scrobbling failed. Status returned: %s - fire-and-forget with no retry/queue vocabulary in the image.

Resolved: the scrobble trigger is the play-report submission path in trackplaymonitor (tpm domain) - the sole caller of the submission builder f_105236c8 is f_104cbf1c at 0x104cc454, the same function that logs 'submitting play report for uuid: %s'. The scrobble entry is built with {track obj, stream/service obj, name, elapsedSecs = sonosClockGetTime - playStartTime, 0, flag} and gated by the post-call 'andi. 0x4' flag test at 0x104cc458. So scrobble entries fire on finalized play reports (track end), not on track-start events.

Resolved: the wire protocol is Audioscrobbler/Last.fm submission protocol 1.2 over plain HTTP to http://post.audioscrobbler.com - handshake 'GET /?hs=true&p=1.2&c=<client>&u=<user>&a=<auth-md5>' built piecewise (0x10ee4c38/4c50/4c58), submission 'POST' body carries session 's=' plus per-track arrays &a[0]=artist &t[0]=title &i[0]=timestamp &o[0]=source &r[0]=&l[0]=rating/length &b[0]=album &n[0]=tracknum &m[0]=mbid (f_105236c8); response handling recognizes 'OK'/'BADTIME' and steals the wall-clock from the HTTP Date: header on BADTIME; 'lastfm' (0x10ee4c98) is the account service key.

Resolved: the handshake URL is built by a literal {fmt,value} pointer table @0x10ee4c08 - GET http://post.audioscrobbler.com/?hs=true&p=1.2&c=son&v=1.0&u=<user>&t=<unix %ld>&a=<auth>; wire verbs are "GET %s HTTP/1.1 / HOST: %s:%d / CONNECTION: close". Submission uses POST with per-track params &b[0]= &n[0]= &m[0]= (&u= &t= reused); CONTENT-TYPE application/x-www-form-urlencoded. On a clock-unset device the handshake falls back to BADTIME - "BADTIME -- stealing time from Date: header" reuses the HTTP Date for &t=.

Resolved: the account key feeding the handshake is the literal service id "lastfm" (0x10ee4c98, inside the scrobbler TU right after BADTIME handling) - so &u=/&a= come from the Last.fm service account record (username + stored auth token). Complete submission param set proven: {&b[0]=, &n[0]=, &m[0]=, &a[0]=, &t[0]=, &i[0]=, &o[0]=, &r[0]=&l[0]=} (0x10ee4ccc-0x10ee4df4) - 9 indexed params per Audioscrobbler 1.2 submission, POST with CONTENT-TYPE: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and CONTENT-LENGTH: %zu.

Resolved: the a= auth token is NOT derived inside the scrobbler TU - the only MD5 implementations in the image are the two vendored init/transform functions at 0x10d45570/0x10d45e3c and every caller of the reachable one sits inside the 0x10d0/0x10d4 vendored crypto region (HTTP digest + md5WithRSAEncryption); no call from any scrobbler function (0x1052x). So the handshake token arrives precomputed from the music-accounts getter for the lastfm account

resolved_findings: Resolved: wake path is WoW magic packets - the wakeMissingPlayers timer task (wake missing players type %d time %ld) generates "WoW magic packet for MAC %02X.." per missing secondary ZP and reports "Attempted to wake %zu missing secondary ZP of primary %s (sent WoW to %zu)"; suspend side suspends the cloud queue during snooze/alarm and runs suspendSession over the suspendable-devices list; suspended-room state is tracked per-zone. Wire protocol for suspend broadcast is the chsrc group-state channel (suspend source), bounded at the injected-delegate layer.

Wake path decoded: suspended devices are woken by sending the powerWakeupFromSemiSleep action (literal at 0x10e86c65) with parameters {secondary, role, useCase} and a retry loop bounded by attempts - We timed out on %zu devices after %u attempts is the give-up path. Timing telemetry uses msTTM/msDRP millisecond counters with %d:%d.%06d timestamps. The wake action rides the inprocess-events observer bus (subject.h/inprocess-events PlaybackEvent; Registering "%s" observer "%s". Total observers: %zu; ie-obs domain with %s-%s naming). Gating flags confirmed adjacent: enableSemiSleep + enableHTSourceSleep (HT source gets a separate sleep opt-in). Wake is thus an outbound RPC to each suspended member, not a broadcast - per-device role/useCase arguments and per-device timeout accounting.

Resolved: the wakeup transport is the local muse/in-process command surface, not UPnP SOAP - the verb 'powerWakeupFromSemiSleep' is embedded in a verb-table record at rodata 0x10e86c4c-0x10e86c7c (name string immediately follows its handler-pointer block; the 'L' prefix marks the local power service namespace, matching the R_/L_ remote/local convention in muse op names). No UPnP action name or wake-on-LAN shim exists for it in this image.

Resolved: the suspend/shutdown reason enum is literal @0x10ef3368+: {APICall, BluetoothConnection, PartnerDisappeared, Recovery, UserSuspend, UserShutdown, APIShutdown, CriticalShutdown, UnknownShutdown} - 9 reasons covering API-driven, BT-disconnect, partner-loss, recovery, user, and critical shutdown paths. Suspend markings also surfaced: "Suspend and reset" (SNTP path), Spotify eSDK op table includes suspendSession among {start, suspendSession, startAudio, pauseAudio, stopAudio, playModesChanged} (0x10ea5420+).

Resolved (member-suspended flag provenance): 'suspended' is a wire-carried group-info doc member, not a locally-computed FSM transition. The producer-side serializer f_101fabdc emits {_objectType, suspended} members with the flag byte read from member-record+8 (0x101fac24-0x101fac40, emit helper f_109d14e0); receiver side parses it into the group-info record at +0x1e, tested at 0x106872b8 where nonzero triggers 'Found Suspended Rooms While Processing %s Group Info' (f_1068712c, then a vfunc+0x10 call with 'VLI' arg at 0x106872cc). So a zone's suspended bit originates in the coordinator's topology document and propagates as doc data; locally it is only parsed and consumed.

Producer chain proven (0x102cbb18): the suspended member byte = (getSuspendState(member->sub+0x1c) == 2) via f_10a0732c - reads the member suspend-FSM state word at sub+0x164, gated on member flag +0x2918 (skip if unset); result stored as the record byte serialized as suspended. So state enum value 2 is the suspended state.

Suspend-FSM state writer located (f_10a07354+): ctor seeds +0x164=0 (idle); the parser path at 0x10a074d4 isel-selects state {1,2} off the parsed wire byte at r1+0x18 - byte value >=0x31 (ASCII '1') maps to 2 (suspended), else 1. So the vocabulary is {0=idle/unset, 1=awake-parsed (flag byte <'1'), 2=suspended}; the wire byte driving it is the group-info doc suspended flag member+8 parsed through the f_10c39xx record helpers.

resolved_findings: Resolved: replication transport = the household HTTPS channel carrying per-setting transfers (replicateOne from %s to %s setting %u version %u); the accept predicate is the version+format negotiation "deciding whether to accept replicated list from: %s; ver: %u format: %u" - accept when version is newer AND format is compatible, else denylist the setting on badFormat/badEncoding; player-level quarantine enforces admission over HTTPS.

Transport and accept predicate decoded (literal block 0x10efd3xx-0x10efd5xx): replicateOne is a pull-model HTTP GET %s%s?id=%u with headers CONNECTION: close, ACCEPT: */*, HOST: %s:%d, USER-AGENT: %s, and X-RINCON-CONTENT-FORMAT: %u carrying the negotiated format version; HTTPS variant formats https://%d.%d.%d.%d:%d. Payloads stream into temp file setrepl.tmp then validate: the failure taxonomy is openStream 0x%08x, filesize bad/unavail, bad version/last update id, denylisted setting %u, badFormat %u denylisting, badEncoding %d denylisting, bad version %u, Cannot open temp file, bad algorithm, signature mismatch - so replicated payloads are signed and version+format checked, and any of {badFormat,badEncoding,bad signature} permanently denylists the setting id. Version bookkeeping via informLocalReplicatedSettingVersion setting %u LUD %s version %u (LUD = LastUpdateDevice); ReplicatedSettingsChangedEvent fires async on accept; Not replicating while unregistered gates the whole path on household registration.

Resolved: the accept ordering in f_10660e58 is fully decoded - accept iff (incoming version > stored version at obj+0x1f0) OR (versions equal AND strcmp(incoming LastUpdateDevice, stored LUD) < 0, i.e. lexicographically smaller LUD wins the tie). version == 0xffffffff (-1 sentinel) skips the newer test and falls straight to the eq/tiebreak branch; eq with a non-smaller LUD rejects. Called from the 'deciding whether to accept replicated list from: %s; ver: %u format: %u' path (0x100c795c) after the version+format handshake.

resolved_findings: Resolved: Starting SNTP server switch sits inside seamless-handoff worker f_10308e48 (chsnk) - after a successful quick/delayed handoff the new source invokes SNTP swap calls f_10497594/f_104973d4/f_10494bf8 and logs Completed SNTP server switch in %dms. No NTP election; the SNTP role follows the group source/coordinator claim.

Server-election rule proven by literal neighborhood: Starting SNTP server switch / Completed SNTP server switch in %dms sit directly inside the seamless coordinator-handoff sequence (Completed seamless handoff wait loop in %dms -> SNTP switch -> setting TXS to %s -> audio source uuid / m_remoteSource / chsnk hint / LSE skip-ahead / CoordChangeAutoStart / newgc / chsnkSync). The household SNTP server is therefore hosted by the group coordinator and transfers to the new GC as a step of the seamless handoff - the election predicate is coordinator role, not a separate vote. The switch is timed like the handoff steps (%dms log), tying clock-master transfer into the audio sync pipeline (LSE/chsnkSync) so group playback scheduling never loses its reference clock during GC changes.

Resolved: the listen port in 'Created SNTP Server, port: %hu clock: %s' (log at 0x104a7880, sntpsrv.cxx) is supplied by a vfunc getter - r29->v[+0x8] on the clock-config object at 0x104a7860 - not an in-image literal; the %hu width proves u16. Socket setup sets SO_REUSEADDR (level 1, opt via immediate path) before bind. Per-stream variant: 'vli sntp port %u' (0x1030d878, vli.cxx) logs a per-vli-transport SNTP port - the SNTP service is instantiated per clock domain, so no single '123' literal exists in the image.

Resolved: the SNTP clock servo (sntppoll.cxx) quality-gate vocabulary is proven - pull rails {Clock pull hit the bottom/top rail}, estimator logs {Current Rate:%d adjustment:%d Target delta ppm:%g, Estimated offset(ms):%g n:%llu}; guards {Time went backward - discard SNTP offset, clock quality suspect (Sdev %f), Slope change detected - bumping slope dispersion}; transitions {Clock transition into PCM, into system time, complete sync reset, Suspend and reset}; server set via "set SNTP server: %d.%d.%d.%d" / "Offset set to %f for server %u.%u.%u.%u:%d"; retry cadence "SNTP request failed, will retry" / "SNTP success after %u failures".

Resolved: the servo constants are literal f32 in .rodata at 0x10ed4b30-0x10ed4b4c - pull rails at +/-10.0 ('Clock pull hit the bottom/top rail' compare against this->rate before clamp), ppm scaling via 1000000.0f, ms scaling via 1000.0f, gate constants {0.25f, 0.01f, 0.05f} (Sdev-quality suspect threshold region). The rail hit path writes this->+0x26c (clamp value) and +0x278 (s16 status).

Resolved: constant bindings inside sntppoll - the pull computation loads {1e6, 0.25, +10.0, -10.0} at 0x1049436c-0x104943c4: offset*gain(0.25) scaled to ppm (1e6), rail-clamped to [-10,+10] with 'Clock pull hit the bottom/top rail.' logs on saturation; 1000.0 at 0x104944e4 scales the 'Estimated offset(ms):%g, n:%llu' report; the pull-rate field obj+0x268 gets 0.01 in the normal arm (0x10496e70) and 0.05 in the 'Clock transition into PCM' arm (0x10496fa8) - i.e. a 5x faster pull during PCM clock transitions; obj+0x238 is the transition flag byte. The 'clock quality suspect. Sdev: %f' reject is gated by an integer counter compare against 0x12c=300 (0x104951b8-0x104951d0), not a float threshold - the Sdev value at obj+0x18f8 is only reported, and the reject arm zeroes the out double. 'Time went backward, discard SNTP offset' stores the raw offset into +0x23c and returns status 0x80000006

Resolved (+0x18f8 identity): the 'Sdev accumulator' member is a shared_ptr pair at {+0x18f4 ptr, +0x18f8 ctrl} - both store sites (0x103fcf0c-0x103fcf1c, 0x103fd4c0-0x103fd4d0) copy a {ptr,ctrl} pair from a stack slot and bump ctrl+4 (intrusive refcount ++, the lwz/addi/stw pattern at 0x103fcf24-0x103fcf2c when ctrl != 0). The update is a shared-pointer assignment of the current sample-set object on each servo sample intake - not a periodic cadence field. The read at 0x103fae88 dereferences the ctrl word for a null check.

resolved_findings: Resolved: speaker-takeover = RSpotifyPlayback.BecomeActiveDevice triggers the generic coordinator-delegation sequence: delegate to %s builds the member list, logs delegating. / delegating. isPlaying set to %d, then delegation. Resetting track queue info on the target; guards are delegate to oneself (self-short-circuit) and delegation target %s not primary (rejects delegation to a non-primary member). The adaptive-bitrate variant logs delegation for adaptive bitrate stream.

Seamless-delegation sequence decoded: on takeover the receiver issues Seeking to %ims in support of seamless delegation (set seek time to %u ms, byte offset: %zu carries the ms+byte pair), then waits for the eSDK AudioStart callback - Timed out waiting for AudioStart from eSDK during seamless delegation is the budget-exceeded path, and %s failed to become active reports BecomeActiveDevice failure. Track identity is bound via spotify:track:/spotify:episode: URI prefixes (Bogus track URI: %s reject). Events fired: SpotifyDelegationNotification + GroupVolumeChangedEvent + SpotifyMDNSRequest; cert rotation re-publishes mDNS (new cert updating mDNS service [%s]). Layering: esdk_api over esdk_spi with the esdk pump thread (W esdk pump log), NTS callbacks including kSpConnectionNotifyTransmittingData, and R_ServiceBitrate settings {ulow,high} feeding %s changed from %d to %d bitrate transitions.

Context proven: this module is part of the vendored Spotify eSDK (source paths /var/lib/spotify/buildagent/teamcity/work/.../esdk/src/) - the client speaks Mercury/hermes (hermes record: methods {SEND, UNSUB, GETX}, vnd.spotify/mercury-mget-request, hwptp device topics) for Spotify Connect.

Resolved: the AudioStart wait is a poll loop in StreamStart (f_10211d7c): each iteration calls the stream object's v[+0x50] (AudioStart-arrived check), sleeps via f_1098a850 -> usleep(ms*1000) with arg 0xa = 10 ms, then tests the deadline via f_1098ca54 -> timevalGeq(deadline, sonosClockGetTime) where the deadline timeval rides in arg2 of StreamStart. On deadline the 'Timed out waiting for AudioStart from eSDK during seamless delegation' path returns without seeking; the seamless path also computes the seek offset as (stored_pos*1000us + (0x10624dd3 - ticks)) and calls v[+0x64] to seek. The absolute wait budget is the caller-filled deadline value - runtime data, not an in-image constant.

Resolved: the noderx/nodetx wire format is decoded from the serializer/deserializer pair f_1063391c/f_106339d0 - every packet is an 8-byte header + fixed 0x400=1024-byte payload (total 0x408=1032, the receive cap): wire bytes {0-3 u32be packet-id, 4 u8 protocol-version, 5 two packed nibbles (hi->rec+6, lo->rec+5), 6-7 u16be} then payload verbatim. f_106339c0 reads the version byte at wire+4 and the receive loop (0x10638508+) drops packets whose version != local byte this->+0x538 with 'ignore NACK packet with incompatible protocol version: %d'; NACK class = record nibble field ==2 (checked at 0x106386a0-0x106386a8); record+0/+0x438 init -1 before deserialize

Resolved: irconfig.txt grammar proven from the writer (0x102459a0 seq) + shipped file. resolved_findings: Resolved: consolidated - ac_impl implements the action surface (CreateAlarm/UpdateAlarm/DestroyAlarm/ListAlarms/GetTimeNow/GetFormat/GetTimeZone/GetTimeZoneAndRule/GetTimeZoneRule/UpdateDailyIndexRefreshTime), the internals block holds the timer store (sqlite timers+paused_timers tables) and the scheduler (StartTime/Recurrence/RoomUUID/ProgramURI/ProgramMetaData fields); muse_validation is the household alarm-mirror path.

Timer-fire path consolidated (ac_impl.cxx literals 0x10eaacxx-0x10eab5xx): time authority is the {0,1,2,3}.sonostime.pool.ntp.org NTP pool plus NTPTimeOffset persisted in the sysclock_state file (Read "%s" from sysclock_state / corrupt / SYNCED/UNSYNCED / timeDiff: %ld with large-adjustment flag); UTC availability gates firing via UTCTimeAvailableEvent and AlarmClockTimeZoneChangedEvent. Scheduling is DailyIndexRefresh + recalculate alarms, num pa %zu over pending alarms (no pending alarm / skip triggered alarm), with jobs handed to timedjobmgr_ac (Alarm's TJM is not running / Failed to ensure alarm job is scheduled) whose persistence lands in the sqlite timers/paused_timers tables (embedded_sqlite record). Fire path: RunAlarm worker (f_102e17dc) reads the persisted zpAlarm keys {id,eventType,start,dur,mode,fb_buzz,vol,linked,sid} and installs the program URI via f_102da774 with buzzer fallback; ReportAlarmStartedRunning reports state to the GC (RACZonePlayer/acZonePlayer). Guards: Ignoring alarm %u for room %s while in Exclusive BT Mode. Migration: Rhapsody/non-OAuth alarm conversion with x-rincon-buzzer:0 fallback. Alarm XML grammar fields proven: StartTime, Recurrence, ProgramURI, ProgramMetaData, PlayMode, IncludeLinkedZones.

Decoded: Recurrence is a 4-value string enum {ONCE, DAILY, WEEKDAYS, WEEKENDS} - literals at 0x10eaaf70/0x10f084b0/0x10f084d0/0x10f084bc, bound into GOT2 slots 0x1108ddb4-0x1108ddc0 and rodata table 0x10fad484; parsed alongside StartTime/Duration in the alarm record reader (f_10282d20 family). Not an RRULE grammar and not a raw day bitmask on the wire.

Resolved: snooze/group arbitration proven - the coordinator suspends cloud-queue playback during both snooze and alarm windows ("suspending cloud queue during snooze" / "suspending cloud queue during alarm" / "suspending cloud queue" at 0x10eb14bc-0x10eb151c), i.e. the alarm/snooze owner preempts group CQ content on the same channel rather than mixing. The muse alarm-state vocabulary is literal: ALARM_{DISABLED,PENDING,SNOOZED,FIRING} (0x10fac86c+) plus outcome states {DISMISSED, INTERRUPTED} and context types {PLAYER_WITHIN_GROUP, BATTERY_SAVER}; button-event names {PLAY_PAUSE, DPAD_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/SELECT, LONG_PRESS} feed the snooze/dismiss path; event classes {PLAYBACK, HT_PLAYBACK, HT_POWER_STATE, AIRPLAY, AUDIO_CLIP, SPEAKER_DETECTION}.

Resolved: the snooze duration is NOT a firmware constant - the SnoozeAlarm handler (0x106ed1a0+) dispatches as 'SnoozeAlarm' on service urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:AVTransport:1 and pulls 'Duration' plus 'InstanceID' out of the request arguments, so the snooze length is a per-request caller parameter. The muse routes are v1/groups/{groupId}/alarms/snooze and v1/households/{householdId}/groups/{groupId}/alarms/snooze (spec groupId,alarms,snoozeAlarm). The state emit is <r:SnoozeRunning val="...">.

resolved_findings: Resolved: session lifecycle = ctrl (vliCommand {apiKey,operation,position,volume}) -> link establishment through the source-manager group hooks {[groupAdded] configureLocalTransport(VLI),[groupRemoved] configureLocalTransport(null),[startLocalPBAsGM],[stopLocalPBAsGM]} -> sink via the vli transport stream; VliSessionEndedEvt tears down.

Session lifecycle consolidated from the sub-block vocabularies: StartSession (ctrl callback) allocates the VLI group id and mints the x-sonos-vli:<id>:<ch>,<backing-source> URI; SessionStartInfoUpdated pushes metadata; the link worker processes the group info (Starting/Found Suspended Rooms/Finished Processing %s Group Info in %llu us) and links member players (Link player %s to %s group %s ret %d, too many members reject); vlintxsink begins NodeTX transmission (NodeTx configured to handle %s audio qos %d) with retransmit-aware frame scheduling; SuspendSession parks the session (Failed to suspend/resume source, Thread entering state %d desired=%d) while suspended rooms stay linked; StopSession deactivates (deactivating current VL). vli_source_manager registers sources (Error 0x%x registering vli source %d).

Session-op enum recovered (~0x10f044xx): TXST_* transmission-state {UNKNOW(typo in image), CHSRC, LINE_IN, HTA_MESH, VLI, NONE} identifies which transport owns the stream; session ops {START_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START_AUDIO_STREAMING, PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE} are the VLI lifecycle verbs - JOIN/BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE prove the session drives group membership transitions directly.

Resolved: the VLI source-manager thread state field is *(mgr+0x2e0) guarded by mutex +0x150 (vli_source_manager.cxx ~0x106a81d4). Valid stored states {1,2,3} (bound r9=cur-1<=2); requested transitions {2,3,4} (bound r31-2<=2). 'Thread entering state %d (desired=%d)' logs current vs requested; the setter returns (requested==stored). There is no state-name rodata table - the enum values map positionally to the source ops {activate=2, suspend=3, deactivate/stop=4} by call-site order rather than named literals.

Narrowed: the {1,2,3}/{2,3,4} VLI thread-state set plausibly indexes one of the proven RESET/OFFLINE/ONLINE FSM families in enum_tables (0x10fad874, 0x10fad8e8 or 0x10fad930) - the family binding is not statically referenced.

Resolved: VLI control is an event-driven FSM (media_player_vli_ctrl.cxx) - event vocabulary {VliVolumeProcessingCompleteEvent, VliSessionProcessingCompleteEvent, VliTransportAction, AvtHaltActionEvent, AvtVliActionEvent, VolumeSetActionEvent, GroupVolumeSetActionEvent} fired by name through a completion-signal mechanism (cookie + flags, "completion signal timed out"/"signaling completed rc:"); vliType names {AirPlay, bluetooth/Bluetooth, tvproxy/"TV Proxy"}; StartSession rejects unusable/unknown types; protocolInfo "x-sonos-vli:*:audio:*".

Resolved: the VLI source-manager thread state at mgr+0x2e0 is a 3-value lifecycle enum, NOT the RESET/OFFLINE/ONLINE FSM family - all writes decoded: 0x106a9c34 stores 1 under mutex+0x150 then signals (thread start); 0x106a8184 waits on condvar+0x1e0 while state==1 then stores 2 (thread exit/stopped); 0x106ab080 stores 0 (reset/idle) together with clearing +0x2dc/+0x2e4; +0x2e4 is a pending-request slot (stw r31 at 0x106a8248, drained to +0x2e0 at 0x106a852c). So {0=idle,1=running,2=stopped} - it never indexes the proven {RESET..ERROR} tables

resolved_findings: Resolved: merged with mpmgr - actor message format = the mp actor queue carrying typed op messages {play,pause,stop,seek,next,prev,setUri,setMetadata} routed per source through the source facet vtable.

Actor IPC is socket-bound by construction: the target key {uuid, ix, port, ssl, mtls} is a transport endpoint tuple, so actor messages ride per-player TCP/TLS connections (mtls flag selects the mutual-TLS variant) rather than in-process calls - consistent with media players running as separately configured actors (per-player config dir + anacapa_logger.toml, Player%s naming, /localsettings.txt). Backup actors are pure availability fallback: resolution tries the primary actor for a target (found actor for %s), falls back to the registered backup (found backup for %s), and fails with no actor available when neither exists.

Actor resolution vocabulary proven (mpvlictrl/vli_ctrl context): registration MediaPlayer [%s] registered. [%zu] / MediaPlayer [%s] created. [%zu]; target-key validation Invalid MediaPlayer target key provided. Aborting construction + collision check uuid: %s ix: %u port: %u ssl: %u mtls: %u already exists or has overlapping values - the {uuid, ix, port, ssl, mtls} key with uniqueness enforcement; resolution found actor for %s / found backup for %s (actor + backup instance) / target [%s] for type %d resolved to %s / no actor available for %s / unexpected target ID type %d / Actor Filter is null.

Per-player bootstrap proven (media_player_mgr.cxx, mediaplayermanager/mpmgr domains): each media player gets a logger config dir + anacapa_logger.toml (Failed to create logger conf dir for media player %s / Failed to register logger) and a config file (Created MediaPlayer %s config at %s / config already exists at %s), with /localsettings.txt and Player%s naming in the same block.

Resolved: each media player is a separately-managed endpoint bound to a TCP port - "Setting up MediaPlayer for port %u" / "Setup for MediaPlayer on port %u complete" (@0x10e74ac8/0x10e74b00) run inside "Setting up ZonePlayer"; anacapad-side ops target the {uuid,ix,port,ssl,mtls} tuple, so the on-wire envelope is the spawned media-player protocol, outside this binary.

Deepened: the anacapad-side request builder at ~f_103fa434 emits path literal '/players/' together with version token '1.1.0' (0x10ecb328) on the media-player socket, so requests carry an explicit proto-version marker; the spawned player binary itself is not present in this rootfs (only anacapad/anacapactl/sonosledmgrd ship), confirming the per-op wire field layout is genuinely out-of-image.

Eligibility and selection ladder proven: only object.item.audioItem.linein.{homeTheater,airplay,bluetooth} classes trigger autoplay (all routed via x-sonos-vli); per-invocation params logged as %s %s vol: %u useVol: %d includeZones %d plus airplay include zones: %d (AirplayIncludeGroupedEvt). Target selection order: choose autoplay room -> resolve its group coordinator (autoplay could not determine coordinator of %s) -> resolve coordinator AVT control URI (could not determine AVT control URI of coordinator %s) -> build http://%s:%u control URI and dispatch for controlURI [%s] for coordinator [%s]. programURI [%s]. %d - %d. Failure modes: no autoplay target for %s, could not determine control URI of zone %s, Not executing on invisible/node proto incompatible ZP %s, Autoplay command failed ret=%d. The lonely local line-in autoplay %s path handles a single-room source. AutoStop called on unhandled URI %s:%s terminates autoplay when the installed URI is replaced by a non-linein class. vliType RCA names the analog line-in type.

Engaging auto stop, and auto play %s silence threshold %ums for resume; mode transitions logged (mode change %s -> %s). DSP persistence file app/debug/dsp/persistentEQ.xml and a system/dsp_disable gate exist.

Deepened (selection shape proven, no numeric ranking exists): StartAutoplay (f_102e14e0) gates on flag bit 0x1 of member +0x465c, then iterates linked-room candidates via f_102da774, resolving each against the topology object at +0x57c (f_1039561c) and applying via f_102c3a34 when member +0x4654 is set; the loop takes candidates in enumeration order - 'Found %zu linked rooms during StartAutoplay%s' is the count log, 'preventing autoplay because operation is overridden' is an early-out. The configured preference is the AutoplayRoomUUID setting (validated 'RINCON_'-prefix + strlen 0x18 at 0x1035c4a4-0x1035c4f0, logged '%s autoplay room UUID changed to %s'). So priority = configured AutoplayRoomUUID when set, else topology enumeration order - there is no score/weight field in the selection loop.

evidence.notes: export fn: builds .tmp filename, fopen64 w, writes </SavedQueues>, r5 flag selects application/gzip vs text/xml

resolved_findings: Resolved: restore path = savedqueues.rsq documents load via the SavedQueue parser -> per-track <Track URI MD> re-enqueue through the queue engine; curated queues carry Curated="1" flag and are read-only via the playlist browse path.

Curated semantics + restore path decoded: Curated is a queue-level editorial flag surfaced in the Queue LastChange event (<Event xmlns="urn:schemas-sonos-com:metadata-1-0/Queue/"> alongside <QueueOwnerID val>, <QueueID val="%.20s">, <UpdateID val>, <Curated val="...">) and mirrored in the track queue as the curation/curationState fields of playmodelEvent (tqueue.cxx). In savedqueues.rsq it persists as the SavedQueue Curated= attribute; SavedQueue curation string: %s logs its value. Cross-device restore rides settings replication: the file arrives as application/gzip or text/xml, validates against Replicated SavedQueue file is not valid and the version/id rules, promotes through the .tmp rename to file:///jffs/settings/savedqueues.rsq with .d.rsq backup, and runs the SQ:%s object-id + service-id migration (Migrating ObjID=%s SN=%u from SID: %u to %u); the export fn at 0x10478f28 selects gzip vs xml on a flag.

Resolved: the SavedQueue parse ladder (f_1047d408) reads attrs positionally via extractor f_10577db8/f_10577c40: Id, Title, Version (strtol), Curated (extracted to a string, logged as 'SavedQueue curation string: %s'), NumTracks, then '>' close; no literal compare pins Curated to a fixed value in the parse path - the extracted string's predicate is inside a helper. Track lines are <Track URI=".." MD=".."/>.

Resolved: SavedQueue header attr ladder @0x1047c270 - strcmp ladder over {Title,Id,Version,NumTracks,Curated} collects value ptrs into r26/r25/r20/r21/r19; requires Title+Id non-null; Curated (r19) passes verbatim as arg8 into the record-build vfunc v[+0xc] of the factory at *(parser+8) (0x1047c368-0x1047c394). NumTracks goes through paranoid_atoi with "Number of tracks not valid %s" rejection; queue id allocation via f_101472a0 with "Next available queue ID not valid %s".

Resolved: the queue-metadata Event emitter (f_10465b80 loop, stride 0x2574 per queue record) writes <Event xmlns="urn:schemas-sonos-com:metadata-1-0/Queue/"> with <QueueID val="%.20s">, <UpdateID val="%u"/>, <Curated val="B"/> where the Curated value is a flag BYTE at queue+0x52a serialized via the bool formatter (f_10676cb0), then <QueueOwnerID val="%s"/>. So Curated is a boolean attribute, not a multi-value enum - the curation string parser maps it to {0,1}. Full .rsq grammar: <SavedQueues LastUpdateDevice Version Next> / <SavedQueue Id Curated NumTracks> / <Track URI MD> / playlistSummary, gzip-wrapped (application/gzip), files {savedqueues.rsq, savedqueues.rsq.tmp, savedqueues.d.rsq}.

Resolved (curation subtype provenance): the handler ~f_10144a90 parses an inbound muse event where eventType=='curation' carries a 'curationState' string field (default '0', compared against '1') and re-emits it as a 'playmodelEvent'. So the curation subtype is a muse-model state - richer values exist on the event channel (curationState is a string, not the .rsq bool); the wire .rsq grammar collapses it to the Curated bool byte at queue+0x52a.

smb.mount_detail: Kernel-cifs mount layer: option strings 'ver=1,directio,sec=ntlmssp,nounix,' and 'ver=1,directio,' (SMB1 only, NTLMSSP, direct I/O); mount lines 'unc=%s,ip=%d.%d.%d.%d,ro,%sdomain=%s,user=%s,pass=%s' / 'user=guest,pass=' (read-only, optional domain); dialect report 'connected to %s with SMB dialect %x'; failure 'Mounting %s failed, addr = %d.%d.%d.%d, ssp = %d, errno = %d, ret = 0x%08x'. Multi-address trial-mounting with strike counter ('Trial mount found unsupported protocol: %s (strike %d/%d)', 'flagging %s as failed', 'chose random %s from %s'). Credential churn: 'credentials for %s changed; unmounting'/'but share in use'. Idle GC: 'unmounting idle share %s', tryCloseAllUnusedShares job (skipped while shares busy). Mount dirs /tmp/smb/%d_%d + /tmp/smb/tmp%d_%u; 'too many shares mounted'/'mount dir already exists!'; refcounted contexts 'release %s -> num contexts: %zu refcount: %u'; '%s on temporary/unmounted share %d'. share_usage accounting + entry cache ('cache at max capacity', 'loaded %d share entries', 'unable to load cache from file'). 'not http mounting %s as %s' alternate transport.
resolved_findings: Resolved: mount protocol = kernel-cifs mount helper with options {ver=1,directio,sec=ntlmssp,nounix} (SMB1-only, NTLMSSP, direct I/O) plus unc= lines; the directory iterator is resilient (Reopened directory/resume, reattempt=%d on connect failure).

Client implementation proven via the import table: libsmb2.so.1 is linked and the smb2_* API family is imported (smb2_set_password, smb2_read, smb2_closedir, smb2_lazy_opendir, smb2_opendir, smb2_stat, smb2_get_timeout, smb2_destroy_context, smb2_destroy_url, smb2_disconnect_share, smb2_set_version, smb2_parse_url, smb2_connect_share, smb2_open, smb2_fstat, smb2_close, nterror_to_str) - a userspace libsmb2 client alongside the kernel-cifs path. Dialect names SMB2/SMB3 are literals in sharelist.cxx (0x10e89d38), which also emits the <Shares>/<Share><Path>/<Mount> XML and the shareProcStatus/slp/shareproc status fields; remoteSettingIsBetter drives share-list conflict resolution. The two stacks split by purpose: kernel mounts serve streamed playback (x-file-cifs:*:* in the protocolInfo caps); libsmb2 serves the indexer/sharelist enumeration where SMB2/3 dialect negotiation matters.
smb.summary: dual SMB client stack: kernel CIFS mounts (ver=1 SMB1, sec=ntlmssp, directio, guest fallback) under /tmp/smb for queue playback of x-file-cifs URIs, plus the libsmb2.so.1 userspace client (smb2_connect_share/opendir/read/stat/set_version family) used by sharelist.cxx for SMB2/SMB3 dialects; resilient directory iterator with reconnect + fast-forward resume

signal_source.name: signal/tone source
signal_source.summary: roomDetection chirp signalling: the muse routes v1/players/{playerId}/roomDetection/chirp (startSignalling) and v1/players/{playerId}/roomDetection/chirp/{playId} (stopSignalling) drive a single-instance audio signal player that emits the ultrasonic chirp on a selectable channelNumber; guards: invalid playId, failed to stop signal, incorrect playId, nothing is currently playing, only one signal can run at any given time, invalid channel, could not create an audio stream, disallowed by policy
resolved_findings: Resolved: the generator is the built-in signal/noise source feeding the audio pipeline test paths; consumer = the DSP/test harness behind the /testpoint and diag surface.

Signal source identified by the adjacent muse route literals: startSignal/stopSignal map to the roomDetection chirp resource ({playerId,roomDetection,startSignalling} verb and the playId-scoped stopSignalling), so the signal is the ultrasonic room-detection chirp, not a generic test tone. Parameters proven: playId (per-signal instance id enforced on stop via incorrect playId) and channelNumber (output channel selector, invalid channel reject). Concurrency is single-shot: only one signal can run at any given time. Policy gate: disallowed by policy. Stream allocation: could not create an audio stream. This is the emit side of the chirp_stack subsystem (sonos-cdma profile, startSignalling/stopSignalling verbs, ERROR_ROOM_DETECTION_SIGNALLING_{FAILED,BUSY}).

stream_fetcher.name: stream playlist fetcher (HLS/radio)
stream_fetcher.summary: notifyFrame ty:%d ln:%zu so:%zu ns:%zu f:%u ctx:%u:%u:%llu; getContentKey (encrypted HLS); "New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d" adaptive switch; playlist FSM {"Timed out looking for playlist","Playlist failure with no time to recover (%ld buffer)","fetch empty","Too many empty playlists and no audio left"/"(still %ldms ahead)","Switching source due to empty playlists","end of static list","Unable to select another DS"/"waiting to fetch new playlist"}; "Startup ahead: %ld"; "URIs for %g seconds, wake up in %d"; "prebuffering %u bytes within %ld msec"; open fmt "open: %s (0x%x) %d len %llu offset %llu"; "stopping decoding while sleeping"; RSpotifyAudioInput/spotifyAudioInput ogg-vorbis VLI framer: 'Final track samples received (last page)','Spotify ogg VLI framer duration: %llds','Invalid samples per second (%ld) in vorbis info','fifo size (%zu) too small for prebuffering %d'; quality-ladder bookkeeping 'update last quality to %u %u %d','add new quality','%s first quality'
resolved_findings: Resolved: merged with abr_engine - DS-selection uses the streamer capability map {accepted_mimes codec ids, ABR ladder} to pick the fetch backend per URI scheme.

DS-selection predicate decoded (literal block 0x10ed3xxx-0x10ed4xxx): each data source is ranked by a happiness test - happy (a > %.2lf): %d %d compares measured fetch rate a against a threshold, with a saturated-buffer override happy (saturated): %d %d; hysteresis via was happy: %d / unhappy: %d counters plus Underruns %u accounting; rate update: a=1 (was %.2lf) resets the estimator. Bitrate switching logs New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d and persists Last estimated bitrate %u (Reset ABR state: start bitrate %u). The failure ladder per DS: fetch failed: 0x%08x (%ld buffer) -> Unable to select another DS, waiting to fetch new playlist -> playlist-level ladder (Timed out looking for playlist, Too many empty playlists, Switching source due to empty playlists rc=%d) -> track-level ladder (track failed 0x%08x, Unable to find playable track, Track failure with no time to recover, Unable to select another DS, fetching new playlist now, Attempting to switch source due to InitFramerForTrackList failure). Prebuffer gate: prebuffering %u bytes within %ld msec; URIs for %g seconds, wake up in %d paces the playlist refresh. Codec filtering uses the mp4a.40. prefix plus a URI version regex /v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(-[a-zA-Z]+)?(\+[a-zA-Z.]+)?([?#/]|$). Status page emits <ABRState Name="ABR State"> with <NodeTXBuffer>%.3lf sec</NodeTXBuffer> and <ProcessRate>%.0lf bps</ProcessRate>.

Resolved: the happy predicate implementation (0x10481b30, logs 'happy (a > %.2lf): %d %d' at 0x10482010 and 'happy (saturated)' sibling) - the estimator a is SPE double math (efdcfs int-to-double, efdmul, efdadd, efddiv around 0x10481f50-0x10481f88) and the threshold is loaded via evldd from the selector object (r31+0x40-class field), NOT a rodata literal - it is a runtime-initialized tunable field. The two trailing %d args are sp-stored counters. So the numeric threshold lives in the object's init config, same boundary class as other tunables.

Corrected (the +0x40 selector member belongs to the ABR bitrate path, and is a running mean not a threshold): the only direct +0x40 write in the TU is the evldd/efdmul/efdadd/efddiv/evstdd update at 0x10481f6c-0x10481f8c in f_10481b30 (the function referencing 'nextBitrate'), computing a cumulative mean m'=(m*(n-1)+x)/n - see abr_engine.

cloud_registration.fsm: cloudregistration.cxx: required fields {sonosId,householdLocationId,dhcpMac,ipAddr,museHHName}: "Missing required information: DHCP Server MAC (%s), Location ID (%s)" defers registration; triggers "Updating cloud registration due to '%s'"/MuseSessionId change/explicit request; "Caching muse cloud registration event %s"; "Network Hash [%s], Muse Household Id [%s]"; cloudRegPollWifiStation monitor job; R_HouseholdLocationID key
resolved_findings: Resolved: FSM = the regdevicecert machine (registration_machine) reconciled with device_registration - cloud paths /product/v2/households/%s/players?action={refresh,complete&token}; states driven by {suspend,expired,success,error,retry-at}.

FSM decoded (cloudregistration.cxx, cloudReg tag): registration waits on the Lechmere WSS connection (Lechmere connection %s, opened) plus required network identity {DHCP Server MAC, Location ID} carried as {dhcpMac, ipAddr, householdLocationId, sonosId, museHHName}; missing fields defer (defer cloud registration due to missing required field(s)). A wifi monitor job (cloudRegPollWifiStation) tracks station state for the dhcpMac input. Events arriving before readiness are cached (Caching muse cloud registration event %s) then flushed; state changes log Updating cloud registration due to %s / Updating cloud registration: %s [%s] with the Network Hash + Muse Household Id pair. Outbound status is serialized by makeMuseCloudRegistrationStatus and fans out locally as SecureRegistrationChangeEvent - the same SecureRegState input the idle-shutdown evaluator and history-gating paths read. This is the muse/cloud half of the device_registration two-phase flow: device-side cert registration first, then household/cloud registration once the WSS channel is up.

Resolved: the registration payload grammar (cloudregistration.cxx @0x10ef10d4+) carries fields {sonosId, householdLocationId, ipAddr, dhcpMac} with a required-field gate "Missing required information: DHCP Server MAC (%s), Location ID (%s)" and "defer cloud registration due to missing required field(s): %s". Payload is cached ("Caching muse cloud registration event %s") and emitted via makeMuseCloudRegistrationStatus on the CloudRegistration path; SecureRegistrationChangeEvent is the related event; a WiFi monitor job (cloudRegPollWifiStation) gates registration on connectivity, and "Network Hash [%s], Muse Household Id [%s]" logs the identity inputs.

Resolved (field order): makeMuseCloudRegistrationStatus (~f_10593274) emits members in literal order {sonosId, householdLocationId, groupId, ipAddr, dhcpMac} - the doc-builder call sequence at 0x10593750-0x10593794 loads the names in that order with a ',' append join. The required-field gate logs 'defer cloud registration due to missing required field(s): %s' and '%s uuid %s was not found' (memcmp-driven check).

Bouncing connection"; backoff "Following backoff schedule, retry in %lld"; msg types: SET_CONFIG (registration send/read), CHECK_CONFIG (registration return), TYPE EVENT ("Unexpected TYPE EVENT"), "support for HTTP message dropped", "Unrecognized message type"; poll loop crt.poll/CRT select failed/ppr read failed/failed to ping/"player request failed: %s"; SwitchingRadiosEvent; museCloudEvtHandler
resolved_findings: Resolved: merged with lechmere_wss - cloudrequest rides the lechmere WSS channel ({version,type,ext-hdr} frames); single channel record covers subscribe + request/response.

Cloud-request path resolved via lechmere_wss: the channel is RFC6455 WSS to lechmere.%s.ws.sonos.com with negotiated subprotocol lechmere.%u, policy-key auth, AA-AK message codes, 73-topic registry (0x14-stride records, dual name pools) - cloudrequest is the request/response sub-record of that channel; local ws endpoints /api/v1/websocket + /websocket/api serve the same event surface.

dev_disc.name: RDevDiscThread/ddt SSDP device discovery
dev_disc.summary: devdiscthr/ddthrd.cxx: rx logging "%s - rx MSEARCH %s from %s:%d (%zd %d %d)", "%s - rx %s ALIVE %s %s %d %u %s (%zd)", "%s - rx %s BYEBYE %s", "%s - rx CDALIVE %s %s %d", "%s - rx CDBYEBYE %s", "rx  QUARANTINE_RECHECK %s"; "%s - %u SSDP messages lost"; zp byebye; "ddt hint:%d"; "Finished working on type %d"; SSDP M-SEARCH response signing: 'Failed to calculate M-SEARCH signature','M-SEARCH signature base64 encoding failed'; header vocabulary: X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD, X-RINCON-PROXY, X-RINCON-REASON, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG, X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION, X-SONOS-DEVICEID, X-SONOS-SESSIONRETRIES, X-SONOS-SESSIONSECONDS, X-SONOS-MDPMODEL, MAN: "ssdp:discover"; socket opts 'Sonos ucast opt error %d %s'/'Sonos mcast opt error %d %s'; notify handler select-threads selthrd.RMSearchNotifyHandler.{reset,data,except,timeout}; 'Failed to setup MSearchNotifyHandler'; manifest gate 'Manifest URL must use HTTPS: %s','Service manifest URI truncated: %s','Failed to load manifest %s (URLs too long?)','OnSuccessStringId'; metrics config rev negotiation 'update the metric report config? existing rev: %d; proposed rev: %d','trying to configure non-existent uploader %s','Failed to add category: %s','reporting xml configuration format error'; orientation enum fragments VERTICAL_ABOVE/VERTICAL_BELOW; also hosts WMP NSS registrar 'urn:microsoft.com:service:X_MS_MediaReceiverRegistrar:1' and DIDL-Lite namespace|element map (DIDL-Lite/item/container/res)
todo: Residual: per-field consumption inside the vfunc+0x4c/+0x64 targets and f_105a4f30 (which members map to household/deviceid/useragent matching) - the handler identity and dispatch shape are proven; per-member use is a per-site read inside the delegate's callees.
resolved_findings: Resolved: message types from the rx parser = the device-discovery frame set; signing input = the household-PSK signed span documented under household_psk_vocabulary.

Discovery message grammar fully enumerated (ddthrd.cxx rx log literals): the RDevDiscThread (devdiscthr) accepts six message types - MSEARCH (rx MSEARCH %s from %s:%d), ALIVE (rx %s ALIVE %s %s %d %u %s), BYEBYE (rx %s BYEBYE %s), CDALIVE (rx CDALIVE %s %s %d - the Sonos change-detected-alive variant), CDBYEBYE, and QUARANTINE_RECHECK (rx QUARANTINE_RECHECK %s). Unknown types log ???? and are dropped (discarding %s type %d); zp byebye marks zone-player departure. Reliability telemetry: %s - %u SSDP messages lost is the drop counter, ddt hint:%d tags worker hints, Finished working on type %d closes each batch. Message-type id is the %d in the per-type logs.

Field sources proven from the outbound header templates: ALIVE packets carry LOCATION: %s, NT: %s, NTS: ssdp:alive, SERVER: %s, ST: %s, USN: %s, BOOTID.UPNP.ORG: %s (the boot sequence), CONFIGID.UPNP.ORG: %d, X-RINCON-VARIANT: %u, plus household tags HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO / GROUPINFO.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO / SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG / X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION / X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD / X-SONOS-DEVICEID. The rx log %s - rx %s ALIVE %s %s %d %u %s therefore logs {interface-or-source, ALIVE-variant, location, usn-or-household, configid, bootseq, household-group string} - the numeric pair is configid (%d from CONFIGID.UPNP.ORG) and bootseq (%u from BOOTID.UPNP.ORG); the two %s strings are location and usn. CDALIVE %s %s %d is the slimmed customer-device announce {location, usn, configid}.

Resolved: rx ALIVE arg order at 0x105a54b4 - fmt '%s - rx %s ALIVE %s %s %d %u %s (%zd)' binds {a1: peer-name *(ctx+0x188), a2: transport tag ('SSDP' or 'mDNS' selected at 0x105a5450/54d0), a3: advert rec +0 inline 0x400-byte id string (canonical usn), a4: rec+0x408 = LOCATION: value, a5: rec+0x424 int, a6: rec+0x428 u32, a7: rec+0x420 str, a8: %zd size}. Header parse ladder (0x10555dc0..) maps by name length: USN:(4)->rec+0x404, LOCATION:(9)->+0x408, SERVER:(7)->+0x410, X-RINCON-VARIANT:(17)->strtoul->+0x414, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO:(29)->stack->+0x448, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG:(24)/X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION:(25)->+0x420 region, plus NOTIFY/HTTP//M-SEARCH first-line and NTS ssdp:alive/ssdp:byebye classification; M-SEARCH responses parse {ST:, X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD:(19), X-SONOS-DEVICEID:(17)}.

Resolved: the SSDP advert parser is a strncasecmp ladder in f_10555a54 consuming {HTTP/, CACHE-CONTROL:, SERVER:, HOST:, X-RINCON-VARIANT:, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO:, X-RINCON-REASON:, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG:, X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION:, X-SONOS-DEVICEID:, X-SONOS-SIG:}. Each value goes through extractor f_105551dc into stack slots sp+{0x2c..0x4c}; VARIANT, SERVER, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO take strtol (numeric), HHSECURELOCATION/SIG stay strings, X-RINCON-REASON pairs with an inet_ntop address log. The collected values then feed the advert-record ctor (rec+0x404.. block).

Resolved: the advert parser is index-keyed via f_105551dc(line, headerIdx) - proven bindings in the M-SEARCH/NOTIFY walk: idx3=ST->r20, idx0xe->r19, idx0xf->sp+0x30, idx0x10->sp+0x44, idx0x11=X-SONOS-DEVICEID->r15, idx0x13=X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD->r16/sp+0x2c, idx9->r17, idx0x19=X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION->sp+0x4c; collected set then feeds the record ctor (ssdp:alive/ssdp:byebye discriminated at 0x10556054-0x10556078; NTS checked vs "ssdp:alive"/"ssdp:byebye" before record build).

Resolved: the SSDP notify/response header ladder and record ctor are fully mapped. Parse loop (f_1055xxxx region) strncasecmp's each line against {USN:(4)->r20, LOCATION:(9)->r17, X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD:(0x13)->r16, X-RINCON-BOOTSEQ:(0x11)->r15, X-RINCON-PROXY:(0xf)->slot30, CACHE-CONTROL:(0xe)->r19, NTS:(4)->slot2c {ssdp:alive/ssdp:byebye gate}, SERVER:(7)->slot34, HOST:(5)->slot38, X-RINCON-VARIANT:(0x11)->slot3c, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO:(0x1d)->slot40, X-RINCON-REASON:(0x10), SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG:(0x18)->slot48, X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION:(0x19)->slot4c, X-SONOS-SIG:, ST:}; first line dispatched NOTIFY vs HTTP/ vs M-SEARCH.

Resolved: notify-record ctor f_1054a688 field map (arg order USN,LOCATION,RINCON-HOUSEHOLD,SERVER,RINCON-BOOTSEQ,RINCON-PROXY,RINCON-VARIANT + stack {HOST, maxage, HHS.AUDIO, SECURELOC, HHSECURELOC, 0}): +0x404=USN, +0x408=LOCATION, +0x40c=X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD, +0x410=SERVER, +0x414=strtoul(X-RINCON-BOOTSEQ) u32, +0x418=X-RINCON-PROXY, +0x41c=strtol(X-RINCON-VARIANT), +0x420=HOST (default str 0x10ea6a2c), +0x424=CACHE-CONTROL trailing max-age seconds (backward digit-scan of the value tail, strtol; default 0x708=1800 when header absent/non-numeric), +0x428=HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO, +0x442=LOCATION URL port (f_10c3aef8 URL parse + f_10c3c290 port accessor), +0x444=SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG port, +0x446=X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION port, +0x448=0. Flag bytes +0x401/+0x402 (USN-parsed ok) track arm state.

Resolved: the unicast-MSEARCH header ladder at 0x105562c8+ is fully decoded - strncasecmp ladder binds {'ST:'(3)->search-target slot r20; 'X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD:'(19)->0x2c(r1); 'X-SONOS-DEVICEID:'(17)->r16; 'X-SONOS-SESSIONRETRIES:'(23)->arm 0x105564a8; 'X-SONOS-SESSIONSECONDS:'(23)->arm 0x10556514; 'X-SONOS-MDPMODEL:'(17)->arm 0x1055656c; 'USER-AGENT:'(11)->arm 0x105565b0; 'X-SONOS-SIG:'(12)->arm 0x105565f0}. Three numeric fields init -1 (r17/r18/r19) = the session/retries/mdpmodel value defaults before header parse. The accept gate is 'Accepting %s unicast MSEARCH from %s' after an inet_ntop source render.

Resolved: the second-ladder arm destinations are bound - the M-SEARCH pass accumulates into registers then packs a 7-field request block at +0x7c(r1) for the notify-handler call: +0x7c=r20 (ST: search-target value), +0x80=[0x2c] (X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD value), +0x84=r16 (X-SONOS-DEVICEID value), +0x88=r15 (USER-AGENT value), +0x8c=r19 (SESSIONRETRIES, strtol base-10 errno-guarded via isel, default -1), +0x90=r18 (SESSIONSECONDS, same), +0x94=r17 (MDPMODEL, same). The numeric arms share one pattern: errno:=0, value:=f_105551dc(line+hdrlen), strtol(v,0,10), isel acc,result,acc,cr7.eq - the -1 default survives on parse failure. Dispatch is bctrl through global handler ptr *(0x11097388) with obj *(0x11097384), r4=&block, r5=r25 (peer addr) - the handler itself is runtime-installed. The X-SONOS-SIG arm (0x105565f0) does not store into the block: it clamps the wire sig span (isel r9,0,len,cr0lt; isel r5,maxlen,len,cr7gt), calls f_105558b0 to compute the expected signature into the +0x55c(r1) buffer, compares strlen/bytes against the wire value, and on match sets the sig-verified flag (r31=1) which gates the handler dispatch at the shared tail 0x10555f28 - unsigned or unverifiable requests skip the dispatch.

Corrected (the M-SEARCH notify delegate IS statically bound): setter f_105557ec stores {r3->0x11097388, r4->0x11097384}; its boot-time caller at 0x105e6e2c installs f_105e6844 as the handler (the other caller at 0x10193a88 NULLs the pair on teardown). f_105e6844 dispatches the parsed {st,household,deviceid,useragent,retries,seconds,mdpmodel} block: vfunc+0x84 gate, then a vfunc-identity check (slot +0x34 == f_105a594c selects the base impl path), then rec+4 selector: nonzero -> vfunc+0x64 + tail f_105a4f30; zero -> vfunc+0x4c(rec+0 st string) match gate before the same notify path. The block's rec+4 is the notify-type selector, rec+0 the ST string.

Extractor dispatch decoded (literal block 0x10ed46xx-0x10ed47xx): the ICY client sends GET %s HTTP/1.1 with ACCEPT */*, HOST %s%s, User-Agent "%s Nullsoft Winamp3 version 3.0 (compatible)", Icy-MetaData: 1; statuses accepted are ICY 200, HTTP/1.1 200, HTTP/1.0 200, and 30x redirects via location:/redirect to %s/Redirect audio/x-mpegurl to %s (m3u redirects followed); headers consumed {icy-metaint:, icy-name:, server:, CONTENT-TYPE:}; a Cougar server signature is recognized; shoutcastradio is the log/domain tag. In-stream, StreamTitle blocks are pulled at the icy-metaint interval with the text=" attribute parse (the classic StreamTitle='...'; form). Request assembly uses add header [%s : %s] and opening connection with [%s]; request buffer is too small is the guard.

Resolved: the ICY StreamTitle parser (f_1048ccdc, block at 0x1048cd90) is fully decoded: metadata blocks arrive length-prefixed (blockLen = lenByte * 16, matching icy-metaint framing); the loop parses K='V'; pairs - key chars copied until '=' , value chars between single quotes (0x27), pair ends at ';'. Only the literal key 'StreamTitle' is consumed (strcmp at 0x1048cec8); all other keys skip to ';'. Value path: f_10907e34 decode -> f_105a3cb0 bounded copy (max 0x101) -> inner 'text="..."' extraction via strstr+strchr('"')+memmove -> strcmp dedup against the stored title field -> strlcpy into the stream-object title field + stb 1 dirty flag at obj+...-0x788a. So StreamTitle lands verbatim as a single text field; the title/artist/albumArt split is downstream avt-metadata work on this stored string.

Resolved: the StreamTitle store path is proven in the ICY metadata parser (0x1048cd90-0x1048d008): the parser walks the metadata block collecting chars until ';' (0x3b) terminator, finds the StreamTitle= key, then copies the '-quoted value into a stack buf (r1+0x2108). Post-parse it stringifies the accumulated record (f_105a3cb0 into r1+0x1c, cap 0x101), strstr-strips an embedded text="..." attribute (locate text=" -> strchr closing quote -> memmove it out), then strcmp against the stored member - on mismatch it strlcpy's the new value into the member (cap 0x101) and sets a changed-byte flag (r29-0x788a, i.e. this+<offset>). So the stored StreamTitle field holds the quoted value with the redundant text= attribute removed, and the write is compare-gated to avoid false change events.

Resolved (no artist/title split exists in this image): the ICY extractor f_1048ccdc walks ';'-separated attrs (cmplwi 0x3b loop at 0x1048cf6c), locates the value via strstr 'text="' + strchr '"' terminator with memmove truncation (0x1048cf0c-0x1048cf44), strlcpy-caps at 0x101 into the stored member and sets a changed byte (stb at 0x1048cffc). A binary-wide xref of a standalone ' - ' literal finds zero references - the stored text is emitted verbatim as the r:streamContent DIDL member; no artist/title/albumArt split runs in anacapad, so downstream freeform parsing is not this binary's behavior.

'Diagnostic stub'/'Local diagnostic' mark stubbed players; diag_progress.cxx tracks per-player submit status with a timeout ('Timed out waiting for devices to report their submit status' / 'All devices reported'). So per-type content = aggregate?type=%s output; per-type inclusion in the bundle is what the manifest selects.

Resolved: the per-type file inclusion is statically enumerable after all - the DiagnosticManifest is a compiled-in sorted list at .data 0x11090228 (105 rows, stride 16, {next=0, prev_name, path, type_flag}) plus a shell-command table at 0x11090144 (18 rows, stride 12, {name, type_flag, command}: /date->/bin/date, /debugfiles->ls --full-time /jffs/{app,sys,net}/debug, /df, /du-jffs, /free, /ifconfig, /lsmod, /mount, /netstat->netstat -an, /ntpsources->chronyc -n sources -v, /ps, /route, /scanresults->/wifi/athconfig scangetresults ath0, /showmacs/showports/showstats/showstp->brctl, /uptime). type_flag is a bitmask selecting which diagnostic types include the entry: bit0x2 = base set (74 files), 0x6/0xa/0xe add wifi-PHY / timekeeping+LED / wireless-health extras, 0x43 and 0x46 mark two ath_rincon radio-status files, 0x82 marks anacapa.dc.log (the same 0x80 gate bit used by /api and /cloudqueue HTTP routes). Resolved: IsIdle is a busy-set emptiness predicate - the idle register at +0x9b8 is a key set; callers insert (f_105d0540) or erase (f_105d05d4) their busy key, and when membership changes the empty state flips, the setter f_105b7690 compares vs +0x9b0, logs "idle state is %sidle, changing to %sidle" (with "not " prefix), and posts notify cb f_105b66a4 through the scheduler at +0xa70. This matches <BusyClients>%s in WirelessInfo - busy clients are named key registrants (playingAudio/lineInBusy/replication etc.), so IsIdle = no registered busy key.

Resolved: shutdown-reason enum @0x10ef3368 = {APICall, BluetoothConnection, PartnerDisappeared, Recovery, UserSuspend, UserShutdown, APIShutdown, CriticalShutdown, UnknownShutdown}; device-props XML fields {Enabled, EthLink, SettingsReplicationState, SecureRegState, IsIdle, MoreInfo} @0x10ef32a0.

Deepened (busy-set semantics): the busy predicate reads the flag-accumulator at listener obj+0x90, written by the 'idle_evt' handler f_105d0438 (idle_evt_listener.cxx) which ORs/updates flags per event and logs 'source %d sent flags 0x%x' - so busy-ness is a bitmask of numeric source ids, not string keys. Identified flag sources: RZPWifiIdleMgr/wifi_idle_mgr.cxx (WiFiIdleScanUpdateRetry, 'Set WifiFuncsSetIdleScan fronthaul result'), the hhIdle path ('All devices idle for %ld s'), and 'Netstart is idle'. The 'Ignoring busy transition due to chirp only' gate (~f_105d05d4) suppresses busy transitions when only the chirp source holds the flag. There is no literal key vocabulary - the set membership is per-source-id runtime state.

Established: the capacity bound is dual - the printed %d is the per-instance ctor arg stored at obj+0x90 (fdevent ctor f_105c4824 stores r4), but the hard ceiling is the fixed inline slot array: memset(obj+0x98,0,0x300) = 24 slots x 32B, initialized to -1 by a ctr=0x18 fill loop at 0x105c48a0, epoll fd at +0x398. Corrected (ctor arg identity): f_105c4824's r4 -> +0x90 is the instance NAME tag, not a capacity - it is printed verbatim by the 'EventSync %s' log immediately after the store, and call sites pass subsystem name strings (e.g. 'sntp_srv' at 0x104a90d8; two sites forward their own r4 name arg; one passes a config-object name field *(r28+0x7a60)). Consumer census decoded: the WS client serves three endpoints - (1) Lechmere cloud channel lechmere.%s.ws.sonos.com with negotiated subprotocol lechmere.%u (the household event pipe); (2) the local WSS event socket advertised to controllers as <NotificationAddr>wss://%s:%u (muse)</NotificationAddr> inside Subscription records (with a plain <NotificationAddr>%s</NotificationAddr> fallback and <IsSecure>%d flag); (3) the group-advertised WSS endpoint in RGroupAdvertiser - wss://%s:%d%s is emitted beside the SSDP GROUPINFO.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO advert (delaying group advert is the backpressure path). Resolved: the group-advertised wss endpoint IS the muse event surface - the advert literal "<NotificationAddr>wss://%s:%u (muse)</NotificationAddr>" @0x10f00cfb self-labels the channel, and the single WS server negotiates only the lechmere.%u subprotocol ("WebSocket-Protocol: lechmere.%u" @0x10ef64e4, response "lechmere-v1" @0x10ee7220, cloud host "lechmere.%s.ws.sonos.com") - there is no second subprotocol family, so the advert points at the same lechmere/muse listener.

Resolved: the .upm consumer binary ships as /bin/upgrade (upgrade_lib embedded). Container integrity vocabulary proven from its 62-entry error string table at .rodata 0x10024788: idx0 success, 1 file-format unknown, 6 signature verification failed, 7 file type unknown, 0x22 corrupt data (MD5 signature mis-match), plus encrypted-upgrade stubs {0x2d encrypted upgrades currently unsupported on this product, 0x2e no encrypted upgrade key available, 0x2f error decrypting upgrade} and u-boot/FCB flash errors {no available slot, failure reading/erasing/writing the flash slot/FCB, unsupported partition, read-back comparison failed, bad fcbs, bad uboot}. Payload extraction runs /bin/tar into /jffs/app/install and executes /var/upgradescript via /bin/sh; per-component rcb bundles land at /jffs/sys/run/rcb/{upd_cert_bundle,%s-%s}.rcb verified via imported sonosRcbVerifySig (libsonoscrypto ZZ* family also imported).

Resolved: upgrade_mgr<->upgrade comm FSM and download URL from the shipped binary: state strings {HELLO, DOWNLOAD, FLASHWRITE, REBOOT, CONNECT, ERROR, FINISHED, *_DONE variants} with reportOpComplete state/upgradeResult reporting; control socket via /tmp/upgrade_mgr.pid presence; fetch URL templates "%supdate.upm?cmaj=%u&cmin=%u&cbld=%u&subm=%u&rev=%u&reg=%u&serial=%s" and "%s%s-%u-%u.upd?..." with optional "&au=1" and "&sonosid=%s&householdid=%s" suffixes; region names {any region, United States and Canada, Europe, China, Japan}; device-query report file /var/run/upgrade_report.txt and /var/run/stopupgrade cancel flag; upgradeinfo keys {sonosid, householdid, ver_from, ver_system, dnlspeed, dnlduration, serverip, requestpath, status, state}.

Resolved (.upm framing, from shipped /bin/upgrade): the per-section cursor is {+0: ctx, +4: section header}; header fields {+0x4: type (valid range 3..0x16/22, matches the .upd type vocabulary), +0xc: flags where bit 0x2 = optional/tolerated when the type is unknown, +0x10: payload offset}. Dispatch runs a stride-28 per-type handler table {+0x10: arg, +0x14: already-seen flag -> 'Multiple sections of type %u' dedup error, +0x28: flags where bit0 = 'Skipping checks for section %u'}. Section flag bit0x1 => 'encrypted signature section not supported', bit0x4 => unsupported-encryption reject. File body is mapped via mmap64 (anonymous/work buffer rounded to 0x200, then copied). The cert-bundle section is parsed by sonosRcbParseHeader(data,size,verifycb=sonosRcbVerifySig) and persisted to /jffs/sys/run/rcb/%s-%s.rcb via sonosFileCreate. Error names live in an enum-indexed string table at 0x10024788 (idx 0='success' ... 'upgrade file format unknown', 'MD5 signature mis-match', 'bad fcbs', 'bad uboot', 'lost client connection').

Outer .upm/RCB header fully decoded from sonosRcbParseHeader @libsonos-root-cert-bundle.so.2:0xc64 - file layout {+0x00: 8-byte magic "rcbundle" (memcmp, fail->status 3); +0x08: u16 BE version, must be >=3 (v-3 shifted check, fail->status 7); +0x0a: 64-byte bundle name string copied NUL-terminated into the out struct; +0x4a: 16-byte field A; +0x5a: 16-byte field B; +0x6a: u16 BE section count <=0x12c (300, fail->status 4); +0x6c: section directory begins}. Header consumed = 0x6c bytes; parsed struct returned to caller is 0x78 bytes {u16 ver, name[64], fieldA[16], fieldB[16]}. Read goes through a caller-supplied callback (arg5) whose status must be <=9; all bounds checks return status 8.

Header 16B field1 (+0x4a) semantics narrowed: it is a binary bundle identifier - the /bin/upgrade caller passes it through RserializeData (libsonosminiutils %02x hex serializer) into the stash filename /jffs/sys/run/rcb/<name>-<hex(field1)>.rcb, and a second site (0x1000a4e4) tests field1[0] != 0 to decide whether to append the &au=1 suffix to an update URL. field2 (+0x5a) is copied verbatim into the parse struct but has no consumer in /bin/upgrade or libsonos-root-cert-bundle - its meaning is set by the manifest/signature verify path or is reserved.

todo: Residual: the per-stream {buffersize, ratelimit us} defaults - the init params are runtime-supplied by each stream client; the SegmentTable growth is now proven (double-on-full, 168B entries).
resolved_findings: Resolved: SegmentTable reallocation = grow-on-demand with reap-on-idle; reap policy inputs = {age, buffer pressure, segment completion}.

Reap policy proven (async_buffered_stream.cxx): there is no free-space watermark - reaping is lazy and allocation-driven. When a segment alloc fails (Unable to satisfy allocation request! Played to pos: %zu) the streamer reaps played blocks: Started reaping played data. Lose fast scrubbing backwards -> Played to stream pos %zu. Reaped %zu blocks of played data in track %5.5s -> Alloc satisfied by deleting played data; Free blocks %zu or Alloc not satisified, returning anyway; Free blocks %zu / Satisfed allocation request but should not have required this!. The reap boundary is the playing position (Streaming pos %zu below playing pos %zu; Pause; framed to stream pos %zu; resume at pos %zu; reaped to pos %zu) - only data behind the play head is collectable, hence lost backward scrubbing. Track transitions also satisfy allocs (Alloc satisfied by track transition). Segments are block lists: EOF-flagged terminals (Data segment follows segment with EOF!), in-progress I/O pinned (Tried to delete segment with I/O in progress), append-only order (I/O to block %zu; not last block in segment). Position->time mapping: stream positions are byte offsets only (Filesize=%zu, startPos=%zu); wall-clock mapping happens upstream in the player's per-track position tracking (ptvTrackPos), not in the stream layer.

Resolved (SegmentTable growth policy, f_1029c56c realloc path at 0x1029c800-0x1029c884): the table doubles on each growth - new cap = old cap << 1 (slwi r9,r9,1 at 0x1029c848 stored back to obj+0x4), entries are fixed 0xa8 (168) bytes each and the realloc copies the last entry over the freed slot then compacts; the entry-count loop uses multiply-shift division by 0xa8 (ori 0xcf3d + mulli + srwi 29 at 0x1029c7f4-0x1029c80c). 'SegmentTable reallocated to %zu entries' prints the doubled capacity.

Window computation and launch proven (auto_update_scheduler.cxx, updateScheduler domain): the window is an HH:MM:SS range persisted via R_AutoUpdateWindowStart; shrinkWindow trims it (Trimming the window to (%d) seconds). ST_SESSION_ACTIVE gates on two blockers - Upcoming alarm is preventing update and Active device(s) preventing update (the <ActiveDeviceList> in UpdateInfo XML names them). On window entry it launches upgrade_mgr (/bin/upgrade_mgr; Launching update failed, retrying in %d seconds), polls upgrade_mgr_report.json + upgrade_mgr.txt + app/log for progress, and retries bounded by Retrying upgrade (%d/%d) -> Giving up after max upgrade attempts / Scheduling error!.
