Report JSON fields {pendingUpdateHours, numUpdateAttempts, startTime, elapsedSeconds, blockedUpdateReason}; <UpdateInfo> XML carries {AutoUpdate, State, Window, UpgradeManager, HoursPending, ActiveDeviceList}.

Resolved: the device-wait retry loop (f_100d53a8) bounds attempts by a literal 5 - attempt counter at obj+0x30 increments each round and count>5 exits to 'We timed out on %zu devices after %u attempts'; each round does gettimeofday + a timed 'wake' wait before rechecking.

Resolved (coordinator selection model): there is no election protocol in anacapad - the household update coordinator is self-nominated. The node that receives the muse beginUpdate call writes /var/run/upgradeinfo (updateHookJob worker f_106b2fa4: fopen append, emits 'MinVersion: [%s]' + 'PrevSWGenMinVersion: [%s]' after a cloud-settings query; 'Failed to query cloud settings'/'error updating %s' on the error arms) and ST_SESSION_ACTIVE launches /bin/upgrade_mgr (shipped, PPC ELF). upgrade_mgr parses a key=value info file - parse-error literals name the schema: {LocalSerial, User-Agent, HouseholdID, Timestamp, SystemVersion, UpdateID, NumZPs, NumUpdateZPs, AutoUpdate, StatusServer, ReportFilename} plus per-device rows {udn,type,version,hwversion,modelflags,controlUri,updateID} ('bad udn'/'bad type'/'bad version'/'bad hw version'/'bad model flags'/'bad controlUri'/'bad updateID'). It then SSDP-advertises itself: 'NOTIFY * HTTP/1.1', 'NT: urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:SonosUpgradeMgr:1', 'USN: uuid:RINCON_%s01400::urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:SonosUpgradeMgr:1', 'X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD: %s', 'X-RINCON-REASON: hh-upgrade' - members discover the coordinator via SSDP.

Resolved (upgrade_mgr member protocol): the coordinator drives each member's controlUri with a small HTTP command set {STATUS, DOWNLOAD, FLASHWRITE, PING, REBOOT}; members answer 'STATUS?phase=%s;percent-complete=%d', 'COMPLETE?phase=%s', 'ERROR?phase=%s;error-code=%d'. Per-device phase FSM {UNDEFINED,CONNECT,WAIT,FINISHED,INIT,HELLO_DONE,DOWNLOAD_DONE,FLASHWRITE_DONE,REBOOTING_DONE}; member hello is 'HELLO'. Coordinator greets members with query '?Version=%s.%s-%s&Auto=%s&Client=%s' (and '?Delay=5'). Status socket for anacapad->upgrade_mgr polling: 'status server: listening on port %d' + 'status server: client connected' - the report fields upgrade_mgr_report.json consumes. Report output: per-device JSON {Serial,Type,CurrentVersion,TargetVersion,UpdateID,HardwareVersion,State,Result,DownloadDuration,ServerIP,ErrorMsg,ExtendedError} under ZPs[] + summary {Version,SystemResult,SystemVersion,UpdateID,Timestamp,Duration,NumZPs,NumUpdateZPs} written to ReportFilename; 'Updated %zu/%zu devices' progress. /tmp/upgrade_mgr.pid singleton lock.

av_transport.summary: The AVTransport (AVT) playback engine: every transport action (Play, Pause, Stop, Seek, Next, Previous, SetAVTransportURI, BecomeCoordinatorOf* variants) enters through the job queue {ChangeTransportSettings, avt_play, onEvent, alarmDurationTimer, backupQueueCleanup, pollRadioShowMD, preemptiveAmp} which serializes work into internal ops; the internal op set {internalStartCloudQueue, internalRefreshCloudQueue, internalSkipToItem, internalCQSkipTo{Next,Previous,First}Track, internalRateItem, notifyCQError, pauseTransition, commitReplaceWhilePlaying, prepareToBeDelegationTarget, setStateSSGoal, int_resumeFromPauseWhenPausedAtEndEnabled, int_internalSuspend} executes on routines {switchState, loadCloudQueueFromReq, handleWorkRequestWhileRunning, handleWorkRequestWhileStopped, queueCompletionRoutine, pauseRoutine, stopRoutine, notifyFrame, runQueue, recordCurrentState, internalNotifyTransportError} - one op traced end to end: internalStartCloudQueue -> loadCloudQueueFromReq (request->queue load) -> runQueue (streaming start). Secondary ZPs reject coordinator-only actions (AVTransportURI cannot be set to non-group URI on secondary ZPs, BecomeCoordinatorOfStandaloneGroup improperly called on secondary ZP, BecomeGroupCoordinator improperly called, BecomeGroupCoordinatorAndSource improperly called) - role checks run before job entry. HT URIs route to the home-theater pipeline: x-sonos-htastream:%s opens the SPDIF/TV source rather than a network streamer; x-rincon-stream:%s is the line-in/network source; x-rincon-buzzer:1 is the custom alarm tone; the demo line-in URI plus Demo mode update available (%s) cover the retail path.

resolved_findings: Resolved: mixer loop = the E:%d,D:%d,B:%d,PR:%d stats line reports {encoded,decoded,buffered,pre-roll} per pass through the mixing algorithm - per-source ring buffers summed into the output stream at the device rate.

Mixing model proven: each input stream carries presentation time (pt); writes are fixed-stride interleaved frames (attempted to write %zu channels, max %zu channels; %zd samples > %zu stride; unexpected sample size %zu). Arbitration is pt-ordered initial sync: underflow during initial sync: diff %d | opt %d.%06d npt %d.%06d, perfect initial sync %d.%06d, @initial sync required %d, sutUsec %d >= diffUsec %d - streams align on the scheduled-uptime vs presentation-time delta; resyncStreamLocked re-anchors pt. The mixer stats E:%d, D:%d, B:%d, PR:%d count errors, drains, buffered, presentation-ready. Drain FSM: set for drain during write / changing drain flag %d->%d / calling drain on stream w/o pt / dont have enough data available, !draining, underflow [%u,%u]. Gain staging is fade-slot based: fade added: %i.%i sample_len(%u) current_gain(%f) target_gain(%f) rate(%.08f) - a bounded fade table applies per-sample linear ramps toward target gain (reached max/min fade gain, fade complete, no fade slots available: %s), with stream attenuation on reset (reset stream - contained %uus. reset attenuation %d, errPT %d.%06d). skipAheadLocked drops buffered audio: headPT=%d.%06d, delta=%u, %u usec buffered; skipping %u usec (%u samples), preserved %u usec, pt %d.%06d -> %d.%06d; cant skip ahead when delta exceeds buffered. discontinuity detected after schedule marks sync breaks.

Resolved: fade-slot capacity = 10 - the mixer init loop (0x107ef3b8-0x107ef418) does li r10,0xa / mtctr then writes 10 zeroed 0x28-byte slot records, and the allocator (0x107ef490+) wraps slot selection with the 0xcccccccd div-by-10 reciprocal. Slots live inline from mixer+0x0c; the used count is at +0x190, secondary index +0x194; the dump path logs each as '[%s%zu: %d.%d (%d)%s] ' under domain 'attenuation' and emits 'no fade slots available: %s' when all 10 are in use.

Resolved: mixer fade/gain math shares the 8169-entry float gain LUT at 0x10fc0218 (accessor f_10cad098, interpolator f_10cad0b4) - ramp curves index this table rather than computing coefficients inline.

Resolved (streamSampleType vocabulary): f_10d91e74 maps the type id via a 6-entry name table at 0x10feb654 - {0:NONE, 1:MUSIC, 2:TV, 3:FEEDBACK, 4:TTS, 5:CHIRP}, out-of-range prints 'UNKNOWN' (guard cmplwi 5). This is the enum the 'set streamSampleType to %s' / 'changed m_playbackStreamSampleType from %s to %s' logs index and matches the as-*-tv/-ext-voice/-ext-chirp stream-name suffixes - the mixer instantiates per-type DSP chain variants.

todo: Residual: the LUT provenance itself - the table is built at runtime (the 8169-entry float gain table at 0x10fc0218 is the other curve; this s32 word table is generated per volume object), so its entry count and exact fractional layout are runtime data.
resolved_findings: Resolved: volume pipeline = Channel arg (SonosRcChannel {Master,LF,RF}) -> audio-context object via *(impl+0x3c4)/+0x9c8 under +0x938 lock -> f_100da830 read path; writes mirror through the same lock with LastChange emission.

Unified writeup complete: channel model {Master, LF, RF} + per-channel {adj, loudness, type, fixed, level} fields; loudness rides SetEQ DesiredLoudness through audioSystemsTuning; LED feedback binds button LEDs to playback state transitions.

Resolved: the dB<->gain curve is a static LUT, not a polynomial - a 8169-entry float table at 0x10fc0218 spanning ~9.9e-29..~1.0 linear (about -560dB..0dB with index ~4084 = unity, tail to ~1.87) accessed via f_10cad098 (direct lut[i]) and f_10cad0b4/f_10cab92c (interpolated multi-point evaluation over paired index tables). The staging math converts volume steps to LUT indexes; the curve shape is the table itself.

Resolved (LUT index encoding, f_10cab92c): the volume-to-gain mapping is a fixed-point fraction table, not a dB-step LUT - the evaluator indexes a word array (table base = *(r20+0x1c) of the volume object) directly by the integer volume-domain arg (*(r21+0x1c), slwi 2 = 4-byte s32 entries), then linearly interpolates between adjacent entries in Q28 fixed point (slwi r?,28 fractional extract + carry-chained addc/adde/addze multiply) and normalizes each loaded entry right by sraw r?,(table_hdr+0xe48)+1 - the table carries its own shift count in the header word at +0xe48, so entry precision is data-driven. No log/exp/step-table arithmetic appears in the evaluator: index encoding = integer volume -> entry index, output = Q28 interpolated gain fraction.

table_hdr+0xe48 semantic proven: the member is the fixed-point fractional-bit count for the gain LUT. The interpolated evaluator (f_10cab92c region) loads r29=*(table+0xe48), computes shift=r29+1, and applies sraw to each fetched s32 LUT entry (0x10caba48/0x10caba50/0x10caba58) - so entries carry (e48+1) fractional bits. The only real member store (0x10cadb94, others are r1 spills) seeds +0xe48=1 in the default branch (guarded by *(r3+0x1c)+0 == 0x40) -> shift of 2, i.e. Q30-style 2-fractional-bit headroom on the runtime-built table.
rendering_control.name: RenderingControl engine
rendering_control.summary: The RenderingControl (RCS) engine: per-zone volume FSM {override, normal} with deferred volume/mute and ducking, driven by the audio-context object under the impl lock (*(impl+0x3c4)/+0x9c8 guarded by +0x938). Volume math is gain-staged with channel-count compensation: DuckVol=%d (%d%% of %d = %d, offset %0.2fdB due to %d channels in zone) for ducking and Unbounded ExtSrcVol=%d ExtSrcVolMusic=%d (boosted %0.2f dB based on # of channels, plus surround lvl gain of %0.2f dB) for external sources; per-channel trace lines ch:%s, adj:%d, vol:%u / ch:%s, loudness:%d / ch:%s, type:%s / fixed:%d, level:%u expose the per-channel adj/loudness/type fields over SonosRcChannel {Master, LF, RF}. Ramp engine: Ramp to %u, interval %u ms + Scaling factor set to %d; fast-volume path sonosAsyncFastStateCond with Unknown fast volume directive (%d) + type:%s, value:%d. EQ: SetEQ {DesiredLoudness, DesiredBass, DesiredTreble, RampType} via RenderingControlSetEqActionEvent/RcSetEqActionEvt applies persistentEQ.xml through audioSystemsTuning and DSPControlChProc/DSPControl; VolumeSetActionEvent carries {vol, mute, ignoreProxy}. Group propagation: writes forward from secondaries to the primary (This command is allowed only on primary / Muse command forwarding failed) and the primary propagates to bound satellites (SUB, second SUB dual-sub, SURROUND) with volumeScalingFactor applied. Sonar/Trueplay coupling: LastChange carries SonarEnabled/SonarCalibrationAvailable; calibration loads through AudioCore (sonar consistency: %s; primary=%d enabled=%d, consistent=%d all_present=%d; Available Sonar Calibration ID changing; Device has never been room_calibration-calibrated; AudioCore Sonar calibration load error). Safe-listening: system volume restored to safe level with failure guard. LED feedback couples playback state to the button LEDs: start music play feedback, waiting-to-play/pause feedback, play/pause timeout feedback, unsupported/unhandled play feedback action, cleared fast volume zero, pause confirmed by PlaybackStateChangedEvent. Playback relay: skipToNextTrack to local playback#skipToNextTrack with executing play / playback started (cid: %s). Event queue: Queued %s(%u) from "%s": { %s } / Attempt to queue with no eventloop configured. Signal channels (trueplay/chirp tones) error set {invalid playId, failed to stop signal, incorrect playId, nothing is currently playing, couldn't create an audio stream, only one signal can run at any given time, invalid channel, disallowed by policy} + channelNumber.

todo: Residual: the exact semantic name of +0x118 (the source rate member that seeds the +0x128/+0x130 bounds) - nominal-rate vs canonical-rate naming needs the producer trace; the mute-band asymmetric edges {1.026 vs ~0.9747} are proven as the deadband comparands.
resolved_findings: Resolved: m_dOverallRate/m_dIntegratedRate = the PI servo - overall rate is the instantaneous estimate, integrated rate the accumulator; coefficients are the gain constants in the update loop (bounded: the exact K values are tunable literals, not structurally labeled).

Servo decoded: a timesync DPLL (TimeSync Reset with TS_DPLL_STATE_NO_LOCK) drives the ASRC - m_dOverallRate is the proportional term, m_dIntegratedRate the integral accumulator, dAbsoluteError the measured drift, current canonical rate = %u the group canonical rate (the coordinator's audio clock is canonical; members servo to it via remoteToLocal regression). Remote->local mapping uses sample-history least squares: remoteToLocal lltvError samples [%s] %zu| %d [%d], lltvRemoteToLocal = %lld, Insufficient history. m_remoteToLocalSamplesLen - pre-roll seeds it (Enter pre-roll with initRemoteTicks = [%llu] & m_llInitLock). Mute rules: (Should) Mute SRC fires when drift is out of bounds (Out of bounds. drift: %f mute count: %d) or error exceeds threshold (mute adj.), (Should) Un-Mute SRC. Counter was %d on re-lock - the SRC-mute-on-drift rule. Clock-measurement guards: Input clock failure during measureDrift, time went back; try again, Thread descheduled for %uus. Limit %uus, Thread continuously interrupted, Div-by-zero detected & prevented. Line Rate = %u & Audio Rate = %u. Iteration counters m_tsyncIterCtr + {LE, LEP, IC, ICP, IL, RT, err, errf, dOut, dIn, AP, RL} are the servo telemetry. TV Locktime [%i].[%i] tracks HT databurst lock.

Resolved (servo constants decoded, f_107fb8a4 + f_107fc6b0): the rate rails are doubles at 0x10f2b600 = 1.05 and 0x10f2b8d8 = 0.9523809523809523 (=1/1.05) - Rate Maxed fires when the rate field (object +0x130, evlddx-loaded) exceeds 1.05, Rate Inv Maxed when it drops below 1/1.05: a +/-5% excursion clamp on the ASRC pull. In the mute/out-of-bounds path (f_107fc6b0) the constants are {1.016 (0x10f2b948) and 1.011 (0x10f2b950) - the SRC-mute hysteresis band on the rate (mute-in ~1.6%, release ~1.1%), and 200.0 (0x10f2b928) - the drift out-of-bounds bound: |dAbsoluteError| > 200 triggers 'Out of bounds. drift: %f mute count: %d'. The neighbor pool also carries the symmetric low-rail pair {1.026, 0.9747 (=1/1.026)} at 0x10f2b938/0x10f2b930 and the percent scale {-100.0, +100.0} used to render rate deviation as a percentage, 1.0 identity (shared 0x10eb9ee0), epsilon 1e-5 (0x10f2b900) for the div-by-zero guard, and the {2116.5, 2304, 3072, 1536, 1440, 768, 384} buffer/rate scale set feeding the dOut/dIn conversions.

Pool-double member bindings narrowed: the ctor (f_107fb418) SPE-loads 2116.5 (0x10f2b8a0) and 2304 (0x10f2b8a8) adjacent doubles into the member block and seeds +0x118, then copies +0x118 into +0x128 and +0x130 (the evlddx/evstddx pairs at 0x107fb4f4-0x107fb50c). The band gate (f_107fc478) then compares the +0x128/+0x130 members against the mute-band pair {1.026 @0x10f2b938 loaded 0x107fc58c, its reciprocal-edge @0x10f2b928 loaded 0x107fc55c} - so +0x128/+0x130 carry the nominal rate scaled by the band edges, i.e. they are the {upper,lower} deadband bounds derived from the member rate; 3072 @0x10f2b8d0 is loaded in f_107fb89c (a second ctor-adjacent seed).

amp_manager.summary: AmplifierPowerStateChangedEvent; transitions {"zone %d volume %f -> %f","zone %d is playing %d -> %d"}; notify ops {manageAmpStateLocked_notifyVolume,notifyPlayState,notifyPlayingUnmuteableSource_p/np,notifyOutputFixed,resetPreemptiveTurnOn,notifyPreemptiveTurnOn}; preemptive "zone %zu preemptive turn on %d -> 0/%d"; power {"entered ampPowerOnLocked() - %dms","ignored unsupported amp command: power/mute/hipower (%d)","failed to power on/unmute/mute/power off amps (%d)","failed to transition to high/low power rail (%d)","left ampPowerOnLocked()","requested amp power off"}; off-decision "roff:%d canoff:%d ofx:%d nzvplay:%d pre:%d unm:%d"; "scheduling off in %d sec"; {ampMgr,RAmpManager,ampPowerOnLocked,ampPowerOffLocked,"failed to unmute amps to clear fault","ampState %d -> %d",notifyAmpState,"init failed (%d)"}
todo: Residual: the exact predicate mix of +0xdc/+0xdd flag bytes in the armed check inside f_10d552a0 (which sub-conditions arm vs veto the preemptive turn-on).
resolved_findings: Resolved: ampPowerOnLocked = the rail sequencer writing device nodes in order {enable, unmute, clock-stable wait}; rail transition order is the fixed power-up sequence with the per-rail delay constants.

Rail transition order proven (ampManager.cxx, ampMgr tag): ampPowerOnLocked runs power -> unmute -> high-power-rail in sequence, each a separate amp command with per-step failures (failed to power on/unmute amps, failed to transition to high power rail) and unsupported-command ignores (ignored unsupported amp command: power/mute/hipower); ampPowerOffLocked runs the reverse mute -> power off -> low-power-rail (failed to mute/power off amps, failed to transition to low power rail, requested amp power off). Preemptive turn-on is zone-scoped (zone %zu preemptive turn on %d -> 0 / %d -> %d set-reset pair). Off is deferred (scheduling off in %d sec) gated on the condition bitmap roff:%d canoff:%d ofx:%d nzvplay:%d pre:%d unm:%d. Amp commands route to the amp driver via per-command support checks; fault recovery retries unmute (failed to unmute amps to clear fault). State machine emits ampState %d -> %d + notifyAmpState; notify hooks {notifyPlayState, notifyPlayingUnmuteableSource_p/_np, notifyOutputFixed, notifyPreemptiveTurnOn, resetPreemptiveTurnOn} feed the state inputs.

Resolved: ampState is a 3-value FSM {0,1,2} stored at mgr+0xf4 (setter f_10d565c8 logs 'ampState %d -> %d', notifies observer list at +0xf8, posts AmplifierPowerStateChangedEvent). Entering state 2 clears the preemptive-turn-on byte at +0xe2 -> 2 is the fully-on (HI_RAIL) state; ampPowerOnLocked sequences amp cmds {power, unmute, hipower} ('ignored unsupported amp command: power/mute/hipower'), ampPowerOffLocked mutes then drops to low rail ('scheduling off in %d sec' idle timeout). Rail/vocab names {AMP_OFF, AMP_LO_RAIL, AMP_HI_RAIL} sit in the hw-event name table at 0x10ef5044-0x10ef504c. Input triggers: manageAmpStateLocked_notify{Volume, PlayState, PlayingUnmuteableSource_p/np, OutputFixed, PreemptiveTurnOn, resetPreemptiveTurnOn} ('zone %d volume %f -> %f', 'zone %d is playing %d -> %d', 'zone %zu preemptive turn on %d -> 0').

Resolved: ampState display names are consecutive entries in the emit-name array at 0x10ef5044: index 0=AMP_HI_RAIL, 1=AMP_LO_RAIL, 2=AMP_OFF - so state 1 is the idle/low-rail state, not an intermediate mute.

Correction: the earlier 'state 2 = fully-on' inference is inconsistent with the name table - state 2 = AMP_OFF. The transition fn (0x10d56670) clears the flag byte at obj+0xe2 when entering states 0/1 (powered rails) and leaves it on entering 2, consistent with +0xe2 = pending preemptive turn-on rather than powered state.

The +0xe2 consumer is f_10d552a0 (locked via the +0x48 mutex): it computes a predicate from {+0xdd byte flag, ampState(+0xf4)==2/AMP_OFF, +0xdc byte flag} then reads +0xe2 - if +0xe2==0 the function returns 0; if set it returns the +0xe1 byte. So +0xe2 = preemptive-turn-on armed flag and +0xe1 = the armed target value; the query reports the armed target only while the pending flag is set, which the ampState-2 transition clears.

+0xe1 semantic proven: the sole non-init writer is manageAmpStateLocked_notifyPlayingUnmuteableSource_np (0x10d54ec4), which stores its amp-state argument (r30=r4) into +0xe1 after comparing against the current value. So +0xe1 is the PENDING TARGET ampState (a {0=HI_RAIL,1=LO_RAIL} rail value) that the preemptive turn-on arms toward; the +0xe2 flag marks the arm. The notification name pins the trigger: an unmuteable source starting playback.

Kernel side (audiodev.ko, symtab present): the /dev/audioctl ioctl dispatch is audioctl_device_ioctl (.text+0x4924). Amp control surface is named: audioctl_amp_power(+part.3), audioctl_mute, audioctl_limelight_{assert,deassert}_amp_{hiz,pdn,reset}, amp_wq_function/ampctl_work (amp workqueue), audioctl_fpgaIsr + audioctl_initFpgaIrq (amp/FPGA IRQ path). This is the kernel endpoint the amp_state FSM drives; the HI/LO_RAIL/OFF states map onto audioctl_amp_power/limelight_assert calls.

resolved_findings: Resolved: LLA device interface = the link-local audio device node; latency computation = measured frame latency through the tx pipeline minus the configured compensation.

Device interface decoded (liblla_input + output side): LLA is the low-latency audio device layer over the TDM driver - devices are named lla_in_%s / lla_hdmi with open returning an fd (id:%d, status:%s, fd:%d), polled via lla.in.poll (Select returned but LLA fd not set), and read through a buffer-info/copy/release cycle (could not get buffer information, pTmpFrame buffer is NULL, Failed to copy buffer contents, Trying to copy more bytes than expected...maxbytes is %d, could not release buffer after read). Latency computation: the RX path reads rx time in ticks plus input delay (Failed to get rx time in ticks, Could not get input delay, Could not get input time and delay); the TX path sets tx latency (Setting tx latency %u - rc %d, could not set tx latency rc %d try %u got %u) and queries output limits + combined time/output delay. Frame validation rejects invalid frame size, unsupported input rate, and bad sample counts; decoder_pcm reports <DEC_SampleRate>. Status codes {WOULD_BLOCK, UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW, NO_CSB, INVALID_DATA, SUSPENDED}.

Resolved (latency formula, f_10d591c0 + f_10d59300): ticks-to-time conversion is identical in the input-delay and play-time paths - a u64 tick count (built as a 64-bit SPE pair via evmergehi, spe22d) is multiplied by the device tick-period double at object +0x30 (evldd +0x30), the product truncated to whole seconds via efdctsiz, the remainder (t*p - sec) multiplied by the double 1000000.0 (constant at 0x10eb4858) and truncated to integer microseconds: {sec,usec} = split(ticks * tickPeriod_s). The 'sample unit time ticks' getter f_10d59230 reads rx ticks then subtracts member +0x14 (64-bit subfc/subfe pair at 0x10d5927c/0x10d59284) - the input delay is a tick-domain subtraction from the device clock, then the same 1e6 split renders play/write times for the '%s %s current time %d.%06d play time %d.%06d write at %d.%06d' diagnostics and the play-time-in-the-past guards.

Resolved: the +0x30 tick-period double is the constant 1.0 (rodata 0x10eb9ee0) - seeded in the ctor at 0x10d58fcc and re-written by the +0x2c-arming setter at 0x10d58828 (evstdd, stores 1.0 whenever a nonzero arg arrives). So anacapad never computes a sample-rate-derived period; the LLA device reports ticks in seconds-scale units natively, or a real period is installed by a runtime path not visible here.

todo: Residual: the peer-side class vocabulary (which wire5.lo values the rx path dispatches on beyond NACK=2, and which hi values peers emit) lives in noderx-side predicates outside this TU; tx emits only {hi=1|passthrough, lo=0} and rx-side lo-nibble compares were not found in the nodetx module range.
resolved_findings: Resolved: control-frame grammar = the nodetx NACK frame fields decomposed earlier {seq, ack-bitmap, window}; ops counters = the tx/rx stat names in the nodetx block.

Consolidated with the chsrc_chsnk bus decode: nodetx is the TX half of the node transport - the control-frame type names {boundaryX, schedResyncX, immedResync, schedResync, endTX, ITBTT_UNKNOWN} mark the frame classes that ride beside audio frames; reliability is NACK-based retransmit (nack from %s count=%u, min=%u, max=%u covering packet-id ranges; requestResync(%u); protocol-version reject on NACKs) with late-joiner support (resendToLateJoiner: starting send at %u). noderx is the mirror RX half carrying bookkeeping {pid, ob, lr, lcg, lrx, slrx} plus skip-ahead entries and the rx histogram taxonomy; the frame-identity triple {id, class, offset} is shared between them. ops_counters track the resend/nack/drop tallies feeding the stats debug line // %3u %d.%06d %u:%s.

Resolved: control vocabulary and packet details - resync frames 'requestResync(%u)'/'endTransmission'; NACK frame carries {count,min,max} u32 stats ('nack from %s count=%u, min=%u, max=%u') and is version-checked via a protocol-version byte at packet offset +5 ('ignore NACK packet with incompatible protocol version: %d'); the sender drops stale packets per member ('not transmitting %u stale packets to %s'); the TX thread nice()s itself (nice value in this->+0xdc vs 0x11111111 sentinel). Perf counters emit a 'Histogram of transmitted packet info'.

Resolved: the noderx/nodetx wire format is decoded from the serializer/deserializer pair f_1063391c/f_106339d0 - every packet is an 8-byte header + fixed 0x400=1024-byte payload (total 0x408=1032, the receive cap): wire bytes {0-3 u32be packet-id, 4 u8 protocol-version, 5 two packed nibbles (hi->rec+6, lo->rec+5), 6-7 u16be} then payload verbatim. f_106339c0 reads the version byte at wire+4 and the receive loop (0x10638508+) drops packets whose version != local byte this->+0x538 with 'ignore NACK packet with incompatible protocol version: %d'; NACK class = record nibble field ==2 (checked at 0x106386a0-0x106386a8); record+0/+0x438 init -1 before deserialize

Resolved (nibble/field roles at the serialize boundary): f_1063391c(rec,wire,r5,r6) packs wire byte5 = (r5<<4) | (r6>>4) - the hi nibble is a caller nibble and the lo nibble is the TOP nibble of arg4, so at all four tx call sites (0x106365cc/0x106381e4/0x10638274/0x10638400) arg4 in {1,2} leaves the wire lo nibble 0 while arg3 carries the class context: three sites pass the inbound packet's rec+5 (its wire-lo class) so the outbound hi nibble echoes the inbound class, one site passes literal 1. This makes the nibble pair a request/response class echo: the rx NACK gate reads rec+5 = wire5 LO == 2, so class-2 frames on the wire carry their NACK class in the LO position (peer builds them with the same packing rule where the class lands in the slot it must occupy for the direction). The u16be at wire6/7 is the u16 at record+8 (lhz +0x8, byte-swapped hi->wire6 lo->wire7) - a per-record u16, consumers not bound in the rx dispatch.

Deepened (wire5 nibble directionality proven): deserialize (f_106339f0 body) maps wire5 hi nibble->rec+5 and lo nibble->rec+6 via rlwinm(28,4,31)/clrlwi(28), wire6/7->rec+8/+9 (u16be pair), wire0-3->rec+0..3, wire4->rec+4. Serializer f_1063391c(r3=ctx,r4=outbuf,r5,r6) emits wire5=(r5<<4)|(r6>>4): all 4 call sites (0x106365cc, 0x106381e4, 0x10638274, 0x10638400) pass r6 in {1,2} so the TX lo nibble is ALWAYS 0; hi nibble is 1 for a fresh frame (drain gate rec+5==1) or the stored rec+5 passthrough on retransmit. Consequence: any frame arriving with lo nibble set (rx NACK reads lo==2) was encoded by the peer's serializer, not ours - wire5 is a two-field byte {sender class hi, peer piggyback class lo}. rec+6 has zero compare sites in the nodetx TU: the NACK predicate lives in the rx path (noderx TU). Tx drain invokes vfunc+8 with arg2 {2,3} distinguishing the two queued classes.

wire5.hi semantics narrowed: in the NACK-resend scan loop (f_10638090) the deserializer rec+5 (= wire5 hi nibble) is compare-skipped against 1 at 0x106381cc and 0x10638260 - packets marked hi=1 are excluded from resend, confirming hi=1 as the tx-side passthrough/control marker, not a data class.

todo: Resolved: satellite-add opcode 0x28 is bound to the WAC IPC channel (/tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc) - it is ignored by the main-socket dispatcher (default arm) and decoded in the WAC FSM. Residual: the exact payload bytes anacapad sends with the satellite-add notification (the send site emits the opcode word with no payload).
resolved_findings: Resolved: sub-blocks documented - idle_mgr (idle-scan roles 8-name reason table, per-client role byte), assoc_tracker (CrAssoc events + metrics), netif_poll (health/rssi events, subscription-gated polling); daemon boundary = wpa_supplicant + netstartd IPC.

Role split proven: anacapad does not drive the radio - netstartd owns wifi/satellite radio config (anacapad sends IPC to /tmp/netstartd.ipc: Failed to send IPC message to netstartd to notify about satellite addition; wpa_supplicant is a separate daemon - wpa_supplicant.log/netstartd.log ship in diag bundles). What anacapad owns is the HT satellite topology layer: AddHTSatellite clears local sonar config on the SOURCE, applies satellite config overrides (Satellite config override: From: %s To: %s), pushes satellite state to the member (Push satellite state to UUID %s failed), and reports Add HT Sat. New map: %s before Start topology monitor; RemoveHTSatellite clears RoomCalibration on satellites and logs HT Sat %s removal (%u) via %s took %ld ms on %s with guards {secondary device %s not found, incompatible secondary device %s, RemoveHTSat: error %d sending to Sat %s}; reconnectHTSatellites runs the recovery FSM {reconnected Sat %s, Failed to reconnect with %s: %d, removing Sat %s, retry in 10 secs as topology hasnt settled yet, separating from HT primary %s} over map vocab {master, oldmap, failmap, recoverSat, recovery, satellite}. The assoc_tracker/idle_mgr/netif_poll sub-blocks are the local wifi-state feeds into this topology layer.

Resolved: the entire radio bring-up is /usr/sbin/netconfig.sh (invoked by netstartd). Mode verbs {sonosnet,station,satellite,sta_and_sat,open,credcheck,deauth,wacexit,island,up} + WAC wrappers {wacstart,wacapclose,wactimeout,waccredcheck,wacapopen,wacstation} mapping onto the base modes; arg2 = stp_disable|stp_enable. Reads /jffs/netsettings.txt keys {WEPKey,HouseholdID,Channel,PriorityBridge,BonjourName,PrimaryUUID,ForceMeshDisable} via keyval; credcheck substitutes /ramdisk/tmp/netsettings_check.txt. UseSSIDList from /jffs/net/settings/ssidlist.txt (recovery swaps in /var/run/softapssidlist.txt). open mode: ath0 = 10.69.69.1 on channel PARAM2 (default 2412MHz, /jffs/debug/openchannel override) after setmac -L. island = sonosnet mesh without eth. deauth = empty br0 with setmac -S. satellite/sta_and_sat build /var/run/htapsatwpa.conf {ssid,psk,scan_ssid=1,priority=4,bssid?} so the HT satellite STA-joins the primary's hidden AP; sta_and_sat appends the block to the running wpa conf. PrimaryUUID in netsettings => ISHTSATELLITE (athconfig setprimaryuuid+satenable). IS_HT_WIRELESS_PRIMARY arch attr in sonosnet|station mode turns ath1 into the HT AP (setuuid RINCON_<eth0mac>0<Port>, acs, acslmenable, wepkey, hhid). ForceMeshDisable => athconfig blockadvertisedpath 1. PriorityBridge=1 => brctl setbridgeprio 0x7000 else 0x9800; arg2 stp_disable turns STP off. Hostname = BonjourName else IS_BRIDGE?SonosZB:SonosZP. udhcpc is launched -f [-F -W 20 when island] -z (station/satellite/sta_and_sat) -s /etc/dhcp.script -i br0 -w ath0 -h <host> -d access.bestbuy.com; /jffs/debug/static_ipaddr bypasses DHCP; waits up to 60s for /tmp/udhcpc.pid; /jffs/debug/{testpoints.sh,wpa_supplicant.conf,wpa_supplicant,supplicant} debug hooks gated on /proc/sonos-lock/exec_enable.

Resolved: the satellite-add notification to netstartd is a virtual send on the IPC object at this->+0x1a9c via vtable slot +0x34 with first arg (msg type/opcode word) 0x28=40 and empty payload args (r5=0, r6=0) at 0x1034f07c-0x1034f098 inside AddHTSatellite; on failure it logs 'Failed to send IPC message to netstartd to notify about satellite addition'. The notify carries no fields - the peer re-reads state itself

Deepened (netstartd is shipped at wifi/netstartd): its WAC-mode event dispatcher is a 41-entry jump table at 0x10031770 (dispatch fn ~f_1000fce4, cmplwi bound 0x28). Opcode 0x28 shares the arm at 0x1000fd2c with 0x27 - a WAC stop/error event: it checks state flags globals+0x10/+0x2c; if in WAC-timeout it logs 'Ignore WAC Mode stop or error event while in WAC timeout'; if in station mode it logs 'Ignore WAC Mode stop or error event while in station mode'; otherwise in active WAC mode it runs the teardown pair f_1000d774(callback) + f_1000e3f4(state=1) then returns. Sibling arms in the same FSM: 'WAC Mode Credentials have been set', 'WAC provided credentials are bad, restart wacd' (also flushes + restarts), 'ASSERT: Open AP not up after WAC cred check, starting', 'Unexpected event %s in WAC Open state', and WifiFuncsSetStationEnabled/WifiFuncsGetOpenMode on 'ath0'.

Resolved (satellite-add channel): in netstartd's main IPC dispatch (jump table @0x1002f6f4, handler f_1000886c) msg id 0x28=40 maps to the DEFAULT arm 0x10008990 - ignored on /tmp/netstartd.ipc. netstartd opens a second socket /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc ('Failed to init WAC IPC'), so the anacapad satellite-add opcode 0x28 rides the WAC IPC channel whose event FSM jump table (@0x10031770) contains the decoded 0x28 arm shared with 0x27.

cert_layer.files: cert.xml + metadata.txt; "Buffer not sufficient to store entire certificate"; "loading %s (0x%x) took %ums"; tmpfile-rename atomic swap; "failed to load replacement (0x%x)"
cert_layer.layout: On-disk cert store layout proven from f_106b268c (path builder): path = constructJFFSRootPath(buf, mgr, mgr->+0x10a4) + [/ + env] + / + file. mgr->+0x10a4 is the per-identity subdirectory, a ctor arg of f_106b20bc (the certManager store object, vtable 0x10f05130) - the only construction site found passes r4='regdevicecert' from f_105a7034, which f_10645bc8 supplies for the registration-device-cert manager (strings regcert/regdevicecert, callback f_106455e4). env is the deployment environment name resolved via f_10556e10 settings-table entry 0x25 with fallback 'prod' - certs are namespaced per environment so a staging device never loads production certs. Filename thunks: cert.xml via flag=0 (env-qualified), metadata.txt via flag=1 (unqualified) and a second metadata.txt via flag=0 (env-qualified). constructJFFSRootPath is a PLT import so the literal root prefix lives outside anacapad.
cert_layer.files_detail: cert.xml: device/client certificate+key store, loaded at startup ('loading %s (0x%x) took %ums', 0x%x byte size), bounds-checked ('Buffer not sufficient to store entire certificate'), replaced atomically via tmpfile+rename on download ('failed to rename tmpfile', 'failed to load replacement (0x%x)'). metadata.txt: persisted cert download metadata (the DeviceCertInfo requestTimeMS/downloadStatusCode/httpResultCode/previousETag/reason fields) written after each fetch attempt. Root-of-trust chain: server/peer TLS certs are validated by the certval layer ('cert validation for %s (local port %u)', certvalStats) against bundles fetched from /certbundles/v4/trusted_roots.rcb with ETag caching and failure backoff; client-auth uses cert.xml through the KEYCERT identity slots (R_CLIENT_KEYCERT_ID_SONOS, _SONOS_DEVICE, _SONOS_DEVICE_ACCEPT_LEGACY, _SONOS_REGISTERED_DEVICE). /regcert serves DeviceCertInfo XML, /root_cert_bundles serves the installed bundle set.

memory_monitor.name: memmon: memory tracking
memory_monitor.summary: reads /proc/meminfo {MemAvailable,MemFree} + /proc/%s/{statm,cmdline}; logs to /tmp/memorylog/log.%d with .old rotation; "memory report avail=%s free=%s"; "report skipped %s (count: %u)"; fields {memavailable,memfree}; threads memlog/memmon/memory_status

evidence.notes: 105-entry diag-bundle file manifest; ring files are entries 88-95, flag 0x2

resolved_findings: Resolved: merged with memmon - ring format = the /tmp/memorylog 4-file ring + .old copy holding periodic RSS/VSS samples.

Duplicate-record pair memmon/memory_monitor consolidated: both describe the same machinery - periodic /proc/meminfo {MemAvailable,MemFree} reads plus per-process /proc/%s/{statm,cmdline} enumeration, written to the /tmp/memorylog/log.%d ring with .old rotation; report line "memory report avail=%s free=%s" with skip accounting "report skipped %s (count: %u)". Threads: memlog/memmon/memory_status.

Established: the report cadence is 900 s (15 min) - the report fn f_106bbf7c writes *(out)=sonosClockGetTime()+0x384 as the next-report timestamp after emitting 'memory report avail=%s free=%s' (memmon domain). The ring reader is proven: all eight ring files (/tmp/memorylog/log.0-3 and /tmp/memorylog.old/log.0-3, flag 0x2) are literal entries in the 105-entry diagnostic-bundle file manifest at 0x11090228-0x110908b8 {path_ptr, flag, 0, path_ptr} per 16B entry, alongside a command manifest at 0x11090144 ({outfile, flag, command} triples incl. /scanresults <- athconfig scangetresults ath0); the pair is bound by the collection descriptor at 0x11090000 whose scheduler tick f_105e98ec re-arms at +60 s. So the ring feeds the diagnostic bundle, not a crashdump attachment.

mdns.controller: MdnsController ops {register service (twice-guard),unregister,update value (dup-guard),replace values}; failures {registration failure %i,TXTRecord populate %i,update unregistered}
mdns.notes: Failed to dump mDNS state into diagnostic: %i; /status/opt/log/mdnsd.log page + /opt/log/mdnsd.log file
resolved_findings: Resolved: published service = _sonos._tcp. with the 9 TXT keys decoded under mdns_stack; overlaps mdns_device.

Published service set decoded (mdns_device_service.cxx): the device advertises a single _sonos._tcp. service (name built via MdnsDevSvc_ prefix + formatted name, Truncation in formatting service name guard) carrying TXT keys {byebyereason, protovers, minApiVersion, mhhid, hhsslport, variant, mdnssequence, wss, locationid, infohash} - mhhid=household id, hhsslport=household TLS port, wss=websocket endpoint, locationid/infohash=cloud identity, mdnssequence=record epoch. Spotify Connect advertises separately as _spotify-connect (0x10ee4f00); no _http._tcp or _soundtouch types exist in this image. Advertise lifecycle: the RAdvertiser holds back SSDP while transitional (RAdvertiser in transitional state; delaying SSDP advertisments / RAdvertiser stable; running SSDP state machine), emits an advertisingStart report on first send (Ready to send network advertisements), and reacts to MDP flag updates; shutdown paths raise SIGTERM (scheduling deferred shutdown / raising SIGTERM to shutdown anacapa) with /tmp/anacapa-has-run written as the liveness sentinel.

Resolved: the mdnssequence consumer rule is decoded (mdns_discovery.cxx, TXT parse at 0x106bf018): key 'mdnssequence' parsed via paranoid_atoi into u16; missing/unparseable defaults to 0xffff (ori 0xffff sentinel at 0x106bf190); stored into the peer device record +0x5c; the notify path logs 'mdnssequence={old %u new %u}' (0x106bf200) and compares old-vs-new to decide topology re-notification; 'older version or missing keys' TXT records are rejected before comparison.

Resolved: the MdnsDeviceService TXT-record field vocabulary is literal @0x10ef7ae0+ (mdns_device_service.cxx): {_sonos._tcp. service, fields byebyereason, protovers, minApiVersion, mhhid, hhsslport, variant, mdnssequence, locationid, infohash} plus "Truncation in formatting service name" bounds guard. Republish triggers sit in the same TU: "MDP flag update: new flags %x" and the advertiser gate strings "RAdvertiser in transitional state; delaying SSDP advertisments" / "RAdvertiser stable; running SSDP state machine" - so an MDP flag update is a republish/bump trigger.

Deepened (republish diff is a key-exclusion ladder, not flag bits): the republish path ~f_106beae8 enumerates the TXT record via TXTRecordGetCount/TXTRecordGetItemAtIndex and strcmp-ladders each key against the exemption set {vers, bootseq, sslport, hhsslport, hhid, mdnssequence, byebyereason} - each match takes a dedicated early-out (no sequence bump); every other key falls through to the value compare (' Value:' log + 'Error enumerating key %zu in TXT record: %i' on the 'mdns-discover' domain) that drives the mdnssequence update. So the bump trigger is any TXT change outside that 7-key exempt set.

update_coordinator.name: update coordinator
update_coordinator.summary: beginUpdate/beginUpdate called./Update already started.; updateHookJob + upgradeinfo + /var/run; "Current Swgen Min downgrade version %s"; "error updating %s"; "Failed to query cloud settings"; update_coordinator actor; cert.xml+metadata.txt loads "loading %s (0x%x) took %ums"
resolved_findings: Resolved: coordinator-mgr split = the per-player upgrade_mgr daemon does download/flash while the household coordinator orchestrates order via the checkDevicesToUpdate manifest pass; hooks = the pre/post-check callbacks registered on the coordinator.

Coordinator/mgr split proven: update_coordinator is anacapad's in-process policy actor - beginUpdate is single-shot (Update already started. rejects reentry), loads cert.xml + metadata.txt via certmanager for signature verification (loading %s (0x%x) took %ums; Buffer not sufficient to store entire certificate), pulls cloud settings (Failed to query cloud settings), enforces the swgen downgrade floor (Current Swgen Min downgrade version %s; MinVersion: [%s] vs PrevSWGenMinVersion: [%s]), and writes the upgradeinfo file under /var/run. updateHookJob is the deferred launch hook that hands execution to /bin/upgrade_mgr - the coordinator decides/stages, upgrade_mgr does the image work (user_update + auto_update both converge on it). Member updates report error updating %s; downloads ride async_file_downloader {Failed to open/write file, Unexpected response (%d), Cancelled/failed download attempt of file (%s) from url (%s)}. Bonus: the DiagnosticManifest v2.0.0 submission schema {serial_num, swversion, secreg, quarantined, ZPSupportInfo, ZPInfo, LocalUID, IPAddress, SoftwareVersion, QuarantineReason} posts to /v2/diags on the product-diagnostics service.

Deepened (trigger edge): updateHookJob is a job object (ctor f_106b2cb0 registers name 'updateHookJob' + callback pair from arg6 {+8,+0xc} -> job+0x4a8/+0x4ac) constructed by the init fn ~f_1069240x and queued onto the 'asynceventloop' - its run vfunc f_10696e78 sits among the inprocess-event delivery thunks (NetworkIfaceBouncedEvt/NetworkIpAddrAssignedEvent cancellation handlers in the same dispatch block). So the hook fires via the async event queue (event-posted), not a periodic timer; the posting source is the upgrade/auto-update scheduler side.

Secondary availability state enum proven (table @0x10fad750, {name,len,id} stride-12): {1=UNDEFINED, 2=ENABLED_AVAILABLE, 3=ENABLED_UNAVAILABLE, 4=DISABLED_AVAILABLE, 5=DISABLED_UNAVAILABLE, 6=SECONDARY_STATE_IGNORED_BY_CR} - the coordinator tracks each secondary member as {enabled x available} plus an ignored-by-coordinator escape state.

Enqueue site proven: beginSoftwareUpdate (0x1073f1c8) writes /var/run/upgradeinfo, then posts to the global async event loop @0x110978c0 via f_106b0538(loop, job_id=5, arg=1) at 0x1073f464 - job id 5 is the updateHookJob registered at init; the post is the sender edge the residual asked for.

todo: Residual: the metadata XML schema inside <SPDIFTap> (which session/format fields) - the wrapper tag is proven; inner elements are written by the audiotap_manager serializer already covered in audio_taps.
resolved_findings: Resolved: reconciled with audio_taps - the tap is a rolling buffer whose snapshot serializes the buffer verbatim with <SPDIFTap> metadata XML.

Object model resolved (datatap.cxx, datatap tag): RDataTap is the generic capture object - instances are typed by name (rolling_data_tap for the audio taps) and serialize a metadata XML wrapper into the buffer ahead of payload (<SPDIFTap>...</SPDIFTap> for the SPDIF tap; Error: failed to read metadata from buffer! on the parse side). Snapshot dumps the rolling buffer to the versioned file (Datatap snapshot failed after %zu bytes) consumed by the /audio_tap /spdiftap /snapshotspdiftap /downloadspdiftap routes documented in audio_taps. Difference from rolling_data_tap: datatap is the base object (metadata + snapshot); rolling_data_tap is the subtype that keeps the circular audio buffer the snapshot drains.

resolved_findings: Resolved: flag report at %zu sbmt marks the per-submission counter; report writer bundles the dropout counters into the metrics doc uploaded via the shared report channel.

Report assembly proven (dropout_event_logging.cxx, DropoutEventHandler): slots accumulate per-dropout context then submit - flag report at %zu sbmt marks the slot, submit at idx %zu emits it (Took %ld.%06lds to s[ubmit]). Per-entry fields {inputType, GroupRole (grp role chg evt: %u -> %u), corr ctx chg evt: type %u, GCI-but-no-CID state, SatChCount (Sat chs %zu), HtsnkVersion (Sat htsnk ver %u), btRole, pt: %d.%06d vs curr: %d.%06d, GC time: %d.%06d + GCTimeValid, msAfterPt, set pt reached: %s}. Counter rollups: {htsnk_missed_total, htsnk_missed_duration_total, htsnk_late_total, htsnk_strm_reset_duration_total, htsnk_strm_silence_duration_total, htsnk_strm_plc_duration_total} + {n%zu, Last, Tot} numbering - HT-sink missed/late/reset/silence/PLC durations. Slot lifecycle: set slot %zu idx %zu to %s, clr slot at %zu, clr states, slot %zu in use skip incr, incr call: %s, %zu, %zu, ch %zu, %d.%06d, dt unchg - incr ctr, no space in list, set pos aud / pt in fut - inaud, hit uninit at %zu. CID tracking: set cid / clear cid, src=%u / skip clear cid src=%u cur=%u. Debug injection: injectdropout command with {dt, paud, missing dt param} params + Injected dropout error. Submission rides the telemetry channel (telemetry record).

Resolved: slot capacity = 10 - the slot index at this+0xf0 advances via the 0xcccccccd reciprocal trick at 0x103682f0-0x10368328 (mulhwu + r9*10 subtract = next mod 10), giving a 10-slot ring of 0xb8-byte records based at this+0x140. The reason-id namespace is bounded cmplwi 0x4b at 0x10368504 - a 75-entry reason-name table at 0x10ebe60c indexed by event type. 'no space in list' (0x103687cc) is only a log emit when the scan finds no free slot.

Counter-name registry fully recovered: an 80-entry string-pointer table at 0x10ebe20c is the radio-log fault/testpoint counter dictionary, indexed by counter id. Entries 0-32 cover link/stream faults (bt_audio, chsnk_lse/ch_data_full/w_err, chsrc_framer_uflw, htsnk_invld_sntp/late_frames/missed_frames/time_backw/stream_err/stream_uflw/stream_reset_duration/wrong_frame, lla_{bad_parm,fault_err,io_err,mem_err,prep_fail,uflw,unkwn}, mix_in_write_err, mix_sod_{late,lack_data_start,too_far_orig}, mix_thrd_{data_idle,gap}, net_io_noderx_{io,nodata,noframe,noframe_full}, net_io_err_other, net_io_unplayable, sound_wemb_uflw_at_start); entries 33-36 are 'uninit' placeholders; entries 37-52 are the per-stream-type family replicated x4 {init_sync,lack_data_no_drain,read_err_full,read_err_part_data} for stream_{music,tts,chirp,tv}; 53-54 stream_ht_{silence_played,plc_played}; 55-66 the tv_decoder/tvp family {dd,ddp,mat,pcm,dts1..3,dsp_error_dap,asrc_error,dialog_extractor_error,input_error,input_overflow}; 67-73 tvp_stream_{uflw,err,sats_uflw,sats_err,dmix_uflw,dmix_err} + xfade_err; 74 'testpoint' (the set/reset pt counters); 75 'uninit'; 76-78 the aud/paud/inaud slot families matching the 'set pos aud'/'pt in fut - inaud' logs; 79 'uninit'. This closes the counter-vocabulary census: the radiolog counter set is static, not runtime-registered.

resolved_findings: Resolved: migrated account to OAuth, type:%u is the writer - reads the legacy creds, mints the OAuth record, writes the migrated account with the new type tag.

Decision tree decoded: migration runs in phases - built-in accounts first (failed to migrate built-in accounts), then pre-cloud-replication accounts (failed to migrate pre cloud replication accounts). Per-account OAuth path (migrateAccountToOAuth / migrateAccountsToSMAPI / migrateAccountSID): if the existing account is not OAuth the record is reset and retried (sr: expected ouath account; reset to retry migration); retries are counted (sr: retry migration, res=%u, retry=%zu); migration defers until cloud connectivity (sr: delay migration until cloud connection); auth failure aborts per-account (Authentication failed during migration of account sn: %u, res=%u). Guest accounts are a special case (Existing account is not a guest account, migrateGuestAccount failing; Bad guest migration: UDN = %s - UserIDHash = %s). Tombstoned replication accounts migrate distinctly (Migrated tombstoned %s replication account). Anonymous accounts migrate via file rewrite (Unable to write/read file while migrating anonymous accounts). Per-object decisions are logged (Migrating ObjID=%s SN=%u from SID: %u to %u vs Not migrating ObjID=%s SN=%u SID=%u). Migrated credentials land in the same accounts file (Created new accounts file; migrated %d accounts; Migrated Account with SID %u. (%u,%u->%u) shows the (old,new) type transition). Legacy service fixups ride along: Sirius URI, Rhapsody/Pandora object IDs, Pandora built-in (%d,%d->%d), TuneIn stations/shows gated by the enableTuneInMigration feature flag (TuneIn Migration enabled from FCS), and the UMTracking -> userMetricsTracking rename.
Established: phased migration (built-in -> pre-cloud), per-account OAuth decision (reset+retry / cloud-defer / auth-abort), guest and tombstoned special cases, file landing, per-service fixups.

resolved_findings: Resolved: mount helper invocations = kernel mount + reconnect + reattempt counters; strike-out rules = the failure-threshold unmount policy.

Mount protocol handlers bounded by the smb record: kernel CIFS handles share mounts (SMB1-era with NTLMSSP auth) while the sharelist path uses the vendored libsmb2.so.1 userspace client; /tmp/smb/%d_%d names final mounts and /tmp/smb/tmp%d_%u trial mounts. Unmount policy: mounts detach on share removal (localRemoveShare) and when the strike bound trips.

Decoded (trial-mount loop f_1042b2fc+): the strike bound is 3 - literal addi r9,0x3 supplies the %d/%d denominator in 'Trial mount found unsupported protocol: %s (strike %d/%d)' at 0x1042b3d4 and cmpwi 0x3 gates the give-up path at 0x1042b3f0 (-> error 0x8100000d). The protocol-name table is the pointer array at 0x10ecde74 = {LOCAL, HTTP, CIFS, SMB2, SMB3, UNKNOWN} indexed by the trial result code (idx<5 valid).

Resolved: share-table capacity = 16 slots - 'invalid mountID (%d)' fires on cmplwi mountID,0xf (0x10427730/0x104277f0); entries are 0x8e8-byte records at mgr+0x890+mountID*0x8e8 (mulli 0x8e8). Acquire context logs 'invalid mountID (%d) used for %s' under mntmgr domain when id>15.

noderx.summary: indices {ob=outputBuf,lr=lastRead,lcg=lastConsecutiveGood,lrx=lastRx}; flight rec " %u r:%d.%06d s:%c p:%d.%06d"; startup {"Starting up; id:%u, delayPkts:%u, delayFrms:%u","Startup large packet gap:%u, don't NACK",bFinalStartPacket,allowing NACK resend of LCG,ignoring discontig NACK resend,ignoring partial frames}; NACK "out of order packet; send nack immediately" + "NACKed for %u IDs, %u packets, ob/lr/lcg/lrx"; pause/resume {thread pausing/resuming, state validation p/sp/pr/ip}; frame layer {wFirstFrameOffset,wBytesOfDataLeftToRead,pwLen,Playtime} + errors {expected frame not found,frame length conflict,Packet stream framing error,frame too large,bufferNextProtocolFrame WOULDBLOCK/E_WOULDBLOCK,readNextDataBlock timeout,forcing decoder reset}; skipAhead entries {immed,shifted,released blocks,too many}; resync {"resynchronization flushing packets %u-%u",resynchronization message}; "Ignore packet with incorrect protocol version"; "Received dup packet id with different class"/oob/mismatch replace; "RX buffer full"/"RX discontig"; threads {noderx-data,noderx-pause,noderx.rxd.usleep,noderx.loc.usleep}; "failing noderx for io error (c=%u t=%lld)"

evidence.notes: NACK ID array bound 0x1f (31); resend delay formula at 0x1044adbc

resolved_findings: Resolved: protocol = the noderx receive-side of the chsnk sync channel (frame fields match the nodetx NACK/ack grammar); resend window = the ack-bitmap window size.

Protocol role proven: noderx is the member-side receiver of the group-audio node transport - the RX half paired with nodetx (chsrc_chsnk family). It receives the coordinator's frame stream into the output buffer and feeds the audio framer; indices {ob=outputBuf head, lr=lastRead, lcg=lastConsecutiveGood, lrx=lastRx} drive both the NACK window and the flight recorder (" %u r:%d.%06d s:%c p:%d.%06d" rows). NACK policy proven: NACK fires immediately on out-of-order packets (out of order packet; send nack immediately) with batched reporting (NACKed for %u IDs, %u packets, ob/lr/lcg/lrx); resends only cover contiguous data (allowing NACK resend of LCG, ignoring discontig NACK resend, ignoring partial frames) and startup suppresses NACK across the initial gap (Startup large packet gap:%u, dont NACK + bFinalStartPacket + Starting up; id:%u, delayPkts:%u, delayFrms:%u). Gap recovery: skipping ahead from:%u to pid:%u / expected block id %u not found / network failed / read timed out. Pause/resume FSM states {p, sp, pr, ip} validated on transitions (pause/resume state not valid, pausing/resuming with the index set). Frame layer fields {wFirstFrameOffset (vs INVALID_SHORT), wBytesOfDataLeftToRead, prevOffset, wBytesLeft, pwLen, Playtime} with errors {expected frame not found, frame length conflict, Packet stream framing error, frame too large, bufferNextProtocolFrame WOULDBLOCK/E_WOULDBLOCK/skipping ahead}.

Constants decoded (f_1044ac30 sweep): NACK request batch window = 31 IDs max (stack array bound cmplwi 0x1f at 0x1044ad0c, flushed via f_1044ab7c with a 0x80-flagged header); startup gap suppression = lrx-lcg > 10 -> 'don't NACK' (cmplwi 0xa at 0x1044ae3c); resend/retry delay = timevalAddMs(30*(pkts>>3) + 50) ms computed at 0x1044adbc-0x1044add0.

longpress.name: longpress: GC-clone cycling
longpress.summary: GC list {head,tail,current} of cloneable group coordinators; "cycling to %s:%s"/"end of list reached"; tracked GC actions {Adding new GC,Moving GC to head,Removing GC,"Updating last PAUSED/STOPPED GC","Last GC in HH to change playback state is no longer cloneable",Untracked GC action}; "not joinable"
longpress.setup_ready_combo: VOL_UP+VOL_DN combo: each press starts a timer ('VOL_UP starts timer, when pops, switch to setup-ready mode' / 'VOL_DN starts timer...'); holding both pops the timer and the device switches to setup-ready mode ('VOL_UP + VOL_DN timer popped, switching to setup-ready mode' and inverse order): the physical-button path into setup/join flow. Button presses can also tear down grouping: 'Becoming standalone due to button press'.
resolved_findings: Resolved: button handler = the long-press list walk cycling remembered group coordinators (per misc_health decode).

Behavior decoded: long-press on play/pause walks the cloneable-GC list and JOINS the player to the next cloneable group coordinator - cycling to %s:%s moves the device to the next GC's playback session (clone semantics = become a group member playing that GC's queue), end of list reached wraps. The list maintains {head, tail, current} ordering with tracked transitions {Adding new GC, Moving GC to head (most-recent-first), Removing GC, Updating last PAUSED/STOPPED GC, Last GC in HH to change playback state is no longer cloneable, Untracked GC} - recency-ordered so each long-press hops to the next-most-recently-active group.

Resolved: the button-event ids are proven by the emit-name enum (enum_tables.10ef4fc8): BUTTON_PLAYPAUSE_PRESSED=78, BUTTON_PLAYPAUSE_HELD=79, BUTTON_VOL_UP_PRESSED=80, BUTTON_VOL_DN_PRESSED=81, BUTTON_JOIN_PRESSED=82, STATE_BUTTON_MICMUTE_PRESSED=83, plus DIAG_MODE=84; runtime-policy actions occupy 50-76.

Resolved: the cycle action binds event id 79 (BUTTON_PLAYPAUSE_HELD) - the dispatch @0x10863400 compares the event byte *(r31+0x14) against 0x45 (ORIENTATION_VERTICAL) and 0x4f (BUTTON_PLAYPAUSE_HELD); either match runs the walk @0x1086341c which advances list index *(r31+0x10) into the GC array *(r31+0xd4) and calls the join delegate f_108382c4 - long-press play/pause (and orientation-vertical events) cycle the cloneable coordinator list.

tj_wakeup.name: TJ: wake-missing-players + backup
tj_wakeup.summary: async wakeMissingPlayers {task,timer,request,retry TJ,cancel,failure} + "Unexpected WakeOnLANRequestEvent type": WakeOnLAN; "Restoring AVT and track queue"/"Backing up track queue"/"Backing up AVT"; "Chirp setup failed - chirp sender does not exist"; "Setup volume not yet calibrated"; "Unable to play chirp"; refreshMdnsRegistration; /players/ api 1.1.0; settings {R_VolNormMode,R_CrossfadeDuration,R_AirplayIncludeLinked}; manual node engine ctor node version; spotmdns thread
resolved_findings: Resolved: wake trigger = the timed-job expiry firing the AVT restore order {queue restore, volume restore, play resume}.

Wake trigger and retry proven: WakeOnLANRequestEvent arrives with a type field - the worker reschedules per-type (reschedule wake missing players type %d time %ld), runs (async wake missing players ran; type %d time %ld), retries via scheduling retry TJ, and rejects unknown types (Unexpected WakeOnLANRequestEvent type); the task/timer/request triple has {stopped, failed to run, cancelled, failure} lifecycle logs plus shutdown drops (shutting down; droping async wake missing players timer/request). The event sits in the household event vocabulary {DeviceStartupEvent, LocalIpChangedEvent, RequestTVTransitionEvent, WakeOnLANRequestEvent, PortableWifiReconnectEvent, PlaybackCorrelationEvt, HouseholdSettingsChangeEvent, TVInputSelectedEvent, RemoteHTSwapStateChangedEvent (source: %s, swap active: %d, are we satellite: %d), VoiceAccountTransactionEvent, updating boot sequence due to registration event}. Restore order: Backing up track queue + Backing up AVT before the timed job, Restoring AVT and track queue after - AVT restore precedes queue restore completion. Adjacent settings {R_VolNormMode, R_CrossfadeDuration, R_AirplayIncludeLinked}; muse scope scopeMp on /v/players/ v1.1.0; refreshMdnsRegistratio[n] post-wake.

Resolved: WakeOnLANRequestEvent has three valid types {0,1,2} dispatched at 0x103f9a28 (type>2 or unhandled -> 'Unexpected WakeOnLANRequestEvent type'). The reschedule logs are 'reschedule wake missing players type %d time %ld' and 'async wake missing players ran; type %d time %ld' - the retry time is a call-parameter (ms) carried in the event, not a fixed literal.

Resolved: the WakeOnLANRequestEvent handler (0x103f9a20) fully decoded - type 0 -> 'Unexpected WakeOnLANRequestEvent type' + RabortIfUnlocked; type 1 -> delegate vcall f_100d5588(target=this->+0x18f4, &time, player=this->+0x2c); type 2 -> delegate vcall f_100d5598 (same signature); type>=3 -> skips the delegate call entirely. Both delegates write a next-wake time into out (default 0x7fffffff; sentinel 0x8000ffff = do-not-reschedule) then the shared tail logs 'async wake missing players ran; type %d time %ld' and calls f_103f9788(this,&time,type) = 'reschedule wake missing players type %d time %ld'

Resolved (WakeOnLANRequestEvent type semantics): the two delegate vfuncs are thin thunks - type 1 -> f_100d5588 -> f_100d53a8(flag=1), type 2 -> f_100d5598 -> f_100d53a8(flag=0). The shared worker f_100d53a8(target, time*, player, flag) writes 0x7fffffff as the time out-init, then selects the resolver by flag: flag=1 uses f_10749f44 (topology-domain resolver - 'topology' log strings), flag=0 uses f_10742074 (device-registry lookup path). Both converge on the same timed wake-and-retry loop: gettimeofday pacing, 'wake' source tag, {msTTM, msDRP} telemetry counters, and the give-up log 'We timed out on %zu devices after %u attempts'. So type 1 = topology-scoped wake of a household member, type 2 = registry/direct wake - both by the same WoL engine.

todo: Residual: semantic roles of the non-key-backed ht_config members inside +0xe0..+0x195 (internal state fields - latency caches, computed thresholds) - no settings key writes them, so each needs its own producer trace.
resolved_findings: Resolved: candidate ranking = the autoplay table {linked zones -> AutoplayRoomUUID/Volume -> silence gate -> alarm fallback} decoded under autoplay.

Target-selection algorithm proven (media_player_autoplay.cxx, MpAutoPlay_/MpAp domains): on a linein-class source ({object.item.audioItem.linein.homeTheater, .airplay, .bluetooth} + x-sonos-vli URIs with vliType {RCA,...}) autoplay resolves a target: the group coordinator via autoplay couldnt determine coordinator of %s -> AVT control URI via couldnt determine AVT control URI of coordinator %s -> zone control URI via couldnt determine control URI of zone %s; invisible or proto-incompatible members are skipped (Not executing on invisible/node proto incompatible ZP %s). No target = local fallback (lonely local line-in autoplay %s; no autoplay target for %s). Dispatch: for controlURI [%s] for coordinator [%s]. programURI [%s]. %d - %d sends the program URI to http://%s:%u AVT control; autoplay: %d; become gc: %d decides whether the player becomes coordinator. Params {vol, useVol, includeZones} with airplay include zones: %d + AirplayIncludeGroupedEvt; silence gating via autoplay. Ignore Silence Threshold (%d). Spotify sources take the VLI path (autoplay Spotify using VLI / autoplay Spotify SMAPI URI: %s (%d)); alarms handle autoplay %s (alarm: %d, buzzer fallback: %d)... not playing; autoplay_tv covers the HT input; AutoStop called on unhandled URI %s:%s; autoplay room UUID changed to %s retargets on zone change.

Resolved (silence-threshold plumbing, htaudio_autoplay.cxx): the auto-stop silence threshold is a caller-supplied SECONDS argument converted inline to milliseconds (mulli 0x3e8 at 0x107dd480) and stored at object +0xac with an enable byte at +0x99 - logged as 'auto stop %s silence threshold %ums' under the 'autoplay_tv' log domain; the parallel 'auto play %s silence threshold %ums' path handles the play side. The setter's single call site (0x107d6858-0x107d6864) sources the seconds from object field +0x2b4 and the enable from +0x2ad - i.e., the default is populated into those fields by config load, not baked as a literal at the setter.

Resolved (settings-key dispatch): the ht_config key dispatcher @0x101bc458 strcmp's each key and tail-calls a per-key setter: HTASilenceThresholdAutoPlaySec -> f_1023d294 -> f_107c92bc (strtol base-10) -> f_107c91f0 stores parsed seconds at obj+0xe4 (logs 'HT audio base latency %uus' on ht_config - the log string is shared/stale across the setter family); HTASilenceThresholdAutoStopSec -> f_1023d2b4 -> f_107c9db4; HTAZPGroupDelayUsec -> f_1023d2c4 -> f_107c9ecc. So the AutoPlay silence threshold is stored as raw seconds at +0xe4, not ms-converted.

Resolved: the auto-stop silence threshold member is ht_config +0x19c (not +0xe4) - the setter chain f_1023d2b4 -> f_107c9db4 -> strtol base10 -> f_107c9ce0 stores r31 at +0x19c under a mutex (0x10988558 lock / 0x10988984 unlock) and logs "auto stop silence threshold %us" on change; the ht_config ctor seeds +0x19c = 0x258 = 600 (default 600 s) at 0x107c8dc4 and seeds the adjacent member +0x198 = 0xa at 0x107c8dbc, alongside embedded subobject ht_config_sat constructed at +0x1b0.

Resolved: full HTA key->member table via the dispatch chain (strcmp at f_101bc458 -> thunk row at 0x1023d294..0x1023d324 loading the +0x134 ht_config member -> strtol stage-1 -> inner setter): HTAUsecDelay -> +0xe4 (f_107c91f0 store), HTAZPGroupDelayUsec -> +0xf0 (f_107c955c), HTASilenceThresholdAutoPlaySec -> +0x198 (f_107c9ce0, logs 'auto play silence threshold %us' at 0x107c9d58), HTASilenceThresholdAutoStopSec -> +0x19c (f_107c9df8, logs 'auto stop silence threshold %us' at 0x107c9e70, ctor seed 600s). The XML grammar corroborates: <AutoPlay><Mode>/<SilentSeconds> + <AutoPlaySilenceThresh>%us / <AutoStopSilenceThresh>%us state fields.

Full dispatcher census (f_101bc458): the household-settings strcmp ladder covers HouseholdID, MuseHouseholdID, LocationID, EQ, ShadowStorageLimit, ChannelMapSet, ActiveZoneID, ChannelMapSetTime, UnpairedLED/ButtonLock/ZoneName/Icon/Configuration, AutoplayIncludeLinked->stb +0x1aa1, AutoplayVolume->sth +0x1abc, UseAutoplayVolume->stb +0x1abe, AmpOffTimerSec, AutoplayRoomUUID, HTSatelliteDefn, the four HTA* keys, IRRepeater->f_10242d00 (strcmp On -> ioctl on member+0x148 object + string copy at +0x1ec), IRControl, IRLEDFeedback, PrimaryMAC. The non-HTA autoplay keys write the large settings object (+0x1a9x..+0x1abx), NOT the +0xe0..+0x195 ht_config member range - so the four HTA* keys are the only key-backed writes into that window; the rest of +0xe0..+0x195 is internal ht_config state.

todo: Residual: which measured quantity feeds the mean (the r28 sample provenance) and the concrete predicate operand the mean is compared against for the bitrate step - the accumulator math is proven, the sample source is a runtime member read.
resolved_findings: Resolved: DS-selection = the rung switcher emits New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d on a successful switch; on ladder exhaustion it reports Unable to select another DS and either waits to fetch new playlist or fetches now depending on urgency; InitFramerForTrackList failure is a distinct exhaustion path; state is dumped via <ABRState>/<ABREvents numEvents=%u> diagnostics.

DS-selection predicate decoded (literal block 0x10ed3xxx-0x10ed4xxx): each data source is ranked by a happiness test - happy (a > %.2lf): %d %d compares measured fetch rate a against a threshold, with a saturated-buffer override happy (saturated): %d %d; hysteresis via was happy: %d / unhappy: %d counters plus Underruns %u accounting; rate update: a=1 (was %.2lf) resets the estimator. Bitrate switching logs New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d and persists Last estimated bitrate %u (Reset ABR state: start bitrate %u). The failure ladder per DS: fetch failed: 0x%08x (%ld buffer) -> Unable to select another DS, waiting to fetch new playlist -> playlist-level ladder (Timed out looking for playlist, Too many empty playlists, Switching source due to empty playlists rc=%d) -> track-level ladder (track failed 0x%08x, Unable to find playable track, Track failure with no time to recover, Unable to select another DS, fetching new playlist now, Attempting to switch source due to InitFramerForTrackList failure). Prebuffer gate: prebuffering %u bytes within %ld msec; URIs for %g seconds, wake up in %d paces the playlist refresh. Codec filtering uses the mp4a.40. prefix plus a URI version regex /v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(-[a-zA-Z]+)?(\+[a-zA-Z.]+)?([?#/]|$). Status page emits <ABRState Name="ABR State"> with <NodeTXBuffer>%.3lf sec</NodeTXBuffer> and <ProcessRate>%.0lf bps</ProcessRate>.

Resolved: the happy predicate implementation (0x10481b30, logs 'happy (a > %.2lf): %d %d' at 0x10482010 and 'happy (saturated)' sibling) - the estimator a is SPE double math (efdcfs int-to-double, efdmul, efdadd, efddiv around 0x10481f50-0x10481f88) and the threshold is loaded via evldd from the selector object (r31+0x40-class field), NOT a rodata literal - it is a runtime-initialized tunable field. The two trailing %d args are sp-stored counters. So the numeric threshold lives in the object's init config, same boundary class as other tunables.

Corrected (+0x40 member is a running mean, not a threshold): the selector object's +0x40 double is a cumulative mean accumulator updated per sample by a read-modify-write pair at f_10481b30 (nextBitrate path): evldd r27,0x40(r31); efdctsi on count n and n-1; efdmul (n-1)*acc; efdadd +sample(r28); efddiv /n; evstdd back to 0x40(r31) - i.e. m'=(m*(n-1)+x)/n (0x10481f6c-0x10481f8c). Companion double constants in the TU's rodata band at 0x10ed3890-0x10ed38c0: {2.5, 2.0, 1.1920929e-7 (FLT_EPSILON), 80.0, 50.0, 0.7, 1.5} plus 3.0 at 0x10ed31b8, loaded via evlddx for the bitrate predicate math.

todo: Established: signed /devmode.bin statement blob, per-statement persistence policy, R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL capability, x-rincon-enc3 wrapping, listener fan-out.
resolved_findings: Resolved: internals = the devmode toggle writing conf/rdmconfig + conf/rdmlocation; gate call sites = the per-route flag checks on the admin/debug surface.

devmode = a signed statement system (devmode.cxx): a /devmode.bin blob (fetched as debug/devmode.bin, staged via /tmp/devmode.tmp.bin) carries statements formatted 0x%s %d.%d-%d.%d (statement id + supported version range). Statements can be persistent or temporary - persistence is restricted per statement (R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL may not be persisted; Removing persistent statement with R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL) so the SSH-pubkey-install capability only ever applies to the running boot. Changes fan out to listeners and processes (Failed to notify listeners/processes about the change). Blob is x-rincon-enc3 wrapped (signed/encoded). So devmode = a secure policy door where a signed blob enables specific capabilities (e.g. SSH pubkey install) without an open flag file.

Resolved: the x-rincon-enc3 verifying algorithm is RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 - the libsonoscrypto verifier imports mbedtls_rsa_rsassa_pkcs1_v15_verify directly, and the parse+verify entry (ZZ0137) decodes a byte-swapped header with magic check cmpwi 0x1E71 before delegating to the RSA verify helpers ZZ0068/ZZ0064. The PEM key path is a caller-supplied arg to the key loader ZZ0053 (not a compiled-in filename).

Key selection proven: ZZ0053 (libsonoscrypto 0x6318) takes a key-container blob pointer, not a file path - it parses a magic-checked header (XOR-magic 0x779B99CA at blob+0, byte-swapped fields) and selects numbered signing keys ({Unknown %s signing key!, %s signing key %u is revoked!, %s signed with key %u} vocabulary). There is no PEM/key-file literal in the image - verifying key material is delivered inside the signed container itself.

Resolved: the uploader identity chain - emit arg pUploader (r4) = *(tracker+0x2c0), installed under the +0x2c8 lock by setter f_105876ac, whose sole caller (0x10199c70, boot-time zone-player wiring) passes member +0x118 of the Meyers singleton at .data 0x110a5448 (ctor f_10559024, destructor f_10559b3c via __cxa_atexit). The CrAssoc consumer is therefore the context singleton's +0x118 uploader object, not a registered event-bus subscriber - the CrAssoc name literal has only the one emitter reference at 0x105879cc.

Negative evidence: the 0x110a5448 uploader singleton lives in .bss (0x1109b000..0x110c9eb8) - no pointer word or code address-formation to it exists anywhere in the image, so the object is reached only via runtime-installed pointers/SDA-relative addressing whose anchor is initialized at startup. audio_fifo.summary: records with {pos,range}; writes {"Advance write to next record","Rejecting write, as provided offset %zu != %zu (pending)","not enough fifo records","truncated write","Audio fifo records reset"}; discontinuity {"Discontinuity @ offset %zu in record %zu (expecting: %zu)","*** Too many discontinuities"}; reads {"Consumed contiguous samples (%zu - %zu)","Advance read to next contiguous record","Read %zu bytes from record","No bytes to read from fifo... EOF","audio fifo read at boundary eof","consumed exactly to the eof marker","reached logical boundary","already has pending offset"}; prebuffer {"prebuffering... (used/prebuffer)","Waited %ums for audio from the eSDK","Finished prebuffering in %u ms (st,flush)","prebuffering elapsed %u ms (used/free)","exit waiting for audio, not rendering"}: Spotify eSDK feed
todo: Established: {pos,range} record model, offset-mismatch write rejection, discontinuity taxonomy, Too many discontinuities -> drop pending + re-anchor reset.
resolved_findings: Resolved: Too many discontinuities triggers the FIFO reset path - drops pending segments and re-anchors the consumer to the next produced frame.

Resolved: afifo layout (audio_fifo.cxx) - byte ring bounds at +0x8/+0xc (capacity = end-start), used-byte counter +0xfc, flag bytes {+0xf8 eof, +0xf9 flush/discard, +0xfa rendering}, a second window pair +0x100/+0x104/+0x108/+0x10c/+0x110, 0x18-byte record array at +0x114 indexed by +0x118, pending boundary record +0x198 (-1=none), +0x19c flag. Record list exhausts -> '*** not enough fifo records to handle this write'; write overflow -> 'truncated write!'. Boundary EOF markers support 'audio fifo read at boundary eof'/'consumed exactly to the eof marker' and logical boundary at offset N. eSDK producer path logs 'Waited %ums for audio from the eSDK (fifo used: %zu)'; prebuffer completes with 'Finished prebuffering in %u ms (st: %d, flush: %d), fifo used: %zu / %zu'. Constant 0x7a120 (~500KB headroom term) appears in the used/total calc at 0x105899d4-0x105899e4.

Resolved: afifo ctor f_1058924c (vptr 0x10ef04d8, log domain audiofifo, file audio_fifo.cxx) has exactly two instantiation sites and both pass capacity 0x40000 (256 KiB): spotsmapicontrol ctor 0x102233b0 embeds the afifo at +0xb8 (call at 0x102234ac, r5 = addis 0x4 = 0x40000 at 0x10219a18) and RSpotifyAudioInput ctor 0x104db630 embeds it at +0x288 (call at 0x104db7b8, r6 = 0x40000 at 0x10219900). The ctor stores the capacity arg at both +0x8 and +0xc, points +0x114 at the object itself, and initializes a FIXED 5-element embedded record array at +0x120 via a mtctr 5 loop (0x18-byte records ending at +0x198) - record count is a compile-time 5, not a ctor arg.

Resolved: ctor arg r4 (stored via the embedded window subobject at +0x4, sibling pair +0x8/+0xc seeded from r5) is the byte-ring backing-store base pointer supplied by the caller. Call census over the whole afifo module (0x10588600-0x10589600) shows NO call to malloc/realloc/calloc/free (imports resolved via .dynsym: malloc=0x11099628, realloc=0x11098418, calloc=0x11099230, free=0x110991a0 - none referenced) - the ring memory is allocated by each owner (spotsmapicontrol / RSpotifyAudioInput), so no lazy first-write allocation exists. Reset/flush path at 0x10588aa8 proven: under the +0x40 lock it re-anchors +0xc=*(+0x8), clears +0x10/+0x14, resets the record container at +0x114, sets EOF flag +0xf8=1, writes +0x198=-1 (write-record pointer reset), clears +0x19c, then signals the +0xa8 condvar.

Resolved: the accept predicate is f_10660e58 over {incoming ver r6, local ver r4, source-id string r5}: {if ver==-1 (unset sentinel): accept iff local==-1 AND strcmp(source,local)<0; else unsigned compare - accept iff ver>local; ver==local falls through to the same strcmp(source,local)<0 tiebreak; ver<local rejects}. Job arbitration decoded (extaudiosrc_playid tags): two queues - playStream (immediate, skipping stream due to exclusivity when a non-shareable type is playing) vs playDeferredStream (deferred j:%zu d:%zu counts, bounded by too many deferred jobs! [%u]). Clip-type enum complete {COMMON, AUDIOCLIP, AVT_HACK, ALEXA_TTS, ALEXA_WELCOME, ALEXA_FAILURE, ALEXA_ALERT, GOOGLE_MEDIA, GOOGLE_ALARM, GOOGLE_TTS, SPS, SVE_TTS, VOCAL_GUIDANCE, ALERT, SETUP_CHIRP, DISCOVERY} each carrying an interrupt flag (processing type %d (intr=%d)). Job lifecycle: queuing job %u (total=%zu) -> playing job %u -> WaitForComplete (state=%d, term=%d) -> removing job %u (a:%d) -> done processJob (state=%d, jobs=%zu); defects logged as playing job %u is missing! / current job %u gone. Per-job volume override with ramp syntax [from, to - target over %ums] or fixed [a, b]. Decode constraints: stereo-only (unsupported channel count > 2: %zu), decoder abort honored (decoder flagged playback stop), start-time resolution required (failed to get start time (offset %u), aborting / new offset %u), zero-length frames dropped (Unexpected zero len frame).

Resolved: complete job-type name table @0x10ec0000 (18 rows): {DISCARDED, COMMON, AUDIOCLIP, CHIRP, AVT_HACK, ALEXA_TTS, ALEXA_WELCOME, ALEXA_FAILURE, ALEXA_ALERT, GOOGLE_MEDIA, GOOGLE_ALARM, GOOGLE_TTS, SPS, SVE_TTS, VOCAL_GUIDANCE, ALERT, SETUP_CHIRP, DISCOVERY}; the "processing type %s %d (intr=%d)" intr byte is a per-JOB flag (*(job+4)), not a type property.

Resolved: exclusivity is driven by job flag bit 0x10 @0x1037841c - when the incoming job carries the exclusive bit and a non-shareable type is playing, playStream logs "skipping stream due to exclusivity" and drops it; otherwise the job queues. There is no static per-type preempt matrix: the preempt-vs-queue-vs-skip decision is {job flags bit0x10, current playing job type} at runtime.

Partial: calculateVolume (f_1039dda4) loads its bound constants from globals 0x10ec3998 (float 100.0) and 0x10ec399c (float 0.0) - the 0..100 normalization/clamp endpoints selected on the ng halfword test; the result is roundf()'d. Log format 'calculateVolume %s: sg:%.4f ng:%u sv:%u nv:%.4f' confirms {sg=scale, ng=new-group, sv=source-member, nv=new-member} operand roles.

Resolved: the sg weighting is SPE embedded-float (e500v2 EFS ops decoded manually: opcode-4 family). At 0x1039ddbc the routine computes a linear interpolation nv = ((cap - sg) * (hi - lo)) / (hi - sg) + lo as: efssub r6=r10-r9; efssub r10=r10-r8; efssub r9=r7-r9; efsmul r10=r9*r10; efsdiv r9=r10/r6; efsadd r31=r9+r8; then roundf(r31) and srwi r3,16 (Q16->int). Inputs converted by efscfsi (signed) and efscfui (unsigned); bound constants loaded as ints from rodata 0x10ec3998/0x10ec399c (branch-selected at 0x1039ddd4). Iterates member records at stride 0x694 with u16 field +0x68e; logs 'calculateVolume %s: sg:%.4f ng:%u sv:%u nv:%.4f' under 'grc'.

Resolved (member-record operands): calculateVolume (f_1039dda4) takes r4 = a member record in the 0x694-stride snapshot array and r5 = the group target volume ng; it reads sv = the u16 at record+0x68e (the snapshot volume - written at snapshot time alongside +0x690 by the 'snapshot %s: %u (was %u)' pass at 0x1039e5f4 and refreshed at 0x1039e9a8, so +0x68e=snapshotVol and +0x690=currentVol/setVol), loads the bound constants 100.0 (0x10ec3998) or 0.0 (0x10ec399c) selected by the +0x68c flag halfword test (fixed-volume members take the 0.0 scale path), then computes nv in e500 SPE float regs, logs 'calculateVolume %s: sg:%.4f ng:%u sv:%u nv:%.4f' with stw r30(ng)@+0x8 and sth sv@+0xc, and returns roundf(nv) >> 16. Member record tail: +0x68c = state/flag halfword (bit0 = update-in-progress, top 2 bits = state class via srwi 2 ==3 check), +0x692/+0x693 = flag bytes.

Resolved: the calculateVolume clamp endpoints are proven rodata float constants - lo=0.0f (.rodata 0x10ec399c, loaded at 0x1039dddc) and hi=100.0f (0x10ec3998, loaded at 0x1039dea4) bracketing the SPE float sequence; the group volume is clamped to the 0-100 scale.
