resolved_findings: Resolved: engine overview written from sub-blocks - dispatch (route->handler), type_registry (spec-pair index), upnp_bridge (15 services x 4 verbs), command_format, client_auth/http_auth, namespaces, playervolume.

Unified engine writeup: the muse layer is a JSON-RPC-style command bus over WSS (lechmere) and local HTTP routes. Commands arrive as JSON arrays [header, body] (command_format) parsed by rapidjson (failed to parse json body (offset: %u)); dispatch resolves {ns=v%u/%s, cmd=%s} through per-namespace actors (RZPMuseActor - missing/uncreated actor errors name the registration) then validates params against the spec-pair table emitting MISSING_VALUE/UNEXPECTED_TYPE/range-coerce errors. The type_registry is a 203-entry alphabetical spec-type name table (0x10f975c0-0x10f98568) - {accessorySwap, accessPolicyControl, alarmList, authzPolicyKeyLechmere, batteryCells, microphoneSwitch, waterState, poeState, wiredSubStatus, chirpRequest, cloudRegistrationStatus, diagnosticSubmissionMetadata, edidStatus...} indexing spec objects by ordinal. Auth runs two layers: client_auth (wssmtls/httpsmtls schemes, audience v2.api.smartspeaker.audio, credentials {apikey, guest_token, guest_token_pin}, policy-key length cap, API key changed [%.8s] tracking) and http_auth (challenge {private, public, realm, error_description, nonce, Basic}; OAuth {invalid_request, invalid_token, insufficient_scope, service_unavailable}; denied/403-503 results; the 8-field Muse auth result log). The upnp_bridge maps v1/{players,households}/.../upnp{Service}[/subscription[/{logicalSID}]] onto call/subscribe/renew/unsubscribe verbs across 15 UPnP services - muse is the cloud-facing shadow of the local UPnP surface. Namespaces span {audioClip, householdUpdate, management, musicServiceAccounts, pinewood, platformInternal, positioning, roomDetection, soundSwap, systemReporting, systemTime, virtualRemoteControl} + settings:* + upnp:*.

Command envelope pinned by parser errors: the wire command is a JSON array [header, body] (muse command must be formatted as an array containing a header object followed by a body object; missing the body object; failed to parse json body (offset: %u)). Token audiences: v1.api.smartspeaker.audio and v2.api.smartspeaker.audio; credential types {apikey, mtls, guest_token, guest_token_pin}; authz policy-key size bounded (Policy key permissions length exceeds maximum size!).

Resolved: the complete namespace-name literal table (contiguous rodata 0x10f96d6c-0x10f9706c) = 41 entries: {audioClip, householdUpdate, management, musicServiceAccounts, pinewood, platformInternal, positioning, roomDetection, soundSwap, svc, systemReporting, systemTime, virtualRemoteControl} top-level; settings:{accessorySettings, business, frontierLlms, global, playback, playerBasic, playerLineIn, playerUI, positioning, preferences, prodashboard, security, video} (13); upnp{AlarmClock, AudioIn, AVTransport, ConnectionManager, ContentDirectory, DeviceProperties, GroupManagement, GroupRenderingControl, HTControl, MusicServices, Queue, RenderingControl, SystemProperties, VirtualLineIn, ZoneGroupTopology} (15). The registration fn f_109eb04c (logs "Namespace may be missing actor (%s)" when the record's actor slot is null) binds each name to an actor object installed at runtime by setupWholeDevicePointers - no static {name,actor} pair table exists (zero .data.rel.ro pointer records for these literals).

resolved_findings: Resolved: refresh scheduler = the device_auth FSM {expiry lookahead -> refresh -> cache}; token file = the cached credential under the token store.

Refresh mechanics decoded (cqatrs_tx/cloudqueue_tr threads): tokens are per cloud-queue account keyed on account serial number (acct. sn. %u); the persisted token loads via using token from file for acct. sn. %u. Refresh runs through UPnP - Refresh token failed with upnp result: %d and Could not find SD, sid=%u show the refresh calls a UPnP service on the coordinator/peer. FSM: requesting new token refresh sync -> requesting token refresh sync %u %d -> %d -> need to wait for token refresh -> waiting for token refresh completion -> waiting for refresh tx complete -> Token refresh succeeded. Beginning retry; wait timeouts (wait for tx ... timed out) and missing entries (expected entry ... not found to complete tx / not found waiting for tx) bound each state. Scheduling uses token expiry: Attempting to refresh token (hrs=%d te=%d) - hours-until-expiry and expiry fields drive proactive refresh; last refresh token for load timed out / no last refresh token time cover cold-start. On success the queued action retries (Beginning retry).

Resolved: the persisted token lives inside the shared accounts store, not a separate token file - the FSM logs 'using token from file for acct. sn. %u' per account serial, and the accounts layer ('accounts.xml' literal + zpserviceaccounts.cxx + accountReplication) owns the file. Cloud/muse X-Sonos family: auth/identity {X-Sonos-Api-Key, X-Sonos-Mac, X-Sonos-Serial, X-Sonos-Udn, X-SONOS-DEVICEID, X-Sonos-DeviceCert, X-Sonos-User-Id/UserId, X-Sonos-User-Role, X-Sonos-Id-Hash, X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION, X-SONOS-INFOHASH, X-SONOS-MDPMODEL, X-SONOS-SERVICETYPE}; household {X-Sonos-Household-Id, X-Sonos-Muse-Household-Id, X-Sonos-MuseHouseholdId, X-Sonos-Muse-Api}; request plumbing {X-Sonos-Corr-Id, X-Sonos-Denylisted, X-Sonos-ErrorType, X-Sonos-Type, X-Sonos-Accept-Language, X-Sonos-Context-TimeZone, X-Sonos-Diagnostics-Api-Key}; firmware {X-Sonos-Firmware, X-Sonos-SWGen, X-Sonos-LatestSWGen (upgrade-check query/response pair)}; playback/cloud-queue {X-Sonos-Playback-Id, X-Sonos-GroupAttribute, X-Sonos-GroupCapability, X-Sonos-MS-Sig, X-Sonos-MAID, X-Sonos-VClockCloud (vector clocks), X-SONOS-SESSIONSECONDS/SESSIONRETRIES}; sync X-Sonos-Latency (the 58-char colon-hex record parsed by sonos_hex_blob_line); telemetry X-Sonos-MessageType: product-data-telemetry. Tunnel headers: x-sonos-upnp-tunnel + x-sonos-upnp-loopback-token + x-sonos-target-udn + X-SONOS-TARGET-UDN (UPnP-over-TLS member-call routing: verb carried by x-sonos-method, URI by x-sonos-uri, per the upnp_eventing LOBS framing). Scheme family on the URI side: x-sonos-http/https (auth variant x-sonos-auth-https%s#%04x-%u), x-sonos-vli:%s:%u,%s, x-sonos-htastream, x-sonos-mms, x-sonos-dock, x-sonos-spotify, x-sonos-clone-gc, x-sonos-gc-cleared-content, x-sonos-sync-method: full, and the SMAPI URI family x-sonosapi-{radio (ST:%s?sid=%d&flags=%x [&sn=%d]), iqradio, show, stream, rtrecent, hls, hls-static} plus x-sonosprog-{http,mms,spotify}.

Resolved: the replicated-document receiver consumes a 5-header strncasecmp ladder in one function (f_10653ec0..0x10654114): X-RINCON-CONTENT-VERSION (match->flag bit store), X-RINCON-LAST-UPDATE-DEVICE (->0x106540b8), X-RINCON-CONTENT-FORMAT (->0x1065400c), CONTENT-ENCODING (->0x106540d8), X-RINCON-SIGNATURE (->0x1065406c). All five headers are matched prefix-wise with trailing ": " in a single scan - so the signed replication POST carries {content-version, last-update-device, content-format, content-encoding, signature} as its header contract.

resolved_findings: Resolved: consolidated - feature_flag_registry holds the ~48 key registry, feature_config holds the fetch path, feature_flags is the umbrella; gate sites = the per-key readers.

Three-record consolidation complete: feature_flags (the enable*/disable* boolean vocabulary read at init from settings) + feature_flag_registry (the featureConfig*/lechmere-delivered channel with per-flag getter accessors) + feature_config (the fetch/persist path) are three views of one flag plane. Delivery splits in two: settings-local booleans read at init (enablePitchfork, enableSemiSleep, featureConfigSemiSleep, semiSleepConfig family proven at their gate sites) vs cloud-delivered flags riding the feature-config channel (modFetchFeatureConfiguration in the mDNS-era block; the feature-config ws service name). Gate pattern: each flag gets a getter (accessor returning the zp+MdpFlags/feature byte) and call sites test-and-branch; service/endpoint registration is the dominant consumer (audio-in flag gates /AudioIn/Control, QPlay gates the capability element).

Resolved (todo was stale): the per-flag reader census is complete - all ~78 keys across both tables (featureConfig* family at 0x10f97ab4, enable*/scalar family at 0x10f9bedc) are xref-mapped to their read sites, concentrated in the config-loader region 0x10a58xxx with the HT tuning cluster at 0x10a63xxx-0x10a65xxx.

todo: Residual: the shutdown ORDER (which subsystems quiesce first per reason) - reasons map to emitters cleanly; the sequencer step list is the same FSM data as the idle_shutdown path.
resolved_findings: Resolved: reasons = {sleeping, unknown, upgrade} + the idle-shutdown emitters; the shutdown sequencer input = the reason string on the power-manager API.

Reason-to-emitter map (9-value enum at ~0x10ef33a4, emitted via SPID KVPair serialization): APICall = SOAP/muse shutdown action (DeviceProperties PowerOff/Reboot path); APIShutdown = the API-verb variant (cloud-triggered); UserSuspend = physical suspend gesture (button hold / standby); UserShutdown = UI-initiated power off; PartnerDisappeared = bonded-zone partner lost (stereo/sat partner vanished mid-session); Recovery = recovery-mode entry; BluetoothConnection = BT-driven power event (dead on model 9 - no BT); CriticalShutdown = hardware-fault shutdown (thermal/battery critical, the hw:st fault path); UnknownShutdown = fallback when no specific reason was recorded. The sequencer input is dpUpdateIdleState - the idle evaluator recomputes IsIdle on LineInStateChangedEvent/ReplicatedSettingsChangedEvent and escalates to the reasoned shutdown path. Adjacent decode: EnetPorts XML <Port port=%d><Link>%d</Link><Speed>%d%s</Speed> per /sys/class/net/eth0 + eth%u naming, EthPrtStats counters {rxPackets, txPackets, rxBytes, txBytes, rxErrors, rxDropped, txDropped, multicasts, collisions}, EthIntrf errors {lngthErr, ovrFlwErr, crcErr, frmeErr, fifoErr, missedErr, RxDtlErr, abrtErr, crErr, hrtBeatErr, wndwErr, TxDtlErr}, battery fields {RawBattPct, BattPct, BattChg, BattTmp, BtSrcName}.

resolved_findings: Resolved: session FSM = VLI session lifecycle {start link, stream, suspend, end} riding the spotify delegation state.

Session lifecycle proven (spotify_vli.cxx, RSpotifyVLIControl, spotify_md domain): the VLI session FSM calls into the Spotify source on transitions - onVirtualLineInSuspendSession / onVirtualLineInStartAudio / onVirtualLineInStopAudio / onVirtualLineInPlayModesChanged (matching the TXST ops START/SUSPEND_SESSION + START/PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING). Cookies are a per-session generation counter guarding stale control: each op logs %s:%d calling onVirtualLineIn*() cookie %d and old-vs-new mismatch discards (spotify old cookie: %d new: %d, Ignoring stale stopSession due to cookie mismatch: %d != %d). During delegation the FSM suppresses all eSDK callbacks (Ignoring audio flush/track changed/seeks (pos %u)/pause/became inactive/volume change while setting state / delegating, isPlaying set to %d) - the delegation handoff is atomic wrt player-visible events. Selection emits Spotify eSDK source selected, isDelegating %d, isActive %d / not selected e=0x%08x / Source Deselected, from sender %d. Metadata flows through the VLI metadata channel: MetadataChanged {track, artist, album, playback_source_uri, bitrate} + Next Metadata {track, artist, album} as R_SPOT_EVT_METADATA_CHANGE.

Cookie generation proven: f_10686ed8 is a lock-free atomic increment (lwarx/stwcx retry loop) on a shared process-global u32 at .bss 0x110a9504 - no mask/mod, so wrap is natural at 2^32 and there is no explicit collision policy; staleness is pure equality check ('Ignoring stale stopSession due to cookie mismatch: %d != %d', 'spotify old cookie: %d new: %d' on select).

resolved_findings: Resolved: hm:// binding = the hermes transport on its socket layer; rate limiting documented in the sub-block.

Identified: hermes is the Spotify eSDK Mercury client (esdk/src/hermes.c) - the Spotify Connect control protocol. Mercury framing: HermesHeader decode (Failed to decode HermesHeader: %s), request line id %u method %d uri %s %d bytes with methods {SEND, UNSUB, GETX} and MIME vnd.spotify/mercury-mget-request; push frames log Got hermes push from %s / Got hermes uri %s status_code %d; defragmentation buffer reassembly (Defragmentation buffer size %d, cannot fit extra %d bytes (max size: %d) / Could not fit packet to defragmentation buffer, clearing the buffer). The hm:// scheme roots are Spotify hwptp (hardware player transport protocol = Connect): hm://hwptp/v1/devices + /tsv + hm://hwptp/v2/resolve/%s/%d/%s (context resolve); device topics %s/devices/%s/{state, state_conflict, volume, play, set_shuffle, set_repeat, pull_playback, queue}; media ops %s/{content_encryption_key/%s, cache_key, offline/restrictions} with {random, checksum, encryption} fields. Rate limiting is server-driven: Request to %s failed with %d Too many requests / %d Service unavailable (%d) / Spotify-Unavailable-For header / Rate limiting active, and set to %llu ms / Message not sent: rate limited for %llums more / Rate limiting deactivated; timeout assert timeout <= 255. sp_* hex ids are Spotify device/session identifiers.

Resolved: Mercury frame payloads are protobuf, not a fixed-layout header - the HermesHeader decode runs through f_10d2a228 ("Failed to decode HermesHeader: %s" @0x10d43d44) into a decoded-message buffer (+0x50), with uri read from +0xd4 and status_code from +0x1dc of the decoded struct; logging "Got hermes uri %s status_code %d" / "id %u method %d uri %s %d bytes"; defragmentation buffer with max-size guard ("Defragmentation buffer size %d cannot fit extra %d bytes (max size: %d)"); send path rate-limits ("Message not sent: rate limited for %llums more" / "Rate limiting deactivated"); UNSUB method literal present; mget content-type "vnd.spotify/mercury-mget-request".

HermesHeader decode binding located: entry f_10d2a228 returns the descriptor-table pointer at 0x110bdcd0 (r3 = 0x110c-0x2330) and the frame decode writes into the decoded struct at this+0x6f8; the nanopb tag table consumed by pb_decode carries the field numbers - uri lands at struct +0xd4 and status_code at +0x1dc (the "Got hermes uri %s status_code %d" read-back). The proto field numbers are the descriptor tags, recoverable from the nanopb field table for this message.

Responsibility diff vs the cert family (account_cert_lifecycle): certmanager = the generic key/cert plumbing (file validation {BAD_FILE,BAD_KEY,BAD_CERT,BAD_ISSUE_DATE}, issuance); regdevicecert = the registration cert carrying the device SonosID (gates token generation); devicecertmanager = the household-scoped device cert - it validates the cert against the household and user (error taxonomy adds MISMATCH_ENV, MISMATCH_ISSUER, MISMATCH_HHID, MISMATCH_USER, not_present) and ships the X-Sonos-Muse-Household-Id + X-Sonos-Denylisted headers on requests. Scheduling cert refresh job); Retrieved manufacturing data: %s covers the mfg data fetch; files are generated lazily (file not available yet, generated on demand).

The request ships X-Sonos-Muse-Household-Id with the household id; the response is checked for header 'X-Sonos-Denylisted' == 'true' which sets state 'denylisted' on the manager. The download is staged to '<certdir>.tmp' (sonosMkDirRecursive + strlcat '.tmp') then committed. Sibling path literal proven: the ROOT cert bundle job (rootcerts_download, CertBundleDownloader block 0x10ef0bcc) downloads literal path '/certbundles/v4/trusted_roots.rcb' with retry log '%zu consecutive cert fetch failures. fd_event.name: fdevent epoll wrapper
fd_event.summary: ops {fdevent.signal.write,fdevent.wait.poll,fdevent.check.poll,fdevent.reset.read,removeFd,waitForEvent}; EventSync %s; epoll {create1,ctl,wait} errors incl "unsupported flags","already monitored","exceeded the fd capacity of %d"

evidence.notes: ctor stores r4 -> +0x90; slot array +0x98 memset 0x300 = 24x32B

resolved_findings: Resolved: capacity constant = the exceeded the fd capacity of %d literal; registrants = the {fdevent.signal/write, wait.poll, check.poll, reset.read, removeFd, waitForEvent} ops + EventSync + epoll trio.

epoll wrapper fully enumerated (literal block 0x10ef40xx): ops {addFd,removeFd,waitForEvent} over epoll_{create1,ctl,wait}; thread names fdevent.{signal.write,wait.poll,check.poll,reset.read} form a self-pipe poll loop; EventSync %s syncs state; error taxonomy covers %s epoll_create1 error errno %d, unsupported flags %u, trying to add fd %d, %d already monitored, exceeded the fd capacity of %d, adding fd %d 0x%08x, epoll_ctl error fd %d errno %d, trying to remove %d, removing %d 0x%08x, epoll_wait %d errno %d, epoll_wait error fd %d events 0x%04x but not in list, called with no events to wait on. This record duplicates fd_event - same machinery.

Established: the capacity bound is dual - the printed %d is the per-instance ctor arg stored at obj+0x90 (fdevent ctor f_105c4824 stores r4), but the hard ceiling is the fixed inline slot array: memset(obj+0x98,0,0x300) = 24 slots x 32B, initialized to -1 by a ctr=0x18 fill loop at 0x105c48a0, epoll fd at +0x398. Effective capacity = min(configured, 24).

Resolved: fdevent ctor f_105c4824 caller census complete - exactly 4 instantiation sites {0x104a9118, 0x107f0d3c, 0x10d5c700, 0x10d5c838}; all four pass the capacity in r4 as a caller-computed value (r26/r27 chains - no immediate anywhere), so per-registry bounds are set by each owner's own field and the claim stands proven, not assumed.

CORRECTION: the fdevent ctor arg r4 stored at obj+0x90 is the object NAME string, not a capacity - the ctor prints it via "EventSync %s" (%s fmt at 0x105c4878). Call-site provenance: site 0x107f0d3c passes the bss singleton pointer 0x11097a60 = literal "mixthrd"; site 0x104a9118 passes a stack string r1+0x30; sites 0x10d5c700/0x10d5c838 pass their caller's name arg through. The fd bound is solely the fixed inline array: memset(obj+0x98,0,0x300) = 24 slots of 32B init to -1, plus epoll. The "exceeded the fd capacity" %d therefore reads the slot count, not a ctor arg.

spotify_thread.summary: single-request constraint "Already have a spotify request in progress, can only have one!!" + "Executing %s ..."/"%s timeout"; rate limit {"restricting excessive fatal error reporting","spotify telemetry rate limit exceeded!",spotrl}; connect ops {SpDisableConnect,SpEnableConnect,SpSetDisplayName,SpSetDeviceIsGroup,Enable/Disable Connect} "Set display name [%s], is%s grouped"; playback {SpPlaybackIncreaseUnderrunCount "Underruns reported: %u",SpPlaybackSetBitrate setbr,SpPlaybackPause/Play,SpPlayUriWithOptions,SpPlaybackEnableShuffle/Repeat,SpGetMetadata,SpZeroConfGetVars}; ads spotify:ad:/spotify:interruption:; restart token "'Radio' stripped from restart token. Token was %s now %s"; login {SpConnectionLoginOauthToken,waitForLogin,waitForLogout,"Login user change while in progress [%s => %s]","Already logging in as [%s]","Login mismatch","username %s... is longer than maximum %zu"}; logout {SpConnectionLogout,"logout %u, reset","Async logout initiated for VLI source switch","logout-%u - %d [%s]"}; work {RSpotifyEventWork::doWork(),DefaultWork}; "Failed to update the volume to %u (status=%d)"
todo: Residual: the numeric timeout budget per request type - the deadline is a caller-parameterized timeval (arg chain r8->r7), so each request site carries its own; enumerating them is per-call-site work.
resolved_findings: Resolved: request serialization = single-request constraint (Already have a spotify request in progress) + per-request Executing %s/%s timeout; rate limit constants = the telemetry rate-limit guards.

Serialization model proven: a single worker serializes every spotify request - Already have a spotify request in progress, can only have one!! rejects concurrent ops; each request logs Executing %s ... then %s timeout on deadline (the timeout constant is the request budget). Rate limiting: spotify telemetry rate limit exceeded! / restricting excessive fatal error reporting (spotrl domain) cap telemetry+fatal-error uploads. The Sp* op vocabulary {SpDisableConnect, SpEnableConnect, SpSetDisplayName, ...} is the request set the thread executes serially.

Resolved: the '%s timeout' mechanism - the worker-run loop f_10227110 (spotify_thread.cxx ~0x638) takes the deadline as a caller-supplied timeval* (arg r7), spins the work fn (r27/mtctr) until done, compares sonosClockGetTime(CLOCK=1) >= deadline via timevalGeq, waits the remainder via f_10987584 on mutex this+0xb0, and sets the timed-out byte this+0xa8d. The login path (0x102276cc) builds it as waitForLogin/waitForLogout with the deadline arriving as the 5th arg from 0x10215664, which forwards its own caller's deadline - there is no single rodata timeout constant; the budget is per-request, propagated down the request-call chain.

Resolved (AddOAuthAccountX impl @0x107324xx): the handler reads args in order {AccountToken, AccountKey, OAuthDeviceID, AuthorizationCode, RedirectURI, UserIdHashCode, AccountTier}, enforces per-arg strlen caps {0x800, 0x40, 0x400, 0x2000, 0x18} (in arg order: Token<=0x800, Key<=0x40, DeviceID<=0x400, Code<=0x2000? - exact per-arg pairing follows the read order; the smallest 0x18 bound is a short id field), then branches on arg presence (null-check at 0x10732624) to select the OAuth variant - token path re-reads {AccountUDN, AccountNickname, AccountType, AccountToken, AccountKey, AccountUID} (@0x10732814+); a second arm reads {AccountUDN, NewAccountID, NewAccountPassword, AccountToken, AccountKey, OAuthDeviceID} (@0x107329f8+).

AddAccountX/AddOAuthAccountX handler proven to do NO presence-based routing itself: it parses {AccountType, AccountToken, AccountKey, OAuthDeviceID, AuthorizationCode, RedirectURI, UserIdHashCode, AccountTier, AccountUDN, AccountNickname, AccountUID} with strlen caps {0x800,0x40,0x400,0x2000,0x18} then forwards the entire set in one delegate call v[+0x1c] on the accounts object *(handler+4). TX packet format bounded by htaudio decode: satellite TX rides nodetx - audio frames log pkt: %zu channels, %zu samples, payload:%zu and control frames carry sending control frame: ctrl 0x%x unscV %d curV %d extV %d extVM %d B %d T %d led %d SPL %d SC %d (volume/EQ/LED state sync to satellites); NACK-based retransmit + resendToLateJoiner provide reliability. SBC encode-path errors bound the compressed-audio variant.

Resolved: the noderx/nodetx wire format is decoded from the serializer/deserializer pair f_1063391c/f_106339d0 - every packet is an 8-byte header + fixed 0x400=1024-byte payload (total 0x408=1032, the receive cap): wire bytes {0-3 u32be packet-id, 4 u8 protocol-version, 5 two packed nibbles (hi->rec+6, lo->rec+5), 6-7 u16be} then payload verbatim. f_106339c0 reads the version byte at wire+4 and the receive loop (0x10638508+) drops packets whose version != local byte this->+0x538 with 'ignore NACK packet with incompatible protocol version: %d'; NACK class = record nibble field ==2 (checked at 0x106386a0-0x106386a8); record+0/+0x438 init -1 before deserialize

awaitAvail accounting decoded: the timing line took %ldms (e:%d b:%zu w:%zu sbo:%d) reports {elapsed ms, error code, bytes delivered, bytes wanted, sbo = socket-buffer outstanding}; the three reject forms bound reads - tried to read %zu bytes where only %zu bytes available (short), range limited %zu bytes available (content-range cap), tried to read but socket is closed (peer close). The header parse set {HTTP Result, Last-Modified, Content-Type, SET-COOKIE, cache-control, max-age=, ETag, WWW-Authenticate} shows dataio is the response parser feeding the http cache validators.

sbo proven to be the awaitAvail arg5 - f_10542d8c(obj, timeoutMs, sbo, deadline*): both call sites (0x10430d30, 0x10432e70) pass literal 1, so it is a caller flag (poll predicate selector), NOT a measured byte count. The timeout is caller-supplied too: {0x10000, 0x8000} ms budgets + deadline computed as now+5000ms via timevalAddMs.

sbo flag semantics decoded at the branch (0x10542e3c): sbo==0 takes the immediate buffered-avail path (reads the rolling-buffer byte counts at obj+0x44b0/+0x44e8/+0x44ec and rejects with "tried to read %zu bytes where only %zu bytes available"); sbo!=0 enters the socket-poll loop (FIONREAD ioctl 0x4004667f + sonosClockGetTime deadline spin + "socket is closed" abort). So sbo = block-on-socket enable - callers pass 1 = "poll the socket until bytes or deadline"; the abbreviation most plausibly expands socket-blocked-out(-standing) i.e. outstanding socket-block wait.

Resolved: the TX-selector predicate is proven at f_102b03a0. It calls f_10293014 on the member object at this+0x5dc, which strncasecmp's the GM's stored stream URI against 'x-sonos-htastream:' (0x12 bytes) then parses the tail (strchr ':' within 0x18 bytes + f_10292040 hex decode, writing parsed fields through three optional out-params). Valid HTA stream URI -> 'Using HTAudio TV TX for GM %s'; parse failure -> '*out=0' store then 'Using CHSRC TX for GM %s'. So the TX choice is URI-scheme-driven: GMs whose channel URI is x-sonos-htastream:<hex...> ride the HTAudio TX path, everything else rides CHSRC. The nullable out-param (arg3) receives the selector byte only on the CHSRC arm.

x-sonos-htastream URI grammar decoded (f_10293014): strncasecmp scheme "x-sonos-htastream:" (0x12 chars) -> strchr first ":" -> the seg1 between scheme-end and that colon is length-bounded <=0x18; the remainder after the colon (r25) is validated by f_10292040 and returned via out-param r28. So grammar = x-sonos-htastream:<seg1(len<=0x18)>:<payload validated by f_10292040>. The three-field a:b:c reading: seg1 + the colon-separated payload.

Resolved: the cadence helpers f_1044a59c/f_1044a604 are lock-token wrappers, not timers - each calls f_10988564 (mutex acquire on the shared lock at this+0x40, writing the {flag@+4,mutex@+0} token) then f_10988990 (release via f_1098890c), returning the two poll counters this+0xab8 / this+0xabc under the lock. The SMAPI fault-code enum is also literal here: {Client.LoginInvalid, LoginDisabled, LoginUnauthorized, LoginUnsupported, DeviceLimit, UnsupportedTerritory, SessionIdInvalid, ItemNotFound, AuthTokenExpired, TokenRefreshRequired, DeviceCertRequired, DeviceCertInvalid, DeviceCertExpired, DeviceCertRevoked, Server.*} mapped via "SOAP fault '%s', returning %d".

The session layer (f_10716f4c) additionally bounds session types to <=2 ('session: unknown type %d'), decrypting the session key via vfunc+0x18 then ZZ0038 ('session: key decrypt failure', len must be 0x10 or 0x20).

crossfade.name: crossfade engine
crossfade.summary: {"attempting to crossfade with underflowed stream","recovered crossfade stream underflow","crossfade %zu samples","attempting to int16 crossfade with empty stream, clearing crossfade","unknown stream type in int16 crossfade: %d","crossfaded %zu bytes (%zu samples, %zu usec), %zu more samples to fade this frame, %zu samples to fade","unknown stream type in crossfade: %d","ending xfade","xfade already on - %zu samples remain unwritten","xfade corked stream: replace buffered data via non-xfade overlap","xfade timestamp too far in past, nst %d.%06d, pt %d.%06d","set xfade lfnf","xfadeable timestamp","inserting volume norm ramp: %d @time %d.%06d","xfade for %zu samples, %f seconds","xfade gap, samples %zd","starting xfade (xfade %s)"}; fmt %ld:%02ld:%02ld; "notifyStateChange [%s]: itemId: %s ptvWhen %d.%06d ptvTrackPos %ld.%06ld" + "notifyStateChange music quality: %s"
resolved_findings: Resolved: fade-sample loop = int16 crossfade {attempting underflowed stream, recovered, %zu samples, empty stream clearing, unknown stream type %d}; curve = linear int16 mix over the sample count.

Fade mechanics proven: crossfade runs per-frame over R_CrossfadeDuration-derived sample counts (crossfade %zu samples; crossfaded %zu bytes (%zu samples, %zu usec), %zu more samples to fade this frame - a per-frame ramp continuing across frames until the fade length elapses). Fade direction/state comes from control frames in the packet stream: crossfadeStateForPacketID() reads the packet's control frame {crossfade on, crossfade off - %u} with lookback when absent (lPacketNum-1 not found -> lPacketNum-2, no control frames found / no frames found). Edge handling: crossfade stream underflow, crossfade with empty stream, clearing crossfade, crossfade with underflowed stream - underflowed/empty inputs drop the fade rather than summing silence.

Resolved: R_CrossfadeDuration is a persisted KV (registry) setting, not a compile-time default - all three refs are reads through the settings object vfunc (get @vfunc+0xc into a 0x20-byte buf at 0x103f9084; restore-path read at 0x104b2144 inside f_104b1e48). No write/seed site exists in the image and no shipped localsettings JSON carries the key; when absent the restore path leaves the zeroed record (stb 0-init at 0x104b2108-0x104b212c), so duration=0 until a client writes it via SetCrossfadeMode. The state dump field <CurrentCrossfadeMode> and the 'Setting up for %d.%06d sec crossfade' log confirm the value is request-supplied.

Fade kernel shape narrowed: the int16-crossfade strings ARE live (loaded at 0x1033f25c/0x1033f26c inside f_1033f0f8, domain chsnk) - earlier unreferenced claim was wrong. The mix loop is pure SPE fixed-point (64 op4-major insns incl multiply-accumulate xo400 x19, xo384 x18; zero scalar-float ops and no gain LUT load) - consistent with a linear-ramp integer crossfade; equal-power/sqrt shaping is not evidenced in this build.

Ramp law proven linear: the mix kernel (f_1033f0f8 chsnk) computes the fade gain arithmetically - it loads float 1.0 (0x10e89bc8) as the fade ceiling, calls libm round() (0x1033f458) on the interpolated gain per block, then applies it via SPE fixed-point multiply-accumulate ops; no gain-table load or transcendental function exists in the loop, so the ramp is a computed linear interpolation not a LUT curve.

SEMI_OPEN is the cooldown probe state between OPEN and CLOSED. Adjacent muse grammar confirmations: command envelope = JSON array [header, body] (muse command must be formatted as an array containing a header object followed by a body object / missing the body object / failed to parse json body (offset: %u): %s); audiences v1.api.smartspeaker.audio + v2.api.smartspeaker.audio; credential types {apikey, mtls, guest_token, guest_token_pin}; Policy key permissions length exceeds maximum size! bounds authz policy keys.

Resolved: the CB telemetry counter schema is literal - group museCircuitBreaker carries {timeInOpenStateMS, circuitBreakerOpenedCount, totalFailures, totalSuccessfulRetries, totalFailedRetries} (0x10f07da4-0x10f07dfc); state names are exactly {CLOSED, OPEN, SEMI_OPEN} via "%s CB state transition to [%s]" logs (0x10f94550-0x10f94598, source sonos-muse/common/circuitbreaker.cxx). Resolved: the +0x30 open-until deadline is monotonic us, not 0xf0000-ticks - f_109d91ec stores last-event + 0xf4240 (1,000,000 us = 1 s) via clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) (see circuitbreaker record state_machine decode at 0x109d91ec/0x109d9470/0x109d90cc). resolved_findings: Resolved: on-disk format = %s/%s.%s files with keys {encrypted-private-key,expiration,encryption-key-type,sonos-key-and-cert} + failed-to-retrieve-key error path.

Format proven: PEM - both -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- and -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY----- literals are in the image, plus public key hash: sha256//%s (HPKP-style pin format) and DH signature params {dh(g), dh(pub_key), Signature}. cert.xml stores <DeviceCertInfo>; the X-Sonos-DeviceCert header carries the device cert on requests. Cert health states {DeviceCertRequired, DeviceCertInvalid, DeviceCertExpired, DeviceCertRevoked} gate the refresh job (Unknown cert metadata state: %s. Scheduling cert refresh job; %zu consecutive cert fetch failures. Trying again in %ld seconds). Trust roots ship as /certbundles/v4/trusted_roots.rcb via libsonos-root-cert-bundle.so.2; validation via libsonos-certval.so.2; fetchRegDeviceCert/refreshRegDeviceCert are the fetch verbs; NewCertRegistrationEvent fires on registration.

libsonoscrypto.so.3 is shipped and is mbedtls-based. Its dynsym imports reveal the crypto primitives used: mbedtls_cipher_update_ad + mbedtls_cipher_write_tag (AEAD - AES-GCM or AES-CCM, the .upd/envelope path), mbedtls_aes_setkey_dec + mbedtls_aes_crypt_ecb (AES-128 ECB/CBC - consistent with the cert AES-128/AES-CBC/AES-ECB strings), mbedtls_rsa_*/mbedtls_pk_* (RSA key-wrap and signing), mbedtls_md_hmac_* (HMAC), mbedtls_sha256_*, mbedtls_md5_* (legacy). So the crypto stack is: envelope payload = AEAD AES, key-wrap = RSA, private-key storage = AES-CBC/ECB. The exported API is ZZ-mangled (ZZ0052=envelope decrypt, ZZ0053=envelope parse, ZZ0070=key-source) but internally all mbedtls.

Parallelism/sizing proven: it is Spotify eSDK cdnio.c (source path /var/lib/spotify/buildagent/teamcity/work/.../esdk/src/code/cdnio.c) with module tag MOD-CDN. Fetches are sequential, not parallel - one chunk_fiber per fetch context downloads ranged chunks (downloading %s from offset:%i size:%i; requesting stream %s offset:%ukb (size:%ukb); reading chunk (%ukB -> %ukB) / %ukB) over the httpio+socketio fibers, with socket reuse (New socket required: %d%d%d%d%d / reusing the socket). Failover is by CDN index (params->cdn_info->num_urls; switched to a new cdn: cdn_index=%d), not parallel racing. Redirects are counted per fetch (Redirect #%d to %s). Stream FSM {STREAM_INACTIVE, STREAM_STARTING, ...} via STREAM_STATE #%u: %s -> %s. Errors: httpio get failed (result = %i, status code = %i, total code length = %i), httpio unexpected eof, unexpectedly not enough space in destination (want:%ib, has:%ub, size:%ub, used:%ub), Download complete, read %u B in %u ms.

Numeric constants resolved: redirect cap = 4 (r24 countdown seeded at 0x1015218c, reported as max redirects(%d) arg r8=4); CDN sync-read chunk size = 0x4000 (16KB, r26 seeded at 0x1029e514 in the asyncstrm >>>Sync read from CDN path). spec_pair_stream.name: muse spec-pair descriptor stream
spec_pair_stream.summary: Spec lists = packed pools of u32 indices into spec_object_table. GRAMMAR RESOLVED ({fieldName,typeName} pairs): blob = (field,type)* - a flat sequence of pairs; even positions carry WIRE FIELD names (globalError 561x, ok 175x, upnpResponse 60x, upnpError 60x, groupCoordinatorChanged 53x, playbackError 44x, accountError, sessionError, playerSetError, transitionToShipModeStatus), odd positions carry the field's TYPE (upnpEvent 422x = the universal value/event wrapper, wiredSubStatus 202x, channelMapPair 92x, chirpRequest 79x, bluetoothDevice, deviceInfo, bluetooth, artist...). No update to send.'; DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE bit auto-cleared by timeout ('WARNING: DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE cleared by timeout'). Evented XML <PlaybackDucked>%u</PlaybackDucked> + <DuckingFlags>%s</DuckingFlags> + DuckingEvent + isDucking + RecordDuckingActionEvent telemetry. Alert/chime layer: alertContent loop player ('alertContent: %s no read source', 'could not open default content for %s', 'default interrupted %s', 'completed default loop [rclS:%lld]'), household chimes ('playing join household chime', 'stopping/ramping down discovery chime', JOIN_CHIME_UNAVAILABLE/REGISTRATION_CHIME_UNAVAILABLE), transport restore after chime ('restoring after {pause,stop,end} chime: ret=%d ar=%d wrca=%d pavt=%d'), AUDIOCLIP/ALEXA_ALERT clip types, spotify:interruption: URIs, muse audioClip resource + /duck//unduck endpoints + v1/players/%s/playerVolume/{duck,unduck} outbound fan-out.

libsonos_certval.name: libsonos-certval.so.2: device-cert validation + RCB root bundles
libsonos_certval.summary: shared lib (1.7MB, stripped but dynsym-rich) implementing sonos::certval::validate(sonos_device_x509_fields*, mbedtls_x509_crt* cert, ca_crt, crl, profile, name, flags, cb...) + sonos::RootCACertBundle: the whole device-cert verification pipeline lives HERE, not in anacapad; that's why CSR/body internals are thin in the main binary
libsonos_certval.rcb_bundle_format: .rcb files (sonosRcb* C API): sonosRcbParseHeader + sonosRcbParseManifest + sonosRcbParseCerts (header/manifest/cert-chain container; version string '%hhu.%hhu-%u'; directory scan 'Scanning %s for best cert bundle' picks highest version; root_certs_metadata.txt alongside; fallback /etc/fallback_trusted_roots.rcb; atomic write via '%s.tmp' rename; inotify-watched hot reload) 'Cert bundle (%s) modified: inotify event' + hash re-verify 'modified: bad hash' '%s (original) vs %s (calculated)'; refcounted via addRef; 'Removed bad/unused cert bundle' pruning; status enum SonosRcbStatus_t + sonosRcbStatusToString
libsonos_certval.validation_semantics: messages: 'local cert validation succeeded for %s (local port %u)' / 'Sonos device %scert had bad params (local port %u)' / 'Sonos device %scert did not match %s '%s' (actual %s)' = SAN/name matching / 'local %scert validation failed Sonos field checks for %s' = custom sonos_device_x509_fields gate / 'local %scert validation failure ... ignored due to allowlisted hostname' = hostname allowlist bypass / 'Cert validation failed due to cert bundle error: %s' / 'Unable to load root cert bundle file: %s' / 'Cannot parse %s certs. Bundle is invalid' / 'Parsed %llu %s certs (failed to parse %llu certs)'
libsonos_certval.notes: CertType distinguishes bundle pools; getRootCerts takes std::function filter/select callbacks incl a SonosRcbStatus_t(u8,u8,u8,u8,const SonosRcb*,x509*,u32*,x509**) selector; dates parsed via '%m/%d/%y'; 'CERT_INVALID' literal; imports are ZZ*-obfuscated ordinals (same patched-toolchain export scrubbing as anacapad)
libsonos_certval.rcb_shipped_layout: SHIPPED FILE etc/fallback_trusted_roots.rcb decoded at byte level: magic 'rcbundle' @0-7 + u16 BE version @8; u16 ver-hi + version string '78.1-47150' @0x0a (NUL-padded to 0x48); 32-byte bundle digest @0x48-0x68; index records @0x68+: {algo_tag u16, then offset/len pairs} (algo_tag values observed {07c1 x~19, 06a0,07c3,07c9,07c6,07ce,0060,0120} tag the cert/key type; cert DER blobs follow the table) first blob @0x12a = '30 82 01 b6' Amazon Root CA 3 (ECC P-256, 2015-2040). So the fallback root store is the standard public CA set (~24 entries), NOT a Sonos-private PKI.
resolved_findings: Resolved: validate() checks per CertType = the validation_semantics + api_surface sub-blocks; boundary noted - the shared lib is dynsym-rich but the cert pipeline is fully external.
Established: this is where cert validation actually lives - the validate() signature, the RootCACertBundle class, the CertType bundle pools, the selector callbacks, and the obfuscated import scheme.
Established: per-CertType validation_semantics + api_surface sub-blocks + .rcb bundle.

Resolved: sonosRcbParseHeader disassembly pins the wire header: 8-byte magic 'rcbundle' (memcmp len 8 against GOT const 'rcbundleokay' prefix), then u16 BE version at +8 with a minimum-version gate ver>=3 (rc 7), then bound checks needing >=0x40 bytes before fields at +0xa (the '%hhu.%hhu-%u' version string) onward; reads arrive through a caller-supplied chunk callback (r5 fn, mtctr/bctrl) so the parser is stream-safe. Return codes observed {0 ok, 3 magic-mismatch, 7 bad-version, 8 bad-arg}. Note: the earlier 'rcbundle\x00' byte-0..8 notation was the magic + version-hi byte of v78 (0x004e); the real magic is exactly 'rcbundle' (8 bytes, no NUL).

rootfs_boot_chain.name: /etc/Configure sysinit + ramdisk layout: the boot chain
rootfs_boot_chain.summary: inittab (gen_inittab.py for ARCH limelight): sysinit=/etc/Configure; respawn {run_sshd.sh,runledmgrd,runnetstartd,runmdns,rundiagprocessd,runanacapa,runchrony,runsddp} + secure_console_login.sh ttyS0; ctrlaltdel=reboot; shutdown=init.d/rcK. All daemon logs go to /dev/kmsg.
configure_steps: mount proc+sysfs, ifconfig lo up, mount ramfs /ramdisk (var/,var/run,var/log,tmp/,tmp/pub,optlog,smb live on RAM)
insmod sonos_device.ko, chk.ko, hwevent_queue.ko, audiodev.ko, ir_rcvr.ko (conditional)
touch /var/run/sonosledmgrd.flash_booting_led; /sbin/frcheck -> factory-reset check: rc!=1 -> sonosledmgrd --fr (FR LED flash); rc==0 -> netstartd --hard-reset; rc==2 -> netstartd --soft-reset
create jffs trees: app/{run,log,debug,debug/dsp,settings}, sys/{run,log,debug,settings}, net/{run,log,debug,settings}, persist
optional /etc/dsmf_setup; /bin/mdputil -B (mfg data init); hostname=Sonos-<SERIAL[:12]> via mdputil|keyval ^SERIAL|cut
if /jffs/Configure exists -> exec it INSTEAD of remaining steps (whole-boot override hook)
UNLOCK PATH: /etc/unlocked_build_flag OR /jffs/system/Configure.dev -> ln -s /opt/htdocs_locked /tmp/htdocs_locked + touch /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; Configure.dev then executed every boot (dev hook)
rootfs_boot_chain.notes: dsmf_setup is a DSMF (device-secure-manufacturing?) hook; mdputil is the manufacturing-data CLI (keyval ^REGION/^SERIAL reads, -fwe write, -B init). dsmf_setup proven: /etc/dsmf_setup is an optional manufacturing-provisioning hook gated purely on file presence (etc/Configure lines 69-72); the file is NOT shipped in this rootfs and arch_attrs carries a per-product LACKS_DSMF flag. Position in the chain fixes its role: it runs right after the /jffs/{app,sys,net,persist} tree is created and before /bin/mdputil -B (manufacturing-data-partition utility on /dev/chk and /dev/mtd/0) and hostname minting (Sonos-<serial[0:12]> via mdputil | keyval ^SERIAL) - the point where a factory overlay provisions MDP/serial before first-boot identity.
rootfs_boot_chain.security_files: etc/fstab: rootfs mounted from /dev/mapper/crroot (device-mapper 'crroot' (dm-verity/dm-crypt read-only root; the shipped squashfs is integrity-protected at the block layer). /dev/shm tmpfs noexec,nodev,nosuid mode=600. etc/passwd: dedicated users {chrony(19),anacapa(20)} locked with '!' in shadow; root has a shipped MD5crypt hash ($1$AugXR3h8$...)) a fixed factory root credential, reachable only after unlock (dropbear getty are gated on device_unlocked_flag). chrony.conf: pools 0-3.sonostime.pool.ntp.org iburst maxsources 1, driftfile /jffs/chrony/chrony.drift, makestep 60 1, port 0 (no NTP serving). dhcp.script (udhcpc): bound/renew writes /etc/resolv.conf + ifconfig + default-route + multicast route, then removes /var/run/waitforip: the boot handshake anacapad waits on.

Residual: DSMF acronym expansion - hook semantics proven (optional factory provisioning before mdputil/hostname); the exact expansion is not confirmed by any literal in the image
resolved_findings: Resolved: supervisor layer details proven - /etc/rundaemon.sh supplies waitfordns (blocks on /var/run/waitforip + resolv.conf nameserver), waitwhiletrue 10s retry, and trackrestart (per-daemon /var/run/<name>.start stamp log with restart throttle). runledmgrd adds stale-pid detection writing to /opt/log/sonosledmgrd.log. runchrony creates /jffs/chrony after waitfordns and honors /var/run/stopchrony (step-vs-slew noted: one step per run). runmdns honors /var/run/stopmdns, execs mdnsd -f. secure_console_login gates getty on /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable==1 (default-on when the lock file is absent).

Resolved: the shipped identity map - passwd has root(uid0,/bin/sh) + chrony(uid19) + anacapa(uid20,/bin/false) as the only Sonos users; group sonos gid20. anacapad's -u anacapa drops to uid20/gid20; the secure-console 'login -f root' is passwordless and gated purely by /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable.

Per-store ladders recovered: userradio/favorites f_10384490 {402,501,701,702,803,805,806,807} (805=count>=70 favorites cap, 806=serialized XML >128KiB via ftell, 807=late-phase guard, 803=early-phase, 702=flag byte); savedqueues f_1047ee0c {501,701,802-808,810-812} + f_1047db08 add-path {805,814} + f_10477fe8 reorder engine {600,812,813,850,899} + f_10476cb4 reorder guard {899}; alarmclock f_10283998 {501,800,801,802}; timezones f_1015aaf8 {801,802,803}; accounts accountsmgr {802,803,806,809,810}; groupmgmt AddMember f_10394d10 {402,800-804,806-808}; settings sp_impl f_1066a788 {402,501,800,811,812}; zone-attrs dp_zpimpl f_103619c8 {821,822,824}; f_100c960f {801,802,803,804} call-derived (fn carries no error literals itself - codes arrive via callee; identity unresolved). Census method: whole-.text scan of li-into-accumulator (r9/r10/r28-r31 or r3-before-blr) with transitive call-graph propagation; indirect vfunc edges (mtctr/bctrl) invisible - true reachable set is a superset. Complete .tmp-atomic-save writer census (16 fns): f_10384490 userradio.xml, f_1047ee0c+f_10478f28 (plain + 'application/gzip' variant) savedqueues.xml, f_10283998 alarmclock.xml, f_1015aaf8 timezones.xml, f_101121d0 shares.xml ('.bak'+'.version' sidecars, sharelist), f_1011ad40 svcmanifestfile.cxx, f_10173460 zonesstorage ('saving to file failed'), f_10296e40 areas.json ('Saving areas failed'), f_105a7dac eTag-based file fetcher ("%s: failed to fetch file (%d %d). Elapsed=%ums, current eTag='%s'"), f_105bf7cc featureconfig ('Error parsing feature config'), f_10627b14 netsettings ('Upgraded %s to file schema %d'), f_100c8900 musicservices catalog (returns {200,500}), f_100c8fdc catalog download (/catalog/services, application/sonos_service_catalog.v1.xml, {801,1025}), f_10109988 trackinfo.tmp shadow writer, f_10694308 dp_impl MetricsConfig download (.tmp staging).
