bin_upgrade.name: upgrade / upgrade_mgr daemons
bin_upgrade.summary: Firmware-update pair: /bin/upgrade performs one upgrade transaction (download, verify, flash, reboot); /bin/upgrade_mgr is the orchestrating daemon that the anacapad update machinery kicks (/var/run/upgradeinfo) and that exposes an SSDP-advertised status server. All evidence below is from stripped 32-bit MSB (PPC) ELF string/dyn-symbol tables plus /etc/runanacapa and /etc/init.d/rcK.
todo: Residual: the internal field layout of the N-byte envelope header (wrapped key/IV offsets parsed by libsonoscrypto ZZ0053) and the key-source id bound by ZZ0070 - inside libsonoscrypto.so.3, not the .upm grammar itself.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): failure/rollback = the upgrade binary pair handles verify-then-write with fallback partition; consolidated into the record - anacapad hands off via update_machinery; binaries themselves are outside the anacapad static surface but the call contract is documented.

bin/upgrade I/O contract: reads /var/run/upgradeinfo ('Error reading upgradeinfo file'); supports a no-op mode ('No-op mode - download/reboot will be skipped' and 'Detected /jffs/VERSION, performing no-op update'); builds the image URL as '%s%s-%u-%u.upd?cmaj=%u&cmin=%u&cbld=%u&subm=%u&rev=%u&reg=%u&serial=%s' plus '&sonosid=%s&householdid=%s'; and ends by calling reboot().

bin/upgrade .upd container: typed sections with a magic header ('Invalid section header. Bad magic value.'), a required/optional split ('Required section %u missing', 'Skipping checks for section %u', 'Unknown section %u', 'Multiple sections of type %u'), a signature section verified via sonosRcbVerifySig ('invalid Sonos signature section length', 'encrypted signature section not supported'), per-section enveloped-data decryption via mbedtls ('Enveloped data parse/decrypt init/decrypt/decrypt final failed', 'Encrypted section too small', 'Out of space while decrypting section'), and cert bundles saved under /jffs/sys/run/rcb/ as upd_cert_bundle.rcb and %s-%s.rcb.

bin/upgrade hardware gating: mutes and powers off amps through libsyslib_hal before flashing ('warning: failed to mute/power off amps'), reads the boot section via hal_flash_get_bootsection, enforces a HW-feature compatibility matrix ('Critical UPD feature (%s: %s) not supported by player', 'Critical player feature not supported by UPD', 'Upgrade supports all my legacy hw features'), skips M4 and BOOTSOUND sections when no partition exists, and writes /var/upgradescript for post-reboot execution.

bin/upgrade client-server mode: can listen on a TCP port for a household controller ('client-server mode: listening on port %d', CONNECT/DOWNLOAD/DOWNLOAD_DONE states, 'waiting for connection from HH', monitored attach/detach) and streams progress to that client ('Failure sending progresss to client. Lost connection to client.'); writes the upgrade report to /jffs/upgrade_sys_report.log (prev rotated to _prev) and /var/run/upgrade_report.txt.

bin/upgrade housekeeping: wipes /jffs/app/install, writes /jffs/sys/run/updateID, references deactivation markers /jffs/persist/deactivation_pending_state.json + deactivated_state, devmode image path /jffs/debug/devmode.bin, and manages /tmp/upgrade_mgr.pid + /var/run/stopupgrade.

bin/upgrade_mgr state machine: verbs {HELLO, STATUS, PING, DOWNLOAD, FLASHWRITE, REBOOT, COMPLETE, ERROR, 'Unrecognized command'} and states {UNDEFINED, INIT, CONNECT, HELLO_DONE, WAIT, DOWNLOAD_DONE, FLASHWRITE_DONE, REBOOTING_DONE, FINISHED}; the status server binds a TCP port ('status server: listening on port %d') and announces itself over SSDP with NT/USN urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:SonosUpgradeMgr:1, X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD, and 'X-RINCON-REASON: hh-upgrade'.

bin/upgrade_mgr reporting: daemonizes (daemon()), reads its info file (ReportFilename must be set), and emits a JSON report to /jffs/app/run/%s with fields {Serial, Type, CurrentVersion, TargetVersion, UpdateID, HardwareVersion, State, ServerIP, ErrorMsg, ExtendedError}; its update-check URL carries '?Version=%s.%s-%s&Auto=%s&Client=%s'.

bin/upgrade .upm section machinery (decoded from the shipped binary): per-section header {+0x4: type, +0xc: flags (bit0x2=tolerated-when-unknown), +0x10: payload offset}; section types accepted in range 3..0x16. Dispatch iterates a stride-28 handler table {+0x10: arg, +0x14: already-seen flag producing 'Multiple sections of type %u', +0x28: flags with bit0='Skipping checks for section %u'}. File body is mmap64'd (work buffer rounded to 0x200 granularity). Section flag bit0x1 rejects as 'encrypted signature section not supported' and bit0x4 selects the unsupported-encryption reject. The cert-bundle section is verified by sonosRcbParseHeader+sonosRcbVerifySig and written to /jffs/sys/run/rcb/%s-%s.rcb.

upgrade_mgr wire vocabularies are ALSO embedded in anacapad rodata as {char* name,u32 len,u32 id} stride-12 tables: verb table @0x10fad660 {1=UNDEFINED,2=CONNECT,3=HELLO,4=DOWNLOAD,5=FLASHWRITE,6=WAIT,7=REBOOT,8=ERROR,9=FINISHED} and state table @0x10fad6d8 {1=INIT,2=HELLO,3=HELLO_DONE,4=DOWNLOAD,5=DOWNLOAD_DONE,6=FLASHWRITE,7=FLASHWRITE_DONE,8=REBOOT,9=REBOOTING_DONE} - the coordinator-side client marshals/parses these exactly.

.upm envelope wire layout decoded from f_100045c8: reads an 8-byte prefix {word0 (first u32), word1 at bytes 4..7 = big-endian envelope-header-length N (validated N>7 and N<=total)}; then reads N-8 more header bytes; ZZ0053 parses the N-byte header into an envelope struct (wrapped key + IV); ZZ0052 decrypts the payload using that struct + key-source 0x100409b8(ZZ0070). So the .upm section payload is a length-prefixed envelope: [u32][u32 BE hdr_len][hdr_len-8 byte envelope hdr][ciphertext]. Errors: short prefix = Encrypted section too small; hdr_len<=7 or >total = Malformed enveloped data header; ZZ0053 fail = Enveloped data parse failed; missing key = No decryption key.

bin_mdputil.name: mdputil
bin_mdputil.summary: Manufacturing-data partition utility (/bin/mdputil) over libsonos-mdp + libflash. Prints keyval-parseable identity lines, validates and writes signed MDP pages on /dev/mtd/0.
todo: Residual: the MDP1/MDP2/MDP3 field offsets outside the 0x28-byte HW manifest (VENDOR/MODEL/SERIAL/DCOFS/etc come from the libflash hal_flash_get_mdp accessors, not this table).
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): tied into the upgrade call graph via get_mdp/mdp_write references in the unlock + update paths - the manufacturing-data partition read/write helper.

Verbs recovered from usage/error strings: bare invocation prints HW manifest ('%sHW manifest entries:') plus SERIAL=, SERIES_ID=, COPYRIGHT=, UNITSIG=, SERIALSIG= keyval lines; -B is the boot manifest print used by /etc/Configure; '-fwn <index>=<value>' writes fields; '-wf' forces a write past the 'There is already a valid MDP in place' guard; '-k keyfile' selects a signing key ('-k option not available' on unsigned builds).

Crypto/integrity surface: keyfile open/read, 'Unrecognised key length', 'Public key error', 'Decrypt error', 'Signature no match error', 'v2 signature no match error', 'Key rejected' - MDP pages carry a public-key signature verified on read/write.

Flash plumbing: opens /dev/mtd/0 via libflash hal_flash_get_mdp/hal_flash_get_mdp2/hal_flash_read_fsn + crc32; errors 'Flash MDP1 error', 'MDP2 error', 'Flash SN error', 'GETFSN failed deviceID %x err %x', 'Manifest parse failed'; exports sonosGetSeriesID/sonosSetSeriesID/sonosGetCertColorVariant from libsonos-mdp.

Consumers: /etc/Configure runs 'mdputil -B' then 'mdputil | keyval ^SERIAL | cut -c1-12' to set hostname Sonos-<serial12>; wacd reads MDP page1/page2 (model + cert-color variant) to build its WAC AppleDeviceIE.

Resolved: the in-anacapad MDP flag-write path is proven (f_105e64fc..0x105e6644, tag mod_zp): gated on a capability word from f_10909620 (requires bit 0x20 set, low bits &0x3 clear); opens the flash info context via hal_flash_info_init, reads the MDP flags word via hal_flash_get_mdp (also hal_flash_get_mdp2 into a 0x200 buffer), then writes back flags with bits 30-31 cleared and bit 0x20 OR'd in via f_10d54658, logging "MDP flag update: new flags %x". So anacapad sets persistent MDP flag 0x20 (a post-boot/upgraded marker) after its capability check passes.

Resolved: libsonos-mdp.so.1 decode - the MDP page carries TWO format variants gated by a leading u32 magic: magic 0xffffae2d (v1: color-variant idx at data+0x44c, MDP struct version must be <=3) and magic 0xfa87b921 (v2: color-variant idx at data+0xa10, version <=4); returns {-2 bad args,-3 unknown magic,-4 unsupported version,-5 color idx >0x12}. sonosGetCertColorVariant picks the arm by magic; sonosGetFinalColorVariant adds a version gate (mdp+0x70 <=5 then more checks).

Resolved: cert color-variant enum (idx->name via jump table, bound 0x12): 0=White,1=Black,2=Blue,3='Limited Edition',4=Shadow,5='Lunar White',6=Olive,7=Wave,8=Sunset,9=Greige,10=Sand,11=Blush,12=Agave; out-of-range -> 'Unexpected color'. Series-ID enum (sonosGetSeriesID switch table): {A100,A200,A101,A102,B100,D100,C201,C100,X999,C200} - 10 series codes (X999 is the engineering/unknown catch-all).

Resolved: sonosMdpSerialToString emits '%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%c' - the 6-byte serial as hex plus a check character computed by a digit-mixing loop (4 bytes summed mod-10 style via the 0x...f0f1 reciprocal multiply, mapped into a char).

Resolved: complete keyval field vocabulary from mdputil's manifest printer: {VENDOR,MODEL,SUBMODEL,SERIES_ID,REVISION,SERIAL,REGION,COPYRIGHT,FLAGS,HWFEATURES,CH11SPURIMMUNITYLEVEL,DCOFS(4-tuple DC offset %d:%d:%d:%d),MDPVERSION,MDP2VERSION,MDP2ENCVERSION,MDP3VERSION,MDP_OLD_VERSION,MDP_NEW_VERSION,PAGESPRESENT,FUSEVAL,SWFEATURES,VARIANT,WILDCARD_VARIANT,NANDID,UNITSIG,DATECODE,LOCATION,SERIALSIG}. FLAGS/HWFEATURES/FUSEVAL print with '# (' bit-decode suffixes. Mutability rules literal: 'MDP HAS_VERSION can't be modified', 'Use -T to modify MDP HAS_HWFEATURES', '-fwn <index>=<value>' writes field index via '%d=%d' parse, '-wf' overrides the 'There is already a valid MDP in place' guard, 'Fixing bad MDP version'/'New MDP flags 0x%08x' repair path. Compiled-in COPYRIGHT default 'Copyright 2025 Sonos, Inc.' at .data 0x1002003c.

Resolved: the REGION field is externally confirmed - preinstall.sh reads it via `mdputil | keyval ^REGION` and rewrites REGION=5 to 2 via `mdputil -fwe 2` (the -fwe <index> write form), so REGION is a first-class keyval field and field-index 2 targets it in this build.

Resolved: mdputil internals - optstring "Aa:whfv:V:M:m:r:Nn:e:s:S:Ik:F:C:P:T:i:d:D:Bpj:u"; field-index bound <0x104 (cmplwi 0x104 at 0x10002960, "Bad parm" on overflow); MDP read via hal_flash_get_mdp + hal_flash_get_mdp2 into two stack structs; the MDP2 signed-write path f_100024c4 opens /dev/mtd/0, ioctls 0x40044d24 (info) + 0x80244d23 (page read), XOR-compares 8-byte blocks, and runs libsonoscrypto ZZ0062/ZZ0064/ZZ0061/ZZ0109/ZZ0087 ops gated on MDP2 magic 0xCA989B4A (word0) and size bound 0x3c3 (word1). Print order of keyval fields: VENDOR,MODEL,SUBMODEL,SERIES_ID,REVISION,SERIAL,REGION,COPYRIGHT,FLAGS,HWFEATURES,...,WIFITYPE=N,FSN; FLAGS bits {KERNEL_PRINTK_ENABLE, CONSOLE_ENABLE, HAS_HWFEATURES, HAS_VERSION}; HWFEATURES bits {ATH_AR2414_WIFI, STMICRO_NAND, REDROCKS, ATH_AR5416_WIFI, ATH_AR9000_WIFI, LED_SWAP, ALT_ANTENNAS}; FSN read via hal_flash_read_fsn printed as %02x bytes or FSN=INVALID. Sensor/misc vocab {AMP, TEMP_SENSOR(AMP), TEMP_SENSOR(CPU), ALS, ACCELEROMETER, FUEL_GAUGE, RADIO}; error literals {Bad parm, Bad hash, Bad mdp, Bad key} and LED subcommand verbs {show, clear} with "%d=%d" + " (dynamic)" output.

-fwn path decoded (f_10002320): the MDP HW manifest is a 0x28-byte block at mdp_obj+0xb4 guarded by magic 0x7a61670e at +0xb0; entries are 8 hardware-presence bytes named by the table @0x10003328 {LED, AMP, TEMP_SENSOR(AMP), TEMP_SENSOR(CPU), ALS, ACCELEROMETER, FUEL_GAUGE, RADIO}. -fwn <index>=<value> validates index<=7 then stores the byte at +0xb4+index and re-arms the magic; per-index value bounds via jump table @0x100031f4: {idx0 rejected; idx{1,3,4} allow value 1..3; idx2 allows 1..5; idx{5,6,7} allow 1..2}. 'clear' memsets the whole 0x28 block and drops the magic.

bin_frcheck.name: frcheck
bin_frcheck.summary: Factory-reset checker (/sbin/frcheck): a 20KB one-shot run once per boot by /etc/Configure that decides whether this boot continues normally or enters a reset. Pure decision component, no daemon.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): verifies rootfs integrity (squashfs/partition consistency) at boot/update; exit contract = nonzero aborts the boot sequence stage.
Invocation site: /etc/Configure calls /sbin/frcheck right after mounting JFFS and touching /var/run/sonosledmgrd.flash_booting_led, before networking modules load.

Exit contract proven from Configure: rc=0 -> 'sonosledmgrd --fr' + 'netstartd --hard-reset' (full factory reset); rc=2 -> 'sonosledmgrd --fr' + 'netstartd --soft-reset' (settings-only reset); rc=1 -> normal boot continues.

Decision inputs from strings+dyn syms: reads /jffs/app/run/factoryReset.txt looking for the SOFT token (soft reset request persisted across reboot), samples front-panel button state via hal_inputs_get_buttons_state (button-held reset), and touches /dev/audioctl; prints 'APUinfo'.

Resolved: frcheck's two inputs are literal: sonosFileExists+sonosFileReadPartial on /jffs/app/run/factoryReset.txt (the persisted reset request written pre-reboot) and hal_inputs_get_buttons_state over /dev/audioctl (the power-on button-hold read). The rc contract {0=hard reset,1=normal boot,2=soft reset} is chosen by combining the file contents with the held-button mask; /dev/audioctl is the only device node it touches.

Resolved: decision logic from the .text (main 0x10000544+): rc starts 1 (normal). If /jffs/app/run/factoryReset.txt exists: sonosFileReadPartial reads 4 bytes + NUL; strcmp=='SOFT' -> rc=2 (soft reset); read<=0 or non-SOFT content -> rc=0 (hard reset); file is unlinked after reading either way (one-shot semantics). Then /dev/audioctl is opened and f_10000904 reads the button-state word into a 4-byte stack buf; if the probed byte ==1 -> rc=0 (hard reset) - a held panel button forces factory reset independent of the file. So: hard=empty/foreign file OR button-held; soft='SOFT' file; normal otherwise.

Resolved (boundary narrowed): hal_inputs_get_buttons_state (libsyslib_hal.so.1 @0x13cc) fills an 8-word (0x20-byte) output struct copied verbatim from a single ioctl 0x40F4FC3E on the button/input device (opened via a PIC-loaded path global; the only device literals in the lib are /dev/ir and /dev/audioctl). There is no GPIO->button-name table in the lib - the 8 words are the raw kernel-driver state word array, so byte-1 slot identity is kernel-module layout, confirmed opaque at this layer. Ioctl magic 0xF4 cmd 0x3E is the driver-defined read-state request.

hal_inputs_get_buttons_state proven (libsyslib_hal.so.1 @0x13cc): ioctl(fd, 0x40F4FC3E, buf) fills 8 u32 words copied verbatim to the out array (word[i]=stack[0x18+4i]); on primary-device failure it retries on a second device fd with ioctl 0x80000002. So the frcheck byte-1 slot is index 1 of the 8-word button-state vector - the per-index button identity is assigned in the kernel input driver, not userspace.

audiodev.ko has full symtab. Button name vocabulary recovered from button_sim_matches (.data+0x300, 72B = 8x{name_ptr,id} pairs via .rela.data): {mute, play-pause, volup, voldn, join, join, demo, demo} - the user-facing button names are {mute, play-pause, volup, voldn, join, demo}. audioctl_get_button_state (.text+0x4820) delivers a 0xf4-byte (61-word) button-state block to userland via hal_inputs_get_buttons_state.
todo: Residual: the 8 frcheck word->physical-button binding is the GPIO/board ordering inside audiodev.ko's button_state block - the name vocabulary is proven but the bit->physical-button order is board-layout data, not a named table.

bin_sddpd.name: sddpd (Sonos discovery daemon)
bin_sddpd.summary: Control4 SDDP (Simple Device Discovery Protocol) daemon (/sbin/sddpd), a third-party discovery channel parallel to SSDP/mDNS so Control4 remotes find the player. Respawned by inittab via /etc/runsddp after waitfordns; -n keeps it foregrounded, /jffs/dev_sddp.conf overrides /etc/sddpd.conf.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): sddpd.conf knobs = the SDDP announce/probe config; wire protocol boundary noted - daemon is external; role = Sonos device discovery parallel to SSDP/mDNS.

Wire surface from strings: builds periodic NOTIFY-style advertisements ('Sending SDDP advertisement', 'Sending Periodic SDDP advertisement', 'SDDP send failed'), answers SEARCH requests when the search target matches ('SEARCH', 'SDDP Search target MATCH'), emits identify on demand ('Sending SDDP identify'), and rejects foreign packets ('Unsupported SDDP request/response packet version: %s', 'Unrecognized SDDP packet: %s'); packet bodies start with the 'SDDP/' version token.

Sockets: one multicast listener + one unicast socket per interface - sets SO_REUSEADDR, IP_PKTINFO, IP_MULTICAST_TTL, joins a multicast group per interface ('Joining multicast group for %s'), enforces a minimum advertise period ('Setting SDDP max_age to minimum of %d seconds').

Config: /etc/sddpd.conf ships Type=sonos:Zoneplayer, PrimaryProxy=media_service, Proxies=media_service,amplifier, Manufacturer=Sonos, Model=Zoneplayer, Driver=sonos.c4z, MaxAge=1800; loader validates the file ('Incomplete config file', 'SDDPSetHost failed: host param too long', 'Unable to set device (index = %d)') and usage is '%s -n'.

bin_mdnsd.name: mdnsd (Sonos mDNS fork)
bin_mdnsd.summary: Stock Apple mDNSResponder daemon (/sbin/sddpd-adjacent /sbin/mdnsd), run foregrounded as 'mdnsd -f' by /etc/runmdns behind the waitwhiletrue /var/run/stopmdns gate. Sonos ships the posix mDNSResponder, not avahi.
todo: Residual: upstream release mapping - the banner is an Engineering Build with no mDNSResponder-XXX tag; DSO/Push presence implies a post-878.x lineage but the exact upstream base is not provable from strings
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): zone/group advertising = the _sonos._tcp announce flow driven by anacapad registration calls (mdns_controller); daemon-side config documented via shipped conf.

Binary is upstream mDNSResponder with the standard internals (mDNSCore*, mDNSPosix::tcpListenCallback, mDNSPlatform{SendUDP,TCPListen,TCPConnect,TCPWritable}, 'mDNSResponder Build %d.%02d.%02d' state-log banner, '---- BEGIN/END STATE LOG ----').

Privileges/sandboxing: attempts setgid+setuid to nobody and warns on failure ('WARNING: mdnsd continuing as group root / as root because setgid/setuid to nobody failed'); usage is '%s [-debug]' (-f foreground flag comes from mDNSPosix main).

Client surface: a dns_sd unix-domain-socket server is compiled in ('ExitCallback: udsserver_exit failed', 'requestIOEvents called with fd %d > FD_SETSIZE') - this is how anacapad registers the _sonos._tcp service/TXT records documented under the mdns record; interface tracking registers/deregisters interfaces at runtime ('Registered interface %s', 'Deregistered interface %s').

Divergence check: no Sonos-patched protocol strings found; the advertised zone/group semantics all live in anacapad's registration calls, not in the daemon. /etc/mdnsd.conf is referenced but absent from the rootfs, so the daemon runs with built-in defaults plus client registrations.

Resolved: /sbin/mdnsd is mDNSResponder Engineering Build (Aug 20 2026 14:46:24) - self-bannered "@(#) mDNSResponder (Engineering Build)", no upstream release tag (build number only, "mDNSResponder Build %d.%02d.%02d" in state-log banners). The UDS path is the upstream default /var/run/mdnsd with pidfile /var/run/mdnsd.pid; supervised by /etc/runmdns (waitwhiletrue /var/run/stopmdns then exec /sbin/mdnsd -f). The build carries the DSO/TLV extension family (dso_add_tlv_*, BuildUpdateMessage, SendGroupUpdates for DNS Push subscriptions) and a client/daemon version handshake ("client version 0x%08X daemon version 0x%08X", DaemonVersion query). Built with crosstool-NG GCC 5.5.0.

bin_netstartd.name: netstartd (netstart2)
bin_netstartd.summary: netstartd (/wifi/netstartd, 'netstart2') is the network bring-up and SonosNet orchestration daemon: it owns the NS2 household-setup protocol (DTLS-encrypted, over-the-air), the anacapad control IPC, the wacd provisioning channel, WEP/WPA key generation for SonosNet, STA/DHCP supervision, and the factory-reset network wipes. Respawned by inittab via /etc/runnetstartd.
todo: Residual: the per-message field layouts inside each NS2_MSG_* payload (msg ids and state ids are proven; the field decoders are per-handler code)
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): WiFi bring-up role = SCI/MRPC bus owner {netstart_mode, netstartd.ipc msg ids 3..108}; wpa_supplicant coordination via the IPC set.

Control IPC: listens on /tmp/netstartd.ipc (pid /tmp/netstartd.pid, stop flag /var/run/stopnetstartd). Clients complete a CLIENT_HELLO handshake carrying {protocol version, SW version, capabilities} ('Netstart2 CLIENT_HELLO: protocol version %u, SW version %s, capabilities 0x%x', 'Netstart protocol version: %d', 'unable to lock registration; already registered', '%s registered: %s'). anacapad drives SonosNet frequency changes and disable through it ('anacapa IPC: setting SonosNet frequency to %u in %u.%u seconds', 'frequency %u not supported', 'setting SonosNet disable'), and the pair handshake the Muse HHID ('Re-sending Muse HHID to anacapad ... expected ... to match', 'Confirmed anacapad received netstartd's Muse HHID').

NS2 wire protocol (the setup channel to apps/pending players): full message catalog NS2_MSG_{KEEP_ALIVE, ACK, SETUP_CLIENT_HELLO, SETUP_SERVER_HELLO, SETUP_SERVER_HELLO_LEGACY, SETUP_CANCEL, ECHO, SETUP_BEGIN, SETUP_CONTINUE, SETUP_STATUS, GET_SCAN_LIST, SCAN_LIST, SET_NET_SETTINGS, GET_PSK, PSK, UPGRADE, START_OPEN_AP, COMMIT_SETTINGS, SETUP_REAUTHORIZE, ENABLE_WIFI, START_ISLAND, TIMED_OUT, LOCK_REGISTRATION, REGISTRATION_KEY}; state machine NS2_STATE_{RESET, SETUP_STANDBY, SETUP_START, SETUP_DISCOVERY, SETUP_DISCOVERY_INTERACTION, SETUP_PIN_EXCHANGED, SETUP_WAITING, SETUP_ACTIVE, SETUP_COMPLETE, SETUP_UPDATE, OPEN_AP_PENDING, OPEN_AP_STANDBY, ENABLE_WIFI_PENDING, DEACTIVATED, REAUTH_PENDING, ISLAND_PENDING, SCANNING, CHECKING_CREDS}; setup modes NS2_SETUP_MODE_{NONE, NFC, CHIRP, MANUAL_PIN, CLIENT_PIN, CHIRP_WITH_BUTTON, QR_CODE, QR_CODE_WITH_BUTTON, QR_CODE_WITH_REMOTE}.

Transport security: the NS2 channel runs inside DTLS with its own FSM (DTLS_STATE_{DISCONNECTED, HELLO_VERIFY, CLIENT_RECONNECT, CONNECTING, CONNECTED, WRITING, CLOSING, CLOSE_IMMEDIATELY, CLOSE_NOTIFY_SENT, CLOSE_NOTIFY_DISCONNECT}, 'netstart2_dtls_write_message failed', handshake-timeout socket re-registration); device frames carry a netstart header in the 'uw' wireless layer ('uw could not add netstart header', 'Netstart msg %d (0x%x) from %d.%d.%d.%d to %d.%d.%d.%d').

WifiFuncs control surface: 50+ imports of the WifiFuncs* API - channel/freq set-get, AP scan start/cancel/results, SSID-in-beacon toggle, HHID WEP key channel, bridge STP/prio, Apple IE + network-settings IE injection, neighbor-probe ignore/block, advertised-path blocking, third-party disable, UWC presence/hops, station assoc bssid/ssid - driving athconfig under the hood.

Runtime files: /var/run/netstart_mode records the active mode; per-attempt setup logs %s/setup.log + %s/setup.dmesg under %s/%s/setup%s dirs; /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc is the wacd channel; settings are read from netsettings.txt, fresh_hh.txt and localsettings.txt; SonosNet WPA PMK is derived locally ('pmk_in_ascii_len too short', 'Failed to generate PMK', 'Failed to serialize'); DHCP is supervised through /tmp/udhcpc.pid + /tmp/udhcpc_renew_option ('DHCP start/renew signal').

Reset surface: flags --hard-reset, --soft-reset, --qareset, --qareset-lite, --preserve-system (wired to frcheck rc 0/2 in /etc/Configure); log at /opt/log/netstartd.log rotated to /jffs/netstartd_prev.log and /jffs/net/log/netstartd.log.

Resolved: the NS2 opcode map is a {u32 id, name*} table at .data.rel.ro 0x1004f848+: {0=KEEP_ALIVE, 1=ACK, 2=SETUP_CLIENT_HELLO, 3=SETUP_SERVER_HELLO, 4=SETUP_SERVER_HELLO_LEGACY, 5=SETUP_CANCEL, 6=ECHO, 7=SETUP_BEGIN, 8=SETUP_CONTINUE, 9=SETUP_STATUS, 0xa=GET_SCAN_LIST, 0xb=SCAN_LIST, 0xc=SET_NET_SETTINGS, 0xd=GET_PSK, 0xe=PSK, 0xf=UPGRADE, 0x10=START_OPEN_AP, 0x11=COMMIT_SETTINGS, 0x12=SETUP_REAUTHORIZE, 0x13=ENABLE_WIFI, 0x14=START_ISLAND, 0x15=TIMED_OUT, 0x16=LOCK_REGISTRATION, 0x17=REGISTRATION_KEY}; immediately followed by the NS2_SETUP_MODE_* enum {0=NONE,1=NFC,2=CHIRP,3=MANUAL_PIN,4=CLIENT_PIN,5=CHIRP_WITH_BUTTON,6=QR_CODE,7=QR_CODE_WITH_BUTTON,8=QR_CODE_WITH_REMOTE}. The NS2_STATE_* table at 0x1004f4ac is 18 rows x 44 bytes {name*, up-to-5 per-state handler slots, common handler 0x1001c094, extra slot, 0,0} with id = row index: {0=RESET,1=SETUP_STANDBY,2=SETUP_START,3=SETUP_DISCOVERY,4=SETUP_DISCOVERY_INTERACTION,5=SETUP_PIN_EXCHANGED,6=SETUP_WAITING,7=SETUP_ACTIVE,8=SETUP_COMPLETE,9=SETUP_UPDATE,0xa=OPEN_AP_PENDING,0xb=OPEN_AP_STANDBY,0xc=ENABLE_WIFI_PENDING,0xd=DEACTIVATED,0xe=REAUTH_PENDING,0xf=ISLAND_PENDING,0x10=SCANNING,0x11=CHECKING_CREDS}

bin_wacd.name: wacd (wireless access config)
bin_wacd.summary: wacd (/wifi/wacd): the Apple WAC (Wireless Accessory Configuration) provisioning agent. It opens the temporary WAC soft-AP, advertises an Apple Device IE built from the unit's MDP identity, and reports provisioning progress to netstartd over a dedicated IPC socket.
todo: Established: full wacd flow - MDP->SSID synthesis, soft-AP + Apple Device IE, WirelessSetup bonjour service, 6-msg progress channel to netstartd, USR1 timeout test hook.
Residual: the exact credential fields inside the WAC STA/DONE payloads (the Apple-side handshake carries them; anacapad/netstartd only see the milestone name)
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): WAC provisioning handoff = the /var/run/wac_mode state machine + wpa_supplicant/netstartd IPC transitions documented under wac_mode.

IPC channel: connects to /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc and sends WAC_AP_OPEN, WAC_AP_CLOSE, WAC_STA, WAC_DONE, WAC_TMO, WAC_STOP, WAC_ERROR notifications ('Send WAC AP Open/Close/Timeout/Done/Stop/Error msg fail'); owns /tmp/wacd.pid; SIGUSR1 simulates a WAC timeout ('USR1 signal received - simulating WAC timeout'); logs a 'Staying aliiiivveee' keepalive.

WAC payload: builds the WAC SSID via WifiFuncsWacFillBinarySsid and Base64-encodes it ('Could not initialize WAC SSID', 'Base64 encoded WAC SSID exceeds max length of SSID'), creates the AppleDeviceIE ('Create Apple Device IE fail', 'Setting up IE and bailing'), and starts the platform software AP ('Platform SW AP start fail').

Identity source: reads MDP page1 (model - 'Could not read MDP page1 data, cannot determine model') and MDP page2 (variant - 'unknown variant', 'Unexpected variant value %u') through the libflash/hal_flash wrappers so the WAC advertisement matches the hardware SKU.

Resolved: wacd internals - links libwifi (WifiFuncsWacFillBinarySsid, PlatformSoftwareAccessPoint{Start,Stop}), libsonosutils IPC (InitializeIPCContext -> /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc), libsonos-mdp (sonosMdpSerialToString + sonosGetFinalColorVariant + sonosGetColorVariantString) and libflash (hal_flash_get_mdp{,2}). The WAC soft-AP SSID is built from MDP: serial hex + color-variant name, base64-encoded with a length guard ('Base64 encoded WAC SSID exceeds max length of SSID'). Advertised Bonjour service type literal 'com.sonos.protocol.WirelessSetup'. Milestone strings {Configuration Started, Configuration Received, Configuration Complete} feed WAC_STA progress. Control: SIGUSR1 = 'simulating WAC timeout' test hook; 'Setting up IE and bailing' = IE-broadcast-only mode (no soft-AP); 'Staying aliiiivveee' keepalive log.

Resolved: failure ladder - 'Could not get flash info' (hal_flash_info_init), 'Could not read MDP page1 data, cannot determine model' (fatal), 'Could not read MDP page2 data, unknown variant'/'Unexpected variant value %u' (warn-only), 'Platform SW AP start fail %u', 'Create Apple Device IE fail %u'. Outbound message set to netstartd proven: WAC_AP_OPEN, WAC_AP_CLOSE, WAC_TMO(timeout), WAC_DONE, WAC_STOP, WAC_ERROR.

bin_wpa_supplicant.name: wpa_supplicant (Sonos build)
bin_wpa_supplicant.summary: wpa_supplicant v2.10 (/wifi/wpa_supplicant) with a custom '-D sonos' driver wrapper instead of nl80211, bound to ath0 and bridge br0. Config is generated on the fly by /wifi/wpaconfig (or manually by /wifi/sta-assoc) rather than shipped.
todo: Residual: the '-D sonos' driver-wrapper ioctl contract lives inside the binary's driver table and the ath_driver.ko interface; not recoverable from strings beyond the fact that it replaces nl80211.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): Sonos build = stock supplicant driven through wpaconfig/sta-assoc + htapsatwpa.conf; control-interface events feed netstartd.

Launch contract (from sta-assoc): 'wpa_supplicant -s -B -D sonos -i ath0 -b br0 -c <conf>' - syslog logging, daemonized, custom 'sonos' driver, bridged to br0; sta-assoc then pokes udhcpc with SIGUSR1 to force a DHCP attempt.

Config generation (/wifi/wpaconfig): writes /var/run/wpa_supplicant.conf with eapol_version=1 + ap_scan=1, then one 'network={ssid=<hex>,scan_ssid=1,psk=<hex>,priority=2}' block per credential plus an open 'key_mgmt=NONE' fallback block for each SSID; sources credentials from NFWSSID/NFWPwd keyval fields of a settings file, or from an SSID-list file of 'SSID=<hexssid>:<hexkey>' lines (SSID_FILE=1 mode).

Driver-side mirroring: wpaconfig pushes the allowed STA SSID list into the Atheros driver with 'athconfig stassidlistclr ath0', 'athconfig wossidclr ath0' and 'athconfig stassidlistadd ath0 <SSIDHEX> <KEYLEN>' - the driver enforces the SSID whitelist independently of supplicant scanning.
Debug knobs: /jffs/debug/wpa_proto, /jffs/debug/wpa_ptk, /jffs/debug/wpa_gtk inject proto=/pairwise=/group= overrides into generated configs.

Build surface: strings show the standard v2.10 feature set (SAE, PMF/IGTK/BIGTK install paths, RRM, Gas/ANQP, bssid_ignore/bssid_accept, roaming_consortiums) plus the 'sonos' driver wrapper ('Override interface parameter: driver/ctrl_interface/bridge'); the Sonos-specific part is the driver shim, the supplicant core is upstream.

bin_athconfig.name: athconfig / radartool (Atheros tools)
bin_athconfig.summary: athconfig (/wifi/athconfig) is the Atheros radio control utility that every other network component shells out to; radartool (/wifi/N/radartool) is its DFS companion. Together they own channel/Freq control, key cache, SSID allowlists, QoS EDCA, scan, antenna, neighbor blocking, and radar/CAC/NOL management on ath0/ath1.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): Atheros radio config + DFS - radar events coordinate channel vacate through dfs.ko with the athconfig ioctls.

Verb catalog from usage strings: setantswitch V|A|B; get/setchannel (+getchannels); scanstart TYPE [SSID], scangetresults, scanclearssid, getacs (auto channel select w/ DFS/CAC/NOL/Radar columns); setopenmode; stassidlistadd netif SSIDINHEX KEYLEN, stassidlistclr, wossidclr; stasetkeylen, setwepkey WEPkey|disable, keycache {0=init,1=free/all,2=clrhw/all,3=bad/all,10=free/4,20=clrhw/4,30=bad/4}, forcegtkrekey; sethhid, setuuid; setnetsettings mode data; ssidinbeaconenable, nsprobeenable, blockadvertisedpath, neighbor MAC allow/filter; getwirelesscnx, getnchains (maxspatialstreams RX/TX), getmcs, getlinkstats [threshTx threshLat], getmibcc, getqosedca/setqosedca qosidx aifsn cwmin cwmax [txop] [minfbp], sethptxqretries ms each total, gettxbackpressure, setlatencybucket ms, settxpower, setintrmitig ath0 rxfirst rxlast txfirst txlast, txtrigger [seqnum], conttx ifs/count/size/burst, senddeauth DA SUBTYPE REASON, packet-sniffer mode (count/mac-filter/len-filter/timeout/conttx), testpoint get/set.

Stats output fields: 'Freq = %u; PHY error count = %u', 'GTKFailMode = %u; GTKFailCount = %u NoGCFailCount = %u', 'SSID = %.*s', 'Security keyMgmt: %s Peer: %s Group: %s', per-neighbor 'Tx pkts/min %d; rssiFrom %d; rssiTo %d; PER %d', rates as 'ath rate: %d Mbps / MCS %d', QoS table 'Q(%d) %3d %4d %4d %5d %3d %2d %3d %5d'.

DFS handling: dfs.ko is loaded by /etc/Configure when present; athconfig verbs nolclear, nolenable 0|1, setnoltimeout, cacenable 0|1, cactimeout, cacreset, bangradar manage the channel-availability-check and non-occupancy-list lifecycle; getacs prints a channel table with FREQ/CM/AGE/CU/APs/LLs/Radar/Flags columns.

radartool: separate diagnostic binary ('radartool (-i <interface>) [cmd]') with commands bangradar, dfstime, dfsdebug, firpwr, rrssi, maxlen, numdetects, en_relpwr_check, relpwr, en_block_check - radar-detection tuning for the Atheros DFS block (some knobs AR5413-only).

bin_dropbearmulti.name: dropbearmulti (SSH)
bin_dropbearmulti.summary: Dropbear SSH multi-call binary v2020.81 (/bin/dropbearmulti). Launched only on unlocked devices: /etc/scripts/run_sshd.sh waits for /tmp/device_unlocked_flag then execs 'dropbear -R -F'.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): consolidated unlock/key story - device_unlock writes the flag + ssh_authorized_keys append path; factory vs dev keys under cert_files.

Version/config: Dropbear 2020.81 built from upstream source (paths ../dropbear-2020.81/... embedded), multi-call dispatch ('Dropbear SSH multi-purpose v%s', applets include dropbear and dropbearkey, 'SSH-2.0-dropbear_2020.81' banner).

Launch gate: inittab respawns run_sshd.sh -> trackrestart dropbear -> waitwhiletrue '[ ! -f /tmp/device_unlocked_flag ]' -> 'dropbear -R -F' (regenerate host keys as needed, foreground). The flag is created by Configure when /etc/unlocked_build_flag or /jffs/system/Configure.dev exists.

Keys: host key /jffs/persist/ssh/dropbear_ecdsa_host_key (ECDSA, regenerated if empty); authorized_keys at /jffs/sys/debug/ssh/authorized_keys (created empty if missing). Console login is a separate channel: inittab respawns secure_console_login.sh on /dev/ttyS0 gated on /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable.

bin_chronyd.name: chronyd / chronyc (time sync)
bin_chronyd.summary: Stock chronyd (/sbin/chronyd) + chronyc (/bin/chronyc) NTP client pair against Sonos pool names; the system clock they maintain feeds the household time consensus (anacapad sntp_server) and muse systemTime/time resources.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): sources from chrony.conf + sntp.txt; feeds household clock via SNTP coordinator (sntp_server); muse systemTime/time resources + AC.* vars consume it.
Build flags string: '+CMDMON +NTP +REFCLOCK +RTC +PRIVDROP -SCFILTER -SIGND +ASYNCDNS -NTS -SECHASH +IPV6 -DEBUG' - async DNS and privdrop on; SCFILTER/SIGND/NTS/SECHASH off; no NTS.

chrony.conf: four pools 0-3.sonostime.pool.ntp.org each 'iburst maxsources 1' (resolve multiple addrs per pool name, stop polling pool once one source answers); driftfile /jffs/chrony/chrony.drift; logging {tracking,rawmeasurements,statistics} to /var/log/chrony; 'makestep 60 1' + 'maxchange 60 1 0' (step clock only once per operation and only when error >60s); 'port 0' disables NTP serving entirely.
Launch: /etc/runchrony via inittab - trackrestart chrony, waitfordns gate (chronyd cannot make progress before IP+DNS), stop flag /var/run/stopchrony, mkdir -p /jffs/chrony.
Sockets/pid: /var/run/chrony/chronyd.sock (chronyc command socket) and chronyd.pid; the diagprocessd menu item 18 runs 'chronyc -n sources -v' for diagnostics.

Resolved: shipped /etc/chrony.conf - pools 0..3.sonostime.pool.ntp.org iburst maxsources 1, driftfile /jffs/chrony/chrony.drift, logging {tracking,rawmeasurements,statistics} to /var/log/chrony, makestep 60 1 (step once per run iff error >60s), maxchange 60 1 0, port 0 (NTP serve disabled).

bin_net_utils.name: udhcpc / brctl / dhcp.script
bin_net_utils.summary: The DHCP/bridge plumbing trio: sbin/udhcpc is a Sonos-forked udhcp 0.9.8 client ('udhcpcd'), etc/dhcp.script is its event hook, and usr/sbin/brctl carries Sonos-specific bridge extensions.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): DHCP client + bridge control feed netconfig_fsm events; bridge topology = SonosNet mesh vs STA mode bridging.

udhcpc fork deltas (strings): signal-gated start ('Waiting up to 60s for a signal to start' / 'Timed out ... starting anyway'), renew steering via /tmp/udhcpc_renew_option (numeric renew type -> 'DHCP confirm/extend lease renew' vs 'init-reboot renew' vs deconfig->SELECTING), a dedicated SSID-change listener socket ('FATAL: couldn't listen for SSID change'), a raw ARP listener socket, gratuitous ARP + zero-conf probe ('Sending zc arp probe', '/tmp/udhcpc_resp_mac_addr'), internal FSMs named TDP and IODP, per-request counters 'rna/rns/rnn/rqa/rqs/rqn/zc/dup', pid /tmp/udhcpc.pid, and a hostname DHCP option.

dhcp.script event emission (etc/dhcp.script): invoked as 'dhcp.script {nak|deconfig|renew|bound}' by udhcpc - deconfig zeroes the interface and installs the 255.255.255.255 + 224.0.0.0/4 local multicast routes; renew|bound rewrites /etc/resolv.conf (search + nameserver lines), ifconfigs the lease ip/broadcast/netmask, replaces default gw routes, re-adds the link-local/multicast routes, and removes /var/run/waitforip to release boot waiters; nak only logs.

Bridge topology: brctl is stock bridge-utils plus the Sonos verbs {setmac, uplink, showstats, showstp}; Configure creates the bridge environment (bridge.ko), setmac assigns eth%d/ath0/ath1/br0 MACs, wpa_supplicant binds ath0 into br0 (-b br0), and SonosNet/STP stats are exposed through showstats/showstp (diagprocessd menu items 11-14).

bin_keyval.name: keyval
bin_keyval.summary: keyval (/usr/sbin/keyval): a KEY=value line extractor used by boot and config scripts, not a persistent store - each call re-parses the given file.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): keyval = the boot/update script KV store; consumers = boot scripts + update machinery.
Semantics: 'keyval ^KEY [file]' scans KEY=value lines and prints the value; -d<sep> and -s change delimiters.

Consumers proven in-tree: /etc/Configure ('mdputil | keyval ^SERIAL' for hostname), /wifi/wpaconfig ('keyval ^NFWSSID', 'keyval ^NFWPwd', 'keyval ^SSID' for WPA config and ssid-list parsing), opt/bin/anacapactl, and the netstartd/wacd flows that read netsettings.txt/localsettings.txt fields.

bin_setmac.name: setmac
bin_setmac.summary: setmac (/usr/sbin/setmac): assigns interface MAC addresses during /etc/Configure, deriving them from the MDP identity page.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): target interfaces = wifi + ethernet MACs sourced from the manufacturing data partition.

Behavior from strings: reads the MDP serial via libsonos-mdp ('Using MDP serial number %s'), reads the radio MAC from /tmp/wifi_card_mac_addr ('Current wifi address'), programs eth%d, ath0, ath1 and br0 via SIOCSIFHWADDR ('SIOCSIFHWADDR for (%s, %s)', refuses overwrite 'mac address already set for (%s)'), and prints 'br0=%s' in keyval form for scripts.

bin_capsh.name: capsh
bin_capsh.summary: capsh (/sbin/capsh): stock libcap capability shell - present in the image but unused by any shipped script or binary.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): capability-shell used by daemon launcher wrappers to drop privileges; identified consumers = the service start scripts.
Binary is upstream capsh: --caps=, --drop=, --keep=, --chroot=, --secbits=, --inh=, --addamb/--delamb/--noamb, --has-ambient, --modes, --strict, --print surface.

No invocation found: a rootfs-wide grep across etc/, opt/, wifi/, init scripts and binary string tables shows zero references; anacapad drops privileges itself via '-u anacapa -C all=eip' in anacapactl. Residual: it is a provisioned-but-dormant tool (available for dev shells on unlocked devices).

bin_pcap.name: pcap
bin_pcap.summary: pcap (/bin/pcap): a libpcap capture wrapper invoked by anacapad's hidden /pcap status route to produce downloadable packet captures.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): output = trace.pcap streamed via the /pcap route; invocation = /bin/pcap with filter args from network_tools.

CLI: 'usage: %s [-B N] [-c N] [-i name] [-P] [-s N] <savefile> [pcap filter]' - buffer size, packet count, interface, promiscuous flag, snaplen, output file, and a compiled bpf filter; implemented directly on libpcap (pcap_create/set_buffer_size/set_snaplen/set_promisc/set_timeout/activate/compile/setfilter/dump_open/dump_flush).

Invocation path: anacapad's /pcap local route builds the command '/bin/pcap - not (host %s and port %d)' - i.e. captures everything except the controller connection that triggered it - and returns the file as 'attachment; filename="trace.pcap"'. Output location/rotation is the caller-specified savefile; no daemon-side rotation exists.

bin_sonosledmgrd.name: sonosledmgrd
bin_sonosledmgrd.summary: sonosledmgrd (/opt/bin/sonosledmgrd): the LED manager daemon that executes the R_LED_* mode vocabulary shared with anacapad's leds_zp library - it owns the physical hal_led device, pattern engine, and captouch feedback color.
todo: Residual: the numeric id assigned to each request kind (set-pattern vs apply-mode etc) - the dispatch is a sequential u32 field reader with the id-to-handler binding inlined in the connection loop, no standalone table.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): sonosledmgrd_logger.toml = the daemon log config; LED state machine + client IPC documented via the anacapad-side R_LED vocabulary.

Mode execution: applies every mode in the anacapad-decoded table ('applyLEDMode R_LED_UPGRADE/BROKEN_DEVICE/JOIN_HH[_OPEN]/BEGIN_SETUP_MODE/IN_SETUP_MODE/WAC/WAC_TIMEOUT/BREAK_POP/SHUTDOWN/HHID/TRANSFER_REGISTRATION/CONTROL_FEEDBACK/IDENTIFY_PLAYER/AUDIO_OFF/MUTED/FAULT/WAITING_TO_PLAY/WAITING_TO_PAUSE/PLAYING/WARN/DEMO_MODE/DEMO_CONFIGURE_IR') plus hardcoded patterns set_pattern_for_mode {FACTORY_RESET, BOOTING, JOIN_HH, JOIN_HH_OPEN, BYPASS_BLOCKED, BYPASS, CLONE_CHECK_FAIL} and resumeDefaultLEDPattern fallbacks.

Pattern record format: 'cksum=%08x, flags=%04x repeats=%u num_steps=%u led_ids=%08x' with per-step 'step[%d]= r=%02x, g=%02x b=%02x hold_time=%u fade=%u' - RGB step sequences with hold/fade timing, repeated and bitmasked across LED ids; writes through hal_led_open/brightness with a hal token guard (led_get_hal_token), plus led_set_feedbackFlash and captouch default-color control.

Lifecycle: /etc/runledmgrd respawns it with trackrestart and a stale-pid watchdog loop; --fr runs the factory-reset flash pattern (driven by frcheck rc != 1 in Configure); /var/run/sonosledmgrd.flash_booting_led marks boot-time LED activity; writes /var/run/sonosledmgrd.pid.

Client surface: socket-based IPC (socket/bind imports, 'hostPort' field, client channel name '/sonosledmgrd-external' referenced from anacapad) serving the leds_zp client lib shared with anacapad and netstartd (netstartd contains the same 'applyLEDMode R_LED_WAC_TIMEOUT' call site).

Logger: /opt/conf/sonosledmgrd_logger.toml (/jffs/conf/ override first) - sonosledmgrd.log at 256KB rotating 64KB preserved, defaultLevel=4 (WARN), domains {ledmgrd, LEDManager, ledmgr-server, leds_zp} at level 6 (INFO).

IPC framing proven: the client socket protocol reads fixed 4-byte words sequentially (read(fd,buf,4) at 0x100e4cf8, 0x100e854c, 0x100e856c, 0x100e8588, 0x100e85d0 inside the connection loop) - each request is a sequence of u32 fields (id/args) rather than a self-describing frame; arg presence branches on each read result. Byte-level arg extraction via rlwinm byte masks.

bin_busybox_applets.name: busybox applet inventory
bin_busybox_applets.summary: BusyBox v1.35.0 multi-call binary (/bin/busybox, 526KB PPC MSB) providing init and the shell/utilities the boot and daemon scripts run on.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): Sonos-relevant applets = the applet table lists available commands (httpd not present; flash/tftp tools per config).

Full compiled-in applet list (133, extracted from the packed applet_names table): [[ arping ash awk basename blkid cat chgrp chmod chown chvt clear cmp cp cttyhack cut date dd df dirname dmesg dnsdomainname du echo egrep env expand expr false fbset fgrep find fold free ftpget ftpput getopt getty grep gunzip gzip halt head hexdump hostname hwclock ifconfig ifdown ifup init insmod iostat kill killall ln login ls lsmod lsof lspci makedevs md5sum mdev mkdir mkfifo mknod modinfo more mount mpstat mv nc netstat nslookup od patch pidof ping ping6 pmap poweroff printf ps pwd reboot reset rm rmdir rmmod route rtcwake rx sed seq sh sha1sum sha256sum sha512sum sleep sort strings stty sync sysctl tail tar taskset tee test time top touch traceroute traceroute6 true tty umount uname uniq uptime usleep uudecode uuencode vi watchdog wc wget which xargs yes zcat

Sonos-relevant subset: init (parses /etc/inittab: sysinit=/etc/Configure, respawn for sshd/ledmgrd/netstartd/mdnsd/diagprocessd/anacapad/chronyd/sddpd/console-login, shutdown=/etc/init.d/rcK, ctrlaltdel=reboot), insmod/lsmod/rmmod for the /modules + /wifi/N .ko stack, ifconfig/route/netstat + mdev for device nodes, hwclock/rtcwake, watchdog, dmesg, killall/pidof used by rundaemon.sh helpers, wget/nc for diagnostics, and getty is bypassed in favor of secure_console_login.sh.

No httpd/tftpd/syslogd/crond applets - services are real binaries; busybox supplies only the POSIX shell layer and core tools (no flash tools either; MTD access goes through libflash in mdputil/upgrade).

kmod_sonos.name: Sonos kernel modules
kmod_sonos.summary: Sonos kernel modules under /modules (loaded by /etc/Configure in this order): sonos_device.ko -> chk.ko -> hwevent_queue.ko -> audiodev.ko -> ir_rcvr.ko (optional). All are Dual BSD/GPL, vermagic 2.6.35-yocto-standard.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): hwevent_queue consumer = the hw_events readEvent path; device nodes {chk, ir_rcvr, audiodev, sonos_device} with ioctl surfaces documented per consumer.

sonos_device.ko: the substrate - 'Sonos device driver' creating the sonos_dev device class (sonos_device_create/destroy exports, device_create_vargs); every other Sonos kmod registers its char node through it ('Error creating <x> sonos device').
chk.ko: 'chk driver' - registers the /dev/chk character device used by anacapad's watchdog health-check; ioctl-based ('Unknown IOCTL called', copy_to/from_user guards).

hwevent_queue.ko: 'Driver for Hardware Event Notifications' - the kernel side of the hw-event ring (hwevtq_send_event_defer); consumed by anacapad's hw_events readEvent dispatch and surfaced to userland via libhwmessagelib netlink multicast groups {AUDIO,BATTERY,BUTTON,BUTTON_POWER,CAPZONE,HT,LED,SENSOR,TEMP,WAKEUP,SWITCH}.

audiodev.ko: the Limelight audio controller - 'Limelight audioctl driver' + Freescale 'TDM Driver For MPC8xxx' + 'MPC8453Q accelerometer driver' merged. Devices/procs: /dev/audioctl char node (buttons via hal_inputs_get_buttons_state, amp power/mute through tas5708_* calls, 'automatically muting amps due to fault', fault latching 'latched faults cleared on mute'), the TDM dsp char node (mpc8xxx_tdm_ioctl, TDM Transmit/Receive Under-Run + Sync error logs), /proc/driver/ledctl, /proc/driver/mma8453q + mma7660 accel + orient procs, thermalsensor proc, fpga_reg/fpga_data/fpga_all procs, SPDIF interrupt counters (lock/block/parity), button simulation ('Simulating %s button press for %dms'), exported audioctl_updateIrSelect.

ir_rcvr.ko: 'IR Receiver driver' - read() returns raw decoded symbols ('Read must be at least %d bytes (1 max-length symbol)', 'IR Data: %08x'), ioctls set IR timeout and runt-filter duration, write/seek unsupported.

kmod_ath_wifi.name: Atheros WiFi modules
kmod_ath_wifi.summary: The Qualcomm Atheros 802.11 stack under /wifi/N plus the bridge module: load order enforced by /etc/Configure is adf.ko -> asf.ko -> ath_hal.ko -> dfs.ko (if present) -> ath_driver.ko, then /wifi/bridge.ko.
todo: Residual: most of the 385 cmd slots route to shared helper arms (ath_stop/reset_rxtx_stats/arg-copy stubs) rather than distinct named handlers - the ~30 bindings above are the strong ones; remaining cmds need per-case-body disasm to bind exact handler (mechanical, voluminous).
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): DFS channel-vacate = radar event -> dfs.ko -> channel switch coordinated with athconfig.

Load order/dependencies (modinfo): adf.ko 'Qualcomm Atheros Device Framework' (no deps), asf.ko 'Atheros Device Module' (adf services), ath_hal.ko 'Atheros HAL' (depends=asf, the proprietary HAL by Errno Consulting/Sam Leffler), dfs.ko 'DFS Support for Atheros 802.11' (optional), ath_driver.ko 'Sonos WiFi driver' (depends=dfs - the Sonos-customized driver on top of the HAL), bridge.ko (GPL, ethernet bridging for br0).

SonosNet control surface: userland does not ioctls the driver directly - it shells to /wifi/athconfig verbs (see bin_athconfig: setchannel/getacs, stassidlistadd/clr, keycache, sethhid/setuuid, ssidinbeaconenable, nsprobeenable, blockadvertisedpath, setnetsettings, txtrigger, conttx, senddeauth) which map onto ath_driver ioctls; wpa_supplicant binds through the custom '-D sonos' driver wrapper.

DFS flow: dfs.ko supplies radar detection; athconfig owns the CAC/NOL lifecycle verbs (cacenable/cactimeout/cacreset, nolenable/setnoltimeout/nolclear) and test injection (bangradar); radartool tunes detector thresholds (firpwr, rrssi, dfstime, numdetects, relpwr/block checks). Channel vacate on radar = driver event -> dfs.ko NOL entry -> netstartd channel reselection via getacs.

athconfig verb->ioctl map RECOVERED: ath_driver.ko is NOT stripped (full .symtab present). ath_ioctl (.text+0xf85c, 0x3580B) bounds-checks cmd<=0x180 then dispatches through a 0x181-entry self-relative jump table at .rodata+0x5c (entries filled by .rela.rodata relocs); cmd>0x180 goes to a tail chain at 0x11524 (handles 0x752f and the 0x8b.. SIOCDEVPRIVATE range). Named handler bindings resolved via relocs: set_uuid=0x97, set_hhid=0x2, set_hhid_aes_key_channel=0x8, set_aes_key=0x15, set_nchains=0xf, set_channel={0x35,0xd9,0xe9}, hostap_set_key=0x28, hostap_clear_key=0xe8, del_key={0x9a,0xc8}, scan_start=0x9d, scan_abort=0x136, scan_get_results=0x163, scan_clear_ssid=0xe4, send_deauth=0x164, sta_get_state=0x139, sta_has_wireless_cnx=0x133, send_netstart={0xd,0x1b,0x1d,0x29-0x2c}, get_wd_info=0x17f, path_mgr_{get_learned_hops=0x65,set_have_uwc=0x9b,get_have_uwc=0x13c}, get_channel_list={0x52,0x53,0x58}, deauth_sta=0x20, sta_scan_start_event=0xdc, sta_simple_data_event=0x17c, rx_hist_to_user=0x16d, wait_on_txqs=0x6e, continuous_beacon_change={0x20,0x21,0x23}, mibcc_show={0xcb,0xcc}.

fmt_upd.name: .upd package format
fmt_upd.summary: The .upd container format, now decoded from package/86.10-80260-1-9.upd. Sections are a linear chain of 16-byte records {magic u32 0x497f1635 (bytes 49 7f 16 35), type u32 LE, length u32 LE including the header, reserved u32} followed by the payload.
todo: Residual: byte-order of {keyId, nonce/iv, wrapped-key, tag} inside the 40-byte block - AEAD scheme and section vocabulary proven; the per-field split needs a dynamic parse or libsonoscrypto internals (exports are stripped ZZnnnn symbols)
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): .upd layout = header {version, MINCOMPATVER-style minimum fields, model targets} + manifest + signature over the payload; update_machinery covers the check side.

Section table of the shipped image (all verified by parsing): type 0x01 = target version triplet {cmaj=86, cmin=10, cbld=80260} as u32 LE; type 0x15 = feature manifest, newline-separated capability names ('2021_11_PATCHES:', 'UBI_RED_KEY_WITH_NONCE:', 'MAX_MDP_VERSION_6:', '2023_01/2023_12/2024_12_PATCHES:') - these are the strings the updater's 'Critical UPD feature (%s: %s) not supported by player' check reads; three type 0x02 blocks carry min/max feature-range tuples ({1,9,1,1,0,-2,-1}, {-3,2,0,0,0,0,0x22,7}, {-2,0x20,0,-2,0,-2,-1} with 0xfffffffe/0xffffffff sentinels = open bounds) - the player-feature compatibility ranges.

Payload sections 0x03 (1.9KB - the preinstall/upgrade script class), 0x06 (1.79MB - kernel.uImage class), 0x04 (13.9MB - rootfs.squashfs class), 0x0d (55KB - device-payload class) all share the same enveloped inner header: u32 magic 0xca996488, u32 0x13a (inner header length 314), u16/u32 fields {ver=1, flags=0, count=1, stamp 0x00140312}, a 40-byte wrapped-key/digest block, then the encrypted blob - matching /bin/upgrade strings 'Enveloped data parse/decrypt*', 'Encrypted section too small', 'Out of space while decrypting section'.

Trust anchors: type 0x16 (149KB, res=0) is the certificate/manifest bundle - the bytes /bin/upgrade saves to /jffs/sys/run/rcb/upd_cert_bundle.rcb on parse failure; it opens with a u32 timestamp 0x621da74d + table-of-contents counters. type 0x11 (364B, res=1) is the trailing signature section sharing the bundle's timestamp prefix - verified via sonosRcbVerifySig; 'encrypted signature section not supported' and 'invalid Sonos signature section length' guard it.

The reserved/flags word discriminates plaintext vs enveloped sections: 0 on the version/feature/cert sections, 4 on all enveloped payloads, 1 on the signature. Minimum-version semantics live in the type-0x02 range tuples and the type-0x15 feature names rather than a MINCOMPATVER field - none exists in this image.

Resolved: the .upd section-type vocabulary is the libsonoscrypto name table @lib fileoff 0x2b90-0x2c54 - 17 stride-12 rows {0x16, name*, sectionId}: {0x20008:UPD, 0x2000c:Kernel, 0x20010:FPGA, 0x20014:M4, 0x20018:LK, 0x2001c:TEE, 0x20020:U-Boot, 0x20024:BL Combined, 0x20028:BL30, 0x2002c:BL31, 0x20030:BL32, 0x20034:BL33, 0x20038:FIP, 0x20040:FIRMWARE, 0x20044:ROOT_CERTS, 0x20048:JFFS_TARBALL, 0x2004c:BOOTSOUND}. Crypto provenance: envelope is mbedtls AEAD (cipher_update_ad + cipher_write_tag/check_tag; error strings "bad tag (decryption AEAD tag check failed)", "bad padding", "full block expected") with numbered signing keys ("%s signed with key %u" / "signing key %u is revoked") verified against {Sonos Device Authentication Root CA, Sonos Test Device Authentication Root CA} embedded roots. So the 40-byte inner block carries {keyId, aead nonce/iv, wrapped key, tag}-class fields.

Resolved: the verifier side (/bin/upgrade) names the inner machinery - "Sonos signature section" (length-checked, invalid length rejected), "Extra section %u found after signature" (signature must be the last section), "Multiple sections of type %u" rejected, "Required section %u missing" enforced, enveloped-data decrypt is EVP-style {init/update/final} with UBI_RED_KEY_WITH_NONCE key type, and per-section skip flags LACKS_{BOOTSOUND,M4}_PARTITION.

fmt_device_payload.name: device-payload.bin format
fmt_device_payload.summary: The per-model device-payload section inside the .upd (also shipped standalone as package/*-device-payload.bin). It is a manufacturing/configuration data image, NOT the kernel/rootfs - those are separate .upd section types (0x06 and 0x04).
todo: Residual: the complete tag namespace past 'e' and the destination flash offset for the payload - the tag walk reaches binary blobs whose per-tag semantics need either a live write trace or the factory producer spec.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): payload = the per-model kernel.uImage + rootfs.squashfs bundle written by the updater.

Layout: a 5-word prologue {0x0009, 0x0ff0, 0x0ff0, 0x0ff0, 0x0000} then a record stream of {u16 id/tag, u16 BE length, value} entries. The first record (id 0x0161, len 0x20) names the payload 'top_level.ncd;UserID=0xFFFFFFFF' (NCD = the board configuration-data class).

Tagged fields follow with ASCII-tag + u16 length: 'b' = firmware tag '3s50avq100', 'c' = date '2012/06/14', 'd' = time '23:19:49', then binary sections (tag 'e' and onwards) carrying erased-flash regions and calibration data.

Relationship to the other payloads: this is the model-specific board data the updater writes to its own flash region - the kernel.uImage and rootfs.squashfs ship as separate .upd sections (and as standalone package files), while device-payload.bin (55KB) is the small per-model calibration/config blob consumed by the type-0x0d section handler.

sonos_custom_libs.name: Sonos-custom shared libraries
sonos_custom_libs.summary: lib/ ships ~40 shared objects. Sonos-built libraries (libsonos*, libflash, libsyslib_hal, libhwmessagelib, libwifi) vs stock (mbedtls, ffmpeg, sqlite, etc.) split below.
todo: Residual: per-export consumer maps for the libsonos* set beyond the anchors already proven (each lib is large; the map above names the owning daemon per lib, not every symbol's call graph).
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): custom set = {libflash, libhwmessagelib, certval, DSP libs} with role map; per-lib exports enumerated from dynsym where present.

Sonos-built set: libsonosutils.so.1 (IPC helpers incl. ReadIPCHeader/WriteIPCMessage + sonosFactoryResetFull + arch info), libsonosminiutils.so.1 (file/int helpers, syslog glue), libsonos-mdp.so.1 (MDP serial/series/cert-variant accessors), libsonoscrypto.so.3 (mbedtls-wrapped crypto incl. sonosRcbVerifySig for .upd/rcb), libsonos-certval.so.2 + libsonos-root-cert-bundle.so.2 (cert validation + bundled roots), libsonos-time-c.so.1 (timeval math + sonosClockGetTime), libsonoseventreporter.so.1 (report_event telemetry), libsonossbcpacket.so.1 (satellite SBC packet codec), libsonossyslog.so.1 (syslog extension used by wpa_supplicant), libflash.so.1 (hal_flash_* mtd/MDP/FSN access), libsyslib_hal.so.1 (the hal_* device layer: audioctl, inputs/buttons/captouch/orientation, amps power/mute/hipower/rails, detect cable states, thermal, IR, gpio switches), libhwmessagelib.so.1 (hw-event netlink multicast groups AUDIO/BATTERY/BUTTON/BUTTON_POWER/CAPZONE/HT/LED/SENSOR/TEMP/WAKEUP/SWITCH), libwifi.so.1 (the 72-export WifiFuncs* API consumed by netstartd/wacd).

Stock third-party set: glibc family (libc/libm/libdl/libpthread/libresolv/libanl/libatomic/libcrypt/libutil/libthread_db/libnss_*/ld.so.1), libgcc_s, libz 1.2.11, mbedtls 2.x trio (mbedcrypto.16/mbedtls.21/mbedx509.7), ffmpeg libavcodec.59/libavformat.59/libavutil.57 (WMA etc.), libmpg123 (mp3), libdcadec (DTS), libsbc (Bluetooth SBC), libsmb2 (SMB2 client), libsqlite3, libdns_sd (mDNSResponder client to sbin/mdnsd), libpcap, libnl-3/libnl-genl-3, libuuid, libtomlc99, libprotobuf-nanopb.

bin_udhcpc.name: udhcpc (Sonos-patched DHCP client)
bin_udhcpc.summary: sbin/udhcpc = a Sonos-modified udhcpc 0.9.8 (banner 'udhcpcd, version %s'). Beyond stock busybox DHCP it adds: a file-based renew IPC (/tmp/udhcpc_renew_option carrying a renew-type integer {confirm/extend, init-reboot, deconfig}), IP-mode sentinels (/var/run/{specialIP,normalIP}), responder bookkeeping (/tmp/udhcpc_resp_mac_addr records the DHCP server MAC for diagnostics + cloud-reg dhcpMac input), IPv4LL fallback ('Force Zeroconf'/'Starting zeroconf process' with address-conflict detect 'Address duplication detected, INITIATING NEW DHCP'), startup gating on a netstartd signal ('Waiting up to 60s for a signal to start'/'Timed out waiting for a signal to start, starting anyway!!!'), and netif readiness waits ('Bridge is %s ready','Driver is %s ready').
resolved_findings: Decoded: renew-IPC contract - the renewer writes an integer type to /tmp/udhcpc_renew_option; udhcpc reads it ('Renew type: %d', 'Error: invalid renew type %d from file %s: Using %d instead' default fallback) and deletes it after consumption ('Error: unable to delete the file %s'). perform_renew() maps types to {confirm/extend-lease renew, init-reboot renew, deconfig-then-SELECTING}; 'Already requested a renew, now deconfig' collapses a second request.

Decoded: result counter line 'rna:%d rns:%d rnn:%d rqa:%d rqs:%d rqn:%d zc:%d dup:%d %s %s %s %s %s' plus named event literals {DHCP_RN_FAIL, DHCP_RQ_FAIL, DHCP_RN_NAK, DHCP_RQ_NAK, DHCP_DUP} - renew/request ack/nak counters, zeroconf count, duplicate-address count.

Decoded: lease lifecycle - 'No lease, forking to background'/'No lease, failing' (daemonize policy), 'Lease lost, entering init state', 'Received DHCP NAK' -> init, 'No lease time with ACK, using 1 hour lease' fallback, 'Sending gratuitous ARP' after bind, lease/renewal/bound/deconfig state names.

Decoded: monitoring - an 'address monitor' socket watches the assigned address, an ARP socket watches for conflicts, and an SSID-change listener triggers re-DHCP ('FATAL: couldn't listen for SSID change'). Reads /jffs/netsettings.txt for static-net config.

Resolved: the client hook is /etc/dhcp.script - verbs {nak,deconfig,renew,bound}; deconfig ifconfigs the iface to 0.0.0.0 and installs 255.255.255.255 + 224.0.0.0/4 multicast routes; renew|bound rewrites /etc/resolv.conf {search <domain>, nameserver per $dns} and sets broadcast/netmask. Launch contract from netconfig.sh: udhcpc -f -s /etc/dhcp.script -i br0 -w ath0 -h <hostname> -d access.bestbuy.com with -z on station/satellite/sta_and_sat and -F -W 20 on island.

Resolved: the /tmp/udhcpc_renew_option type enum is {0=init-reboot renew, 1=confirm/extend lease renew} - the file is fscanf'd '%d\n', one-shot deleted, values >1 clamp to 0 ('Error: invalid renew type %d from file %s: Using %d instead'); perform_renew(type): type==0 enters the state-indexed init-reboot flow (jump tables 0x100070c8/0x100070a4 over the 9-state DHCP FSM), type==1 runs the confirm/extend path ('Performing a DHCP confirm/extend lease renew' -> renew send, unicast/broadcast by flag); in the wrong states it logs 'Already requested a renew, now deconfig' or 'Renew requested in state %d, back to SELECTING'

CONSUMER: no tag-compare dispatch exists anywhere in .text (0x82/0x86/0xae/0x93/0x94 compares absent) - the entries are opaque field descriptors walked generically by the f_109dxxxx TLV serialization family (stride-8 {tag,val} pairs, FFFFFFFF terminator), the same helper class used by the WSS registry. spec_pairs.consumer: CONSUMER FOUND: the layout/validator switch rooted at 0x10927c84 (epilogue tail 0x10927c70) dispatches on the b-field type index (r4): explicit cases 0x4e/0x62/0x70/0x71/0x72/0x120/0x144/0x146 with a default branch for indices < 0x13a that bitfield-decodes a packed member descriptor (rlwinm/slwi/or chains) into {count, byte-size} pairs stored at consecutive state slots (0x348/0x34c here, parallel slots 0x190/0x194, 0x330/0x334, 0x340/0x344, 0x380/0x384). So each spec entry {a=field_id, b=name_table_index} declares one member; the switch resolves the declared type into the member runtime layout.

spec_pair_decode_v2.observed_grammar: entries are bimodal: {0x82, 0x21-0x6a} (a=const, b=index-like value across 74 distinct values) vs {X, 0x34} (b=const 0x34, a=wide id space 0x13-0x141 incl. the unique ascending ids previously read as cmd-ids) plus small {n,n} pairs (counts) and occasional b=0x36/0x38/0x33/0x6a/0x4e variants
spec_pair_decode_v2.working_model: INFERRED: serialization schema ({field_id, schema_tag=0x34} declare fields; {0x82, type_index} entries reference param/field types (type-code enum 0x21-0x6a); consumed by the f_1015xxxx serializer-execs which walk the member arrays. a=0xae common-field marker vs unique ids = field identity, not cmd-id) revises the earlier per-OP cmd-id hypothesis; the unique-id correlation with lechmere-numbered ops may still hold if field-ids double as cmd-field keys

spec_pair_decode_v2.decoded_block_structure: op-descriptor blocks decode further: N x 0x80-byte op records (e.g. alarms: 6 recs @ 0x10f9f8c4..fc44, each {2 data ptrs, 0x109c9854, vtable_ptr, ~9 thunk ptrs into 101c06xx, shared 109d9770, per-op vtable ptr, thunks, 109d973c x2, 10ac45xx impl-vtable, ffffff88, 0, then 10acXXXX impl ptr, 10acXXXX, 109e8570, 109e857c, 109e858c, 0, 0}) followed by a shared 12-ptr block, then the {u32,u32} spec-pair stream terminated by ffffffff/ffffffff, then zero padding + a u32 op-count (alarms: 2), then the verb-name string pool + default-value literals (snoozeAlarm default 'PT0H5M0S' ISO-8601 duration sits in the pool after the verb names). The 101c06xx entries are trivial this-adjusting vfunc trampolines (stwu/addi/blr), confirming the records are vtable-bound polymorphic op descriptors.
spec_pair_decode_v2.pair_tag_hypothesis: b=0x34(52)=name_table[52]='upnpEvent' dominates the second slot; {0x82,T} pairs have T in 0x21-0x6a which all index the name table -> the pair stream is {tag_or_fieldid, name_table_index}; first slot alternates between unique ids (0x13..0x141 = likely field/verb numeric ids) and const tags (0x82, 0x86, 0xae). Second slot = the declared TYPE name (index into the 331-entry name table). Consistent with 'serialization schema': {field_id, type_tag} where type_tag 0x34 is the common upnpEvent wrapper type.
spec_pair_decode_v2.consumer_layout_dispatch: the spec-stream consumer found: dispatch rooted at 0x10927d24 (fn body ~0x10927c70+) is a per-member LAYOUT/validator switch keyed by name-table index (r4), with r5 carrying a packed member descriptor/value. Default branch (index<0x13a) decodes r5 bitfields (rlwinm/slwi/or chains) into {count,byte-size} pairs stored at consecutive slots of a state object (offsets 0x190/0x194, 0x330/0x334, 0x340/0x344, 0x380/0x384...): i.e. it computes member byte offsets into the runtime object. Special-cased indices: 0x118='track'/0x119='trackQuality' store raw u32s at 0x380/0x384 (trackQuality clamped <=0x4000 else saturates at 0x200000); 0x5b='deviceSoftwareUpdateStatus' + 0x5c='diagnosticInfo' pack into bits 0-1 of the word at 0x3ac (rlwimi); 0x8c='hdmiStatus'/0x8d='versionChanged' take value<=2 through converter f_1093bfc0 -> halfword at 0x3a2; 0x14='upnpEvent'/0x47='channelMapPair' store r5 at 0x394. Return codes: 0x2b=43 propagated as an error/skip code, 0 on handled members.
spec_pair_decode_v2.grammar_decoded: full alarms-block decode proves the pair stream IS {member_name_idx, type_name_idx}: {ok,upnpEvent} {ok,upnpEvent} {alarmList,upnpEvent} {alarm,upnpEvent} then {globalError,T}-runs where T cycles through the allowed member payload types (channelMapPair, chirpRequest, accessoryId, none, wiredSubStatus, bluetoothDevice). So: the SECOND slot is the declared payload type (a name-table index of a TYPE entry), the FIRST slot is the member/field name index. 'globalError' is a polymorphic member whose permitted type-set is enumerated as consecutive rows. 'upnpEvent' is the dominant wrapper type for evented members. ffffffff/ffffffff terminates the stream. The per-member applier f_10927c1c(r3=state, r4=member_idx, r5=value, r7=aux) is one slot in the 7-entry object vtable at 0x10f7f724, invoked via vfunc from the stream driver.
spec_pair_decode_v2.extracted: 51 spec-pair streams extracted to reference/muse_spec_streams.md (every muse resource's member→type map. Grammar confirmed: first slot = member/field name index, second slot = declared payload type index (both into the 0x10f97094 table); ffffffff/ffffffff terminates. Verbs/params follow the stream. 'ok' members always carry upnpEvent; 'globalError' rows enumerate the error/variant payload types; named members (alarmList, entitlementsList, zoneDefinition...) carry their typed payload. The 0x10ffca08 stream is a DIFFERENT table (none/accessoryId pairs) likely an enum/identity map, not the member:type grammar).
todo: Residual: the semantic name of each column element (the {4,1,6} triple shape and the single-word arity value) is not recoverable from .text - the column is build-time schema data consumed by the same generic TLV walk as the pair tags; no code dispatch reads it. Boundary documented.
resolved_findings: Established: {a,b} bimodal grammar, block structure (0x80-byte op records, 23-slot vtable spine, FFFFFFFF terminator), the accessor + serializer-exec consumers, and that tag dispatch is data-driven (no code compares on tag values). Still unknown: field-name bindings per entry index and the boundary between decoded spec pairs and the opaque descriptor tail. Next step: join entry indices to the verb/param literal run order to name each declared field.

Arity-table column census (13 blocks): the u32 run between the ffffffff terminator and the verb-name pool carries one arity word per pool name, repeated per op. Single-word ops: getRelativeTime block (1 verb -> {4}), startSignalling/stopSignalling ({4,4}), triggerSwap/requestSwap ({4,4}), subscribeUser/unsubscribeUser/getEntitlements ({6,6,6}), the clip block (4 names -> {4,4,4,4}). The settings block is the only multi-word form: 4 verbs -> {4,1,6} repeated once per verb, so all four settings ops share an identical 3-slot signature shape. The values do not count spec-pair stream entries (settings: 22 entries vs arity sum 44; subscribeUser: 7 entries vs arity 18), so the column is a declared-signature arity - most consistent with {in_params, out_params, total_fields} style member counts of the op request/response records, single-word blocks degenerating to a total. Whether the 3-word form is {in,out,total} or another triple remains data-model vocabulary: no .text consumer reads the column (same boundary as the spec-pair tags themselves).
spec_pair_decode_v2.tail_decode: OPAQUE TAIL DECODED on the alarms block (0x10f9fc74): after the ffffffff/ffffffff terminator comes a zero pad, a u32 count field (alarms: 2 - its semantic is ambiguous, channel/variant count vs subfield count), then the verb-name string pool as consecutive NUL strings ('getAlarms','fetchAlarm','createAlarm','updateAlarm','snoozeAlarm','removeAlarm') followed by param default literals ('PT0H5M0S' for snoozeAlarm), then the next descriptor block's pointer records (0x10f9fdac). The tail is the verb+default literal pool, not opaque data.
spec_pair_decode_v2.per_op_grouping: the 22 spec entries in the alarms block group per-op: marker entries {0xae,0x34}/{0x13,0x34}/{0x16,0x34} alternate with member runs {0x82,type_index}, yielding ~5 member-groups for 6 verbs (e.g. {0x13,0x34}+{0x82:0x47} vs {0x13,0x34}+{0x82:0x48,0x1,0x0,0x3f} vs {0x86,0x42}+{0x82:0x48,0x3f}). The marker word selects the op variant/dispatch id while the 0x82 run declares that op's typed members - consistent with {field/marker, name_table_type} pairs consumed by the layout switch at 0x10927c84.
spec_pair_decode_v2.tail_grammar: post-terminator tail verified across 7 descriptor blocks: {ffffffff/ffffffff terminator, 0..7 words zero pad, arity-u32 sequence, NUL-terminated name pool, 4-byte pad, next op-descriptor block}. The name pool holds the block's verb and field names verbatim (alarms: getAlarms..removeAlarm + 'PT0H5M0S' default; settings: getAllSettings/getSettingsGroup/updateAllSettings/updateSettingsGroup; registration: getRegistrationStatus/setRegistrationState/transferDevice*; entitlements: subscribeUser/unsubscribeUser/getEntitlements; fields: volumeRampDownSeconds/cancelAudioClip/clipMetadata/audioClips).
spec_pair_decode_v2.arity_table: the u32s between pad and name pool are a small-integer arity table keyed to the spec groups: observed uniform runs {4}x4 (fields), {6}x3 (entitlements), {2}x6, {4}x5, {4}x2 and one mixed run {4,1,6}x6 (settings, 18 words). Per-name arity holds in the uniform blocks (4 counts for 4 names, 3 counts for 3 names); the settings block packs three values per op signature, consistent with {member-count, signature-flag, spec-entry-count} triples but the exact column meanings are not pinned by any single block.

muse.spec_binding_note: Per-op spec binding RESOLVED: each op vtable (route impl.vtables) carries spec accessors at slot +0x58 returning {classId, blob ptr into packed u32 rodata pools}. The index->name lookup is f_109ecb5c (cmplwi 0x146 bound, slwi x4, lwzux on base 0x10f97094 = name-table slot 3) and the name->index reverse lookup is f_109ecb90 (strcmp walk from 'none'). SEMANTIC INDEX i MAPS TO TABLE SLOT 3+i: the first three pointer-table slots at 0x10f97088 are function pointers (f_10809540...), semantic index 0 = 'none'. 331 name entries, 383 object-spec descriptors across 0x10e9ba80 (96) + 0x10f9f87c (287), ~0x80B each, common accessor +0x58, classIds 1-12. Blob grammar = flat {fieldName, typeName} pairs: field slots carry wire keys (ok leads 170 response specs; globalError 561x; upnpResponse/upnpError for bridge ops; accountError/sessionError/playbackError), type slots carry 'upnpEvent' (the universal value wrapper) or concrete types. Repeated field name = type union (e.g. globalError:{chirpRequest|accessoryId|none|wiredSubStatus}); 'none' marks absent/optional slots. 'networkTestId' is an ordinary optional request field (16 ops, typed upnpEvent) whose name comes from the real resource v1/players/{playerId}/networkTest/{networkTestId} -- not an envelope marker. ~1116/1206 routes bound; ~45 unbound routes are outbound/client ops (no impl vtables) whose request shape is the per-namespace verb vocabulary.
muse.outbound_ops_note: ~45 ops ({authorization,catalog,entitlements,groups,history,playback,smartplay,systemReporting,zones} verbs (the full {ns,verb} registry at .data 0x110941d4-0x110943f4) are registered as 'outbound_registry': the player is the CLIENT, requests forward to the cloud over lechmere/WSS. They carry no local impl vtables and no +0x58 spec accessor BY DESIGN) the request body is serialized from the per-namespace field vocabulary (shared_primitives outbound vocab extraction). Per-verb field subsetting is code-driven and not statically enumerable.
